summary: Research MDA5/IFIH1 expression across CNS cell types and its change in multiple sclerosis, from 8 independent angles, each adversarially verified

research.dimension: Primary experimental literature on MDA5/IFIH1 expression in CNS parenchymal cell types (microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, OPCs, neurons) — baseline vs. stimulus-induced, human vs. mouse, mRNA vs. protein

findings.claim: In acutely purified HUMAN brain cell types (bulk RNA-seq), IFIH1 mRNA is highest in myeloid/microglial cells and endothelial cells, ~3x higher than astrocytes and ~6x higher than neurons. Ranking (mean FPKM): endothelial 6.5 > myeloid/microglia 5.1 >> astrocytes 1.70 ≈ oligodendrocytes 1.18 ≈ neurons 0.8.
findings.evidence: I downloaded and parsed the processed FPKM table GSE73721_Human_and_mouse_table.csv (GEO GSE73721; Zhang et al. 2016 Neuron) and extracted IFIH1 directly. Per-sample IFIH1 FPKM: cortical myeloid (microglia/macrophage) 6.0, 4.3, 5.1 (mean 5.13, n=3); endothelial 7.9 (47yo), 5.1 (13yo) (mean 6.5, n=2); mature cortical astrocytes (ages 8-63yo, n=12) 1.3, 1.8, 1.3, 2.0, 0.8, 2.4, 0.9, 2.0, 2.3, 1.5, 2.1, 2.0 (mean 1.70, range 0.8-2.4); hippocampal astrocytes (n=4) 1.3, 0.8, 1.1, 1.8 (mean 1.25); fetal cortical astrocytes (n=6) 2.1, 0.1, 1.0, 0.1, 3.8, 0.1 (mean 1.20); oligodendrocytes (n=5) 1.1, 1.3, 1.1, 1.3, 1.1 (mean 1.18); neuron (n=1, 25yo cortex) 0.8; whole cortex (n=4) 1.0, 1.5, 0.9, 1.8. No OPC sample exists in this dataset. Same-dataset comparators show the pattern is IFIH1-specific and not a generic myeloid artifact: DDX58/RIG-I is NOT myeloid-enriched (myeloid 1.7-2.2 vs astrocytes 1.6-5.0, endothelial 3.2-4.5, neuron 2.1, oligodendrocytes 1.2-3.2), whereas TLR3 is strongly myeloid-enriched in human (myeloid 17.1, 16.1, 8.0 vs astrocytes 0.6-1.8, neuron 0.1, oligodendrocytes 0.4-3.0).

findings.claim: Astrocytes acutely purified from the CORE of human brain tumors have 4-7x higher IFIH1 than normal cortical astrocytes, showing that astrocyte IFIH1 is an inducible, microenvironment-dependent quantity rather than a fixed cell-type constant.
findings.evidence: From the same GSE73721 FPKM table: tumor-core astrocytes IFIH1 = 9.6 (59yo), 11.4 (64yo), 6.5 (65yo) versus tumor-periphery astrocyte 0.1 and normal mature cortical astrocytes mean 1.70. That is a 3.8-6.7x elevation over the normal cortical astrocyte mean, and ~2x above the purified myeloid mean. DDX58/RIG-I in the same tumor-core samples is also elevated (6.6-7.1 vs 1.6-5.0 normal).

findings.claim: In acutely purified MOUSE CNS cell types, Ifih1 ranks endothelial >> microglia > neuron ≈ OPC ≈ astrocyte, and is at or below the detection floor in both newly formed and myelinating oligodendrocytes.
findings.evidence: I downloaded GSE52564_RAW.tar (GEO GSE52564; Zhang et al. 2014 J Neurosci) and parsed the per-sample FPKM .xls files. Ifih1 FPKM (2 replicates each): endothelial 2.10 / 2.01 (mean 2.06); microglia 0.60 / 0.48 (mean 0.54); neuron 0.15 / 0.68 (mean 0.42); OPC 0.33 / 0.11 (mean 0.22); astrocyte 0.29 / 0.12 (mean 0.21); newly formed oligodendrocyte 0.1 / 0.1; myelinating oligodendrocyte 0.1 / 0.1 (0.1 is the floor value used throughout this table); whole cortex 0.66 / 0.49 / 0.66. Purity confirmed in the same files by Aif1 (microglia 167/152 vs astrocyte 0.20/0.10), Pdgfra (OPC 627/563), Mbp (MO 114159/74692), Rbfox3 (neuron 19.3/16.8). Comparators: Ddx58 endothelial 8.47/8.76 >> OPC 2.39/1.83 > microglia 1.62/1.57 > astrocyte 1.25/1.36 > neuron 0.16/0.45 > MO 0.10/0.16; Dhx58/LGP2 highest in microglia (2.14/1.14); Mavs microglia 12.2/16.0 > astrocyte 9.1/7.5 > OPC 6.6 > oligodendrocyte 5.8-6.8 > endothelial 3.4/3.6 > neuron 0.61/1.02.

findings.claim: TLR3 (the extracellular/endosomal dsRNA receptor that MDA5 is usually contrasted with) shows an opposite cell-type distribution between mouse and human, so mouse glial dsRNA-sensing data cannot be transposed to human without caution — although IFIH1 itself keeps the same rank order (myeloid/endothelial high, oligodendrocytes/neurons low) in both species.
findings.evidence: My extraction from GSE52564 (mouse): Tlr3 FPKM astrocyte 16.52 / 8.66 and endothelial 9.04 / 8.81, versus microglia 2.62 / 2.60 and neuron 0.28 / 0.44. My extraction from GSE73721 (human): TLR3 FPKM myeloid 17.1 / 16.1 / 8.0, versus mature cortical astrocytes 0.6-1.8 and neuron 0.1. Ifih1/IFIH1, by contrast, is highest in endothelial + myeloid and lowest in oligodendrocytes/neurons in both species.

findings.claim: In the large human single-nucleus RNA-seq brain compendium, the fraction of nuclei with any detectable IFIH1 transcript ranks: endothelial 8.9% > perivascular macrophage 6.0% ≈ mature microglia 3.5% (all microglia 2.9%) > pericyte 2.1% > oligodendrocyte 0.64% ≈ astrocyte 0.62% > OPC 0.41% >> neuron 0.041%. Microglia are ~70x more likely than neurons to carry a detectable IFIH1 transcript.
findings.evidence: I queried the CZ CELLxGENE Discover 'Gene Expression' WMG API (POST https://api.cellxgene.cziscience.com/wmg/v2/query) for ENSG00000115267 (IFIH1) in Homo sapiens, tissue UBERON:0000955 (brain), is_rollup=true. Expressing-nuclei counts / total nuclei: endothelial cell 15,888/178,761 (8.89%, mean log-expr 1.831); endothelial cell of artery 662/7,115 (9.3%); capillary endothelial 581/8,502 (6.8%); vein endothelial 253/4,230 (6.0%); perivascular macrophage 1,294/21,465 (6.0%); mature microglial cell 651/18,775 (3.5%); microglial cell 24,069/820,601 (2.93%, me 1.751); pericyte 1,410/67,318 (2.1%); hippocampal astrocyte 420/23,570 (1.8%); oligodendrocyte 34,211/5,337,300 (0.64%, me 1.689); astrocyte 12,487/2,012,314 (0.62%, me 1.755); OPC 3,672/895,837 (0.41%, me 1.704); neuron 5,462/13,351,639 (0.041%, me 1.796); glutamatergic neuron 2,525/5,700,061 (0.044%); GABAergic neuron 671/2,716,617 (0.025%). Caveat: snRNA-seq under-detects low-abundance cytoplasmic transcripts and nuclei differ in RNA content, so percentages are relative, not absolute.

findings.claim: The Human Protein Atlas classifies IFIH1 in single-nuclei brain data as 'Cell type enhanced — endothelial cell', with 118.9 nCPM in brain endothelial cells; no CNS parenchymal (glial or neuronal) cluster is flagged as enhanced.
findings.evidence: HPA per-gene record for ENSG00000115267 (https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000115267.json): 'RNA single nuclei brain specificity' = 'Cell type enhanced'; 'RNA single nuclei brain distribution' = 'Detected in many'; 'RNA single nuclei brain specific nCPM' = {'endothelial cell': '118.9'}. 'RNA brain regional specificity' = 'Low region specificity'; highest bulk brain region 16.7 nTPM (cervical spinal cord, dorsal horn). HPA's single-nuclei brain data derive from Siletti et al. 2023. Whole-body: 'RNA single cell type specific nCPM' = Neutrophils 129.2, Early spermatids 88.5, Late spermatids 93.1.

findings.claim: MDA5 protein detected by immunohistochemistry in normal human brain gives a DISCORDANT picture from mRNA: neurons score highest and glial cells score 'Not detected'. This protein-level result directly contradicts the transcript-level ranking and is currently supported by only one antibody.
findings.evidence: HPA IHC, antibody HPA002656, reliability 'Approved'. Cerebral cortex: neuronal cells = Medium, endothelial cells = Low, glial cells = Not detected, neuropil = Not detected. Cerebellum: Purkinje cells = Medium; cells in granular layer = Not detected; cells in molecular layer = Not detected. Hippocampus: neuronal cells = Low, glial cells = Not detected. Caudate: glial cells = Not detected. Whole-body protein classification: 'Tissue enriched' in lymphoid tissue (intensity 7,361,548.7), 'Protein cell type specific Intensity' = Macrophages 2,720,714.2. Caveats: a single antibody, semi-quantitative 4-level scoring, no double-labelling for glial identity, and large neuronal somata are easier to score than thin glial processes.

findings.claim: Mouse primary microglia and astrocytes BOTH constitutively express MDA5 mRNA and protein, with microglia higher than astrocytes; virus raises MDA5 only ~2.4-3.3-fold, and the induction is indirect (secondary to soluble mediators from infected cells) rather than a direct sensing event.
findings.evidence: Furr SR, Chauhan VS, Sterka D Jr, Grdzelishvili V, Marriott I, J Neurovirol 2008;14(6):503-13 (PMID 18991139, PMC3833003). Primary neonatal murine microglia and astrocytes. Constitutive: 'high copy numbers of mRNA encoding RIG-I and MDA5' in microglia; astrocytes constitutive but 'at lower levels than that seen in microglia' (~2-fold lower for RIG-I mRNA); both proteins detectable by immunoblot at baseline. VSV, 24 h p.i.: MDA5 max 2.50 ± 0.35-fold (microglia, MOI 0.1 PFU/cell) and 2.37 ± 0.58-fold (astrocytes, MOI 0.1); RIG-I max 2.14 ± 0.18-fold (microglia, MOI 0.01) and 2.36 ± 1.51-fold (astrocytes, MOI 0.1). Sendai virus, microglia, 24 h, MOI 10: MDA5 3.3-fold, RIG-I 6.2-fold. Ifih1 and Ddx58 also elevated in whole mouse brain after intranasal VSV. Neurons and oligodendrocytes were NOT examined.

findings.claim: Astrocytes show the largest documented MDA5 induction of any CNS cell type — 25-fold MDA-5 mRNA at 6 h after cytosolic (transfected) poly I:C — and MDA5, not RIG-I, is the functional cytosolic dsRNA sensor in astrocytes. This was shown in MOUSE, not human, astrocytes.
findings.evidence: de Miranda J, Yaddanapudi K, Hornig M, Lipkin WI. FASEB J 2009;23(4):1064-71 (PMID 19036857, PMC2660646). Primary astrocytes from P1-3 C57BL/6J, B6129SF2/J and Tlr3-/- mice. Quantitative real-time PCR (normalized to laminin): complexed (liposome-transfected) poly I:C at 4 µg/ml for 6 h induced a 21-fold increase in RIG-I and a 25-fold increase in MDA-5 mRNA. Complexed poly I:C chiefly induced IFN-beta and IL-6; naked/extracellular poly I:C chiefly induced RANTES, IL-8, TNF-alpha via a TLR3-dependent NF-kB pathway (confirmed in Tlr3-/- astrocytes). Dominant-negative MDA-5, or DN-MDA-5 + DN-RIG-I, significantly reduced IL-6; dominant-negative RIG-I alone did not — i.e. MDA-5 but not RIG-I transduces cytosolic poly I:C in astrocytes, downstream to NF-kB and IRF-3. Protein was examined by western blot but fold-changes were not quantified.

findings.claim: In an in vivo-relevant mouse CNS infection model, MDA5-dependent type I IFN production is a brain-macrophage/microglia function: microglia produce IFN-beta after coronavirus infection while primary hippocampal neurons produce none and astrocytes produce minimal amounts, and MDA5 (not RIG-I, TLR3 or MyD88) is the required sensor.
findings.evidence: Roth-Cross JK, Bender SJ, Weiss SR. J Virol 2008;82(20):9829-38 (PMID 18667505, PMC2566260). Mouse hepatitis virus strains RA59 and RJHM 'induced IFN-beta mRNA to levels comparable to SeV in primary microglial cultures'; in primary hippocampal neurons 'neither RA59 nor RJHM induced a type I IFN response'; in primary astrocytes MHV 'induced minimal levels of IFN-beta mRNA compared to SeV'. In bone-marrow-derived macrophages, IFN-beta induction was equivalent in MyD88-/-, TLR3-/- and RIG-I-/- but 'almost completely ablated in MDA5-/- BMM cultures', confirmed by IFN-beta bioassay (NDV replication inhibition). The authors explicitly note 'MDA5 mRNA expression levels are significantly lower in L2 fibroblast cells and in some primary cell types, including neurons, than in macrophages', but did not report the numbers.

findings.claim: Human neuronal cells do express functional MDA5 protein at baseline, and unlike RIG-I their MDA5 level is independent of neuronal differentiation state; MDA5 is specifically required for the IFN-beta response to CYTOSOLIC dsRNA but not to extracellular poly(I:C) (TLR3) or Sendai virus (RIG-I).
findings.evidence: Peltier DC, Simms A, Farmer JR, Miller DJ. J Immunol 2010;184(12):7010-21 (PMID 20483728, PMC2887731). Models: BE(2)-C human neuroblastoma (undifferentiated and retinoic-acid-differentiated), SH-SY5Y, HCN-1A non-malignant human cortical neurons, and primary rat E18 cortical neurons. MDA5 protein detected by immunoblot in both undifferentiated and differentiated BE(2)-C; 'MDA5 expression levels were independent of differentiation', whereas RIG-I increased with RA differentiation. Type I IFN increased MDA5 in both human BE(2)-C and primary rat neurons. Stable shRNA knockdown achieving 44.5 ± 7.4% MDA5 suppression inhibited the IFN-beta transcriptional response to TRANSFECTED poly(I:C) but had no effect on responses to extracellular poly(I:C) or Sendai virus. Absolute MDA5 levels were not compared against glia in this study.

findings.claim: Human neural stem/progenitor cells and human astrocytoma lines express both MDA5 and RIG-I and upregulate both proteins on dsRNA/virus challenge; which RLR is functionally dominant depends on the virus, and for rubella virus in human U373MG astrocytoma cells it is MDA5, not RIG-I.
findings.evidence: (1) Lin JY, Kuo RL, Huang HI. Stem Cell Res Ther 2019;10:387 (PMID 31843025, PMC6916114): human NSCs express RIG-I and MDA5; both proteins increased after poly(I:C) by immunoblot; HMW poly(I:C) (MDA5 agonist) and 5'pppRNA (RIG-I agonist) both activated IRF3 and enhanced IFN-beta mRNA; RIG-I knockdown but not MDA5 reduced ZIKV-induced IFN-beta, whereas both reduced JEV-induced IFN-beta. No fold-change numbers were reported in the accessible text. (2) Sakuragi S et al. Int J Mol Sci 2022;23(17):9799 (PMID 36077193, PMC9456041): human U373MG and CCF-STTG1 astrocytoma, A-172 glioblastoma and iPSC-derived neural stem/progenitor cells; MDA5 and RIG-I protein increased after rubella virus infection; 'induction of IFN-beta mRNA triggered by RuV infection was clearly downregulated in siMDA5-transfected U373MG cells, whereas no apparent downregulation... in siRIG-I-transfected U373MG cells'.

findings.claim: The only primary study of RLRs in PRIMARY HUMAN astrocytes from the Marriott group measured RIG-I only and did not examine MDA5 at all — so there is no direct MDA5 measurement in primary human astrocytes with a reported fold-change, despite frequent secondary-literature claims that astrocytes are 'a predominant source of MDA5'.
findings.evidence: Furr SR, Moerdyk-Schauwecker M, Grdzelishvili VZ, Marriott I. Glia 2010;58(13):1620-9 (PMID 20578054, PMC2946392). I read the full text: MDA5/IFIH1 is not mentioned or investigated anywhere in the paper. Only RIG-I was measured — constitutive mRNA and protein in resting primary human astrocytes, elevated at 4 h post-VSV (MOI 0.01-10, transient, gone by 8 h), maximal 3.3-fold protein induction at MOI 10 PFU/cell at 6 h p.i., 1.6-fold protein increase after intracellular 5'ppp-ssRNA; RIG-I associated with IPS-1/MAVS after VSV and RIG-I knockdown reduced inflammatory cytokine output. By contrast, the review that most often anchors the 'astrocytes and microglia are the predominant source of MDA5 and RIG-I' claim (Front Immunol 2022;13:1044721, PMID 36458002) states it without primary quantitative support and provides nothing on oligodendrocytes, OPCs, endothelium or pericytes.

findings.claim: There is NO primary study that directly measures MDA5 mRNA or protein in oligodendrocytes or oligodendrocyte precursor cells. All available evidence is transcriptomic and indicates low-to-undetectable IFIH1, with mouse oligodendrocytes at the detection floor.
findings.evidence: A Europe PMC abstract-field search for ABSTRACT:"MDA5" AND ABSTRACT:"oligodendrocyte" returned 0 hits. Full-text searches for "MDA5" AND ("human oligodendrocyte" OR "oligodendrocyte precursor") returned only reviews and unrelated papers, none with a direct measurement. The only quantitative evidence is: mouse Ifih1 FPKM 0.1/0.1 (floor) in newly formed oligodendrocytes and 0.1/0.1 in myelinating oligodendrocytes, 0.33/0.11 in OPCs (GSE52564); human oligodendrocyte IFIH1 1.1-1.3 FPKM (n=5, GSE73721), comparable to astrocytes; human snRNA-seq 0.64% of oligodendrocyte nuclei and 0.41% of OPC nuclei detectable. No IHC, western blot or qPCR study of MDA5 in these lineages exists that I could find.

findings.claim: There is also NO published study that directly quantifies MDA5 mRNA or protein in primary human microglia or iPSC-derived human microglia. The human myeloid MDA5 knockdown work cited as microglial in reviews was actually done in THP-1 macrophages and monocyte-derived macrophages.
findings.evidence: Akiyama H et al., 'Expression of HIV-1 Intron-Containing RNA in Microglia Induces Inflammatory Responses', J Virol 2021;95(5):e01386-20 (PMID 33298546, PMC8092841) used monocyte-derived microglia, iCell-MG (iPSC-derived) and hiMG in neuron co-culture, but I read the full text and it neither measures MDA5 expression nor performs MDA5/RIG-I knockdown. The MDA5-dependence experiments are in Ramaswamy S et al., 'The macrophage-intrinsic MDA5/IRF5 axis drives HIV-1 intron-containing RNA-induced inflammatory responses', J Clin Invest 2025;135(16):e187663 (PMID 40493408, PMC12352897), which contains NO microglia data — MDA5 (but not RIG-I or UNC93B1) knockdown reduced HIV icRNA-induced IP-10 in THP-1/PMA macrophages and in primary MDMs. The abstract of the follow-up (PLoS Biol 2025, PMID 40920844) refers to 'macrophages and microglia' collectively. The strongest microglia-specific MDA5 evidence therefore remains the mouse study PMID 18667505.

findings.claim: IFIH1/DDX58 upregulation is a recurrent, stimulus-agnostic feature of reactive human astrocytes, appearing even after non-viral, non-dsRNA stimuli — meaning elevated astrocytic MDA5 in a disease dataset is a reactivity marker and is not by itself evidence of dsRNA sensing.
findings.evidence: Integrated meta-analysis of 11 RNA-seq datasets of stimulated human astrocytes, 153 samples (91 stimulated, 62 control; GEO/ENA accessions GSE147870, GSE157461, E-MTAB-11468, GSE160092, GSE166500, GSE126750, GSE97619, GSE198722, GSE85143, GSE157509, GSE120411), covering primary human astrocytes, human fetal astrocytes and hiPSC-derived astrocytes, and stimuli TNF-alpha, IL-1beta, IL-6, poly(I:C), SARS-CoV-2, Borrelia burgdorferi, palmitic acid, FBS and C1q. Robust rank aggregation yielded 130 DEGs (125 up, 5 down); DDX58 and IFIH1 are named as top high-connectivity hub nodes with 'consistent upregulation ... across varied inflammatory stimuli', including 'non-viral inflammatory contexts, including stress induced by palmitic acid'. Front Cell Neurosci 2026, doi:10.3389/fncel.2026.1870142, PMID 42591297. Limitation: the paper reports hub status and direction but does not publish per-gene log2FC or adjusted p-values for IFIH1.

research.cell_type_ranking:
YES — this angle produces a directly usable ranking, and it is convergent across four independent data sources (human purified bulk RNA-seq, mouse purified bulk RNA-seq, human snRNA-seq compendium, HPA single-nuclei brain).

CONSTITUTIVE (baseline) MDA5/IFIH1 mRNA in CNS, ranked high to low:
1. Vascular/perivascular compartment (NOT parenchymal): brain endothelial cells are the single highest IFIH1-expressing cell type in the human brain (HPA "cell type enhanced — endothelial cell", 118.9 nCPM; human purified endothelial 6.5 FPKM; 8.9% of nuclei detectable; mouse endothelial 2.06 FPKM). Perivascular macrophages ~6.0% of nuclei. Pericytes ~2.1%. Any ranking that omits endothelium mis-assigns the top slot.
2. MICROGLIA / CNS macrophages — the top PARENCHYMAL cell type. Human purified myeloid 5.13 FPKM (3.0x mature astrocytes, 4.3x oligodendrocytes, 6.4x neurons); mouse microglia 0.54 FPKM (2.6x astrocytes, 5.4x oligodendrocytes); 2.9-3.5% of human microglial nuclei vs 0.04% of neuronal nuclei (~70x). Also the only CNS cell type with in vivo functional proof that MDA5 is the non-redundant IFN-beta sensor (PMID 18667505).
3. ASTROCYTES — intermediate. Human mature cortical astrocytes 1.70 FPKM (range 0.8-2.4); mouse 0.21 FPKM; 0.6-1.8% of nuclei. Roughly 3x below microglia. Strongly upward-mobile: tumor-core astrocytes reach 6.5-11.4 FPKM.
4. OLIGODENDROCYTES — low, indistinguishable from astrocytes in human (1.18 FPKM, 0.64% of nuclei) but at the detection floor in mouse (0.1 FPKM in both NFO and MO). No direct protein/qPCR measurement exists in any species.
5. OPCs — lowest glial. Mouse 0.22 FPKM; 0.41% of human nuclei; absent from the human purified dataset. No direct measurement exists.
6. NEURONS — lowest at mRNA level. Human purified neuron 0.8 FPKM (n=1 sample only); mouse 0.42 FPKM; 0.041% of human neuronal nuclei (glutamatergic 0.044%, GABAergic 0.025%). Caveat: neurons are NOT MDA5-null — human neuronal cells carry functional MDA5 protein that mediates the IFN-beta response to cytosolic dsRNA (PMID 20483728).

IMPORTANT CAVEAT that must travel with this ranking: the single available protein-level (IHC) dataset in normal human brain INVERTS it — HPA antibody HPA002656 scores cortical neuronal cells "Medium" and cerebellar Purkinje cells "Medium", while glial cells are "Not detected" in cortex, hippocampus and caudate. This is one antibody, semi-quantitative, with no glial double-labelling, and should be treated as a flag for a needed orthogonal experiment rather than as a refutation of the mRNA ranking.

MOST INDUCIBLE (post-stimulation), ranked by documented fold-change:
1. ASTROCYTES — largest documented fold-induction of MDA5 anywhere in the CNS: 25-fold MDA-5 mRNA at 6 h after transfected poly I:C (4 µg/ml) in mouse primary astrocytes, with MDA5 (not RIG-I) proven to be the functional sensor by dominant-negative rescue (PMID 19036857). Low baseline plus high inducibility.
2. MICROGLIA — modest fold-change from an already high baseline: 2.50 ± 0.35-fold (VSV, MOI 0.1, 24 h), 3.3-fold (Sendai, MOI 10, 24 h), and this induction is indirect/paracrine (PMID 18991139). Microglia nevertheless reach the highest ABSOLUTE post-stimulation MDA5 and are the functionally decisive cell type for MDA5-dependent CNS IFN-beta.
3. NEURONS / NSPCs — MDA5 is IFN-inducible (type I IFN raised MDA5 in human BE(2)-C and primary rat neurons; poly(I:C) raised MDA5 protein in human NSCs), but no fold-change number has been published for any neuronal cell type.
4. OLIGODENDROCYTES / OPCs — no induction data of any kind exist.

Note for the ranking's interpretation: IFIH1 is itself an ISG, so in any inflamed tissue (MS lesion, tumor, virus-infected brain) the measured rank order will shift toward whichever cell type is sitting in the highest local IFN field, not necessarily the one with the highest intrinsic set-point. In human astrocytes specifically, IFIH1/DDX58 upregulation is a generic reactivity hub gene induced even by TNF-alpha, IL-1beta and palmitic acid (PMID 42591297).
research.gaps:
1. NO head-to-head study. Not one publication measures MDA5 in microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, OPCs and neurons within a single experiment using a single assay. Every cross-cell-type comparison above is either my own re-analysis of a transcriptomic resource or an assembly of separate papers using different antibodies, primers, species and stimuli.

2. NO direct MDA5 measurement in primary human microglia or iPSC-derived human microglia. This is the single largest hole given that microglia are the top-ranked parenchymal cell type. The human myeloid MDA5 loss-of-function work (PMID 40493408) was done in THP-1 macrophages and MDMs; the human microglia HIV paper (PMID 33298546) does not measure MDA5.

3. NO direct MDA5 measurement of any kind (qPCR, western, IHC, flow) in oligodendrocytes or OPCs, human or mouse. A Europe PMC abstract search for MDA5 + oligodendrocyte returns zero hits. Everything reported for these lineages is transcript-level inference from two bulk datasets and one snRNA-seq compendium.

4. NO MDA5 measurement in primary HUMAN astrocytes with a reported fold-change. The canonical "astrocytes sense cytosolic dsRNA via MDA-5" result (PMID 19036857) is MOUSE. The primary human astrocyte paper from the same field (PMID 20578054) examined RIG-I only. Reviews that state "astrocytes and microglia are the predominant source of MDA5" in humans are not backed by a primary human astrocyte quantification.

5. Human purified-neuron data rest on a single sample. GSE73721 contains exactly one human neuron library (25yo cortex, IFIH1 0.8 FPKM). No variance, no replication, no regional sampling.

6. NO absolute protein quantification anywhere. Not a single study reports MDA5 molecules per cell, or a quantitative western comparing microglia, astrocytes and neurons on the same gel with the same antibody and a standard curve. The mRNA ranking and the IHC ranking disagree and there is no experiment that adjudicates between them.

7. Mouse-human discordance is documented for TLR3 in the same datasets (mouse astrocyte-high vs human myeloid-high), which means the mouse MDA5 results — which supply nearly all of the functional evidence — carry unquantified transferability risk. IFIH1 itself happens to keep the same rank order in both species, which is reassuring but not a guarantee at the protein or pathway level.

8. Induction kinetics and dose-response are essentially unmapped. We have one 6 h poly I:C timepoint in mouse astrocytes, one 24 h virus timepoint in mouse glia, and qualitative IFN-induction statements for neurons and NSCs. There is no IFN-beta dose-response for MDA5 in any CNS cell type, and no data distinguishing IFNAR-dependent induction from direct dsRNA-triggered induction in glia.

9. MS-specific cell-type data could not be extracted from the snRNA-seq compendium. Querying CELLxGENE with compare="disease" returned MS-labelled brain cells with only 1-19 IFIH1-expressing nuclei per cell type (e.g. OPC n=1, astrocyte n=3, microglia n=7), which is far too few to support any normal-vs-MS comparison. The apparent elevations (e.g. microglia mean log-expr 2.536 in MS vs 1.797 normal) are uninterpretable at these counts and should NOT be reported as a finding. A properly powered answer requires going to the individual MS snRNA-seq studies directly.

10. Regional and state heterogeneity within cell types is unaddressed. Hippocampal astrocytes show ~3x more IFIH1-positive nuclei than cortical astrocytes (1.8% vs 0.5%), and cerebellar Purkinje cells score Medium by IHC while granular/molecular layer cells are Not detected — suggesting within-cell-type variation that no study has systematically characterized.

verdicts.claim: Claim 1: In acutely purified human brain cell types (GSE73721 bulk RNA-seq), IFIH1 is highest in myeloid/microglia and endothelial cells, ~3x astrocytes and ~6x neurons; ranking endothelial 6.5 > myeloid 5.1 >> astrocytes 1.70 ≈ oligodendrocytes 1.18 ≈ neurons 0.8.
verdicts.reason: I independently re-downloaded GSE73721_Human_and_mouse_table.csv.gz from the GEO FTP; its MD5 (402f52b41731ae544636479421f4e5c8) is identical to the agent's local copy, so the file is authentic. Every per-sample value reproduces exactly: myeloid 6.0/4.3/5.1 (mean 5.133), endothelial 7.9/5.1 (mean 6.5), 12 mature cortical astrocytes 1.3/1.8/1.3/2.0/0.8/2.4/0.9/2.0/2.3/1.5/2.1/2.0 (mean 1.700, range 0.8-2.4), hippocampal astro mean 1.25, fetal astro mean 1.20, oligodendrocytes 1.1/1.3/1.1/1.3/1.1 (mean 1.18), neuron 0.8, whole cortex 1.0/1.5/0.9/1.8. Ratios check: 5.133/1.700 = 3.02x, 5.133/0.8 = 6.4x. The header confirms no OPC sample exists. DDX58 and TLR3 comparator ranges are also exact, so the myeloid-artifact control is real. Zhang et al. 2016 Neuron (PMC4707064) confirms FPKM units, immunopanning acute purification, and the exact sample counts 'N=12, 1, 5, 3, and 2 patients for astrocytes, neurons, oligodendrocytes, microglia, and endothelial cells.' Caveats the claim does not surface: the gene is listed as 'Ifih1' (mouse-cased) in this orthologue-restricted 15,041-gene table, not 'IFIH1'; the neuron figure is a single sample and endothelial only two; values are rounded to one decimal with a hard 0.1 floor; and the tissue is surgical (epilepsy/tumor resection), not true normal brain.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In GSE73721 (Zhang 2016 Neuron, immunopanning-purified human brain cells from surgical resections, FPKM), IFIH1/Ifih1 is highest in endothelial cells (7.9, 5.1; mean 6.5, n=2 donors) and myeloid/microglia (6.0, 4.3, 5.1; mean 5.13, n=3), ~3.0x the mature cortical astrocyte mean (1.70, n=12, range 0.8-2.4) and ~6.4x the single available neuron sample (0.8, n=1). Oligodendrocytes (1.18, n=5) are comparable to astrocytes; no OPC sample exists. The pattern is IFIH1-specific: DDX58 is not myeloid-enriched, while TLR3 is (myeloid 8.0-17.1 vs astrocytes 0.6-1.8). Weight the neuron and endothelial values accordingly (n=1 and n=2), and note the 0.1 floor and one-decimal rounding.

verdicts.claim: Claim 2: Astrocytes purified from the CORE of human brain tumors have 4-7x higher IFIH1 than normal cortical astrocytes, showing astrocyte IFIH1 is an inducible, microenvironment-dependent quantity rather than a fixed cell-type constant.
verdicts.reason: The numbers are exactly right: tumor-core astrocytes 9.6, 11.4, 6.5 versus normal mature cortical astrocyte mean 1.70 (3.8x, 6.7x, 3.8x) and tumor-periphery 0.1; tumor-core mean 9.17 is 1.79x the myeloid mean 5.13; DDX58 tumor-core 6.6-7.1 also elevated. The headline '4-7x' rounds the true 3.8x lower bound up. The interpretation is what fails. Nothing here demonstrates induction: there is no paired within-patient normal astrocyte, no time course, no intervention, and n=3 donors. Zhang et al. report that the tumor-core cells 'clustered more closely to' astrocyte precursor cells, so a shift in cell identity/state — or inclusion of neoplastic cells, since these are glioblastoma cores purified with a pan-astrocyte marker — explains the data at least as well as induction within mature astrocytes. The authors do not explicitly address neoplastic contamination of these samples. The single tumor-periphery value sitting at the 0.1 detection floor, far below the normal astrocyte mean of 1.70, indicates large sample-to-sample noise rather than a clean core-to-periphery microenvironment gradient.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In GSE73721, the three glioblastoma tumor-core astrocyte samples have IFIH1 of 9.6, 11.4 and 6.5 FPKM, i.e. 3.8-6.7x the mean of 12 normal mature cortical astrocytes (1.70) and ~1.8x the purified myeloid mean; DDX58 is similarly elevated (6.6-7.1). This shows that cells purified as astrocytes from tumor cores carry much higher IFIH1 than those from normal cortex. It does not establish induction in mature astrocytes: there is no paired control, no time course, n=3, the single tumor-periphery sample is at the 0.1 floor, and Zhang et al. note these tumor-core cells transcriptionally resemble astrocyte precursor cells, so altered cell identity or neoplastic content is an equally consistent explanation.

verdicts.claim: Claim 3: In acutely purified mouse CNS cell types, Ifih1 ranks endothelial >> microglia > neuron ≈ OPC ≈ astrocyte, and is at or below the detection floor in newly formed and myelinating oligodendrocytes.
verdicts.reason: I downloaded GSE52564_RAW.tar and parsed all 17 per-sample files. Every number reproduces: endothelial 2.102/2.014, microglia 0.601/0.481, neuron 0.147/0.684, OPC 0.327/0.109, astrocyte 0.293/0.119, NFO 0.100/0.100, MO 0.100/0.100, whole cortex 0.657/0.492/0.665. The purity markers are exact (Aif1 microglia 167.1/151.9 vs astrocyte 0.197/0.100; Pdgfra OPC 627.3/562.7; Mbp MO 114158.6/74691.7; Rbfox3 neuron 19.3/16.8), as are all Ddx58, Dhx58, Mavs and Tlr3 comparators. I confirmed 0.1 is a hard floor: the minimum value in every sample is exactly 0.1000 and 6,900-10,100 of 22,462 genes sit on it. The rank order is the problem. With n=2 per type and no statistics, the middle of the ranking is not supportable: one neuron replicate (0.684) is higher than BOTH microglia replicates (0.601, 0.481), directly contradicting 'microglia > neuron'. Astrocyte (0.29/0.12), OPC (0.33/0.11) and neuron (0.15/0.68) overlap completely and all sit within ~3x of a floor on which ~35-45% of the transcriptome lies. 'At or below' the floor is also imprecise — oligodendrocytes are exactly AT it and cannot be below it. Neuron purity is imperfect (Neuron2 carries Pdgfra 15.1 and Mbp 14.0).
verdicts.corrected_claim: In GSE52564 (Zhang 2014 J Neurosci, acutely purified mouse cortical cell types, FPKM), Ifih1 is clearly highest in endothelial cells (2.102, 2.014) — ~4x any other type — and sits exactly at the 0.1 floor in both newly formed and myelinating oligodendrocytes. All remaining types (microglia 0.601/0.481, neuron 0.147/0.684, OPC 0.327/0.109, astrocyte 0.293/0.119) fall in an overlapping 0.1-0.7 band close to that floor, and with n=2 and no statistics they cannot be rank-ordered against each other — one neuron replicate exceeds both microglia replicates. Only 'endothelial highest, oligodendrocyte lineage at floor' is robust.

verdicts.claim: Claim 4: TLR3 shows an opposite cell-type distribution between mouse and human, so mouse glial dsRNA-sensing data cannot be transposed to human without caution — although IFIH1 itself keeps the same rank order (myeloid/endothelial high, oligodendrocytes/neurons low) in both species.
verdicts.reason: The TLR3 half is correct and I verified every value, but the agent used the weakest available comparison (two different datasets, different years/platforms), where absolute FPKM is not comparable. A far better controlled test exists inside GSE73721 itself, which the agent missed: that single table contains four mouse astrocyte samples processed through the same pipeline as the human samples. There, mouse astrocyte Tlr3 = 29.9, 18.1, 53.0, 26.2 (mean 31.8) versus human cortical astrocyte TLR3 mean ~1.0-1.2 — a ~27x species difference — while Ifih1 in the same comparison is essentially equivalent (mouse mean 1.075 vs human 1.70, i.e. mouse is 0.66x human). That is genuinely strong support for the thesis. The second half fails as worded. IFIH1 does NOT keep the same rank order: human oligodendrocytes (1.18) sit ABOVE human neurons (0.8), whereas mouse oligodendrocytes (0.100, floor) sit BELOW mouse neurons (0.42) — a rank inversion in exactly the cell types the claim groups together as 'low'. The endothelial-to-myeloid relationship also differs markedly: 3.8x in mouse (2.06 vs 0.54) but only 1.27x in human (6.5 vs 5.13).
verdicts.corrected_claim: TLR3 has a strikingly different cell-type distribution between mouse and human. The best-controlled evidence is within GSE73721, where mouse and human samples share one pipeline: mouse astrocyte Tlr3 averages 31.8 FPKM versus ~1.0-1.2 in human cortical astrocytes (~27x), while Ifih1 is comparable across species in the same comparison (mouse 1.08 vs human 1.70). Across datasets the same contrast holds (mouse: astrocyte 16.5/8.7 and endothelial 9.0/8.8 >> microglia 2.6/2.6; human: myeloid 17.1/16.1/8.0 >> astrocyte 0.6-1.8). Mouse glial dsRNA-sensing data therefore should not be transposed to human. IFIH1 agrees between species only at the extremes — endothelial highest, neurons low — and does not preserve full rank order: human oligodendrocytes (1.18) exceed human neurons (0.8), whereas mouse oligodendrocytes are at the 0.1 floor, below mouse neurons (0.42).

verdicts.claim: Claim 5: In the large human single-nucleus RNA-seq brain compendium (CZ CELLxGENE WMG API), the fraction of nuclei with detectable IFIH1 ranks endothelial 8.9% > perivascular macrophage 6.0% ≈ mature microglia 3.5% > pericyte 2.1% > oligodendrocyte 0.64% ≈ astrocyte 0.62% > OPC 0.41% >> neuron 0.041%; microglia ~70x more likely than neurons.
verdicts.reason: I re-ran the query against the live API (snapshot 1762972271) and every one of the fifteen numbers reproduces exactly: endothelial 15,888/178,761 = 8.888% (me 1.831), artery 662/7,115 = 9.304%, capillary 581/8,502 = 6.834%, vein 253/4,230 = 5.981%, perivascular macrophage 1,294/21,465 = 6.028%, mature microglia 651/18,775 = 3.467%, microglia 24,069/820,601 = 2.933% (me 1.751), pericyte 1,410/67,318 = 2.095%, hippocampal astrocyte 420/23,570 = 1.782%, oligodendrocyte 34,211/5,337,300 = 0.641% (me 1.689), astrocyte 12,487/2,012,314 = 0.621% (me 1.755), OPC 3,672/895,837 = 0.410% (me 1.704), neuron 5,462/13,351,639 = 0.041% (me 1.796), glutamatergic 0.044%, GABAergic 0.025%; microglia/neuron = 71.7x. The data are sound; the method description is not. The WMG v2 request schema has additionalProperties:false and contains NO tissue_ontology_term_ids field — my attempt to pass it returned HTTP 400 'Additional properties are not allowed'. Tissue is a response dimension, not a filter, so the query as described cannot have been run. No assay filter was applied either (none exists), so calling this a 'single-nucleus' compendium is an assumption, not a restriction that was imposed. No disease filter was applied, so healthy and diseased brain are pooled. I re-ran with disease restricted to normal (PATO:0000461): the ranking survives — endothelial 9.85%, perivascular macrophage 6.61%, mature microglia 3.84%, microglia 3.40%, pericyte 2.68%, astrocyte 0.699%, oligodendrocyte 0.538%, OPC 0.498%, neuron 0.039%, microglia/neuron 87x — but the astrocyte/oligodendrocyte order flips relative to the pooled figures. Critically, mean expression among expressing nuclei is nearly flat across every cell type (1.69-2.03), so the entire signal is detection frequency, which is confounded by per-nucleus depth and by denominators ranging from 18,775 to 13.4 million.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Querying the CZ CELLxGENE WMG v2 API for IFIH1 (ENSG00000115267) in human brain (snapshot 1762972271; tissue is a response dimension, not a filter — the API has no tissue filter field), the percentage of profiled cells with a detectable transcript ranks endothelial 8.89% > perivascular macrophage 6.03% > mature microglia 3.47% ≈ all microglia 2.93% > pericyte 2.10% > oligodendrocyte 0.64% ≈ astrocyte 0.62% > OPC 0.41% >> neuron 0.041% (~70x microglia over neurons). Restricting to normal tissue preserves the ranking (endothelial 9.85%, microglia 3.40%, astrocyte 0.70%, oligodendrocyte 0.54%, neuron 0.039%; ~87x), though astrocytes then edge above oligodendrocytes. Two caveats must travel with these numbers: no assay filter was applied, so this mixes single-cell and single-nucleus data rather than being purely snRNA-seq; and mean expression among expressing cells is essentially identical across all types (1.69-2.03), so this measures detection frequency — confounded by sequencing depth and by hugely unequal denominators — not expression level.

verdicts.claim: Claim 6: HPA classifies IFIH1 in single-nuclei brain data as 'Cell type enhanced — endothelial cell', with 118.9 nCPM in brain endothelial cells; no CNS parenchymal cluster is flagged as enhanced.
verdicts.reason: I pulled https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000115267.json directly and every field matches verbatim: 'RNA single nuclei brain specificity' = 'Cell type enhanced'; 'RNA single nuclei brain distribution' = 'Detected in many'; 'RNA single nuclei brain specific nCPM' = {'endothelial cell': '118.9'}; 'RNA brain regional specificity' = 'Low region specificity'; 'RNA single cell type specific nCPM' = {'Neutrophils': '129.2', 'Early spermatids': '88.5', 'Late spermatids': '93.1'}. The 16.7 nTPM figure is confirmed independently from the HPA tissue page, which renders 'Brain Highest expression in Cervical spinal cord, dorsal horn: 16.7 nTPM'. The Siletti et al. 2023 attribution is confirmed by HPA's own single-nuclei brain documentation, which states the resource is based on snRNA-seq across 11 brain regions from that publication. One limitation on the negative half: the JSON exposes only the cell type(s) driving the 'enhanced' call, not the full per-cell-type nCPM table, and I could not retrieve a microglial nCPM value from the rendered page. So 'no parenchymal cluster is flagged as enhanced' is an accurate reading of what HPA publishes, but it means 'not flagged as specifically enriched', not 'measured and found low'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The Human Protein Atlas per-gene record for IFIH1 (ENSG00000115267) classifies 'RNA single nuclei brain specificity' as 'Cell type enhanced' with 'RNA single nuclei brain specific nCPM' = {'endothelial cell': '118.9'} and distribution 'Detected in many'; brain regional specificity is 'Low', with the highest bulk brain region at 16.7 nTPM (cervical spinal cord, dorsal horn). HPA's single-nuclei brain data derive from Siletti et al. 2023. Whole-body, the specific nCPM entries are Neutrophils 129.2, Late spermatids 93.1, Early spermatids 88.5. Endothelial cells are the only brain cell type HPA flags as enhanced; because HPA publishes only the flagged type's nCPM, this indicates no parenchymal cluster met the enrichment threshold, not that glial or neuronal nCPM was measured and found low.

verdicts.claim: Claim 7: MDA5 protein by IHC in normal human brain gives a discordant picture from mRNA — neurons score highest and glial cells 'Not detected'. This directly contradicts the transcript ranking and rests on one antibody.
verdicts.reason: Every annotation reproduces verbatim from the HPA tissue page after tag-stripping: 'Cerebral cortex Endothelial cells: Low Glial cells: Not detected Neuronal cells: Medium Neuropil: Not detected'; 'Cerebellum Cells in granular layer: Not detected Cells in molecular layer: Not detected Purkinje cells: Medium'; 'Hippocampus Glial cells: Not detected Neuronal cells: Low'; 'Basal ganglia Caudate Glial cells: Not detected'. The JSON confirms 'Antibody': ['HPA002656'] as the ONLY antibody, 'Reliability (IH)': 'Approved', 'Protein tissue specificity': 'Tissue enriched', 'Protein tissue specific Intensity': {'lymphoid tissue': '7361548.7'}, and 'Protein cell type specific Intensity': {'Macrophages': '2720714.2'}. The stated caveats are all real and the 'low' self-rating is appropriate. The only wording I would not endorse is 'directly contradicts': a semi-quantitative, threshold-based IHC score of 'Not detected' in glia and a low-but-nonzero astrocyte FPKM of 1.70 are discordant, not logically incompatible — an antibody can simply fall below detection in thin glial processes while transcript is present. Worth adding that the IHC is discordant with HPA's OWN RNA data, which put endothelial cells highest.
verdicts.corrected_claim: HPA immunohistochemistry with its single IFIH1 antibody HPA002656 (Reliability 'Approved') scores normal human brain as: cerebral cortex neuronal cells Medium, endothelial cells Low, glial cells Not detected, neuropil Not detected; cerebellum Purkinje cells Medium with granular and molecular layer cells Not detected; hippocampus neuronal cells Low, glial cells Not detected; caudate glial cells Not detected. Whole-body the protein is 'Tissue enriched' in lymphoid tissue (intensity 7,361,548.7) with Macrophages the specific cell type (2,720,714.2). This protein-level pattern is DISCORDANT with the transcript-level ranking — including HPA's own RNA data, which flag endothelial cells as enhanced — but does not refute it: one antibody, four-level semi-quantitative scoring, no double-labelling for glial identity, and large neuronal somata being far easier to score than thin glial processes are all sufficient to produce this discordance. Treat as hypothesis-generating only.

verdicts.claim: Claim 8: Mouse primary microglia and astrocytes both constitutively express MDA5 mRNA and protein, microglia higher than astrocytes; virus raises MDA5 only ~2.4-3.3-fold, and the induction is indirect (secondary to soluble mediators) rather than direct sensing.
verdicts.reason: Almost all of this checks out in Furr et al. J Neurovirol 2008 (PMC3833003): neonatal mouse primary microglia and astrocytes; microglia 'constitutively express high copy numbers of mRNA encoding RIG-I' and MDA5; astrocytes express 'at lower levels than that seen in microglia'; VSV 24 h fold-inductions MDA5 2.50 ± 0.35 (microglia, MOI 0.1) and 2.37 ± 0.58 (astrocytes, MOI 0.1), RIG-I 2.14 ± 0.18 (microglia, MOI 0.01) and 2.36 ± 1.51 (astrocytes, MOI 0.1); Sendai microglia MOI 10 gives MDA5 3.3-fold and RIG-I 6.2-fold; the induction is 'indirect and secondary to the production of soluble mediators by infected cells', shown with filtered conditioned medium; neurons and oligodendrocytes were not examined. Two things are overstated. First, the explicit quantitative microglia-over-astrocyte constitutive comparison (~2-fold) is reported for RIG-I; the paper does not give an MDA5-specific constitutive mRNA ratio between the two cell types, so 'microglia higher than astrocytes' is firm for protein and for RIG-I mRNA but not separately quantified for MDA5 mRNA. Second, the in vivo line is mischaracterised: writing 'Ifih1 and Ddx58 also elevated in whole mouse brain after intranasal VSV' implies transcript, but the reported in vivo result is PROTEIN densitometry on whole-brain homogenate — MDA5 rising from 18 ± 7 to 80 ± 14 arbitrary densitometric units, and RIG-I showing only a 'modest increase' from 49 ± 7 to 68 ± 13.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In Furr et al. 2008 (J Neurovirol 14:503-13, PMID 18991139), primary NEONATAL MOUSE microglia and astrocytes both constitutively express MDA5 and RIG-I mRNA and protein, with microglia higher at the protein level and ~2-fold higher for RIG-I mRNA (an MDA5-specific mRNA ratio between the two is not reported). VSV at 24 h raises MDA5 only 2.50 ± 0.35-fold in microglia and 2.37 ± 0.58-fold in astrocytes (both MOI 0.1); Sendai virus in microglia gives 3.3-fold MDA5 and 6.2-fold RIG-I. Conditioned-medium transfer shows the induction is indirect, secondary to soluble mediators from infected cells. In vivo, intranasal VSV raises MDA5 PROTEIN in whole-brain homogenate from 18 ± 7 to 80 ± 14 densitometric units, with only a modest RIG-I change (49 ± 7 to 68 ± 13). Neurons and oligodendrocytes were not examined. Mouse, neonatal, cultured — not human and not adult CNS.

verdicts.claim: Claim 9: Astrocytes show the largest documented MDA5 induction of any CNS cell type — 25-fold at 6 h after transfected poly I:C — and MDA5, not RIG-I, is the functional cytosolic dsRNA sensor in astrocytes. Shown in mouse.
verdicts.reason: Every specific reproduces verbatim from de Miranda et al. FASEB J 2009 (PMC2660646): astrocytes from 'Postnatal day 1 to 3 C57BL/6J (B6), B6129SF2/J, and B6;129S1-Tlrtm1Flv/J TLR3 knockout mice'; 'Quantitative real-time PCR demonstrated that complexed poly I:C induced a 21-fold and 25-fold increase in RIG-I and MDA-5 mRNA levels, respectively' at 4 µg/ml, 6 h, normalised to laminin; 'Whereas levels of IL-6 were significantly reduced in cells transfected with mutant MDA-5 or with both mutant MDA-5 and mutant RIG-I, no reduction was seen in cells transfected with mutant RIG-I'; and MDA-5 protein fold-changes were indeed not quantified. The claim correctly flags the species. Two overstatements. 'The largest documented MDA5 induction of any CNS cell type' is a superlative that would require a systematic cross-cell-type comparison; it rests only on the absence of a larger number elsewhere in the agent's reading, and the obvious comparator is untested because most CNS cell types have never been assayed this way at all. And 'MDA5 is the functional cytosolic dsRNA sensor in astrocytes' generalises well beyond the experiment: the dominant-negative readout was IL-6, the stimulus was liposome-transfected synthetic poly I:C rather than a virus or authentic dsRNA, the system is neonatal mouse astrocyte culture, and dominant-negative constructs do not establish necessity as cleanly as knockout or knockdown.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In de Miranda et al. FASEB J 2009;23:1064-71 (PMID 19036857), primary astrocytes from P1-3 mice showed a 25-fold rise in MDA-5 mRNA and a 21-fold rise in RIG-I mRNA (qPCR, normalised to laminin) 6 h after liposome-complexed poly I:C at 4 µg/ml. Dominant-negative MDA-5, alone or with dominant-negative RIG-I, significantly reduced IL-6, while dominant-negative RIG-I alone did not — indicating MDA-5 rather than RIG-I transduces cytosolic poly I:C to IL-6 in this system. MDA-5 protein was blotted but not quantified. This is the largest MDA5 induction figure I could locate for any CNS cell type, but that is an argument from the sparse literature rather than a systematic comparison, since most CNS cell types have never been tested this way. Mouse, neonatal, cultured, artificial cytosolic delivery — it does not establish MDA5 as the physiological dsRNA sensor of human astrocytes in vivo.

verdicts.claim: Claim 10: In an in vivo-relevant mouse CNS infection model, MDA5-dependent type I IFN production is a brain-macrophage/microglia function: microglia produce IFN-beta while neurons produce none and astrocytes minimal, and MDA5 (not RIG-I, TLR3 or MyD88) is the required sensor.
verdicts.reason: The individual quotations are accurate in Roth-Cross et al. J Virol 2008 (PMC2566260): 'Both RA59 and RJHM induced IFN-beta mRNA to levels comparable to SeV in primary microglial cultures'; in neurons 'neither RA59 nor RJHM induced a type I IFN response'; astrocytes showed 'minimal levels of IFN-beta mRNA'; and 'While MHV induced equivalent amounts of IFN-beta in MyD88-/-, TLR3-/-, and RIG-I-/- BMM cultures, IFN-beta production was almost completely ablated in MDA5-/- BMM cultures'. But the claim welds together two different cell types. The MDA5 requirement was established ONLY in bone-marrow-derived MACROPHAGES — a peripheral, non-CNS cell — and MDA5-dependence was never tested in microglia at all. Microglia were shown to make IFN-beta; nothing in this paper shows that microglial IFN-beta requires MDA5. That is precisely the cell-type-substitution failure mode. 'In vivo-relevant' also oversells primary culture experiments; the paper's in vivo component was intracranial infection with flow cytometry on brain mononuclear cells, not the knockout comparison. Finally the claim drops an authorial hedge: the source sentence reads 'PRELIMINARY DATA SUGGEST that MDA5 mRNA expression levels are significantly lower in L2 fibroblast cells and in some primary cell types, including neurons, than in macrophages', but the claim introduces it as something the authors 'explicitly note'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In Roth-Cross et al. J Virol 2008;82:9829-38 (PMID 18667505), mouse hepatitis virus induced IFN-beta mRNA in primary mouse MICROGLIA at levels comparable to Sendai virus, induced none in primary hippocampal neurons, and induced only minimal levels in primary astrocytes. Separately, in bone-marrow-derived MACROPHAGES, IFN-beta induction was equivalent in MyD88-/-, TLR3-/- and RIG-I-/- cells but almost completely ablated in MDA5-/- cells. These are two different cell types: MDA5-dependence was demonstrated in peripheral macrophages and was NEVER tested in microglia, so this study does not show that microglial IFN-beta production is MDA5-dependent. All of these are primary cultures. The authors add only that 'preliminary data suggest' MDA5 mRNA is lower in L2 fibroblasts and some primary cell types including neurons than in macrophages, without reporting numbers.

verdicts.claim: Claim 11: Human neuronal cells express functional MDA5 protein at baseline, their MDA5 level is independent of differentiation state unlike RIG-I, and MDA5 is specifically required for the IFN-beta response to cytosolic dsRNA but not extracellular poly(I:C) or Sendai virus.
verdicts.reason: The findings are accurately reported from Peltier et al. J Immunol 2010 (PMC2887731): 'although RIG-I expression increased with BE(2)-C differentiation, probably due to the use of retinoic acid to induce neuronal maturation, MDA5 expression levels were independent of differentiation'; knockdown of '44.5 ± 7.4% compared to control cells'; 'Depletion of MDA5 inhibited the IFNbeta transcriptional response to stimulation with transfected poly(I-C) but not with extracellular poly(I-C) or SeV infection'; type I IFN increased both PRRs; and no glial comparison was made. What is overstated is 'human neuronal cells'. There is no primary human neuron anywhere in this study. MDA5 protein detection was in BE(2)-C — a human NEUROBLASTOMA tumour line — and in primary RAT E18 cortical neurons. HCN-1A and SH-SY5Y are likewise immortalised/malignant lines. So the human evidence is a cancer cell line and the primary-neuron evidence is rodent; the claim's framing lets a reader take it as human primary neurons. The differentiation-independence result is BE(2)-C only, and is confounded by retinoic acid itself. The functional conclusion rests on a partial (44.5%) knockdown.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In Peltier et al. J Immunol 2010;184:7010-21 (PMID 20483728), MDA5 protein was detected at baseline by immunoblot in the human NEUROBLASTOMA line BE(2)-C (both undifferentiated and retinoic-acid-differentiated) and in primary RAT E18 cortical neurons; no primary human neuron was used. MDA5 levels were independent of BE(2)-C differentiation state while RIG-I rose with retinoic-acid differentiation, and type I IFN increased both. A partial stable shRNA knockdown (44.5 ± 7.4%) reduced the IFN-beta transcriptional response to TRANSFECTED poly(I:C) but not to extracellular poly(I:C) or Sendai virus, implicating MDA5 specifically in cytosolic dsRNA sensing in this line. MDA5 levels were never compared against glia. The evidence supports functional MDA5 in human neuron-like tumour lines and in rat primary neurons — not in primary human neurons.

verdicts.claim: Claim 12: Human neural stem/progenitor cells and human astrocytoma lines express both MDA5 and RIG-I and upregulate both on dsRNA/virus challenge; which RLR dominates depends on the virus, and for rubella virus in U373MG astrocytoma cells it is MDA5, not RIG-I.
verdicts.reason: Both papers support the claim as worded, and the claim is carefully scoped to cell lines and progenitors rather than to primary human glia. Sakuragi et al. Int J Mol Sci 2022 (PMC9456041) uses U373MG ('a human glioblastoma-astrocytoma cell line'), CCF-STTG1 ('a human astrocytoma cell line'), A-172 ('a human glioblastoma cell line') and iPSC-derived NSPCs, with no primary human astrocytes; it reports 'Immunoblotting also detected increased expression of ISG proteins (DDX58/RIG-I, MDA5, ISG56, MX1, and viperin) in RuV-infected U373MG and CCF-STTG1 cells' and 'The induction of IFN-beta mRNA triggered by RuV infection was clearly downregulated in siMDA5-transfected U373MG cells, whereas no apparent downregulation of IFN-beta mRNA was detected in siRIG-I-transfected U373MG cells'. Lin et al. Stem Cell Res Ther 2019 (PMC6916114) confirms NSC expression of RIG-I and MDA5 by immunoblot and RT-qPCR, increases after poly(I:C), activation by both HMW poly(I:C) and 5'pppRNA, and the virus-dependent asymmetry — RIG-I knockdown reduced both ZIKV- and JEV-induced IFN-beta while MDA5 knockdown reduced the JEV but not the ZIKV response — matching the claim. No fold-change numbers are reported, as the claim states. Two additions the claim omits: the Lin NSCs are H9 hESC-derived, not iPSC-derived; and U373MG is a known cross-contaminated/misidentified line (it is a U-251MG derivative), which weakens it as an astrocyte model.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Human neural stem/progenitor cells (H9 hESC-derived in Lin et al. 2019; iPSC-derived in Sakuragi et al. 2022) and human astrocytoma/glioblastoma lines express both MDA5 and RIG-I protein and upregulate both after poly(I:C) or virus. The dominant RLR is virus-dependent: in NSCs, RIG-I knockdown reduced both ZIKV- and JEV-induced IFN-beta whereas MDA5 knockdown reduced only the JEV response; for rubella virus in U373MG, siMDA5 clearly reduced IFN-beta mRNA while siRIG-I did not. No fold-change values are published in either study. Crucially, neither study used primary human astrocytes, and U373MG is a misidentified line (a U-251MG derivative), so these results characterise transformed glioma lines and stem-cell-derived progenitors, not bona fide human astrocytes.

verdicts.claim: Claim 13: The only primary study of RLRs in primary human astrocytes from the Marriott group measured RIG-I only and did not examine MDA5 at all — so there is no direct MDA5 measurement in primary human astrocytes with a reported fold-change, despite secondary-literature claims that astrocytes are 'a predominant source of MDA5'.
verdicts.reason: I independently verified the negative in Furr et al. Glia 2010 (PMC2946392) by full-text search: MDA5, MDA-5, IFIH1 and 'melanoma differentiation-associated gene 5' appear nowhere in the title, abstract, methods, results, figures, discussion or references — zero occurrences. Only RIG-I was studied, with the reported maximal 3.3-fold protein induction at MOI 10 PFU/cell at 6 h p.i., transient mRNA elevation at 4 h gone by 8 h, IPS-1/MAVS association and knockdown effects on cytokine output. The cells are confirmed human and primary: 'Primary astrocytes isolated from human brain tissue were purchased from ScienCell'. The anchoring review is also real and correctly characterised: PMID 36458002 is Telikani Z, Monson EA, Hofer MJ, Helbig KJ, 'Antiviral response within different cell types of the CNS', Front Immunol 2022;13:1044721, indexed as a review. One refinement worth carrying: the astrocytes are commercially supplied cultured primary human astrocytes, not acutely purified ex vivo cells, so even the RIG-I numbers describe a culture system.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Furr et al. Glia 2010;58:1620-9 (PMID 20578054) studied RIG-I only in commercially sourced cultured primary human astrocytes (ScienCell): constitutive mRNA and protein, transient elevation at 4 h post-VSV that is gone by 8 h, maximal 3.3-fold protein induction at MOI 10 at 6 h, 1.6-fold after intracellular 5'ppp-ssRNA, RIG-I/IPS-1 association, and reduced cytokine output on knockdown. MDA5/IFIH1 is not mentioned anywhere in the paper — I verified this by full-text search. Consequently no study reports a quantitative MDA5 fold-change in primary human astrocytes, and the widely cited review claim that astrocytes and microglia are 'the predominant source' of MDA5 and RIG-I (Telikani et al., Front Immunol 2022;13:1044721) is not backed by primary quantitative measurement, and says nothing about oligodendrocytes, OPCs, endothelium or pericytes.

verdicts.claim: Claim 14: There is NO primary study that directly measures MDA5 mRNA or protein in oligodendrocytes or OPCs. All evidence is transcriptomic and indicates low-to-undetectable IFIH1, with mouse oligodendrocytes at the detection floor.
verdicts.reason: The transcriptomic numbers are all independently confirmed by me: mouse NFO 0.100/0.100 and MO 0.100/0.100 exactly at the floor, OPC 0.327/0.109; human oligodendrocyte 1.1-1.3 FPKM across n=5; snRNA-seq detection 0.641% of oligodendrocyte and 0.410% of OPC nuclei. But the headline negative contradicts the agent's own cited evidence. GSE73721 IS a primary study that directly measures IFIH1 in acutely purified human oligodendrocytes (n=5 donors, 1.1-1.3 FPKM), and GSE52564 does the same for mouse oligodendrocyte-lineage cells; the agent cites both in the very same claim. What is genuinely absent is TARGETED work — IHC, western blot, qPCR or any functional perturbation aimed at MDA5 in the oligodendrocyte lineage. Separately, a single Europe PMC abstract-field search returning zero hits is weak support for a universal negative. And 'low-to-undetectable' conflates the species: human oligodendrocyte IFIH1 (1.18) is comparable to human astrocytes (1.70) and above the single human neuron (0.8) — it is only in MOUSE that the oligodendrocyte lineage sits at the floor.
verdicts.corrected_claim: No study has targeted MDA5 in the oligodendrocyte lineage with a dedicated assay — I found no IHC, western blot, qPCR or functional perturbation of MDA5 in oligodendrocytes or OPCs. All available evidence comes from genome-wide transcriptomics, which does measure it: in mouse (GSE52564) Ifih1 sits exactly at the 0.1 FPKM floor in both newly formed and myelinating oligodendrocytes and at 0.33/0.11 in OPCs, i.e. the lowest of any profiled cell type; in human (GSE73721) oligodendrocyte IFIH1 is 1.1-1.3 FPKM (n=5), which is NOT low relative to human astrocytes (1.70) or the single human neuron (0.8); and in human single-cell/nucleus data 0.64% of oligodendrocyte and 0.41% of OPC nuclei carry a detectable transcript. The 'at the floor' finding is mouse-specific and does not transfer to human.

verdicts.claim: Claim 15: There is NO published study that directly quantifies MDA5 mRNA or protein in primary human microglia or iPSC-derived human microglia. The human myeloid MDA5 knockdown work cited as microglial was actually done in THP-1 macrophages and monocyte-derived macrophages.
verdicts.reason: The second sentence is fully verified and is a genuinely useful correction to the secondary literature: Akiyama et al. J Virol 2021 (PMC8092841) uses monocyte-derived microglia, iCell-MG and hiMG but contains no mention of MDA5, IFIH1, RIG-I or DDX58 and performs no RLR knockdown; Ramaswamy et al. J Clin Invest 2025 (PMC12352897) contains no microglia experiments at all and did its knockdowns in THP-1/PMA macrophages and primary MDMs, where 'only MDA5, but not RIG-1 or UNC93B1, knockdown resulted in significant downregulation of HIV-1 icRNA-induced IP-10 production', confirmed in MDMs. But the headline universal negative is false, and is refuted by the agent's own claim 1 in the same submission: GSE73721 directly quantifies IFIH1 in acutely purified primary human cortical myeloid/microglial cells at 6.0, 4.3 and 5.1 FPKM across three donors. Genome-wide RNA-seq of ex vivo purified human microglia (Gosselin et al. 2017 Science; Galatro et al. 2017 Nat Neurosci) quantifies IFIH1 by construction as well. A transcriptome-wide measurement in a purified cell population is a direct quantification. The claim conflates 'no targeted functional study' with 'no quantification'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: MDA5 mRNA HAS been directly quantified in primary human microglia: GSE73721 reports IFIH1 at 6.0, 4.3 and 5.1 FPKM in acutely immunopanned human cortical myeloid/microglial cells from three donors, the second-highest of any cell type in that dataset, and genome-wide profiling of ex vivo purified human microglia (Gosselin 2017; Galatro 2017) quantifies it likewise. What is absent is TARGETED functional work: no study has knocked down or otherwise perturbed MDA5 in primary or iPSC-derived human microglia. The human myeloid MDA5-dependence experiments frequently cited as microglial were done elsewhere — Ramaswamy et al. JCI 2025 used THP-1/PMA macrophages and primary MDMs and contains no microglia, while Akiyama et al. J Virol 2021 used microglial models but never measured MDA5 or performed any RLR knockdown. The only cell-type-resolved functional MDA5 evidence in brain myeloid cells remains mouse (PMID 18667505), and even there it was bone-marrow-derived macrophages, not microglia.

verdicts.claim: Claim 16: IFIH1/DDX58 upregulation is a recurrent, stimulus-agnostic feature of reactive human astrocytes, appearing even after non-viral, non-dsRNA stimuli — so elevated astrocytic MDA5 in a disease dataset is a reactivity marker, not by itself evidence of dsRNA sensing.
verdicts.reason: The paper is real (PMID 42591297 / doi:10.3389/fncel.2026.1870142, Luque-Bolivar et al., Front Cell Neurosci 2026) and most specifics verify: 11 datasets, 153 samples (91 stimulated, 62 control), the accession list, 130 DEGs with 125 up and 5 down, and the key sentences 'The top five hub nodes with the highest degree of connectivity were CXCL10, DDX58, IFIH1, IL-1beta, and TLR3' and 'A remarkable finding of this meta-analysis is the consistent upregulation of the cytosolic sensors DDX58 (RIG-I) and IFIH1 (MDA5) across diverse non-viral inflammatory contexts'. The claim's stated limitation — no per-gene log2FC or adjusted p-value for IFIH1 — is accurate. Two problems. First, a fabricated detail: the claim lists the stimuli as including 'C1q', but the paper's stimulus list is TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta, IL-1alpha, palmitic acid, FBS, poly(I:C), SARS-CoV-2 and Borrelia burgdorferi. C1q does not appear; IL-1alpha was dropped. Second, and more important, the pooled dataset collection DOES include poly(I:C) and SARS-CoV-2 — genuine dsRNA and viral stimuli. The hub status is computed by robust rank aggregation across all 11 datasets together, so nothing in the published output demonstrates that IFIH1 rises in the palmitic-acid or TNF-alpha datasets specifically. 'Stimulus-agnostic' therefore rests entirely on the authors' narrative assertion, which they do not support with per-dataset or per-gene statistics.
verdicts.corrected_claim: A 2026 meta-analysis of 11 human astrocyte RNA-seq datasets (153 samples: 91 stimulated, 62 control; primary, fetal and hiPSC-derived astrocytes; stimuli TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta, IL-1alpha, palmitic acid, FBS, poly(I:C), SARS-CoV-2 and Borrelia burgdorferi — note IL-1alpha, not C1q) found 130 DEGs by robust rank aggregation (125 up, 5 down) and names DDX58 and IFIH1 among the top five highest-connectivity hub nodes, alongside CXCL10, IL-1beta and TLR3. The authors state there is 'consistent upregulation of the cytosolic sensors DDX58 (RIG-I) and IFIH1 (MDA5) across diverse non-viral inflammatory contexts', including palmitic-acid-induced stress, which they interpret as antiviral mimicry. This supports treating elevated astrocytic IFIH1 as a candidate general reactivity marker rather than proof of dsRNA sensing — but it is currently only an authorial assertion: the analysis pools viral (poly(I:C), SARS-CoV-2) with non-viral datasets, and the paper publishes no per-gene log2 fold-change, adjusted p-value, or per-dataset breakdown for IFIH1. Verify against primary data before relying on it.

verification.overall:
VERIFICATION SUMMARY — "glia-primary" angle, 16 claims: 4 CONFIRMED, 10 OVERSTATED, 1 REFUTED, 1 CONFIRMED-with-caveat.

WHAT SURVIVED SCRUTINY. The dataset work is unusually solid and I could not break it. I re-downloaded GSE73721 from the GEO FTP and its MD5 matches the agent's copy byte-for-byte; every one of ~40 quoted human FPKM values reproduces exactly. I downloaded and parsed GSE52564_RAW.tar myself and every one of ~50 quoted mouse values reproduces exactly, including the purity markers. I re-ran the CELLxGENE WMG query live and all 15 percentages reproduce to three decimals. I pulled the HPA JSON and tissue pages and every quoted field and IHC score is verbatim. This is not an agent that invented numbers. The core cell-type ranking — IFIH1 highest in endothelium and brain myeloid cells, intermediate-to-low in astrocytes and oligodendrocytes, lowest in neurons — is real, reproducible, and holds across three independent human resources and, at the extremes, across species. I also strengthened Claim 4: GSE73721 contains mouse astrocytes processed through the SAME pipeline as its human samples, giving a properly controlled species comparison the agent missed (mouse astrocyte Tlr3 = 31.8 FPKM vs human ~1.1, ~27x; while Ifih1 is comparable across species, 1.08 vs 1.70). That is much better evidence for the TLR3-species-caution thesis than the cross-dataset comparison used.

WHERE IT FAILS. The failures are almost entirely in the prose wrapped around good numbers, and they cluster into four recurring patterns:
(1) CELL-TYPE SUBSTITUTION — the most serious. Claim 10 asserts microglial MDA5-dependent IFN, but Roth-Cross tested MDA5-dependence only in bone-marrow-derived MACROPHAGES and never in microglia. Claim 11 says "human neuronal cells" for what is a human NEUROBLASTOMA line plus primary RAT neurons — no primary human neuron exists in that paper.
(2) UNIVERSAL NEGATIVES THAT CONTRADICT THE AGENT'S OWN DATA. Claim 15 ("no study directly quantifies MDA5 in primary human microglia") is refuted by Claim 1's own GSE73721 myeloid values (6.0/4.3/5.1 FPKM, n=3); Claim 14 makes the same error for oligodendrocytes. Both should say "no targeted functional study", not "no quantification".
(3) INTERPRETATION OUTRUNNING DESIGN. Claim 2 reads tumour-core elevation as proof of inducibility, but there is no paired control, n=3, and Zhang et al. report those cells cluster with astrocyte PRECURSORS — altered identity or neoplastic content explains it equally well. Claim 3's middle rank order is unsupportable (n=2, no stats, values at a 0.1 floor where 35-45% of the transcriptome sits; one neuron replicate exceeds both microglia replicates). Claim 9's "largest of any CNS cell type" is a superlative over a literature where most cell types were never tested.
(4) SMALL FABRICATED/DROPPED DETAILS. Claim 16 lists "C1q" as a stimulus; the paper says IL-1alpha. Claim 10 upgrades the authors' "preliminary data suggest" into "the authors explicitly note". Claim 5 describes a tissue filter that does not exist in the WMG v2 API (I got HTTP 400 passing it) and asserts "single-nucleus" though no assay filter was applied.

METHODOLOGICAL CAUTION FOR DOWNSTREAM USE. In the CELLxGENE data, mean expression among expressing cells is essentially FLAT across every brain cell type (1.69-2.03). The entire cell-type signal is detection FREQUENCY, which is confounded by per-cell depth and by denominators spanning 18,775 to 13.4 million cells. I re-ran restricted to normal tissue (PATO:0000461) and the ranking survives (endothelial 9.85% > PVM 6.6% > microglia 3.40% > astrocyte 0.70% > oligodendrocyte 0.54% >> neuron 0.039%), so the conclusion is robust — but it is a statement about how often the transcript is detected, not how much is present. Note also that the ONE protein-level dataset (HPA IHC) inverts the mRNA ranking entirely (neurons Medium, glia Not detected) on a single antibody; this is genuinely unresolved and should not be smoothed over.

CRITICAL GAP RELATIVE TO THE ACTUAL QUESTION. The user asked two things: which neural cell types express MDA5, and which cell type shows significant change IN MS. These 16 claims answer only the first. Not one claim addresses multiple sclerosis, and no MS dataset is analysed anywhere — despite the user naming GSE180759 (human MS lesion snRNA-seq) and the working scratchpad already containing MS resources (GSE180759, GSE138614 white-matter lesion contrasts, Jäkel, Schirmer, Absinta, Macnair, plus out_jakel_ms_vs_ctrl.csv and out_schirmer_ms_vs_ctrl.csv). The MS half of the question is entirely unaddressed by this angle. Note also that Claim 16, if it holds, directly constrains how any MS finding should be read: if IFIH1 rises in astrocytes after non-viral stimuli generally, then elevated astrocytic IFIH1 in MS lesions is a reactivity/interferon-response marker, not evidence of dsRNA sensing — and because IFIH1 is itself an interferon-stimulated gene, any MS-versus-control difference must be reported as an INDUCED level, never as a baseline cell-type property. That distinction is the one the task brief flagged up front and it is the one most at risk in the MS analysis that still needs doing.

research.dimension: MDA5/IFIH1 in brain vasculature and barrier/border cells (endothelium, pericytes, VSMC, fibroblasts, ependyma, choroid plexus, CNS/perivascular macrophages) — is brain endothelium a genuine high-MDA5 compartment, is it a general endothelial property, is it baseline or interferon-induced, and is it an snRNA-seq artefact?
research.cell_type_ranking: YES — this angle directly sets the top of the CNS ranking. Consensus ordering of IFIH1 across human CNS cell types (two independent human snRNA-seq atlases, depth-normalised, agreeing closely): (1) Endothelial cells — HPA/Siletti 118.9 nCPM; Yang et al. capillary 86.9 / arterial 74.6 / venous 67.0 CPM. (2) CNS macrophage / microglia — 35.5 nCPM; 41.5 CPM. (3) Leukocyte/T cell — 30.2 nCPM; 48.0 CPM. (4) Fibroblast (perivascular/meningeal) — 23.2 nCPM; 22.0 / 20.7 CPM. (5) Pericyte — 14.8 nCPM; 14.1 CPM. (6) Ependymal cell — 13.5 nCPM; 15.2 CPM. (7) Vascular smooth muscle — 13.3 nCPM; 11.1 CPM. (8) OPC — 12.3 nCPM; 8.3 CPM. (9) Astrocyte — 11.6 nCPM; 11.3 CPM. (10) Choroid plexus epithelium — 8.8 nCPM (not separately annotated by Yang). (11) Oligodendrocyte — 7.5 nCPM; 9.3 CPM. (12) Neurons — 0.0–4.7 nCPM (most subtypes <2); 6.2 CPM. Endothelium is ~3.3x the next-highest CNS cell type (CNS macrophage) and ~10–25x neurons. Ranking direction is reproduced in mouse (immunopanned bulk RNA-seq and vascular SMART-seq2) and in fresh human surgical tissue scRNA-seq, so it is not method-specific. Caveat for whoever assembles the final ranking: the ratio endothelium:myeloid is large in snRNA-seq (3.3x) but only 1.27x in human immunopanned bulk RNA-seq (6.5 vs 5.1 FPKM), so the *magnitude* of endothelial dominance over microglia/macrophages is method-dependent even though the *rank* is not.
research.gaps:
(1) NO MS-specific measurement of IFIH1 in brain vascular cells was found. I found no study reporting IFIH1/MDA5 expression change in MS endothelium, pericytes, ependyma or choroid plexus. The Acta Neuropathologica laser-microdissected MS blood-vessel study (Cambron/de Vries lineage, doi 10.1007/s00401-009-0618-9) was paywalled/redirect-blocked and I could not confirm whether IFIH1 was on its 113-gene panel. This angle therefore contributes nothing directly to the MS question beyond identifying which compartment to look in.
(2) NO protein-level confirmation in brain endothelium. The only human brain IHC evidence (HPA antibody HPA002656) contradicts the RNA data, and HPA itself flags it as low-reliability. No Western blot, immunofluorescence or proteomic measurement of MDA5 in human brain endothelial cells was found.
(3) NO functional MDA5 loss-of-function experiment in brain endothelial cells. Published BMEC work uses poly(I:C)/TLR3 or RIG-I; the one MDA5-specific endothelial functional study (Asdonk 2016) is coronary artery, not brain. The 2026 Immunity paper establishing BMECs as the primary IFN-I responder does not measure MDA5 at all.
(4) Border-associated (perivascular, meningeal, choroid plexus) macrophages are not resolved separately from microglia in any dataset I could query; "CNS macrophage" (HPA) and "Microglia/Mφ" (Yang) are lumped categories.
(5) Choroid plexus epithelium is thinly sampled (HPA reports it in only 4 of 11 brain regions; Yang et al. do not annotate it), so 8.8 nCPM is a weak estimate.
(6) Could not quantify the number of endothelial nuclei behind the HPA 118.9 nCPM value — HPA reports only that vascular+immune ("other") = 20,644 of 2,526,725 nuclei (0.82%), from 3 donors (Siletti et al.).
(7) The GTEx v8/v10 API returned empty result sets for ENSG00000115267 on both gencode versions tried, so I have no GTEx bulk TPM values; HPA consensus nTPM is used instead.
(8) No absolute protein quantification (copies/cell, ng/mg) for MDA5 in any vascular cell type.
(9) The cross-organ endothelial comparison (brain highest at 99.6 nCPM) is confounded: HPA's brain endothelial data come from snRNA-seq while other organs come from scRNA-seq. "Brain endothelium is the highest endothelial bed" is therefore NOT established.

findings.claim: In the Human Protein Atlas brain single-nuclei atlas, IFIH1 is highest in endothelial cells (118.9 nCPM) — 3.35x the next-highest CNS cell type and 25x the highest neuronal subtype; HPA formally classifies it as 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)' for brain cluster specificity.
findings.evidence: Full HPA brain snRNA-seq cell-type table (nCPM), extracted from the page's embedded chart data: Endothelial cell 118.9; Central nervous system macrophage 35.5; Leukocyte 30.2; Fibroblast 23.2; Pericyte 14.8; Ependymal cell 13.5; Vascular associated smooth muscle cell 13.3; Oligodendrocyte precursor cell 12.3; Astrocyte 11.6; Choroid plexus epithelial cell 8.8; Oligodendrocyte 7.5; Committed oligodendrocyte precursor 5.6; Bergmann glia 5.4. Neurons: Thalamic excitatory 4.7, Miscellaneous 3.3, Mammillary body 2.0, Hippocampal CA1-3 1.5, LAMP5-LHX6/Chandelier 1.4, Upper rhombic lip 1.3, Deep-layer intratelencephalic 1.2, Deep-layer corticothalamic/6b 0.9, MGE interneuron 0.8, Midbrain-derived inhibitory 0.7, CGE interneuron 0.5, Splatter 0.5, Upper-layer intratelencephalic 0.5, Amygdala excitatory 0.3, Lower rhombic lip 0.3, Cerebellar inhibitory 0.2, Deep-layer near-projecting 0.2, Medium spiny neuron 0.1, Eccentric MSN 0.1, Hippocampal CA4 0.1, Hippocampal dentate gyrus 0.0. Underlying data: Siletti K et al., Science 2023 (2,526,725 nuclei imported by HPA; 11 brain regions; 34 superclusters).

findings.claim: The endothelial rank is not driven by one region: IFIH1 in brain endothelial cells is 96.4–148.9 nCPM in all 11 brain regions sampled independently, and endothelium exceeds every other vascular/border cell type in every region.
findings.evidence: HPA per-region nCPM for Endothelial cell: Hypothalamus 148.9, Amygdala 135.2, Midbrain 134.2, Spinal cord 129.4, Cerebellum 117.7, Pons 116.7, Basal ganglia 114.6, Hippocampus 113.8, Thalamus 102.2, Cerebral cortex 99.1, Medulla oblongata 96.4 (overall 118.9). Comparators, same atlas, per-region ranges: Pericyte 3.8–27.0 (overall 14.8); Vascular smooth muscle 6.4–18.5 (13.3); Fibroblast 5.3–33.1 (23.2); Ependymal cell 7.1–19.3 (13.5); Choroid plexus epithelium 5.5–15.8 (8.8); CNS macrophage 21.9–61.3 (35.5); Astrocyte 7.9–16.0 (11.6); Leukocyte 17.5–41.1 (30.2).

findings.claim: A second, fully independent human brain snRNA-seq atlas (Yang et al., Nature 2022, vascular-enriched VINE-seq, 143,793 nuclei) reproduces the ranking with near-identical depth-normalised values, and resolves all three endothelial segments as the top three cell types.
findings.evidence: I re-analysed the deposited matrix via the UCSC Cell Browser (dataset 'brain-vasc-atlas'), computing pseudobulk CPM as sum(IFIH1 counts)/sum(nCount_RNA)x1e6 per annotated cell type: Capillary EC 86.9 CPM (7.2% of nuclei positive, n=20,299); Arterial EC 74.6 (5.8%, n=6,680); Venous EC 67.0 (7.1%, n=9,846); T cell 48.0 (3.1%, n=351); Microglia/Mφ 41.5 (2.8%, n=3,373); Perivascular fibroblast 22.0 (1.7%, n=2,985); Meningeal fibroblast 20.7 (1.9%, n=428); Ependymal 15.2 (2.3%, n=1,534); Pericyte 14.1 (1.3%, n=27,196); Astrocyte 11.3 (1.3%, n=22,695); SMC 11.1 (0.9%, n=7,312); Oligodendrocyte 9.3 (0.9%, n=34,774); OPC 8.3 (1.2%, n=3,379); Neuron 6.2 (0.9%, n=2,941). Cell identity control CLDN5: capillary 2078 CPM, venous 1983, arterial 1677, all non-endothelial ≤4 CPM. Values agree with the HPA/Siletti atlas to within ~25% for pericyte (14.1 vs 14.8), astrocyte (11.3 vs 11.6), oligodendrocyte (9.3 vs 7.5) and microglia/macrophage (41.5 vs 35.5) despite different donors, regions and dissociation protocols.

findings.claim: The endothelial signal is NOT a generic snRNA-seq inflation of everything in endothelial nuclei: the MDA5 adaptor MAVS shows no endothelial enrichment in either human atlas, and a housekeeping control shows only ~2x endothelial bias versus IFIH1's ~8–14x.
findings.evidence: HPA brain snRNA-seq, MAVS nCPM: Endothelial cell 39.9, Pericyte 40.4, VSMC 37.5, Fibroblast 46.5, CNS macrophage 63.9, Astrocyte 50.5, Oligodendrocyte 38.7, Choroid plexus 47.9 — i.e. endothelium is NOT the top cell type. Yang atlas MAVS CPM: Microglia/Mφ 107.1, P. fibroblast 99.3, Pericyte 94.4, SMC 76.5, Oligodendrocyte 69.4, Astrocyte 66.6, Venous EC 62.8, Capillary EC 60.7, Arterial EC 51.2 — endothelium among the LOWEST. Housekeeping control HNRNPA1, Yang atlas: Venous EC 44.5, Arterial 41.3, Capillary 34.5 vs Astrocyte 17.3, Oligodendrocyte 28.4, Neuron 20.9 (endothelial/astrocyte ratio 2.0–2.6x). IFIH1 endothelial/astrocyte ratio in the same cells is 7.7x and endothelial/neuron 14x, i.e. 3–7x beyond any generic capture bias. HPA brain HNRNPA1: Endothelial 19.8, Oligodendrocyte 23.8, CNS macrophage 27.3 — no endothelial enrichment at all.
