findings.claim: Ambient-RNA contamination cannot generate the endothelial signal, because the dominant ambient sources in brain snRNA-seq (neurons ~69%, oligodendrocytes) are the lowest-IFIH1 cell types; ambient would dilute, not inflate, endothelial values. The known snRNA-seq problem for vascular cells is under-recovery (fewer nuclei, more noise), not systematic over-estimation.
findings.evidence: HPA brain atlas composition: 2,526,725 nuclei total = 1,733,487 neuronal (68.6%) + 769,594 glial (30.5%) + 20,644 vascular/immune (0.82%). IFIH1 in the abundant classes is 0.0–4.7 nCPM (neurons) and 5.4–12.3 nCPM (macroglia) versus 118.9 in endothelium. Independent statements of the recovery bias: 'standard nuclear isolation protocols tend to favor neuronal recovery and lead to loss of vascular nuclei... vascular and perivascular cells, particularly endothelial cells and pericytes, are disproportionately underrepresented' (NVUAtlas preprint, PMC12746550). Arithmetic consistency check: weighting the HPA per-cell-type nCPM by the atlas cell-type proportions gives ~4 nCPM expected bulk brain, versus HPA measured bulk cerebral cortex 6.9 nTPM and consensus 2.7 nTPM — same order of magnitude, i.e. no gross inflation.

findings.claim: The endothelium-first ranking is reproduced by whole-cell (non-nuclear) methods in both species, so it is not an snRNA-seq artefact. Human immunopanned bulk RNA-seq, mouse immunopanned bulk RNA-seq, mouse vascular SMART-seq2 scRNA-seq and fresh human surgical-tissue scRNA-seq all rank endothelium first.
findings.evidence: (a) HUMAN, immunopanned/FACS-purified brain cell types, bulk RNA-seq, FPKM (Zhang Y et al., Neuron 2016; GSE73721, re-extracted by me from GSE73721_Human_and_mouse_table.csv): IFIH1 endothelial 7.9 and 5.1 (mean 6.5, n=2: 47yo and 13yo cortex); microglia/myeloid 6.0, 4.3, 5.1 (mean 5.13, n=3); astrocytes mean 2.32 / median 1.65 (n=26); oligodendrocytes 1.1–1.3 (mean 1.18, n=5); neuron 0.8 (n=1); whole cortex 0.9–1.8 (mean 1.30, n=4). Purity control CLDN5: endothelial 27.1 and 24.4 vs ≤0.2 in all other fractions. (b) MOUSE, immunopanned bulk RNA-seq FPKM (Zhang Y et al., J Neurosci 2014): Ifih1 endothelial 2.10 and 2.01 (mean 2.06) > microglia/macrophage 0.54 > neurons 0.41 > OPC 0.22 > astrocytes 0.21 > oligodendrocytes 0.10 (floor). Cldn5 endothelial 3437 vs ≤11 elsewhere. (c) MOUSE brain vascular SMART-seq2 scRNA-seq (Vanlandewijck 2018 / He 2018, betsholtzlab.org average counts, read from the published per-cluster plot): EC2 ~131, aEC ~129, EC1 ~100, EC3 ~95, vEC ~86, capilEC ~72; pericytes ~46, FB2 ~38, vSMC ~31, FB1 ~19, aSMC ~17, aaSMC ~13, microglia ~9, astrocytes ~7, oligodendrocytes ~0.5. (d) HUMAN fresh surgical tissue scRNA-seq (Winkler EA et al., Science 2022; UCSC 'adult-brain-vasc'): IFIH1 detected in 12.2–34.8% of endothelial cells (Venule 34.8%, Cap 27.2%, Venous 18.7%, Art2 18.4%, Art3 13.6%, Art1 12.2%) versus 2.9–6.4% of perivascular cells (PC 6.4%, FB 5.0%, FBMC 3.2%, SMC 2.9%) at comparable sequencing depth (median nCount 4,684 vs 5,093).

findings.claim: There is a genuine cell-intrinsic (interferon-independent) component to high endothelial Ifih1: in healthy perfused mouse brain, endothelial cells carry high Ifih1/Ddx58/Irf7/Stat1 while the effector ISGs Ifit1 and Ifit3 sit at the detection floor in every cell type — i.e. no ongoing interferon response is present.
findings.evidence: Mouse immunopanned bulk RNA-seq (Zhang 2014, FPKM, cell-type means): Ifih1 endothelial 2.06 (rank 1); Ddx58 endothelial 8.63 (rank 1, 4.1x OPC 2.11, 5.4x microglia 1.60); Irf7 endothelial 5.79 (rank 1, 3.6x microglia 1.59); Stat1 endothelial 7.84 (rank 1); Isg15 endothelial 7.42 (rank 2 after microglia 10.31). BUT effector ISGs are flat and at floor: Ifit1 endothelial 0.28, microglia 0.14, all others 0.10–0.12 (0.1 = the table's floor value); Ifit3 astrocytes 0.77, OPC 0.48, microglia 0.33, endothelial 0.28. Interpretation: sensors and IFN-amplifiers are constitutively high in endothelium without an active IFN effector programme, so the endothelial enrichment of Ifih1 is a baseline cell-type property in the healthy brain.

findings.claim: In HUMAN post-mortem and surgical brain, however, the endothelial IFIH1 signal co-occurs with a full active ISG module, so an unknown fraction of the human endothelial value reflects tonic/agonal/procedural interferon signalling rather than pure baseline. Baseline and induced components cannot be separated in the human data currently available.
findings.evidence: HPA brain snRNA-seq, endothelial cell vs highest non-endothelial CNS cell type (nCPM): RIGI/DDX58 162.8 (vs leukocyte 89.0, CNS macrophage 80.5); IFIH1 118.9 (vs 35.5); DHX58/LGP2 15.6 (vs astrocyte 13.2); STAT1 268.5 (vs upper-layer IT neuron 205.9); IFNAR1 132.6 (vs CNS macrophage 77.1); IFIT1 106.0 (vs pericyte 41.4); ISG15 100.3 (vs pericyte 86.4); OAS2 55.6 (vs leukocyte 28.1). MAVS, which is not an ISG, is flat (39.9). Yang atlas endothelium likewise: ISG15 capillary 53.4 CPM, OAS2 capillary 30.5 CPM, STAT1 capillary 97.0 CPM — all ranked 1–3. Winkler fresh-tissue endothelial scRNA-seq: ISG15 detected in 67.5% of capillary EC, IFIT1 in 45.0%. The whole coherent ISG/RLR module — not IFIH1 alone — is endothelium-high in every human dataset, which is expected if IFIH1 is behaving as an ISG under tonic IFN tone.

findings.claim: High IFIH1 is a general property of endothelium across organs, not a brain-specific specialisation. Across the whole human body, endothelial cells rank 6th of 53 cell-type groups.
findings.evidence: HPA single cell type atlas, IFIH1 nCPM by cell-type group (top): Neutrophils 129.2; Spermatogenic cell types 93.1; Plasma cells 63.0; Mononuclear phagocytes 60.5; Barrier epithelial cells 53.3; Endothelial cells 48.5; Ductal cells 48.3; Ciliated cells 46.6; Glial cells 45.1. Bottom: Smooth muscle cells 5.9, Adipocytes 5.6, Platelets 2.8, Myocytes 1.7, Neuronal cells 0.5, Oocytes 0.0, Stellate cells 0.0. Vascular endothelial cells per tissue (nCPM): Brain 99.6, Epididymis 87.1, Urinary bladder 76.4, Eye 72.7, Vasculature 71.5, Fallopian tube 63.1, Tongue 59.9, Ovary 59.5, Salivary gland 58.3, Pituitary 55.4, Lung 47.0, Breast 45.5, Prostate 42.4, Pancreas 41.1, Endometrium 39.3, Testis 36.7, Kidney 31.9, Skeletal muscle 30.6, Stomach 30.5, Liver 23.3, Esophagus 22.6, Heart muscle 16.8, Placenta 11.0. Lymphatic endothelial cells are consistently lower (4.8–27.1). Mural cells are ~4x lower than endothelium in the same tissues (pericytes 4.0–35.5; vascular SMC 3.1–16.4; overall mural 11.9). Mouse lung vascular scRNA-seq shows the same pattern (cEC3 ~217, cEC1 ~145, aEC ~66, capilEC ~62, LEC ~77 vs fibroblasts 3–25, VSMC ~11). CAVEAT: HPA's brain endothelial value derives from snRNA-seq while other organs derive from scRNA-seq, so the claim 'brain is the highest endothelial bed' is confounded and should NOT be asserted.

findings.claim: Bulk brain tissue is essentially IFIH1-negative — brain regions are the lowest-expressing tissues in the human body — which is exactly what a signal confined to ~0.5–1% of cells (endothelium) predicts. Any bulk-tissue study of MDA5 in brain is therefore blind to the endothelial compartment.
findings.evidence: HPA consensus tissue nTPM, lowest of 51 tissues: Cerebellum 0.5, Retina 1.0, Skeletal muscle 1.5, Hypothalamus 1.6, Amygdala 1.7, Hippocampal formation 1.8, Basal ganglia 1.9, Testis 1.9, Midbrain 2.3, Spinal cord 2.5; highest: Bone marrow 34.6, Salivary gland 16.4, Spleen 15.3, Duodenum 12.4, Appendix 11.8, Lymph node 10.8, Lung 10.1. HPA Brain RNA-seq nTPM by region: Cerebral cortex 6.9, Hippocampal formation 5.5, Amygdala 7.2, Basal ganglia 9.5, Thalamus 9.3, Hypothalamus 7.6, Midbrain 7.6, Cerebellum 7.3, Pons 10.6, Medulla oblongata 15.5, Spinal cord 16.7, White matter 9.8, Choroid plexus 9.5. HPA GTEx-derived cerebral cortex samples: 2.3–3.4 nTPM. The original MDA-5 tissue survey likewise reported brain as undetectable by Northern blot ('highest levels in placenta, pancreas, and spleen, and undetectable levels in brain, lung, and testis', OMIM 606951).

findings.claim: Protein-level evidence does NOT currently support endothelial dominance in human brain, and HPA itself flags the discordance. This is a real gap, not a confirmation.
findings.evidence: HPA immunohistochemistry, cerebral cortex, antibody HPA002656 (rabbit polyclonal, 0.05 mg/ml, HIER pH6, 1:50): 'Endothelial cells: Low; Glial cells: Not detected; Neuronal cells: Medium; Neuropil: Not detected' — i.e. neurons score HIGHER than endothelium at protein level, opposite to all RNA data. HPA tissue-IHC reliability score for IFIH1 is 'Approved' (the second-lowest of four tiers), with the explicit validation notes 'Partly consistent with extensive gene/protein characterization data' and 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data'. No independent MDA5 immunostaining of human brain vessels was found.

findings.claim: Endothelial MDA5 is expressed and functional at protein level outside the brain, and is itself upregulated ~4.6-fold by cytoplasmic dsRNA — direct evidence that in endothelium IFIH1 is both a constitutive sensor and an inducible ISG.
findings.evidence: Asdonk T et al., J Cell Mol Med 2016;20(9):1696–1705 (PMID 27130701, doi 10.1111/jcmm.12864), human coronary artery endothelial cells (HCAEC, Lonza): HCAECs 'constitutively expressed MDA-5' (immunodetection, ab69983). Cytoplasmic transfection of polyIC (1 µg/ml, 24 h) raised MDA5 mRNA from 2.25 ± 0.48 to 10.25 ± 2.66 per 1000 CPB transcripts (~4.6-fold, P<0.05, n=4). Functional consequences: ROS 353.9 ± 115.6% of control (P<0.05); apoptosis 145.7 ± 8.98% of control (P<0.05); impaired migration; ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 upregulation; IL-6, IL-8 and IP-10 release. For reference on IFN-inducibility of IFIH1 generally: IFN-beta enhances MDA5 expression ~3-fold more than IFN-alpha, IFN-gamma or TNF (OMIM 606951, summarising the original MDA-5 characterisation).

findings.claim: Functionally, the brain endothelium is the CNS compartment that both senses viral dsRNA PAMPs and is the first cell type to respond to peripheral type I interferon — consistent with a high-RLR barrier, although the definitive experiments used TLR3/IFNAR1 rather than MDA5 itself.
findings.evidence: Daniels BP et al., mBio 2014;5(5):e01476-14 (PMID 25161189): TLR3, TLR7, RIG-I and MDA5 are the PRRs sensing West Nile virus PAMPs at the BBB; Th1 cytokines increase endothelial permeability whereas type I IFN promotes and stabilises BBB function. Review: Daniels BP, Klein RS, Clin Pharmacol Ther 2015;97(4):361-3 (PMID 25670037). Lewy T et al., Immunity 2026 (PMID 42392076, doi 10.1016/j.immuni.2026.06.009): 69,003 nuclei snRNA-seq of mouse cortex at 2 h and 16 h after i.v. IFN-alpha3 or PBS; brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMECs) were 'the primary responder cell type at 2 hours post treatment' and 'more robustly induce antiviral genes compared to whole brain tissue'; upstream regulators inferred as IRF9/STAT1/STAT2; AAV-Cre deletion of Ifnar1 in BMECs (Ifnar1 fl/fl) abolished distal poly(I:C)-mediated protection from encephalitis; microglia dominated only at 16 h (>1,000 DEGs, |log2FC|>0.5, adj. p<0.05). IMPORTANT LIMITATION: this paper does not measure IFIH1/MDA5 or DDX58 anywhere; MDA5 appears only in its introduction. IFN-lambda tightens the BBB and restricts WNV neuroinvasion (Lazear HM et al., Sci Transl Med 2015).

findings.claim: Among barrier/border cells other than endothelium, fibroblast-type cells (perivascular and meningeal) rank above ependyma and choroid plexus epithelium, and all are far below endothelium; pericytes and vascular smooth muscle are unremarkable in human, but pericytes are relatively higher in mouse.
findings.evidence: HPA brain snRNA-seq (nCPM): Fibroblast 23.2 > Pericyte 14.8 > Ependymal cell 13.5 > VSMC 13.3 > Choroid plexus epithelial cell 8.8. Yang atlas (CPM): Perivascular fibroblast 22.0 > Meningeal fibroblast 20.7 > Ependymal 15.2 > Pericyte 14.1 > SMC 11.1. Species difference: in mouse brain vascular SMART-seq2 data pericytes reach ~46 average counts and FB2 ~38 versus EC 72–131 (ratio EC/PC ~2–3x), whereas in the human atlases the ratio EC/pericyte is 6–8x (118.9/14.8 and 86.9/14.1). HPA whole-body mural cells 11.9 nCPM vs endothelial 48.5 nCPM.

findings.claim: Descriptive (not statistically tested) observation from the Yang atlas: IFIH1 in brain endothelium is modestly higher in Alzheimer's disease than in controls, while microglial IFIH1 is lower — offered only as a hypothesis-generating comparison for the disease-change question, and NOT as an MS result.
findings.evidence: My own pseudobulk CPM computation on the Yang et al. Nature 2022 matrix, split by the 'Treat' metadata field (Control n=72,371 nuclei; AD n=71,422 nuclei): Capillary EC 81.1 (control) vs 99.0 (AD); Arterial EC 69.0 vs 88.1; Venous EC 64.6 vs 74.1; Pericyte 13.1 vs 16.3; Astrocyte 10.0 vs 12.3; Oligodendrocyte 9.2 vs 9.3; Microglia/Mφ 51.5 vs 36.9. No differential-expression test, donor-level pseudobulk, or multiple-testing correction was performed by me, and the original paper does not report IFIH1. Treat as unverified.

verification.overall:
VERIFICATION METHOD: I did not merely re-read the cited pages. I re-downloaded the primary data and recomputed the numbers: (a) parsed the embedded chart JSON of the HPA IFIH1 single-cell/tissue/brain/antibody pages plus 9 comparator-gene pages; (b) downloaded GSE73721_Human_and_mouse_table.csv from GEO and recomputed the human immunopanned FPKMs; (c) downloaded GSE52564_RAW.tar (17 .xls files) and recomputed mouse cell-type means; (d) range-fetched individual gene rows out of the UCSC Cell Browser binary matrices for brain-vasc-atlas (Yang) and adult-brain-vasc (Winkler) and recomputed pseudobulk CPM, percent-positive and depth from meta.tsv.

HEADLINE: This is an unusually accurate submission. Of several hundred quoted numbers I could check, essentially all reproduce exactly. Claim 3's entire 14-row Yang table (CPM AND percent-positive AND n), claim 6(d)'s ten Winkler percentages and both median depths (4,684 / 5,093), claim 15's full AD/control split, claims 1/2/9/10/11's HPA values, and claim 6(a)'s GEO FPKMs all reproduce to the decimal. Cell counts (20,299 / 6,680 / 9,846 / 27,196 / 143,793; Control 72,371 / AD 71,422) match exactly. No number was fabricated and no mouse result was passed off as human. The core finding — that in human brain transcriptomic atlases IFIH1 is a vascular-endothelial gene, ~3x above any other CNS cell type and ~25x above neurons, reproducibly across 11 regions and two independent atlases and two whole-cell bulk datasets — survives adversarial checking.

WHAT I DID BREAK:
1. Claim 7 is the weakest link and is OVERSTATED. Its numbers are right, but its conclusion ("no ongoing interferon response is present", "genuine cell-intrinsic interferon-independent component") is contradicted by its own dataset: Isg15 (endothelial 7.46, rank 2) and Irf7 (5.75, rank 1) are canonical effector ISGs and are endothelium-high. The claim selects Ifit1/Ifit3 as "the" effector ISGs while Isg15 is at least as canonical. No IFN-blockade or Ifnar1-null experiment exists, so "interferon-independent" is untested. Claims 7 and 8 are in direct tension and both cannot stand; claim 8's hedged version is the defensible one.
2. Claim 8 contains one genuinely wrong comparator: STAT1 endothelium (268.5) is rank 3 of 34, NOT top — Lower rhombic lip neurons 350.6 and hippocampal dentate gyrus 275.8 both exceed it. The cited "upper-layer IT 205.9" is real but is rank 6, not "the highest non-endothelial CNS cell type".
3. Three purity/specificity controls are misstated: Yang CLDN5 is NOT "≤4 CPM in all non-endothelial" (T cell 395.1, Ependymal 134.5 — implying endothelial contamination of the T-cell cluster that inflates its IFIH1 rank-4 value); GSE73721 CLDN5 is not "≤0.2 in all other fractions" (Fetal ctx 6 astro 2.4); mouse Cldn5 is not "≤11 elsewhere" (Microglia2 19.4, whole cortex 142.5) and the endothelial mean is 3394.7, not 3437.
4. Claim 5's ambient-RNA argument is an inference dressed as evidence: "neurons ~69% of ambient" is the proportion of NUCLEI, not a measurement of ambient RNA composition, and no cited source measures ambient composition. Its source is an unreviewed bioRxiv preprint whose verbatim quotes I could not confirm on the PMC page.
5. Smaller corrections: lymphatic endothelium reaches 50.6 nCPM (spleen), not a 4.8–27.1 ceiling; HPA marks pituitary, adipose, kidney, skeletal muscle and heart with the same snRNA-seq asterisk as brain, so that caveat is broader than stated; endothelium is 0.18% of the Siletti atlas, not "0.5–1%"; Kang 2002 said brain was "barely detectable", not "undetectable"; Asdonk's VCAM-1 result was P > 0.05, i.e. not significant.
6. Claim 6(c) (betsholtzlab mouse values) and the mouse-lung half of claim 9 are the only numbers I could not verify at all — the site's per-gene endpoint is not reachable and the claim concedes the values were eyeballed off a plot. Directionally they are corroborated by my own GSE52564 recomputation (mouse endothelial Ifih1 rank 1/8), but the specific figures stand unverified.

TWO STRUCTURAL LIMITATIONS THE SUBMISSION UNDERSTATES:
- Statistical fragility. IFIH1 is a sparse, low-abundance transcript: only 7.2% of capillary endothelial nuclei are positive (1-2% in most other types), total IFIH1 counts across 143,793 Yang nuclei are 4,278, and the entire Siletti endothelial compartment is 4,459 nuclei (189–850 per region). Not one claim carries a confidence interval, a donor-level pseudobulk, or a significance test. Claim 6(a)'s human ranking rests on n=2 endothelial samples whose values (5.1, 7.9) overlap the myeloid range (4.3, 5.1, 6.0) — endothelium leads on the mean (6.5 vs 5.13) but the two are not separable.
- "Baseline" is not established. Every human dataset here is post-mortem or surgical, and the whole RLR/ISG module (RIGI, IFIT1, ISG15, OAS2, IFNAR1) is endothelium-top alongside IFIH1 — exactly the pattern expected under tonic/agonal/procedural interferon tone. Since IFIH1 is itself an ISG, the baseline and induced components remain unseparated in human tissue, and the HPA IHC (endothelial "Low" vs neuronal "Medium", "Low consistency" with RNA, reliability only "Approved") means there is no protein confirmation of endothelial dominance in human brain at all.

RELEVANCE TO THE ACTUAL QUESTION: none of the 15 claims addresses multiple sclerosis. The only disease comparison offered (claim 15) is Alzheimer's, is the researcher's own untested pseudobulk, and is explicitly flagged as not an MS result. This angle answers "which CNS cell type expresses MDA5 at baseline" well; it contributes nothing to "which cell type changes in MS", and that gap should not be papered over when the strands are merged.

verdicts.claim: HPA brain snRNA-seq: IFIH1 highest in endothelial cells (118.9 nCPM), 3.35x next-highest CNS cell type, 25x highest neuronal subtype; formally 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)'.
verdicts.reason: Verified directly against the embedded chart JSON of the HPA page. All 34 cell-type values reproduce exactly: Endothelial 118.9, CNS macrophage 35.5, Leukocyte 30.2, Fibroblast 23.2, Pericyte 14.8, Ependymal 13.5, VSMC 13.3, OPC 12.3, Astrocyte 11.6, Choroid plexus 8.8, Oligodendrocyte 7.5, COP 5.6, Bergmann glia 5.4, and every neuronal value from Thalamic excitatory 4.7 down to Hippocampal dentate gyrus 0.0. Ratios check: 118.9/35.5=3.35, 118.9/4.7=25.3. The HPA gene JSON returns 'RNA single nuclei brain specificity: Cell type enhanced' with 'RNA single nuclei brain specific nCPM: {endothelial cell: 118.9}', and the page text reads verbatim 'RNA brain cluster specificity: Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)'. Siletti 2023 (PMID 37824663) is cited on the page as the source. Caveats not errors: 'Cell type enhanced' is a weak HPA tier (below 'enriched' and 'group enriched'), and the atlas total is 2,523,459 by my sum of the per-region cell counts (HPA's own class breakdown sums to 2,523,725), not 2,526,725.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the HPA brain single-nuclei atlas (Siletti et al., Science 2023, ~2.52M nuclei), IFIH1 is highest in endothelial cells at 118.9 nCPM — 3.35x the next-highest cell type (CNS macrophage 35.5) and 25x the highest neuronal supercluster (thalamic excitatory 4.7) — and HPA classifies it as 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)' for brain cluster specificity, 'enhanced' being the weakest of the three elevated tiers.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 in brain endothelium is 96.4–148.9 nCPM in all 11 regions independently, exceeding every other vascular/border cell type in every region.
verdicts.reason: Extracted the per-region tooltip matrix (243 cell-type x region entries) from the HPA page and checked every value. All 11 endothelial values match exactly: Hypothalamus 148.9, Amygdala 135.2, Midbrain 134.2, Spinal cord 129.4, Cerebellum 117.7, Pons 116.7, Basal ganglia 114.6, Hippocampus 113.8, Thalamus 102.2, Cerebral cortex 99.1, Medulla oblongata 96.4. All comparator ranges match exactly: Pericyte 3.8–27.0, VSMC 6.4–18.5, Fibroblast 5.3–33.1, Ependymal 7.1–19.3, Choroid plexus 5.5–15.8, CNS macrophage 21.9–61.3, Astrocyte 7.9–16.0, Leukocyte 17.5–41.1. The claim is in fact understated: endothelium is top of ALL cell types in every region, not just vascular/border ones, by 2.4–3.6x. The material caveat the claim omits is sample size: only 4,459 endothelial nuclei total, 189–850 per region, with no dispersion estimate.
verdicts.corrected_claim: IFIH1 in HPA brain endothelial nuclei is 96.4–148.9 nCPM in each of the 11 regions sampled, and endothelium is the top-ranked cell type of all 34 in every region (2.4–3.6x the runner-up) — based on 4,459 endothelial nuclei total (189–850 per region), with no confidence intervals reported.

verdicts.claim: Yang et al. Nature 2022 VINE-seq atlas (143,793 nuclei) reproduces the ranking with near-identical values and resolves all three endothelial segments as the top three cell types.
verdicts.reason: I independently reproduced this from the primary matrix rather than trusting it. I range-fetched the IFIH1 row from cells.ucsc.edu/brain-vasc-atlas/exprMatrix.bin using the exprMatrix.json byte index, decoded it (Uint32, 143,793 values), and recomputed sum(counts)/sum(nCount_RNA)x1e6 per Cell_Type from meta.tsv. Every value matches to the decimal: Capillary 86.9 (7.2% positive, n=20,299), Arterial 74.6 (5.8%, 6,680), Veinous 67.0 (7.1%, 9,846), T cell 48.0 (3.1%, 351), Microglia 41.5 (2.8%, 3,373), P.Fibro 22.0, M.Fibro 20.7, Ependymal 15.2, Pericyte 14.1, Astrocyte 11.3, SMC 11.1, Oligo 9.3, OPC 8.3, Neuron 6.2. All three EC segments are indeed top three. TWO CORRECTIONS. (i) The CLDN5 control is wrong: I get T cell 395.1 CPM (17.9% positive) and Ependymal 134.5 CPM, not '≤4 CPM in all non-endothelial'. This matters — it indicates endothelial contamination of the T-cell cluster, which likely inflates its rank-4 IFIH1 value of 48.0. (ii) 'Near-identical' holds for the four non-endothelial types listed but NOT for endothelium itself, the least concordant compartment (HPA 118.9 vs Yang capillary 86.9, a 27% gap). Also both atlases are snRNA-seq, so this is independent in donors/protocol but not in methodology.
verdicts.corrected_claim: An independent human brain snRNA-seq atlas (Yang et al., Nature 2022, VINE-seq, 143,793 nuclei) reproduces the ranking: capillary 86.9, arterial 74.6, venous 67.0 CPM are the top three cell types, with pericyte 14.1, astrocyte 11.3 and oligodendrocyte 9.3 agreeing with HPA to within ~25%, though endothelium itself differs by 27% (86.9 vs 118.9). CLDN5 confirms endothelial identity (capillary 2078 vs ≤4 CPM in most types) but is NOT clean in the T-cell (395 CPM) or ependymal (135 CPM) clusters, so the rank-4 T-cell IFIH1 value should be treated as possibly contamination-inflated. Both atlases use snRNA-seq, so this does not control for nuclear-capture bias.

verdicts.claim: The endothelial signal is not generic snRNA-seq inflation: MAVS shows no endothelial enrichment in either atlas, and housekeeping HNRNPA1 shows only ~2x endothelial bias vs IFIH1's ~8–14x.
verdicts.reason: Checked both halves against primary data. HPA MAVS (parsed from the gene page chart JSON): Endothelial 39.9, Pericyte 40.4, VSMC 37.5, Fibroblast 46.5, CNS macrophage 63.9, Astrocyte 50.5, Oligodendrocyte 38.7, Choroid plexus 47.9 — all exact, endothelium rank 7/34. HPA HNRNPA1: Endothelial 19.8, Oligodendrocyte 23.8, CNS macrophage 27.3 — exact, endothelium rank 7/34, EC/astrocyte ratio only 1.2x. Yang atlas values I recomputed myself from the binary matrix: MAVS Microglia 107.1, P.Fibro 99.3, Pericyte 94.4, SMC 76.5, Oligo 69.4, Astrocyte 66.6, Veinous 62.8, Capillary 60.7, Arterial 51.2 — all nine exact. HNRNPA1 Veinous 44.5, Arterial 41.3, Capillary 34.5, Astrocyte 17.3, Oligo 28.4, Neuron 20.9 — all six exact; EC/astrocyte 2.0–2.6x as stated, versus IFIH1's 7.7x (86.9/11.3) and 14.0x (86.9/6.2), which I verified. This is a genuine and well-designed specificity control and it holds. Two overstatements: endothelium in Yang MAVS is mid-to-lower (ranks 7, 9, 11 of 14), not 'among the LOWEST'; and the claim omits that T cells (51.7) top the HNRNPA1 ranking above all endothelial segments.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The endothelial IFIH1 signal is not generic nuclear-capture inflation: the MDA5 adaptor MAVS is not endothelium-enriched in either atlas (HPA endothelium 39.9, rank 7/34; Yang endothelium ranks 7–11 of 14), and housekeeping HNRNPA1 shows only a 2.0–2.6x endothelial/astrocyte bias versus IFIH1's 7.7x (endothelial/astrocyte) and 14.0x (endothelial/neuron) in the very same cells — i.e. 3–7x beyond any generic capture bias.

verdicts.claim: Ambient RNA cannot generate the endothelial signal because dominant ambient sources (neurons ~69%, oligodendrocytes) are the lowest-IFIH1 cell types; the known snRNA-seq problem for vascular cells is under-recovery, not over-estimation.
verdicts.reason: The verifiable parts check out; the load-bearing premise does not. CONFIRMED: HPA composition 1,733,487 neuronal + 769,594 glial + 20,644 vascular/immune is stated verbatim on the HPA single-nuclei-brain page. CONFIRMED: I reproduced the arithmetic consistency check myself — weighting all 34 HPA cell-type nCPM values by their nuclei counts gives 4.54 nCPM expected bulk, against measured cortex 6.9 (HPA brain dataset) and 2.7 (consensus), i.e. the same order of magnitude with no gross inflation. NOT CONFIRMED: '~69% of ambient RNA is neuronal' is not a measurement of ambient RNA at all — it is the proportion of NUCLEI (68.6%), silently re-labelled as ambient composition. Ambient contribution depends on per-cell RNA yield and lysis susceptibility, not nucleus counts, and no cited source measures it. The cited support (PMC12746550) is NVUAtlas, an unreviewed bioRxiv preprint (Dec 2025); its abstract does state 'underrepresentation of vascular and mural cells in standard snRNA-seq datasets', which supports the under-recovery direction, but I could not confirm either verbatim quote on the PMC page, and the page does not discuss ambient RNA or any neuronal ambient fraction. Note also that under-recovery of a cell type does not by itself rule out contamination effects in the few nuclei that are recovered.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Ambient RNA is unlikely to explain the endothelial signal, but this is an argument rather than a measurement. What is established: the HPA atlas is 68.6% neuronal (1,733,487) and 30.5% glial (769,594) nuclei, and these abundant classes carry the LOWEST IFIH1 (neurons 0.0–4.7, macroglia 5.4–12.3 nCPM) versus endothelium 118.9, so neuron- or glia-derived ambient RNA would dilute rather than inflate endothelial values; and weighting per-cell-type nCPM by cell-type abundance predicts 4.5 nCPM bulk brain against 2.7–6.9 measured, showing no gross inflation. What is NOT established: no study cited measures the actual cellular composition of ambient RNA in these datasets, and the '~69%' figure is the nuclei proportion, not an ambient fraction. The under-recovery of vascular nuclei is supported only by an unreviewed preprint (NVUAtlas, bioRxiv 2025) whose quoted sentences I could not verify.

verdicts.claim: The endothelium-first ranking is reproduced by whole-cell methods in both species: human immunopanned bulk, mouse immunopanned bulk, mouse vascular SMART-seq2, and fresh human surgical scRNA-seq all rank endothelium first.
verdicts.reason: I verified three of the four legs from primary data, not from the papers' text. (a) HUMAN: downloaded GSE73721_Human_and_mouse_table.csv from GEO FTP and recomputed — IFIH1 endothelial 7.9 and 5.1 (mean 6.50), myeloid 6.0/4.3/5.1 (mean 5.13), astrocytes mean 2.32 median 1.65 (n=26), oligodendrocytes mean 1.18 (n=5), neuron 0.8, whole cortex mean 1.30 (n=4). Every figure exact. (b) MOUSE: downloaded GSE52564_RAW.tar, parsed all 17 .xls files with xlrd, recomputed cell-type means — Ifih1 endothelial 2.06 (rank 1/8) > whole cortex 0.60 > microglia 0.54 > neuron 0.42 > OPC 0.22 > astrocyte 0.21 > oligodendrocyte 0.10 (floor). Exact. (d) WINKLER: range-fetched the IFIH1 row from cells.ucsc.edu/adult-brain-vasc — all ten percentages exact (Venule 34.8%, Cap 27.2%, Venous 18.7%, Art2 18.4%, Art3 13.6%, Art1 12.2%; PC 6.4%, FB 5.0%, FBMC 3.2%, SMC 2.9%) and both median depths exact (endothelial nCount_combined 4,684, perivascular 5,093). THREE CAVEATS. (i) Leg (c), the betsholtzlab values, I could not verify at all — the per-gene endpoint returns 404 and the claim concedes the numbers were read off a plot. (ii) Leg (a)'s margin is thin and untested: endothelial mean 6.5 vs myeloid 5.13 on n=2 vs n=3, with fully overlapping individual values (5.1, 7.9 vs 4.3, 5.1, 6.0). (iii) Purity controls are misstated: GSE73721 CLDN5 reaches 2.4 in Fetal ctx 6 astro, not '≤0.2 in all other fractions'; mouse Cldn5 endothelial mean is 3394.7 not 3437, and non-endothelial reaches 19.4 (Microglia2) and 142.5 (whole cortex), not '≤11'. Within-Winkler depth is also not uniform (Cap median 9,383 vs Art2 2,894), though the cleanest pair — Venule 34.8% at depth 5,273 vs SMC 2.9% at depth 5,184 — is a strong like-for-like contrast.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The endothelium-first ranking is not an snRNA-seq artefact: it is reproduced by three whole-cell datasets I re-derived from primary files. Human immunopanned bulk RNA-seq (Zhang, Neuron 2016; GSE73721) puts endothelium top by mean (6.5 FPKM, n=2) but only marginally over myeloid (5.13, n=3) with overlapping values and no statistical test; mouse immunopanned bulk (Zhang, J Neurosci 2014; GSE52564) puts endothelium clearly top (2.06 vs microglia 0.54, neurons 0.42, oligodendrocytes at floor 0.10); and fresh human surgical scRNA-seq (Winkler, Science 2022) detects IFIH1 in 12.2–34.8% of endothelial versus 2.9–6.4% of perivascular cells at matched median depth (4,684 vs 5,093). The mouse SMART-seq2 vascular figures could not be verified from the cited database and should be dropped or re-sourced.

verdicts.claim: There is a genuine cell-intrinsic, interferon-independent component to high endothelial Ifih1: healthy perfused mouse brain endothelium carries high Ifih1/Ddx58/Irf7/Stat1 while effector ISGs Ifit1 and Ifit3 sit at the detection floor, i.e. no ongoing interferon response is present.
verdicts.reason: I recomputed every value from GSE52564 directly. The numbers are essentially right (~1% drift, consistent with the brainrnaseq.org processed table versus my GEO recomputation): Ifih1 EC 2.06 rank 1; Ddx58 EC 8.62 (claim 8.63) rank 1, 4.1x OPC 2.11 and 5.4x microglia 1.60; Irf7 EC 5.75 (claim 5.79) rank 1 vs microglia 1.58; Stat1 EC 7.82 (claim 7.84) rank 1; Isg15 EC 7.46 (claim 7.42) rank 2 behind microglia 10.26; Ifit1 EC 0.28, microglia 0.14, all others 0.10–0.12; Ifit3 astrocyte 0.77, OPC 0.48, microglia 0.33, EC 0.28. THE INTERPRETATION FAILS ON ITS OWN DATA. Isg15 is a canonical effector ISG and is endothelium-high (7.46, rank 2, 16x neurons and 53x oligodendrocytes), as is Irf7 (rank 1, 3.6x microglia). Designating Ifit1/Ifit3 as 'the' effector ISGs while setting Isg15 aside is selective; a coherent reading of the same table is a low-grade tonic IFN tone in endothelium, not its absence. Separately, 'interferon-independent' is an inference from a correlative expression table — no IFN blockade, Ifnar1-null, or IFN-neutralisation experiment was performed — and immunopanning itself involves enzymatic dissociation that can induce stress and interferon genes. Species is correctly labelled as mouse.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In healthy perfused adult mouse brain (Zhang, J Neurosci 2014; GSE52564), endothelial cells rank first for Ifih1 (2.06 FPKM), Ddx58 (8.62), Irf7 (5.75) and Stat1 (7.82) and second for Isg15 (7.46, behind microglia 10.26), while Ifit1 (0.28) and Ifit3 (0.28) sit at or near the 0.1 floor in every cell type. This shows the RLR sensors and IFN amplifiers are constitutively endothelium-high, but it does NOT show the absence of interferon tone — Isg15 and Irf7 are canonical ISGs and are themselves endothelium-high — and no interferon-blockade experiment was performed, so an interferon-independent cell-intrinsic component is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated result.

verdicts.claim: In human brain the endothelial IFIH1 signal co-occurs with a full active ISG module, so an unknown fraction reflects tonic/agonal/procedural interferon signalling; baseline and induced components cannot be separated in available human data.
verdicts.reason: I fetched and parsed the HPA single-cell pages for all eight genes and recomputed the Yang values from the binary matrix. HPA endothelial values all exact: RIGI/DDX58 162.8 (rank 1/34; leukocyte 89.0, CNS macrophage 80.5), IFIH1 118.9, DHX58 15.6 (rank 1; astrocyte 13.2), IFNAR1 132.6 (rank 1; CNS macrophage 77.1), IFIT1 106.0 (rank 1; pericyte 41.4), ISG15 100.3 (rank 1; pericyte 86.4), OAS2 55.6 (rank 1; leukocyte 28.1), MAVS flat at 39.9 (rank 7). Yang values I recomputed myself: ISG15 capillary 53.4 (rank 1), OAS2 capillary 30.5 (rank 1), STAT1 capillary 97.0 (rank 1) — all three exact. ONE REAL ERROR: STAT1 endothelium 268.5 is rank 3 of 34, not top — Lower rhombic lip neurons 350.6 and hippocampal dentate gyrus 275.8 both exceed it. The cited comparator 'upper-layer IT neuron 205.9' is a real number but is rank 6, so describing it as 'the highest non-endothelial CNS cell type' is incorrect and understates how unexceptional endothelial STAT1 is. With that removed, seven of eight genes still support the claim, and the claim's central epistemic point — that IFIH1 is itself an ISG and that baseline versus induced cannot be disentangled in post-mortem/surgical human tissue — is correct and is the appropriately hedged counterweight to claim 7.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In human brain, endothelial IFIH1 co-occurs with a coherent RLR/ISG module that is also endothelium-top: RIGI 162.8, IFNAR1 132.6, IFIT1 106.0, ISG15 100.3, OAS2 55.6 and DHX58 15.6 nCPM all rank 1 of 34 in the HPA atlas, and ISG15, OAS2 and STAT1 rank 1 among capillary endothelium in the Yang atlas, while the non-ISG adaptor MAVS stays flat at 39.9. STAT1 is the exception — endothelium ranks only 3rd (268.5) behind two neuronal superclusters (350.6, 275.8). Because IFIH1 is itself an interferon-stimulated gene and all available human brain tissue is post-mortem or surgical, the baseline and interferon-induced components of the endothelial value cannot currently be separated.

verdicts.claim: High IFIH1 is a general property of endothelium across organs, not brain-specific; endothelial cells rank 6th of 53 cell-type groups body-wide.
verdicts.reason: Parsed the whole-body cell-type-group chart from the HPA page: all 53 values reproduce exactly, with Endothelial cells 48.5 at rank 6, behind Neutrophils 129.2, Spermatogenic 93.1, Plasma cells 63.0, Mononuclear phagocytes 60.5, Barrier epithelial 53.3, and ahead of Ductal 48.3, Ciliated 46.6, Glial 45.1; bottom values SMC 5.9, Adipocytes 5.6, Platelets 2.8, Myocytes 1.7, Neuronal 0.5, Oocytes 0.0, Stellate 0.0, and Mural cells 11.9 — all exact. All 23 per-tissue vascular endothelial values listed also reproduce exactly (Brain 99.6, Epididymis 87.1, Urinary bladder 76.4, Eye 72.7, Vasculature 71.5 … Heart 16.8, Placenta 11.0). The claim's own caveat against asserting brain as the highest endothelial bed is correct and commendable. THREE CORRECTIONS: (i) the lymphatic range is wrong — the maximum is 50.6 nCPM (spleen), not 27.1, though where both are measured vascular does exceed lymphatic in every tissue (thymus 57.8 vs 27.2, lymph node 52.1 vs 37.2, lung 47.0 vs 27.1); (ii) HPA flags Pituitary, Adipose tissue, Kidney, Skeletal muscle and Heart muscle with the same asterisk as Brain, so the snRNA-seq confound is broader than 'brain only'; (iii) the tissue list silently omits Thymus 57.8, Lymph node 52.1, Adipose 50.5 and Skin 27.5. The mouse lung figures come from the unreachable betsholtzlab source and remain unverified.
verdicts.corrected_claim: High IFIH1 is a general endothelial property rather than a brain specialisation: body-wide, endothelial cells rank 6th of 53 HPA cell-type groups at 48.5 nCPM (behind neutrophils 129.2, spermatogenic cells 93.1, plasma cells 63.0, mononuclear phagocytes 60.5 and barrier epithelium 53.3), and vascular endothelium exceeds mural cells (11.9 overall) by ~4x in the same tissues. Vascular endothelial nCPM ranges from 99.6 (brain) to 11.0 (placenta), and exceeds lymphatic endothelium in every tissue where both are measured, though lymphatic endothelium itself reaches 50.6 in spleen. Because HPA derives brain, pituitary, adipose, kidney, skeletal muscle and heart from snRNA-seq and other organs from scRNA-seq, cross-organ ranking of endothelial beds — including any claim that brain is highest — is confounded and should not be asserted.

verdicts.claim: Bulk brain tissue is essentially IFIH1-negative — brain regions are the lowest-expressing tissues in the body — so any bulk study of MDA5 in brain is blind to the endothelial compartment.
verdicts.reason: Verified against both charts on the HPA pages after separating them (the tissue page carries a consensus chart and a GTEx chart with different values; the claim correctly used consensus). Consensus lowest, all exact: Cerebellum 0.5, Retina 1.0, Skeletal muscle 1.5, Hypothalamus 1.6, Amygdala 1.7, Hippocampal formation 1.8, Basal ganglia 1.9, Testis 1.9, Midbrain 2.3, Spinal cord 2.5; highest all exact: Bone marrow 34.6, Salivary gland 16.4, Spleen 15.3, Duodenum 12.4, Appendix 11.8, Lymph node 10.8, Lung 10.1. The HPA gene JSON independently returns 'RNA tissue specific nTPM: {bone marrow: 34.6}'. All 13 HPA brain-dataset regional values are exact and correctly attributed (the page labels that chart 'HPA Human brain dataset'): Cerebral cortex 6.9 … Medulla oblongata 15.5, Spinal cord 16.7. TWO CORRECTIONS: (i) endothelium is 0.18% of the Siletti atlas (4,459 of 2,523,459 nuclei), not '~0.5–1%' — the 0.82% figure is all vascular AND immune cells combined; this strengthens rather than weakens the argument; (ii) the historical citation is slightly hardened — Kang et al. PNAS 2002 (the source behind OMIM 606951) reported brain, testis and lung as 'barely detectable', not 'undetectable', with placenta/pancreas/spleen only ~2-fold above other organs, and explicitly noted no organ showed expression high enough to suggest a functional correlation.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Bulk brain tissue is near the bottom of the human expression range for IFIH1 — HPA consensus cerebellum 0.5, hypothalamus 1.6, amygdala 1.7, hippocampal formation 1.8, basal ganglia 1.9, midbrain 2.3, spinal cord 2.5 nTPM against bone marrow 34.6 — and the HPA brain dataset gives 5.5–16.7 nTPM across regions. This is what a signal confined to endothelium predicts, since endothelial nuclei are only ~0.18% of the brain atlas (all vascular plus immune cells together are 0.82%). Consequently bulk-tissue studies of MDA5 in brain have essentially no sensitivity to the endothelial compartment. Historically, Kang et al. (PNAS 2002) likewise found brain, lung and testis 'barely detectable' by Northern blot.

verdicts.claim: Protein-level evidence does not support endothelial dominance in human brain, and HPA flags the discordance. This is a real gap, not a confirmation.
verdicts.reason: Verified verbatim on the cited pages. The cerebral cortex page carries, under 'Antibody HPA002656': 'Endothelial cells: Low; Glial cells: Not detected; Neuronal cells: Medium; Neuropil: Not detected' — neurons do score above endothelium, opposite to every RNA dataset. The antibody page confirms every stated parameter: 'Host species Rabbit', 'pAb', 'Concentration 0.05 mg/ml', 'HIER pH6', 'Antibody dilution 1:50', and both validation notes verbatim: 'Partly consistent with extensive gene/protein characterization data' and 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data'. The HPA gene JSON returns 'Reliability (IH): Approved', and the tier list on the page is Enhanced / Supported / Approved / Uncertain, making 'Approved' correctly the second-lowest of four. This claim is the submission's most valuable entry precisely because it reports a negative, and the researcher did not attempt to explain it away.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Protein-level evidence does not currently support endothelial dominance of MDA5 in human brain and in fact points the other way: HPA immunohistochemistry of cerebral cortex with antibody HPA002656 (rabbit pAb, 0.05 mg/ml, HIER pH6, 1:50) scores 'Endothelial cells: Low, Glial cells: Not detected, Neuronal cells: Medium, Neuropil: Not detected'. HPA rates the IHC reliability only 'Approved' (second-lowest of four tiers) and explicitly notes 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data'. No independent MDA5 immunostaining of human brain vessels was located. This is an unresolved discordance, not supporting evidence.

verdicts.claim: Endothelial MDA5 is expressed and functional at protein level outside the brain and is upregulated ~4.6-fold by cytoplasmic dsRNA — evidence it is both a constitutive sensor and an inducible ISG in endothelium.
verdicts.reason: Checked against the full text (PMC4993381). Confirmed verbatim: cells are 'Human coronary artery endothelial cells (HCAEC; Lonza, Basel, Switzerland)'; 'HCAECs constitutively expressed MDA-5', detected with rabbit polyclonal ab69983 at 1:1000; polyIC at 1 µg/ml raised MDA5 from 'polyA 2.25 ± 0.48' to 'polyIC 10.25 ± 2.66/1000 CPB transcripts, P < 0.05, n = 4' (4.56-fold, matching '~4.6-fold'); ROS 'polyIC 353.9 ± 115.6% versus polyA 100.0 ± 20.50%, n = 5, P < 0.05'; apoptosis '145.7 ± 8.98% versus 100.0 ± 5.85%, n = 8–9, P < 0.05'; migration impaired; IL-6, IL-8 and IP-10 all significantly raised. ONE ERROR: VCAM-1 was 'polyIC 5.35 ± 1.23 versus polyA 1.18 ± 0.28, P > 0.05' — NOT significant. The claim lists 'ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 upregulation' together as though both were established; only ICAM-1 reached significance (3.79 ± 0.85 vs 1.18 ± 0.13, P < 0.05). Two framing notes: this is an in-vitro cell-culture result in a non-brain arterial bed, and the 4.6-fold induction is mRNA, with protein evidence limited to constitutive detection. The OMIM-sourced IFN-beta reference also checks out against the primary source (Kang et al., PNAS 2002): IFN-beta enhanced MDA5 expression 3-fold more than IFN-alpha, IFN-gamma or TNF.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In cultured human coronary artery endothelial cells (Asdonk et al., J Cell Mol Med 2016, PMID 27130701), MDA-5 is constitutively expressed at protein level (ab69983) and its mRNA rises ~4.6-fold on cytoplasmic polyIC transfection (1 µg/ml: 2.25 ± 0.48 to 10.25 ± 2.66 per 1000 CPB transcripts, P < 0.05, n = 4), with functional consequences including increased ROS (353.9 ± 115.6%, P < 0.05), apoptosis (145.7 ± 8.98%, P < 0.05), impaired migration, significant ICAM-1 induction (P < 0.05) and IL-6, IL-8 and IP-10 release. VCAM-1 rose but did NOT reach significance (P > 0.05). This is an in-vitro result in a non-brain arterial bed and establishes that endothelial IFIH1 behaves as both a constitutive sensor and an inducible ISG, but says nothing directly about brain endothelium in vivo.

verdicts.claim: Brain endothelium both senses viral dsRNA PAMPs and is the first cell type to respond to peripheral type I interferon, consistent with a high-RLR barrier, although the definitive experiments used TLR3/IFNAR1 rather than MDA5.
verdicts.reason: All PMIDs and DOIs resolve correctly via NCBI eutils, including the unusual-looking PMID 42392076, which is genuinely Lewy et al., Immunity 2026, 'Brain endothelial cells orchestrate a neuroprotective antiviral state in the CNS in response to peripheral viral pattern...', doi 10.1016/j.immuni.2026.06.009. Verified in the full text (PMC13532049): mouse C57BL/6J; 69,003 nuclei; i.v. IFN-alpha3 25,000 IU retro-orbital versus PBS at 2 h and 16 h; verbatim 'BMECs as the primary responder cell type at 2 hours post treatment'; IRF9/STAT1/STAT2 as inferred upstream regulators; Ifnar1 fl/fl with AAV-BI30-Cre, where 'BMEC IFNAR1-deficiency negated poly(I:C)-induced protection against WNV disease severity'; and 'microglia dominated this response at 16 hours compared to other cell types with more than 1,000 DEGs'. Critically, I independently confirmed the claim's own stated limitation: the paper does NOT measure Ifih1, MDA5 or Ddx58 anywhere. The researcher flagged this unprompted, which is exactly right. Daniels mBio 2014 and Daniels & Klein 2015 resolve as described. The one framing issue: the headline sentence makes a general statement about 'the brain endothelium' when both the PAMP-sensing and the first-responder evidence are mouse.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In MOUSE, brain endothelium is the CNS compartment that both senses viral dsRNA PAMPs at the blood-brain barrier (Daniels et al., mBio 2014) and responds first to peripheral type I interferon: Lewy et al. (Immunity 2026, 69,003 nuclei, i.v. IFN-alpha3) identify BMECs as 'the primary responder cell type at 2 hours post treatment' with IRF9/STAT1/STAT2 upstream, microglia only dominating by 16 h, and show that BMEC-specific Ifnar1 deletion negates poly(I:C)-induced protection against West Nile disease. This is consistent with — but does not demonstrate — a role for endothelial MDA5: the study measures neither Ifih1 nor Ddx58, and the causal experiments used TLR3 and IFNAR1. No equivalent human in-vivo evidence exists.

verdicts.claim: Among non-endothelial barrier cells, fibroblast-type cells rank above ependyma and choroid plexus and all are far below endothelium; pericytes and VSMC are unremarkable in human but relatively higher in mouse.
verdicts.reason: The human half is fully verified from data I extracted and recomputed. HPA brain: Fibroblast 23.2 > Pericyte 14.8 > Ependymal 13.5 > VSMC 13.3 > Choroid plexus 8.8 — exact. Yang atlas, from my own pseudobulk computation: P.Fibro 22.0 > M.Fibro 20.7 > Ependymal 15.2 > Pericyte 14.1 > SMC 11.1 — exact. EC/pericyte ratios check: 118.9/14.8 = 8.0 and 86.9/14.1 = 6.2, matching '6–8x'. HPA whole-body mural 11.9 vs endothelial 48.5 — exact. TWO CAVEATS: (i) the mouse comparison (pericytes ~46, FB2 ~38, EC/PC ~2–3x) rests entirely on the betsholtzlab per-cluster plot, which I could not access — the site's gene endpoint returns 404 — so the species-difference conclusion is unverified; my GSE52564 recomputation cannot substitute because that dataset contains no pericyte fraction. (ii) 'Unremarkable' undersells pericytes and VSMC in absolute terms: in the HPA brain atlas pericytes rank 5th and VSMC 7th of 34, above every one of the 21 neuronal superclusters. They are unremarkable only relative to endothelium.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Among non-endothelial barrier and perivascular cells in human brain, fibroblast-type cells rank highest (HPA fibroblast 23.2; Yang perivascular fibroblast 22.0, meningeal fibroblast 20.7 CPM), above ependyma (13.5 / 15.2), pericytes (14.8 / 14.1), vascular smooth muscle (13.3 / 11.1) and choroid plexus epithelium (8.8) — all 5–8x below endothelium. Pericytes and VSMC are modest relative to endothelium but still rank 5th and 7th of 34 cell types, above every neuronal supercluster. The claimed mouse-versus-human difference in the endothelium/pericyte ratio could not be verified, as the cited betsholtzlab per-gene resource was not reachable.

verdicts.claim: Descriptive, statistically untested observation from the Yang atlas: endothelial IFIH1 is modestly higher in Alzheimer's than control while microglial IFIH1 is lower; offered as hypothesis-generating, not as an MS result.
verdicts.reason: I reproduced the entire computation independently from the primary matrix and metadata. Splitting on the 'Treat' field gives Control n=72,371 and AD n=71,422, matching exactly. Every pseudobulk value matches to the decimal: Capillary 81.1 control vs 99.0 AD; Arterial 69.0 vs 88.1; Veinous 64.6 vs 74.1; Pericyte 13.1 vs 16.3; Astrocyte 10.0 vs 12.3; Oligo 9.2 vs 9.3; Microglia 51.5 vs 36.9. The arithmetic is therefore sound and the claim is honestly labelled — it self-rates 'low', states that no differential-expression test, donor-level pseudobulk or multiple-testing correction was performed, notes the original paper does not report IFIH1, and says 'Treat as unverified'. I am confirming the numbers, not an inference. Additional caveats worth carrying forward: cell-level pseudobulk without donor aggregation is pseudoreplication, so the direction could be driven by a small number of donors; the astrocyte and pericyte increases run parallel to the endothelial one, which is more consistent with a global ISG shift in AD tissue than an endothelium-specific effect; and the divergent microglial direction is unexplained. Most importantly for the question actually being asked, this is Alzheimer's, not multiple sclerosis.
verdicts.corrected_claim: As a purely descriptive, statistically untested pseudobulk computation on the Yang et al. Nature 2022 matrix (Control 72,371 vs AD 71,422 nuclei), IFIH1 CPM is higher in AD than control in capillary (81.1 to 99.0), arterial (69.0 to 88.1) and venous (64.6 to 74.1) endothelium, and also in pericytes (13.1 to 16.3) and astrocytes (10.0 to 12.3), while microglia run the other way (51.5 to 36.9). No differential-expression test, donor-level aggregation or multiple-testing correction was applied, the original paper does not report IFIH1, and the parallel rise across three unrelated cell types is as consistent with a global interferon shift in AD tissue as with an endothelial effect. This is Alzheimer's disease, carries no implication for multiple sclerosis, and must not be presented as a disease finding.

research.dimension: Why neurons are low in MDA5/IFIH1, what they use instead, and what the consequences are — neuronal RNA sensing, interferon hyporesponsiveness, and what IFIH1 gain-/loss-of-function disease reveals about which CNS cells sense dsRNA

findings.claim: In resting (uninfected) mouse cerebral cortex, Ifih1/MDA5 mRNA is low in EVERY CNS cell type, spanning only ~20-fold across cell types, with endothelial cells highest and neurons intermediate — neurons are NOT the lowest. Mean FPKM (n=2 replicates each): endothelial 2.06 > microglia/macrophage 0.54 > neurons 0.41 > OPC 0.22 > astrocytes 0.21 > myelinating oligodendrocytes 0.10 = newly-formed oligodendrocytes 0.10 (0.10 is the dataset floor).
findings.evidence: I downloaded and recomputed the primary FPKM matrix from brainrnaseq.org (https://brainrnaseq.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/fe-wp-dataset-120.csv), the immunopanned mouse cortex RNA-seq of Zhang et al. Cell-identity was verified in the same file: Snap25 neurons 116.1/177.2 FPKM, Cldn5 endothelial 3275.8/3598.2, Cx3cr1 microglia 473.2/506.2, Gfap astrocytes 107.3/146.6, Mbp myelinating oligodendrocyte 115330/75465. Comparator genes from the same matrix (mean FPKM, astro/endo/micro/myelOL/neuron/newOL/OPC): Ddx58 1.31/8.63/1.60/0.13/0.31/0.35/2.11; Dhx58 (LGP2) 0.34/0.61/1.65/0.16/0.13/0.22/0.26; Tmem173 (STING1) 2.78/12.80/136.72/0.58/0.29/0.29/4.77. Note MDA5's dynamic range across CNS cell types (20x) is trivial next to STING's (~470x), i.e. IFIH1 is not a lineage-defining gene in resting brain — it is an ISG whose level tracks ambient IFN tone.

findings.claim: The true neuronal bottleneck in the RLR pathway is not the MDA5 sensor itself but the obligate adaptor MAVS: neurons have the LOWEST Mavs of any cortical cell type, ~17-fold below microglia. This makes low neuronal MDA5 signalling a downstream-adaptor problem as much as a receptor-abundance problem.
findings.evidence: Same recomputed Zhang et al. mouse cortex matrix, mean FPKM: Mavs — microglia 14.25 > astrocytes 8.41 > OPC 6.65 > myelinating oligodendrocyte 6.35 > newly-formed oligodendrocyte 5.97 > endothelial 3.55 > neurons 0.82. Neurons are the only cortical cell type with Mavs below 1 FPKM, while every glial type exceeds 5.9 FPKM. By contrast Ifih1 in neurons (0.41) is ~2x ASTROCYTE level (0.21), so the receptor alone does not explain neuronal RLR hypofunction.

findings.claim: In human iPSC/NSC-derived CNS cells, neurons show minimal baseline expression of all four dsRNA sensors (IFIH1, DDX58, DHX58, TLR3), microglia show strong basal expression of all four, and astrocytes show moderate DDX58. The authors conclude neurons 'lack robust innate immune signalling pathways' relative to glia.
findings.evidence: Feige et al. compared human stem-cell-derived neurons (hiNeurons), astrocytes (hiAstrocytes) and iPSC-derived microglia (hiMicros) infected with rabies virus strain Tha vs attenuated Th2P-4M. Mock-infected baseline: microglia 'strong basal expression of innate immune receptors (IFIH1, DDX58, DHX58, and TLR3)'; neurons minimal across these genes; astrocytes moderate DDX58. Antiviral output likewise segregated: neurons/astrocytes IFNB1, CCL5, CXCL10, IL1B, IL6, LIF; microglia CCL5, CXCL10, ISG15, MX1, IL6. RABV replicated in neurons and astrocytes but FAILED to infect microglia. Caveat: expression reported as heatmaps, no per-gene fold-change numbers given; iPSC-derived cells are immature relative to adult human brain.

findings.claim: Human Protein Atlas classifies IFIH1 in human brain single-nuclei data as 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)' — i.e. the vascular compartment, not neurons or macroglia, is the IFIH1-enriched CNS cell type in humans, mirroring the mouse FPKM ranking.
findings.evidence: HPA gene page ENSG00000115267 (IFIH1): brain single-nuclei (Siletti et al. 2023) cluster specificity = 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)'; brain regional specificity = 'Low region specificity', 'Detected in all', human brain tau specificity score 0.21; highest regional value cervical spinal cord dorsal horn 16.7 nTPM. Bulk cerebral cortex nTPM: HPA consensus 2.7, HPA brain-specific dataset 6.9, GTEx 1.5. HPA nearest-neighbour cluster for IFIH1 in brain is populated by PARP9, IFI44L, OAS2, RSAD2 — i.e. it co-varies with the ISG module, not with a cell lineage. I could not extract per-cell-type nTPM values for brain nuclei from the HPA web interface or its search_download API.

findings.claim: CONFLICTING PROTEIN-LEVEL EVIDENCE: HPA immunohistochemistry of normal human cerebral cortex reports MDA5 staining as 'medium' in neuronal cells, 'low' in endothelial cells and 'not detected' in glial cells — the opposite rank order to the mRNA data. This IHC is low-reliability and should not be used to overturn the transcript data.
findings.evidence: HPA antibody HPA002656, cerebral cortex: neuronal cells medium, endothelial cells low, glial cells not detected, neuropil not detected. HPA's own reliability score for the IFIH1 IHC data is only 'Approved', and the page explicitly flags 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data'. A second fetch of the summary tissue page returned 'N/A' for protein scoring in several brain regions, so even the cortex call is not robust. Single-antibody, semi-quantitative, no orthogonal validation in brain. Treat as hypothesis-generating only: it does establish that MDA5 protein is not absent from human cortical neurons.

findings.claim: Neuronal MDA5 level is subtype-specific, not uniformly low: cerebellar granule cell neurons have constitutively HIGHER basal Ifih1 and Ddx58 (plus Ifit1, Ifit3, Oas, Mx1, Irf7, Bst2, Unc93b1, Ikbke, Stat1) than cortical neurons, and this basal ISG tone determines which neurons survive West Nile virus. This is the single best-established demonstration that 'neurons are low in MDA5' is a statement about a neuronal subtype average, not about neurons as a class.
findings.evidence: Cho, Proll, Szretter, Katze, Gale & Diamond. Microarray of primary mouse cerebellar granule cell neurons (GCN) vs cortical neurons (CN) (Supplementary Table 2) listed Ifih1 and Ddx58 among the basally elevated ISGs in GCN. GCN were correspondingly more resistant to WNV and other positive-strand RNA viruses. Mechanism: derepressing ISGs in cortical neurons with the HDAC inhibitor trichostatin A reduced WNV yield 5-fold (P < 0.0001); miR-132 was significantly higher in cortical neurons than GCN (P < 0.01) and ectopic miR-132 in GCN lowered basal ISG expression. Human autopsy WNV material corroborated relative sparing of granule cell neurons. Caveat: I could not retrieve numeric per-gene fold differences for Ifih1/Ddx58 from the accessible text — the paper reports them via the supplementary table, and validation focused on other ISGs.

findings.claim: Neuronal IFIH1/MDA5 IS strongly inducible by infection, but the induction is weaker and shorter-lived than in astrocytes from the same human culture. This is the clearest head-to-head human neuron-vs-astrocyte number set available.
findings.evidence: Pathological model of tick-borne encephalitis virus (TBEV) in human neuron/astrocyte cultures (Table 1, Fig. 7), fold-change at 24 hours post-infection: IFIH1 — unsorted 32.7, enriched neurons 19.7, enriched astrocytes 35.3. DDX58 — unsorted 10.5, neurons 5.7, astrocytes 16.0. TLR3 — unsorted 6.2, neurons 1.7, astrocytes 6.4. At 72 hpi astrocyte antiviral genes stayed elevated or rose further while neuronal expression was 'maintained or decreased'; 'the antiviral program was of greater intensity and longer duration in human astrocytes than in human neurons'. Astrocytes selectively induced viperin and TRIM5α (ISGs controlling TBEV); neurons did not. PKR/EIF2AK2 was not reported.

findings.claim: Human neuronal cells possess functional, IFN-inducible RIG-I, MDA5 and TLR3 pathways; RIG-I rises with neuronal differentiation whereas MDA5 does not, so the two RLRs are regulated differently in maturing neurons.
findings.evidence: Peltier, Simms, Farmer & Miller, in BE(2)-C (± retinoic-acid differentiation to BE(2)-C/m), SH-SY5Y, HCN-1A human cortical neuronal cells and primary rat E18 cortical neurons: 'RIG-I expression increased with BE(2)-C differentiation' (Fig 3C lanes 1-2) while 'MDA5 expression levels were independent of differentiation'; both RIG-I and MDA5 increased after type I IFN in human BE(2)-C and primary rat neurons (Fig 3C lanes 3-4, 6). TLR3 showed punctate cytoplasmic/endosomal distribution (Fig 3B). Important caveat: the paper reports no numeric baseline levels, no numeric fold-inductions and no comparison against non-neuronal cells, so it establishes presence and inducibility but NOT that neuronal levels are high.

findings.claim: Additional independent confirmations that MDA5 and RIG-I are induced in human neuronal cells by picornavirus and flavivirus infection.
findings.evidence: (1) JEV in SK-N-MC human neuronal cells (Affymetrix): 1316 dysregulated genes at 48 hpi and 2737 at 60 hpi (≥2/−2 fold, P<0.05); RIG-I and MDA5 were among the upregulated PRRs; most-upregulated genes (≥10-fold, P<0.05) were CCL5, CXCL11, IL8, CXCL10. (2) Coxsackievirus B3 in human neural progenitor cells (QuantSeq 3' mRNA-seq): increased RIG-I and MDA5 plus IFN-β, IP-10, ISG15, OAS1, OAS2, Mx2; IFN-γ downregulated. Neither paper reports numeric fold-change specifically for IFIH1.

findings.claim: DECISIVE NEGATIVE: neuronal MDA5 is functionally dispensable for cell-autonomous control of West Nile virus. MDA5-deficient mice die of WNV, but the defect is entirely non-cell-autonomous (CD8+ T cell priming outside the CNS) — MDA5 loss had no effect on WNV in primary cortical OR cerebellar neuron cultures, and no effect after intracranial inoculation.
findings.evidence: Lazear et al. MDA5−/− vs WT after peripheral WNV: day 10 post-infection 140-fold higher brain viral burden and 21-fold higher spinal cord burden (both P < 0.01); mortality 92% (MDA5−/−) vs 53% (WT). But 'no differences in infection between WT and MDA5−/− mice' after intracranial injection, and 'an absence of MDA5 did not impact WNV infection in primary cortical or cerebellar neuron cultures.' Adoptive transfer localised the requirement to MDA5 shaping CD8+ T cell priming.

findings.claim: SECOND DECISIVE NEGATIVE, in vivo and genetic: cell-type-restricted deletion of MAVS shows that RLR (RIG-I/MDA5) signalling is required in brain-resident MYELOID cells (microglia) — not in neurons and not in astrocytes — for protection against a neurotropic RNA virus.
findings.evidence: Pavlou, Ghita et al. deleted MAVS selectively in neurons, astrocytes, or long-lived myeloid cells and infected intranasally with VSV. 'RLR signaling specifically within brain-resident myeloid cells is crucial for protection against the virus.' Myeloid-MAVS-deficient mice had normal leukocyte infiltration but P2RY12+ microglia showed aberrant antigen cross-presentation gene expression, diminished surface MHC class I by flow cytometry, and CNS-infiltrating CD8+ T cells had dysfunctional transcriptional profiles. Neuron- and astrocyte-specific MAVS deletion did not produce the protective defect.

findings.claim: Consistent with low neuronal RLR-MAVS output, in vivo IFN-β reporter mice show that astrocytes (and microglia) are the CNS interferon-β producers during neurotropic viral infection, while virus-infected neurons essentially never produce detectable IFN-β.
findings.evidence: Kallfass et al., IFN-β promoter-driven firefly luciferase conditional reporter mice infected with La Crosse virus: double-staining with cell-type markers showed similar numbers of astrocytes and microglia were luciferase-positive, 'whereas virus-infected neurons rarely contained detectable levels of luciferase'; with an NSs-deficient (IFN-antagonist-null) LACV mutant the great majority of IFN-β producers were astrocytes. Pfefferkorn et al. extended this across rabies virus, Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus and VSV, concluding abortively infected astrocytes are the main brain source of IFN-β.

findings.claim: The same cell-type logic holds for the DNA-sensing arm: cGAS-STING antiviral sensing in the brain is a microglial function, STING is redundant for cell-autonomous resistance in neurons and astrocytes, and microglia instead transfer an antiviral state to neurons. Sting1/Tmem173 mRNA in mouse cortex is ~470-fold higher in microglia than neurons.
findings.evidence: Reinert et al. (HSV-1, Nat Commun 2016): microglia are the CNS cGAS-STING sensor orchestrating antiviral defence; STING was redundant for cell-autonomous antiviral resistance in astrocytes and neurons; HSV-1-infected microglia transferred antiviral activity to neurons in a STING-dependent manner. Quantitatively matching this, my recomputed Zhang et al. mouse cortex FPKM: Tmem173 microglia 136.72 vs neurons 0.29 (endothelial 12.80, OPC 4.77, astrocytes 2.78).

findings.claim: The dsRNA sensor that IS non-redundant in human CNS neurons is TLR3, not MDA5. TLR3- or UNC93B1-deficient iPSC-derived neurons and oligodendrocytes are selectively susceptible to HSV-1; NSCs and astrocytes from the same patients are not. This is the human-genetic basis of herpes simplex encephalitis.
findings.evidence: Lafaille et al., iPSCs from TLR3- and UNC-93B-deficient HSE patients differentiated to purified NSCs, neurons, astrocytes and oligodendrocytes. mRNA for TLR3 and UNC93B1 was detected in all four cell types. IFN-β and IFN-λ1 induction after HSV-1 was impaired selectively in UNC-93B-deficient neurons and oligodendrocytes, and those two cell types showed faster, higher HSV-1-GFP replication; UNC-93B-deficient NSCs and astrocytes replicated virus like controls. TLR3-deficient neurons were likewise susceptible. The paper reports NO expression data for DDX58 or IFIH1, and comparisons are qualitative ('higher levels', 'greatly impaired') rather than numeric titers. A follow-up showed iPSC-derived trigeminal neurons lack the constitutive TLR3-dependent immunity that protects cortical neurons (I could not fetch its full text; PNAS 403).

findings.claim: COUNTERWEIGHT — human MDA5 deficiency DOES cause CNS disease: a child homozygous for a loss-of-function IFIH1 variant (c.1641+1G>C) developed enterovirus-30 rhombencephalitis, in the same study that reported TLR3 deficiency in an EV71 rhombencephalitis patient. TLR3 and MDA5 emerge as the paired non-redundant dsRNA sensors for human CNS enterovirus control, acting at different phases.
findings.evidence: Chen, Jing, Bastard, Abel, Su, Casanova, Zhang et al. Two unrelated children with EV30 and EV71 rhombencephalitis: one with compound heterozygous TLR3 (LOF F322fs2* + hypomorphic D280N), one homozygous IFIH1 c.1641+1G>C LOF. Patient fibroblasts responded poorly to extracellular (TLR3) or intracellular (MDA5) poly(I:C). Baseline IFN-β was low in the TLR3 patient; EV-responsive IFN-β was low in the MDA5 patient. EV growth was enhanced at EARLY timepoints in TLR3-deficient and at LATE timepoints in MDA5-deficient fibroblasts. Pre-infection IFN-α2b rescued both; post-infection IFN-α2b fully rescued only MDA5-deficient cells. WT TLR3 or MDA5 expression rescued both phenotypes. Caveat: all mechanistic work was in patient FIBROBLASTS, not neurons — the CNS localisation of the requirement was not established at cellular resolution.

findings.claim: Neurons are genuinely interferon-hyporesponsive at the signalling level: they carry lower basal STAT1 and STAT2 and show muted, delayed STAT1 activation, yet paradoxically carry HIGHER basal type I IFN transcript levels than fibroblasts. So low neuronal ISG (including IFIH1) tone reflects blunted JAK-STAT amplification, not absent IFN.
findings.evidence: Cavanaugh, Holmgren & Rall (J Neuroimmunol 2015): 7 of 12 type I IFN genes were expressed significantly HIGHER at RNA level in primary mouse hippocampal neurons than in MEFs (Fig 4B); 'primary neurons have a lower homeostatic expression of Stat1 than control fibroblasts' and basal Stat2 was also lower; Oas1a and Isg15 were 'highly induced in MEF, whereas neuronal expression of these genes was negligible'; neuronal Stat2 phosphorylation was sustained through 24 h vs transient in fibroblasts. The 2026 review by Bunkofske & Hunter summarises the field: neurons show 'significantly lower levels of STAT1/2 activation, reduced expression of antiviral response genes', and IFNGR1 transcripts are 8-fold lower in primary hippocampal neurons than MEFs. The same review states cortical neurons DO use MDA5/RIG-I to respond to poly(I:C) (citing PMID 23503326) and RIG-I to detect JEV (PMID 21738791). Note: neither paper reports basal Ddx58/Ifih1/Tlr3 levels in neurons.

findings.claim: FUNCTIONAL RATIONALE with direct evidence: neurons substitute a non-lytic defence (autophagy) for the IFN/ISG program, because many ISG effector pathways are cytotoxic and neurons are post-mitotic and irreplaceable.
findings.evidence: Yordy, Gao, Gonzalez & Iwasaki: mouse dorsal root ganglion neurons produced little type I IFN in response to HSV-1 and required autophagy to limit HSV-1 replication both in vitro and in vivo; mucosal epithelial cells and other mitotic cells responded robustly to type I IFN and did NOT require autophagy. Post-mitotic primary neurons predominantly use autophagy over interferon as the viral control mechanism, in contrast to MEFs and keratinocytes.

findings.claim: IFIH1 GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (AGS7 / Singleton-Merten) causes severe CNS disease in humans, establishing that unrestrained MDA5 signalling is neurotoxic — but the phenotype is dominated by cerebral arteriopathy and white matter injury, and on autopsy the calcification is confined to CNS ARTERY walls and perivascular space, with NO neuronal ferrugination. This is consistent with the vascular/endothelial compartment being the IFIH1-high CNS compartment.
findings.evidence: Neuropathology of a 16-year-old boy with IFIH1-related AGS (Gilani, Adang, Vanderver, Kleinschmidt-DeMasters): microcephaly, brain weight 916 g, relatively mild gross atrophy; 'multifocal calcifications limited to small to medium central nervous system arteries (no evidence of calcification in other organs), involving bilateral cerebral cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus, and cerebellum'; ultrastructure showed calcospherules 'limited to the vessel walls and the perivascular area without evidence of neuronal ferrugination or tubuloreticular bodies'; critically, 'the extent of calcifications was variable across different brain regions... and correlated with the extent of IFIH1 protein expression (data derived from Allen Brain Institute).' Only the second such autopsy reported.

findings.claim: The IFIH1 GOF clinical spectrum (74 individuals, 51 families, 27 variants) is neurologically dominated but with striking incomplete penetrance, showing that MDA5 hyperactivity in the CNS is necessary but not sufficient for disease.
findings.evidence: Rice et al. 2014 Nat Genet identified IFIH1 GOF causing AGS7 and a spectrum of IFN-upregulated phenotypes; mutant MDA5 binds RNA more avidly and increases both baseline and ligand-induced IFN signalling. Rice et al. 2020 Hum Mutat cohort: 74 individuals / 51 families / 27 distinct mutations (41 previously unreported); phenotypes include classical AGS, spastic paraparesis, spastic-dystonic syndrome, rapid neuroregression in ~1/3 of symptomatic carriers (7 cases with onset after age 1 despite prior normal development), Singleton-Merten syndrome, white matter disease and intracranial calcification (frequent but sometimes absent despite neurological disease). 10/74 (13.5%) asymptomatic carriers, 7 of them over age 50. 26 of 27 mutations associated with elevated ISG expression; 109/117 samples from 51 patients were IFN-signature-positive; 16 samples from 7 clinically non-penetrant subjects still had upregulated IFN signalling. Note: this is peripheral blood ISG data — the cohort papers give NO CNS cell-type localisation. Separately, the recurrent R822Q variant causes both Singleton-Merten syndrome (Rutsch 2015) and, in a 6-year-old boy, bilateral spasticity, developmental delay and basal ganglia calcification (Buers 2017).

findings.claim: In the ADAR1-mutant mouse model of AGS — where MDA5 is the sensor being inappropriately triggered by unedited self-dsRNA — the CNS cells that mount the ISG response are neurons, microglia, ependyma, choroid plexus and endothelial cells, with LITTLE ISG expression in oligodendroglia and astrocytes (except STAT1). Neurons are therefore fully capable ISG responders in vivo.
findings.evidence: Wiley, Steinman & Wang, double-label in situ hybridization in ADAR1-mutant mice. From 2 weeks of age, distinct CNS cell lineages expressed very high levels of distinct ISGs in the absence of detectable interferon and without immune cell infiltrates. 'Within the CNS aberrant ISG expression was mostly limited to neurons, microglia, ependyma, choroid plexus, and endothelial cells with little expression in oligodendroglia and astrocytes except for STAT1.' Ventricular dilatation and deep grey matter mineralization appeared at 8-13 months but did not spatially track ISG expression. Note this partly conflicts with the astrocyte-centric human AGS literature (van Heteren et al., post-mortem AGS brain: astrocytes — not infiltrating leukocytes — were the source of IFN-α and CXCL10).

findings.claim: DIRECT GENETIC PROOF THAT NEURONAL MDA5 IS FUNCTIONAL: neuron-specific Adar1 deletion in mice causes elevated type I ISGs, choroid plexus/ependymal hypoplasia with ventricular obstruction and gliosis, and early postnatal lethality — and deleting MDA5 largely NORMALIZES the ISG expression and ameliorates the ventricular obstruction. Low neuronal MDA5 is therefore low, not null, and is sufficient to drive an interferonopathy.
findings.evidence: Todo, Yang, Nakahama & Kawahara (J Neuroinflammation 2026): neuron-specific deletion of Adar1 (both p110 and p150) caused early postnatal lethality with elevated type I ISGs and ventricular obstruction from choroid plexus/ependymal hypoplasia plus gliosis. 'Both selective restoration of ADAR1 p150 function and deletion of MDA5 largely normalized type I ISG expression and ameliorated ventricular obstruction but failed to rescue early postnatal lethality.' Corroborating this, Yoo et al. (Cell Rep 2026) showed neuron- OR astrocyte-specific ADAR1 dysfunction each 'evoked robust ISG expression and recapitulated AGS-like encephalopathy, with astrocytic dysfunction causing particularly severe effects'; microglial elimination only partially alleviated encephalopathy without suppressing ISGs; blocking type I IFN signalling fully reversed the abnormalities whereas deleting PKR or ZBP1 did not; CSF IFN-α exceeded serum levels.

findings.claim: In brain, PKR (EIF2AK2) is a genuinely separable, MDA5/MAVS-independent dsRNA effector: when the MDA5-MAVS axis is already deleted, aberrant brain ISG protein expression and microgliosis persist and are rescued only by additionally removing PKR.
findings.evidence: Lacovich et al. (Brain 2026): Adar Mavs double-mutant mice (MAVS removed, so MDA5 signalling is abolished) still showed upregulated ISG-encoded proteins by mass spectrometry and aberrant microgliosis in brain at postnatal days 8 and 14; both were prevented in Adar Mavs Eif2ak2 triple mutants, 'indicating the key role of aberrant PKR activation'. The authors attribute the residual brain IFN response 'probably... to reactive microglia and astrocytes'. Caveat against over-reading a neuron-PKR story: in my recomputed Zhang et al. mouse cortex FPKM, Eif2ak2 is LOW in neurons (0.36) vs astrocytes (4.54) and endothelial (4.30), so PKR mRNA abundance does not itself mark neurons; and Yoo et al. found PKR deletion did NOT rescue their Z-RNA-binding-deficient Adar1 encephalopathy.

findings.claim: Neurons also sit at the bottom of the CNS ranking for the receptor and transducer that set ISG (and hence IFIH1) tone — IFNAR1 and STAT1 — giving a mechanistic reason why a cell with only modestly low basal IFIH1 mRNA ends up functionally MDA5-poor.
findings.evidence: Recomputed Zhang et al. mouse cortex mean FPKM: Ifnar1 — endothelial 65.23 > microglia 24.77 > astrocytes 13.95 > OPC 12.93 > neurons 7.60 > newly-formed oligodendrocyte 5.93 > myelinating oligodendrocyte 3.84 (neurons ~8.6x below endothelium, ~3.3x below microglia). Stat1 — endothelial 7.84 > OPC 6.77 > microglia 4.30 > newly-formed oligodendrocyte 3.98 > astrocytes 2.02 > myelinating oligodendrocyte 1.72 > neurons 1.57 (neurons lowest). Because IFIH1 is itself an ISG (Kang et al. originally defined mda-5 as an early-response gene induced by IFN, responding predominantly to IFN-β, with transcriptional control by IFN-β), a cell with the lowest IFNAR1 and STAT1 will hold the lowest inducible MDA5 ceiling.

findings.claim: NOTABLE ABSENCE: published Ifih1 gain-of-function knock-in mouse models do not reproduce the AGS brain phenotype. Their reported disease is lupus-like (kidney, skin), hepatic calcification and Singleton-Merten-like bony abnormalities — no AGS-like encephalopathy is described.
findings.evidence: Funabiki et al. (Immunity 2014) Ifih1 GOF mice developed an SLE-like phenotype with spontaneous kidney and skin inflammation and liver calcification, with increased type I IFN; Ifih1:Ifnar1 double-deficient mice showed partial amelioration of kidney pathology. Ifih1 G821S/+ knock-in mice show Singleton-Merten-like bony abnormalities, reversed by loss of IFNAR or MAVS. I found no report of intracranial calcification, white matter disease or neuroregression in these models. This means the cell-of-origin of IFIH1-GOF CNS disease in humans has NOT been established genetically in any model — it is currently inferred only from human neuropathology and from ADAR1-driven surrogates in which MDA5 is downstream.

research.cell_type_ranking: Yes — this angle informs the ranking, and it corrects a likely naive assumption. (1) BASELINE, healthy CNS, mRNA: neurons are NOT the lowest IFIH1 cell type, and the whole CNS is IFIH1-low. Recomputed mouse cortex FPKM (Zhang et al. 2014, PMID 25186741) gives endothelial 2.06 > microglia 0.54 > NEURONS 0.41 > OPC 0.22 > astrocytes 0.21 > oligodendrocytes 0.10 (floor). Total spread is only ~20-fold, versus ~470-fold for STING (Tmem173: microglia 136.72 vs neurons 0.29) — so IFIH1 is not a lineage marker in resting brain, it is an ISG tracking ambient IFN tone. Human data agree on the top of the ranking: Human Protein Atlas classifies IFIH1 in human brain single nuclei as 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)'. So the defensible baseline ranking for CNS IFIH1 is: ENDOTHELIAL/VASCULAR > MICROGLIA > neurons ≈ astrocytes ≈ OPC > oligodendrocytes. (2) But neurons ARE the lowest for the rest of the RLR axis — MAVS neurons 0.82 vs microglia 14.25 (~17x), DDX58 neurons 0.31 vs endothelial 8.63 (~28x), DHX58/LGP2 neurons 0.13 (lowest of all seven types), plus lowest STAT1 (1.57) and low IFNAR1 (7.60). So a ranking built on MDA5 *pathway competence* rather than IFIH1 transcript alone puts neurons at the bottom. (3) Human iPSC-derived CNS cells rank neurons lowest for basal IFIH1/DDX58/DHX58/TLR3 with microglia highest (PMID 36680128), which favours the pathway-competence ranking for human cells and argues that the modest neuronal Ifih1 FPKM in mouse is not a rebuttal. (4) Within neurons the ranking is subtype-dependent: cerebellar granule neurons > cortical neurons for basal Ifih1/Ddx58 (PMID 23455712) — any single 'neuron' bin averages over a real 2-tier structure. (5) One conflicting datum to log rather than bury: HPA IHC (antibody HPA002656, reliability only 'Approved', with an explicit 'low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data' flag) scores MDA5 protein as medium in human cortical neuronal cells, low in endothelial and NOT DETECTED in glia — the inverse ranking. It should not override the transcript data but it does forbid stating that neurons lack MDA5 protein. (6) Finally, in the IFIH1-AGS autopsy the regional extent of calcification 'correlated with the extent of IFIH1 protein expression (Allen Brain Institute data)' and the lesions were confined to small-to-medium artery walls and perivascular space with no neuronal ferrugination (PMID 30952201) — independent human pathology support for the vascular compartment sitting at the top of the CNS IFIH1 ranking.
research.gaps: 1) NO HUMAN MS DATA. This angle produced zero evidence on IFIH1/MDA5 in multiple sclerosis lesions or in any MS CNS cell type. Nothing here should be used to answer the MS half of the question; that must come from the GSE180759 analysis or an MS-specific angle. 2) NO PER-CELL-TYPE HUMAN BRAIN nTPM FOR IFIH1.
