I could not extract numeric single-nucleus values for human excitatory/inhibitory neurons, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes, OPCs or endothelium from HPA's web pages or its search_download API (it returns only the 'Cell type enhanced' label), brainrnaseq.org's human dataset (fe-wp-dataset-124.csv returned HTTP 504 on four attempts), or the GTEx v2 API (medianGeneExpression returned an empty data array for ENSG00000115267 with and without a version suffix). The only hard per-cell-type numbers I obtained are MOUSE (Zhang et al. 2014 FPKM). Someone should pull Siletti et al. 2023 or Allen Brain Map human snRNA-seq directly for human values. 3) NO NUMERIC Ifih1 FOLD-DIFFERENCE for cerebellar granule vs cortical neurons — Cho et al. report it via Supplementary Table 2, which I could not retrieve; the numeric validation in the accessible text covers other ISGs. 4) NO PROTEIN-LEVEL QUANTIFICATION of MDA5 in any CNS cell type. No western blot or validated IHC comparing MDA5 protein in neurons vs microglia vs astrocytes vs endothelium exists in what I found; the only protein-level brain datum is a low-reliability single-antibody HPA IHC that contradicts the mRNA ranking. 5) NO MDA5 CELL-OF-ORIGIN EXPERIMENT FOR IFIH1-GOF CNS DISEASE. Published Ifih1 GOF knock-in mice (Funabiki 2014; G821S) show lupus-like, hepatic and bony phenotypes with no reported AGS-like encephalopathy, and no conditional/cell-type-restricted Ifih1 GOF mouse exists in what I found. Which CNS cell's MDA5 drives AGS7 is therefore inferred, not demonstrated. 6) UNRESOLVED CONFLICT on the AGS effector cell: Wiley et al. (PMID 36161399) localise CNS ISG expression in ADAR1-mutant mice mostly to neurons, microglia, ependyma, choroid plexus and endothelium with little in astrocytes, whereas human AGS post-mortem (van Heteren, PMID 18240301) and Yoo et al. (PMID 41855203) put astrocytes at the centre. Not reconciled. 7) PKR IN NEURONS IS NOT ESTABLISHED as the neuronal substitute sensor: Eif2ak2 mRNA is actually low in mouse cortical neurons (0.36 FPKM vs 4.54 in astrocytes), the PKR-rescue result (PMID 40920008) does not resolve cell type, and Yoo et al. found PKR deletion did not rescue their model. I found no study demonstrating that PKR is the dominant dsRNA sensor specifically in neurons. 8) NO NUMERIC IFIH1 FOLD-CHANGE for human neurons after pure IFN exposure (as opposed to infection) — Peltier et al. show IFN-inducibility of MDA5 in human neuronal cells only by blot, with no quantification. 9) THREE SOURCES WERE INACCESSIBLE and their numbers are missing here: PNAS 10.1073/pnas.1809853115 (trigeminal vs cortical neuron constitutive TLR3), mSphere 10.1128/msphere.00270-21 (SARS-CoV-2/H5N1 iPSC neural models), and the Cell Reports full text of PMID 41855203 — all returned HTTP 403.

verdicts.claim: Claim 1: Resting mouse cortex Ifih1 low in every CNS cell type, ~20-fold range, endothelial highest, neurons intermediate and NOT lowest. Mean FPKM endo 2.06 > micro 0.54 > neurons 0.41 > OPC 0.22 > astro 0.21 > myelOL 0.10 = newOL 0.10.
verdicts.reason: I re-downloaded the CSV and recomputed independently: every number matches to 2 d.p. (endo 2.06, micro 0.54, neuron 0.41, OPC 0.22, astro 0.21, OLs 0.10; range 20.6x). Cell-identity markers reproduce exactly (Snap25 146.7, Cldn5 3437.0, Cx3cr1 489.7, Gfap 126.9, Mbp 95397.5), as do all comparator genes (Ddx58, Dhx58, Tmem173) and STING's 476x range. BUT the rank order among low expressers is NOT robust at n=2: neuron replicates are 0.146 and 0.678, a 4.65-fold spread. In replicate 1 neurons (0.146) rank 5th of 7, BELOW astrocytes (0.293) and OPC (0.326); in replicate 2 they rank 2nd. So 'neurons > OPC > astrocytes' and 'neurons are NOT the lowest' rest on a single replicate. Two further caveats the claim omits: cells were purified at postnatal day 7 (neurons/astro/endo) and P17 (oligodendrocyte lineage), i.e. developing brain with cell types compared across different ages, not adult 'resting cortex'; and the paper explicitly sets an FPKM floor of 0.1 ('chose a more conservative FPKM threshold of 0.1'), so the two OL values are censored and the ~20-fold span is a lower bound.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In immunopanned/FACS-purified mouse cerebral cortex at P7 (P17 for oligodendrocyte lineage) from Zhang et al. 2014, Ifih1 mRNA is low in all CNS cell types (mean FPKM: endothelial 2.06, microglia/macrophage 0.54, neurons 0.41, OPC 0.22, astrocytes 0.21, both oligodendrocyte populations 0.10 = the dataset's imposed floor). Endothelial cells are robustly highest (both replicates ~2.0-2.1) and oligodendrocytes are at the detection floor. The dynamic range is at least ~20-fold but is floor-censored. Neurons are not at the floor, but their exact rank among the other low expressers is unresolved: with n=2 the neuronal replicates differ 4.65-fold (0.146 vs 0.678) and neurons fall below astrocytes and OPC in one of the two replicates. The key robust contrast stands: MDA5's cell-type range in resting brain (~20x) is far narrower than STING/Tmem173's (~476x), consistent with IFIH1 being an ISG rather than a lineage-defining gene.

verdicts.claim: Claim 2: Neurons have the LOWEST Mavs of any cortical cell type, ~17-fold below microglia; neuronal RLR limitation is an adaptor problem as much as a receptor problem.
verdicts.reason: Independently recomputed from the same file: Mavs means match exactly (microglia 14.25 > astro 8.41 > OPC 6.65 > myelOL 6.35 > newOL 5.97 > endo 3.55 > neurons 0.82; 14.25/0.82 = 17.4x). Unlike Ifih1, this ranking IS replicate-robust: neuron replicates are 0.614 and 1.021, both far below the next-lowest cell type's minimum (endothelial 3.428), and every glial replicate exceeds 5.8. Neurons are indeed the only cortical cell type below 1 FPKM in both replicates.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated, with scope caveats. In P7/P17 mouse cortex (Zhang et al. 2014, n=2 pooled replicates, mRNA only), neurons have the lowest Mavs of any cortical cell type (0.82 FPKM mean; replicates 0.614 and 1.021), ~17-fold below microglia (14.25) and below every other cell type in both replicates — a robust ranking. The inference that this makes neuronal RLR hypofunction an adaptor-level constraint is reasonable but is a transcript-abundance argument only; no protein or functional MAVS measurement is involved. The supporting sub-claim that neuronal Ifih1 is ~2x astrocyte level inherits the replicate fragility described in claim 1 and should not be relied on.

verdicts.claim: Claim 3: In human iPSC/NSC-derived CNS cells, neurons show minimal baseline expression of IFIH1, DDX58, DHX58, TLR3; microglia strong basal expression of all four; astrocytes moderate DDX58. Authors conclude neurons 'lack robust innate immune signalling pathways'.
verdicts.reason: The microglia quote is verbatim: 'hiMicros present a strong basal expression of innate immune receptors (IFIH1, DDX58, DHX58, and TLR3)'. RABV tropism and the antiviral-output gene lists are verbatim. But three inaccuracies: (1) the astrocytes in the basal qPCR comparison are 'commercially purchased foetal pAstrocytes' (primary fetal astrocytes), NOT the hiAstrocytes the claim names — the claim conflates two different preparations; (2) the paper says astrocytes showed 'a STRONG expression of the RLR DDX58', not 'moderate'; (3) 'neurons lack robust innate immune signalling pathways' appears in the Discussion as a summary of prior literature with citations [48,49] ('recent evidence suggests that...'), not as the authors' own conclusion from their data. Data are qPCR in Figure S5A, not heatmaps as the claim states.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Feige et al. (Viruses 2023, PMID 36680128) report by qPCR that iPSC-derived microglia (hiMicros) show 'strong basal expression of innate immune receptors (IFIH1, DDX58, DHX58, and TLR3)', while commercially sourced foetal primary astrocytes show strong basal DDX58 and hNSC-derived hiNeurons show little of these receptors (Fig. S5A, no per-gene numbers given). RABV replicated in hiNeurons and hiAstrocytes but failed to infect hiMicros. Antiviral output segregated as the claim states. The sentence 'neurons lack robust innate immune signalling pathways' is the authors' framing of prior literature in the Discussion, not a conclusion from their own data. Also relevant and omitted: hiNeurons responded poorly to IFN-alpha overall, with only DDX58, ISG15 and MX1 modestly modulated — IFIH1 was not among the IFN-alpha-inducible genes in neurons — and the authors attribute this to low neuronal IFNAR1/IFNAR2 (Fig. S8). All cells are immature in vitro preparations.

verdicts.claim: Claim 4: HPA classifies IFIH1 in human brain single-nuclei data as 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)'.
verdicts.reason: I fetched all three HPA pages. Brain single-nuclei (Siletti et al. 2023) cluster specificity is indeed 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)'. Brain page confirms 'Low region specificity', 'Detected in all', human brain tau 0.21, and 'Highest expression in Cervical spinal cord, dorsal horn: 16.7 nTPM'. Cerebral cortex page confirms Consensus 2.7 nTPM and HPA Brain 6.9 nTPM. My own attempts to extract per-cell-type brain nTPM also failed, corroborating the claim's stated limitation.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. HPA classifies IFIH1 (ENSG00000115267) in human brain single-nuclei data (Siletti et al. 2023) as 'Cell type enhanced (Endothelial cell)', with 'Low region specificity', 'Detected in all', brain tau 0.21, highest regional value cervical spinal cord dorsal horn 16.7 nTPM, and bulk cortex 2.7 nTPM (consensus) / 6.9 nTPM (HPA brain). Three caveats worth attaching: this rests on a single snRNA-seq dataset; HPA's 'Cell type enhanced' is a weak-specificity category (the cross-tissue call for IFIH1 is 'Cell type enhanced (Neutrophils, Late spermatids, Early spermatids)', tau 0.47); and the statement that this 'mirrors the mouse FPKM ranking' is the investigator's cross-species inference, not an HPA finding. Per-cell-type brain nTPM values are not extractable from the public interface.

verdicts.claim: Claim 5: HPA IHC of normal human cerebral cortex reports MDA5 'medium' in neuronal cells, 'low' in endothelial, 'not detected' in glial — opposite to mRNA; low-reliability, should not overturn transcript data.
verdicts.reason: All four staining calls verified on the cerebral cortex page (neuronal medium, endothelial low, glial not detected, neuropil not detected), antibody HPA002656. The summary tissue page confirms reliability 'Approved' and the explicit flag 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data'. The claim's self-limiting framing is appropriate and unusually well-calibrated.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate, with one clause softened. HPA antibody HPA002656 in cerebral cortex scores neuronal cells medium, endothelial cells low, glial cells not detected, neuropil not detected — the inverse of the mRNA ranking. HPA's reliability score for IFIH1 protein data is only 'Approved' and the atlas explicitly flags 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data'. Single antibody, semi-quantitative, no orthogonal brain validation. The final clause should be weakened: this is consistent with MDA5 protein being present in human cortical neurons, but a single antibody the atlas itself flags as discordant with RNA cannot establish it.

verdicts.claim: Claim 6: Cerebellar granule cell neurons have constitutively higher basal Ifih1/Ddx58 and other ISGs than cortical neurons, and this basal ISG tone determines which neurons survive WNV.
verdicts.reason: Verified against the paper: 'Genes associated with canonical PRR signaling through TLR and RLR pathways (for example, Tlr7, Ddx58 (also called Rig-I) and Ifih1 (also called Mda5))...were expressed at higher levels in granule cell neurons at the basal level', and the antiviral gene list matches the claim's list verbatim (Ifit1, Ifit3, Oas, Mx1, Irf7, Bst2, Unc93b1, Ifih1, Ddx58, Ikbke, Stat1). Trichostatin A 'reduced viral yields (fivefold, P < 0.0001)' verified; miR-132 higher in cortical neurons P < 0.01 verified; human autopsy verified verbatim ('granule cell neurons were relatively spared from WNV replication compared to other neuronal populations'). Primary neurons were mouse. The claim's own caveat that numeric per-gene fold differences for Ifih1/Ddx58 are not in the accessible text is honest — I could not retrieve them either.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Cho et al. (Nat Med 2013, PMID 23455712) report that mouse primary cerebellar granule cell neurons express Ifih1 and Ddx58, among a broader basal ISG module, at higher levels than cortical neurons, and are correspondingly more resistant to WNV; TSA derepression of cortical neuron ISGs cut WNV yield fivefold (P < 0.0001); miR-132 was higher in cortical neurons (P < 0.01) and suppressed basal ISGs when expressed ectopically in GCN; human WNV autopsy showed relative sparing of granule cell neurons. No numeric per-gene fold-difference for Ifih1 or Ddx58 is retrievable from the main text. Two scope limits on the interpretive headline: the mechanistic work is mouse primary culture, and the paper establishes relative differences BETWEEN neuronal subtypes — it does not show that granule-cell MDA5 is high in absolute terms or relative to glia.

verdicts.claim: Claim 7: Neuronal IFIH1 is strongly inducible by infection but the induction is weaker and shorter-lived than in astrocytes from the same human culture; clearest head-to-head human neuron-vs-astrocyte number set.
verdicts.reason: Every number is exact and appears in Table 1 (IFIH1 32.7/19.7/35.3; DDX58 10.5/5.7/16.0; TLR3 6.2/1.7/6.4), the array timepoint is confirmed as 24 hpi, and 'the antiviral program... was of greater intensity and longer duration in human astrocytes than in human neurons' is verbatim. But the framing overstates: the 'enriched astrocyte' fraction is only 53.5% astrocytes with 35.7% NEURONS and 10.8% oligodendrocytes, and the authors themselves write that 'for 12/13 of common genes, the magnitude of upregulation was correlated to the percentage of astrocytes in the cultures' — so the Uns-C/En-N/En-As gradient is substantially a cell-composition gradient, not a clean cell-intrinsic contrast. Cells are human FETAL hNPC-derived GABAergic neurons, n=2 independent experiments. Also, fold-changes are each population's induction over its OWN baseline and so say nothing about absolute MDA5 levels. The claim omits a directly relevant result from the same figure: basal MDA5 was significantly HIGHER in enriched astrocytes than neurons (Fig. 7n).
verdicts.corrected_claim: In human fetal-NPC-derived neuronal/glial cultures infected with TBEV (Fares et al., J Neuroinflammation 2020, PMID 32127025), a 24-hpi antiviral PCR array gave IFIH1 fold-regulation of 32.7 (unsorted), 19.7 (enriched neurons) and 35.3 (enriched astrocytes); DDX58 10.5/5.7/16.0; TLR3 6.2/1.7/6.4. At 72 hpi neuronal MDA5 decreased while astrocytic MDA5 was maintained, and the authors conclude the antiviral program was 'of greater intensity and longer duration in human astrocytes than in human neurons', with viperin and TRIM5alpha induced selectively in astrocytes. Three limits: the 'enriched astrocyte' population is only 53.5% astrocytes (35.7% neurons), and the authors attribute the gradient for 12/13 shared genes to astrocyte percentage rather than cell-intrinsic difference; the cells are immature fetal-derived GABAergic neurons; and fold-change is relative to each population's own baseline, so it does not report absolute MDA5 abundance. The same figure (7n) shows basal MDA5 was significantly, though slightly, HIGHER in enriched astrocytes than neurons — a human baseline comparison that runs opposite to the mouse ranking in claim 1.

verdicts.claim: Claim 8: Human neuronal cells possess functional IFN-inducible RIG-I, MDA5 and TLR3 pathways; RIG-I rises with neuronal differentiation whereas MDA5 does not.
verdicts.reason: Both key quotes verified: 'although RIG-I expression increased with BE(2)-C differentiation, probably due to the use of retinoic acid to induce neuronal maturation' and 'MDA5 expression levels were independent of differentiation'; and 'the expression of both PRRs increased in response to type I IFN stimulation in both human BE(2)-C neuronal cells... and primary rat neurons'. Confirmed there are no numeric baselines or fold-inductions and no comparison to non-neuronal cells — exactly as the claim's caveat states. This claim is well-calibrated.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated, with one attribution nuance. Peltier et al. (J Immunol 2010, PMID 20483728) show in human BE(2)-C (±retinoic acid), SH-SY5Y and HCN-1A cells plus primary rat E18 cortical neurons that RIG-I and MDA5 are present and both increase after type I IFN, while 'MDA5 expression levels were independent of differentiation' and RIG-I increased with BE(2)-C differentiation — though the authors themselves attribute the RIG-I rise 'probably... to the use of retinoic acid', so it may be an RA effect rather than differentiation per se. The paper reports no numeric baselines, no numeric fold-inductions and no non-neuronal comparator, so it establishes presence and inducibility only, not that neuronal levels are high. Evidence is human transformed neuronal lines plus rat primary neurons.

verdicts.claim: Claim 9: Additional confirmations that MDA5 and RIG-I are induced in human neuronal cells by picornavirus and flavivirus infection.
verdicts.reason: Both abstracts verified verbatim. JEV/SK-N-MC: '1316 and 2737 dysregulated genes (>=2/-2 fold change, P < 0.05) were found at 48 hours post-infection and 60 hpi'; 'Among the most highly upregulated genes (>=10 folds, P < 0.05) were chemokines CCL5, CXCL11, IL8 and CXCL10'; 'RIG-1 and MDA5 were also upregulated'. CVB3/hNPC: 'Increased expression levels of viral RNA sensors (RIG-I, MDA5) and interferon-stimulated genes, such as IFN-beta, IP-10, ISG15, OAS1, OAS2, Mx2... while IFN-gamma expression level was significantly downregulated', by QuantSeq 3' mRNA sequencing. Neither reports an IFIH1-specific fold-change, as the claim states.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated, with the cell-identity caveat sharpened. RIG-I and MDA5 were reported as upregulated in JEV-infected SK-N-MC cells (PMID 30481615; 1316 and 2737 dysregulated genes at 48 and 60 hpi, >=2-fold, P<0.05; top upregulated CCL5, CXCL11, IL8, CXCL10) and in CVB3-infected human neural progenitor cells (PMID 32192194; RIG-I, MDA5, IFN-beta, IP-10, ISG15, OAS1, OAS2, Mx2 up, IFN-gamma down). Neither paper reports a numeric fold-change for IFIH1 specifically. Note neither system is a mature human neuron: SK-N-MC is an immortalised line of Ewing sarcoma/neuroepithelioma lineage and hNPCs are progenitors, so these support inducibility of MDA5 in human neural-lineage cells rather than in neurons proper.

verdicts.claim: Claim 10: MDA5-deficient mice die of WNV but the defect is entirely non-cell-autonomous; MDA5 loss had no effect in primary cortical or cerebellar neuron cultures and none after intracranial inoculation.
verdicts.reason: All five elements verified verbatim from the paper: '140-fold-higher viral burden in the brain (P < 0.01)' and '21-fold-higher viral burden in the spinal cord (P < 0.01)'; 'MDA5-/- mice exhibited enhanced mortality (92% versus 53%; P < 0.001)'; 'we observed no differences in infection between WT and MDA5-/- mice following intracranial injection (P > 0.05)'; 'an absence of MDA5 did not impact WNV infection in primary cortical or cerebellar neuron cultures (P > 0.05)'; and the CD8+ T cell priming attribution. This is the strongest-sourced claim in the set.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Lazear et al. (J Virol 2013, PMID 23966390): after peripheral WNV, MDA5-/- mice had 140-fold higher brain and 21-fold higher spinal cord viral burden at day 10 (both P < 0.01) and 92% vs 53% mortality (P < 0.001), yet showed no difference from WT after intracranial inoculation (P > 0.05) and no effect of MDA5 loss on WNV replication in primary cortical or cerebellar neuron cultures (P > 0.05), with adoptive transfer localising the requirement to MDA5-dependent CD8+ T cell priming. Mouse only. The word 'entirely' is the authors' practical conclusion for this virus and route; it should not be generalised to other neurotropic viruses.

verdicts.claim: Claim 11: Cell-type-restricted MAVS deletion shows RLR signalling is required in brain-resident myeloid cells — not in neurons and not in astrocytes — for protection against a neurotropic RNA virus.
verdicts.reason: The headline sentence is verbatim from the abstract: 'By selectively deleting MAVS in neurons, astrocytes, or long-lived myeloid cells, we discovered that RLR signaling specifically within brain-resident myeloid cells is crucial for protection against the virus.' The microglial mechanism (P2RY12+ cross-presentation genes, reduced surface MHC-I, normal leukocyte infiltration, dysfunctional CNS CD8+ T cells) is all confirmed. BUT the claim's assertion that neuron-specific deletion 'did not produce the protective defect' is contradicted by the paper's own body text: 'Syn1-Cre± MAVSfl/fl mice showed moderately and CX3CR1-CreER± MAVSfl/fl mice massively enhanced susceptibility to lethal VSV infection.' Neuronal MAVS deletion DID increase susceptibility to lethal infection, just far less than myeloid deletion. Astrocyte-specific (GFAP-Cre) deletion showed no significant phenotype, so that half of the claim holds.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Pavlou, Ghita et al. (J Neuroinflammation 2025, PMID 40619428) deleted MAVS selectively in neurons (Syn1-Cre), astrocytes (GFAP-Cre) or long-lived myeloid cells (CX3CR1-CreER) and infected intranasally with VSV, concluding that 'RLR signaling specifically within brain-resident myeloid cells is crucial for protection against the virus'. Myeloid-MAVS deletion caused massively enhanced susceptibility with normal leukocyte infiltration but aberrant antigen cross-presentation gene expression in P2RY12+ microglia, reduced surface MHC class I, and dysfunctional CNS-infiltrating CD8+ T cells. Importantly, the hierarchy is graded, not all-or-none: neuron-specific MAVS deletion produced MODERATELY enhanced susceptibility to lethal infection (though without elevated viral loads), while astrocyte-specific deletion produced no significant phenotype. The myeloid requirement is mechanistically about cross-presentation and CD8+ T cell relicensing rather than cell-autonomous viral restriction. Mouse.

verdicts.claim: Claim 12: IFN-beta reporter mice show astrocytes and microglia are the CNS IFN-beta producers during neurotropic viral infection, while virus-infected neurons essentially never produce detectable IFN-beta.
verdicts.reason: Kallfass verified verbatim: 'similar numbers of astrocytes and microglia of infected brains were luciferase positive, whereas virus-infected neurons rarely contained detectable levels of luciferase.' The NSs-deficient mutant result is confirmed with numbers I did not have before: 89% of luciferase-positive cells were astrocytes with the mutant vs 35% with WT virus. Pfefferkorn independently verified via its own full text (astrocytes as main IFN-beta source across TMEV, RABV and VSV).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate, with one wording correction. Kallfass et al. (J Virol 2012, PMID 22875966) using IFN-beta-promoter luciferase reporter mice infected with La Crosse virus found similar numbers of luciferase-positive astrocytes and microglia, 'whereas virus-infected neurons rarely contained detectable levels of luciferase'; with an NSs-deficient LACV mutant, 89% of IFN-beta-producing cells were astrocytes (vs 35% with WT virus). Pfefferkorn et al. (PMID 26656686) extended this to rabies virus, TMEV and VSV, concluding abortively infected astrocytes are the main brain source of IFN-beta. 'Essentially never produce detectable IFN-beta' should be 'rarely contained detectable reporter signal' — this is a luciferase-reporter readout in mice, with a detection threshold, not a direct measurement of neuronal IFN-beta protein.

verdicts.claim: Claim 13: cGAS-STING antiviral sensing in brain is a microglial function; STING redundant for cell-autonomous resistance in neurons and astrocytes; microglia transfer antiviral state to neurons. Sting1/Tmem173 ~470-fold higher in microglia than neurons.
verdicts.reason: All three Reinert elements verified verbatim: microglia are the main STING-dependent type I IFN producers after HSV-1; 'Although STING is redundant for cell-autonomous antiviral resistance in astrocytes and neurons, viral replication is strongly increased in neurons in STING-deficient mice'; and 'HSV-infected microglia confer STING-dependent antiviral activities in neurons', with supernatant-transfer experiments confirming STING-deficient microglia fail to transfer antiviral activity. My recomputation confirms Tmem173 microglia 136.72 vs neurons 0.29 (476x), and this ranking is replicate-robust (microglia 110.8/162.6 vs neurons 0.186/0.388).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Reinert et al. (Nat Commun 2016, PMID 27830700) identify microglia as the main STING-dependent type I IFN producers after CNS HSV-1 infection; STING is redundant for cell-autonomous antiviral resistance in astrocytes and neurons, yet viral replication is strongly increased in neurons in STING-deficient mice because HSV-infected microglia confer STING-dependent antiviral activity on neurons via transferable factors. Consistent with this division of labour, Tmem173/Sting1 in P7 mouse cortex is 136.72 FPKM in microglia vs 0.29 in neurons (~470-fold; robust across both replicates). Note the paired finding the framing should retain: neurons are still protected by STING, non-cell-autonomously. Mouse.

verdicts.claim: Claim 14: The dsRNA sensor non-redundant in human CNS neurons is TLR3, not MDA5. TLR3- or UNC93B1-deficient iPSC-derived neurons and oligodendrocytes are selectively susceptible to HSV-1; NSCs and astrocytes are not.
verdicts.reason: All elements verified: 'detected mRNA for key genes of the TLR3-responsive pathway, including TLR3 and UNC93B1, in all four cell types tested'; IFN-beta/IFN-lambda1 induction 'greatly impaired in UNC-93B-deficient neurons and oligodendrocytes'; UNC-93B-deficient NSCs and astrocytes replicated HSV-1 like controls; TLR3-deficient neurons likewise showed faster, higher HSV-1 replication. Confirmed the paper reports NO expression data for DDX58 or IFIH1, exactly as the claim states. The follow-up PNAS title (PMID 30154162) matches the claim's description verbatim.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Lafaille et al. (Nature 2012, PMID 23103873) differentiated iPSCs from TLR3- and UNC-93B-deficient HSE patients into NSCs, neurons, astrocytes and oligodendrocytes; TLR3 and UNC93B1 mRNA was detected in all four, but IFN-beta/IFN-lambda1 induction after HSV-1 was impaired selectively in UNC-93B-deficient neurons and oligodendrocytes, which also showed faster and higher HSV-1 replication, while NSCs and astrocytes behaved like controls; TLR3-deficient neurons were similarly susceptible. The paper reports no DDX58 or IFIH1 expression data and its comparisons are qualitative, not numeric titers. Zimmer et al. (PNAS 2018, PMID 30154162) showed iPSC-derived trigeminal neurons lack the constitutive TLR3-dependent immunity protecting cortical neurons. Scope limit: this establishes TLR3/UNC93B1 non-redundancy for HSV-1 specifically in iPSC-derived cells; it does not test MDA5 and so does not by itself show MDA5 is dispensable in human neurons.

verdicts.claim: Claim 15: A child homozygous for IFIH1 c.1641+1G>C developed enterovirus-30 rhombencephalitis, in the same study that reported TLR3 deficiency in an EV71 rhombencephalitis patient.
verdicts.reason: The viruses are swapped. From the paper's own clinical section: Patient 1 (the TLR3 patient, compound heterozygous F322fs2*/D280N) 'developed fever, vomiting, drowsiness, and stiff neck' at age 3.5 yr with 'PCR tests for EV30 on cerebrospinal fluid, stool, and respiratory samples' positive. Patient 2 'developed EV71 encephalitis at the age of 12 mo' and the text states 'P2 is homozygous for an essential splicing variant (c.1641+1G>C) of IFIH1'. Rescue confirms the mapping: 'stable overexpression of exogeneous WT MDA5 restored normal resistance to EV71 infection in SV40-fibroblasts from P2'. So the MDA5-deficient child had EV71 and the TLR3-deficient child had EV30 — the reverse of the claim. All other elements of the claim verified verbatim, including the early/late kinetics split, the baseline-vs-EV-responsive IFN-beta contrast, and the IFN-alpha2b rescue asymmetry.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Human MDA5 deficiency does cause CNS disease: in Chen et al. (J Exp Med 2021, PMID 34726731), a child homozygous for the loss-of-function IFIH1 splice variant c.1641+1G>C (P2) developed enterovirus-71 rhombencephalitis at 12 months, while a second, unrelated child with compound heterozygous TLR3 variants (loss-of-function F322fs2* plus hypomorphic D280N; P1) developed enterovirus-30 rhombencephalitis at 3.5 years. Patient fibroblasts responded poorly to extracellular (TLR3) or intracellular (MDA5) poly(I:C); baseline IFN-beta was low in the TLR3 patient and EV-responsive IFN-beta low in the MDA5 patient; EV growth was enhanced at early time points in TLR3-deficient and at late time points in MDA5-deficient fibroblasts; pre-infection IFN-alpha2b rescued both, post-infection IFN-alpha2b fully rescued only MDA5-deficient cells; WT TLR3 or MDA5 expression rescued the respective phenotypes. All mechanistic work was in SV40-immortalised fibroblasts, not neurons, so the CNS requirement was not localised at cellular resolution.

verdicts.claim: Claim 16: Neurons are interferon-hyporesponsive at the signalling level — lower basal STAT1/STAT2, muted delayed STAT1 activation — yet carry HIGHER basal type I IFN transcripts than fibroblasts.
verdicts.reason: Cavanaugh verified: 'Expression of the majority (7/12 genes) of type I IFNs examined at an RNA level was significantly higher in neurons than MEF under unstimulated conditions'; 'primary neurons have a lower homeostatic expression of Stat1 than control fibroblasts'; basal Stat2 also lower; 'Antiviral genes Oas1a and Isg15 were highly induced in MEF, whereas neuronal expression of these genes was negligible'; sustained neuronal STAT2 phosphorylation through 24 h. Confirmed no basal Ddx58/Ifih1/Tlr3 data, as the claim states. Bunkofske & Hunter (J Immunol 2026, PMID 42378512, PMCID PMC13318093 — both verified) confirmed verbatim for the IFNGR1 8-fold figure, the STAT1/2 activation sentence, cortical neurons using MDA5/RIG-I for poly(I:C), and RIG-I detecting JEV.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Cavanaugh, Holmgren & Rall (J Neuroimmunol 2015, PMID 25669994) found 7 of 12 type I IFN genes expressed significantly higher in unstimulated primary mouse hippocampal neurons than MEFs, alongside lower homeostatic Stat1 and Stat2 and negligible neuronal Oas1a/Isg15 induction where MEFs induced them strongly. Bunkofske & Hunter's 2026 review summarises that neurons show significantly lower STAT1/2 activation and reduced antiviral gene expression, with IFNGR1 transcripts 8-fold lower in primary hippocampal neurons than MEFs, while noting cortical neurons do use MDA5/RIG-I to respond to poly(I:C) and RIG-I to detect JEV. Neither reports basal neuronal Ddx58, Ifih1 or Tlr3 levels. All mouse. One framing note: Cavanaugh's own conclusion (and title) is that this homeostatic neuronal IFN is SUFFICIENT for early control of viral infection — a more neuron-favourable reading than hyporesponsiveness alone conveys.

verdicts.claim: Claim 17: Neurons substitute a non-lytic defence (autophagy) for the IFN/ISG program, because ISG effector pathways are cytotoxic and neurons are post-mitotic and irreplaceable.
verdicts.reason: The author list is wrong: the paper (PMID 22980330, Cell Host Microbe 2012) is by Yordy B, Iijima N, Huttner A, Leib D, Iwasaki A — there is no 'Gao' or 'Gonzalez'. The title, 'A neuron-specific role for autophagy in antiviral defense against herpes simplex virus', supports the substance, and I confirmed the paper's identity and framing, but I did not independently verify the in-vitro/in-vivo DRG specifics or the epithelial comparison beyond the title and abstract framing. More substantively, the claim is labelled 'FUNCTIONAL RATIONALE with direct evidence': the autophagy dependence is a measured result, but the stated REASON (ISG effectors are cytotoxic, neurons are irreplaceable) is a teleological hypothesis widely held in the field, not something this experiment measures.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Yordy, Iijima, Huttner, Leib & Iwasaki (Cell Host Microbe 2012, PMID 22980330) showed that mouse dorsal root ganglion neurons rely on autophagy rather than type I IFN to limit HSV-1 replication, in contrast to mitotic cells such as MEFs and mucosal epithelial cells, establishing a neuron-specific role for autophagy in antiviral defence. Note the author list is Yordy, Iijima, Huttner, Leib & Iwasaki — not 'Yordy, Gao, Gonzalez & Iwasaki'. The evolutionary rationale that neurons trade IFN for autophagy BECAUSE ISG effectors are cytotoxic and neurons are post-mitotic and irreplaceable is a plausible and widely-held interpretation, not a result demonstrated by this study. Mouse.

verdicts.claim: Claim 18: IFIH1 GOF causes severe CNS disease but the phenotype is dominated by cerebral arteriopathy; autopsy calcification confined to CNS artery walls and perivascular space with NO neuronal ferrugination.
verdicts.reason: Every quoted string verified verbatim against the paper: 'multifocal calcifications limited to small to medium central nervous system arteries (no evidence of calcification in other organs)'; 'microcephaly (brain weight: 916 g)'; 'Calcospherules limited to the vessel walls and the perivasulcar area without evidence of neuronal ferrugination or tubuloreticular bodies'; 'correlated with the extent of IFIH1 protein expression (data derived from Allen Brain Institute)'; and 'this is the second reported case of AGS resulting from a mutation in IFIH1 gene.'
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Gilani et al. (Pediatr Dev Pathol 2019, PMID 30952201) report the second neuropathological case of IFIH1-related AGS: a 16-year-old boy with microcephaly (brain weight 916 g vs 1351 g expected), multifocal calcifications limited to small-to-medium CNS arteries with no calcification in other organs, and calcospherules limited to vessel walls and perivascular area without neuronal ferrugination or tubuloreticular bodies; regional calcification extent correlated with IFIH1 protein expression from Allen Brain Institute data. Two limits on the inference: n=1 autopsy, and the Allen correlation is with REGIONAL IFIH1 expression, so reading it as support for the vascular/endothelial compartment being the IFIH1-high CNS cell type is the investigator's inference, not a finding of the paper.

verdicts.claim: Claim 19: The IFIH1 GOF clinical spectrum (74 individuals, 51 families, 27 variants) is neurologically dominated but with striking incomplete penetrance.
verdicts.reason: Cohort numbers all verified: 74 individuals / 51 families / 27 mutations; 'Ten adult individuals, 13.5% of all mutation carriers, were clinically asymptomatic (with seven of these aged over 50 years)'; 'Where tested, all mutations (i.e., 26 of 27) were associated with increased expression of ISGs in peripheral blood' — so the claim's 26/27 is right and more precise than the abstract's summary; '109 of 117 values were positive' across 51 patients; 'Sixteen samples from seven clinically nonpenetrant subjects exhibited an upregulation of interferon signaling'; neuroregression 'in at least 20 patients, in seven of whom an acute loss of skills occurred after the age of 1 year'. Rice 2014 mechanism quote verified verbatim. TWO ERRORS: (a) '41 previously unreported' refers to INDIVIDUALS, not mutations; (b) the citation for Rutsch 2015 is wrong — PMID 25620203 is Jang et al., 'Mutations in DDX58, which encodes RIG-I, cause atypical Singleton-Merten syndrome', a different gene. The Rutsch IFIH1 Singleton-Merten paper is PMID 25620204.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate on all cohort statistics, with two citation corrections. Rice et al. (Hum Mutat 2020, PMID 31898846) describe 74 individuals from 51 families with 27 likely pathogenic IFIH1 mutations (41 of the 74 INDIVIDUALS — not mutations — previously unreported); 26 of 27 mutations where tested were associated with increased peripheral-blood ISG expression; 109 of 117 samples from 51 patients were interferon-signature positive; 16 samples from 7 clinically non-penetrant subjects still showed upregulated interferon signalling; 10/74 (13.5%) carriers were asymptomatic, 7 of them over 50; rapid neuroregression occurred in at least 20 patients, 7 with onset after age 1 on a background of normal development. Rice et al. 2014 (PMID 24686847) showed mutant MDA5 binds RNA more avidly, increasing baseline and ligand-induced interferon signalling. The recurrent R822Q variant causes Singleton-Merten syndrome (Rutsch et al. 2015, correct PMID 25620204 — NOT 25620203, which is Jang et al. on DDX58/RIG-I) and, in a 6-year-old boy, spasticity, developmental delay and basal ganglia calcification (Buers et al. 2017, PMID 28475458). These are peripheral-blood ISG data with no CNS cell-type localisation.

verdicts.claim: Claim 20: In ADAR1-mutant mice the CNS cells mounting the ISG response are neurons, microglia, ependyma, choroid plexus and endothelial cells, with little in oligodendroglia and astrocytes except STAT1.
verdicts.reason: The central sentence is verbatim: 'Within the CNS aberrant ISG expression was mostly limited to neurons, microglia, ependyma, choroid plexus, and endothelial cells with little expression in oligodendroglia and astrocytes except for STAT1.' Also confirmed: double-label in situ hybridization, onset from 2 weeks of age, absence of detectable interferon and of immune cell infiltrates, and ventricular dilatation plus deep grey matter mineralization at 8-13 months showing no spatial relationship to ISG expression. The claim's own flag of tension with van Heteren's astrocyte-centric human AGS data is appropriate and correctly cited.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Wiley, Steinman & Wang (Brain Pathol 2023, PMID 36161399) used double-label in situ hybridization in ADAR1-mutant mice and found that from 2 weeks of age 'aberrant ISG expression was mostly limited to neurons, microglia, ependyma, choroid plexus, and endothelial cells with little expression in oligodendroglia and astrocytes except for STAT1', in the absence of detectable interferon or immune cell infiltrates; ventricular dilatation and deep grey matter mineralization appeared at 8-13 months without spatially tracking ISG expression. This is mouse in-situ data and supports that neurons are capable ISG responders in vivo; it stands in tension with post-mortem human AGS findings implicating astrocytes as the source of IFN-alpha and CXCL10 (van Heteren et al., PMID 18240301).

verdicts.claim: Claim 21: Neuron-specific Adar1 deletion causes ISG elevation and ventricular obstruction, and deleting MDA5 largely normalizes ISG expression — direct genetic proof that neuronal MDA5 is functional.
verdicts.reason: The data are verified essentially verbatim from both abstracts. Todo et al. (J Neuroinflammation 2026, PMID 42400013): 'neuron-specific deletion of Adar1 (both p110 and p150) in mice caused early postnatal lethality with elevated expression of type I IFN-stimulated genes... Of note, both selective restoration of ADAR1 p150 function and deletion of MDA5 largely normalized type I ISG expression and ameliorated ventricular obstruction but failed to rescue early postnatal lethality.' Yoo et al. (Cell Rep 2026, PMID 41855203) verified verbatim including the astrocyte-severity point, microglial elimination, IFN blockade reversing abnormalities where PKR/ZBP1 deletion did not, and CSF IFN-alpha exceeding serum. BUT the headline overreaches: Adar1 was deleted neuron-specifically while MDA5 deletion is reported without a cell-type qualifier, i.e. apparently global. The experiment therefore shows that neuron-derived unedited dsRNA drives an MDA5-dependent ISG response — it does not establish that the sensing MDA5 is the neuron's own.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Todo et al. (J Neuroinflammation 2026, PMID 42400013) show neuron-specific deletion of Adar1 (p110 and p150) causes early postnatal lethality with elevated type I ISGs and ventricular obstruction from choroid plexus/ependymal hypoplasia with gliosis, and that deletion of MDA5 (as reported, not cell-type-restricted) largely normalized ISG expression and ameliorated ventricular obstruction while failing to rescue lethality. This establishes that loss of ADAR1 editing IN NEURONS generates an MDA5-dependent interferonopathy, but because the MDA5 deletion is not neuron-restricted it does not localise the sensing MDA5 to neurons themselves — the responding sensor could reside in microglia, astrocytes or vasculature. Yoo et al. (Cell Rep 2026, PMID 41855203) corroborate that neuron- or astrocyte-specific ADAR1 dysfunction each evokes robust ISGs and AGS-like encephalopathy, with astrocytic dysfunction causing particularly severe effects, and that blocking type I IFN signalling fully reverses the abnormalities whereas deleting PKR or ZBP1 does not.

verdicts.claim: Claim 22: In brain, PKR (EIF2AK2) is a separable, MDA5/MAVS-independent dsRNA effector: with MDA5-MAVS deleted, aberrant brain ISG protein expression and microgliosis persist and are rescued only by additionally removing PKR.
verdicts.reason: Verified verbatim from the Brain 2026 abstract (PMID 40920008): 'The proteomic analyses showed upregulation of ISG-encoded proteins in the Adar Mavs double mutant, and the morphological analyses confirmed aberrant microgliosis in the brains. Both are prevented in Adar Mavs Eif2ak2 triple mutants, indicating the key role of aberrant PKR activation'; brains collected at postnatal days 8 and 14 by mass spectrometry, IHC and RT-qPCR; and the residual response 'probably attributable to reactive microglia and astrocytes'. The Eif2ak2 FPKM values are confirmed by my own recomputation (neurons 0.36, astrocytes 4.54, endothelial 4.30). Yoo et al.'s non-rescue by PKR deletion is also verified. The claim is appropriately self-critical.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Accurate as stated. Lacovich et al. (Brain 2026, PMID 40920008) found that Adar Mavs double-mutant mice still showed upregulated ISG-encoded proteins by mass spectrometry and aberrant microgliosis in brain at postnatal days 8 and 14, both prevented in Adar Mavs Eif2ak2 triple mutants, 'indicating the key role of aberrant PKR activation', with the residual brain IFN response attributed by the authors 'probably... to reactive microglia and astrocytes'. Consistent with the claim's own caveat, Eif2ak2 mRNA is low in P7 mouse cortical neurons (0.36 FPKM) relative to astrocytes (4.54) and endothelium (4.30), so PKR abundance does not mark neurons; and Yoo et al. found PKR deletion did not rescue their Z-RNA-binding-deficient Adar1 encephalopathy. Mouse.

verdicts.claim: Claim 23: Neurons sit at the bottom of the CNS ranking for IFNAR1 and STAT1, explaining why a cell with only modestly low basal IFIH1 ends up functionally MDA5-poor.
verdicts.reason: All numbers reproduce exactly in my recomputation, but the rank claims are partly wrong and partly fragile. For IFNAR1, neurons (7.60) are 5th of 7 — ABOVE both newly-formed (5.93) and myelinating (3.84) oligodendrocytes — so 'neurons sit at the bottom of the CNS ranking' is incorrect for IFNAR1, though the specific ratios the claim gives (~8.6x below endothelium, ~3.3x below microglia) are exact and replicate-robust (neuron reps 7.418/7.773). For STAT1, the claimed 'neurons lowest' is NOT robust at n=2: neuron replicates are 1.147 and 1.991, and rep2 exceeds both myelinating-OL replicates (1.699/1.749) and astrocyte rep1 (1.844). The Kang et al. 2002 framing of mda-5 as interferon-inducible is correct (title: 'mda-5: An interferon-inducible putative RNA helicase...'). The closing mechanistic inference is untested.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In P7/P17 mouse cortex (Zhang et al. 2014), neurons are low but not lowest for the IFN receptor and transducer. Ifnar1 mean FPKM: endothelial 65.23 > microglia 24.77 > astrocytes 13.95 > OPC 12.93 > neurons 7.60 > newly-formed OL 5.93 > myelinating OL 3.84 — neurons rank 5th of 7, roughly 8.6-fold below endothelium and 3.3-fold below microglia (robust across replicates). Stat1: endothelial 7.84 > OPC 6.77 > microglia 4.30 > newly-formed OL 3.98 > astrocytes 2.02 > myelinating OL 1.72 > neurons 1.57 by mean, but this last ranking is not robust — the two neuronal replicates are 1.147 and 1.991, the higher one exceeding both myelinating-oligodendrocyte replicates. IFIH1 is itself an interferon-inducible gene (Kang et al. 2002, PMID 11805321), so a lower IFNAR1/STAT1 setpoint plausibly lowers the inducible MDA5 ceiling in neurons, but that causal link is an inference from mRNA abundance and has not been measured directly.

verdicts.claim: Claim 24: Published Ifih1 gain-of-function knock-in mouse models do not reproduce the AGS brain phenotype; their disease is lupus-like, hepatic calcification and Singleton-Merten-like bony abnormalities, with no AGS-like encephalopathy described.
verdicts.reason: Funabiki et al. (Immunity 2014, PMID 24530055) verified: the mice 'spontaneously developed lupus-like autoimmune symptoms without viral infection', inflammation was MAVS-dependent, and 'intercrossing the mutant mice with type I IFN receptor-deficient mice ameliorated clinical manifestations' — with no CNS phenotype mentioned. I independently corroborated the Ifih1 G821S/+ bone phenotype (SMS-like decreased bone mineral density, thin cortical bone, abnormal growth plate cartilage) and its rescue in Ifih1gs/+ Mavs-/- and Ifih1gs/+ Ifnar1-/- mice. Targeted searching surfaced no report of intracranial calcification, white matter disease or neuroregression in any Ifih1 GOF mouse. One imprecision: Funabiki's model is an ENU-induced point mutant, not a knock-in.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Largely accurate, with one terminological correction and one epistemic caveat. Funabiki et al. (Immunity 2014, PMID 24530055) generated an ENU-induced Ifih1 point mutant (not a knock-in) that spontaneously developed lupus-like autoimmunity with kidney and skin inflammation and liver calcification, MAVS-dependent and ameliorated by Ifnar1 deficiency; Ifih1 G821S/+ knock-in mice show Singleton-Merten-like bone abnormalities rescued by Mavs or Ifnar1 ablation. I found no published report of intracranial calcification, white matter disease or neuroregression in any Ifih1 GOF mouse model, consistent with the claim — but this is absence of evidence from a non-exhaustive search rather than a demonstrated negative, and a dedicated review of interferonopathy mouse models would be the appropriate place to confirm it. The downstream inference stands: the cell of origin of IFIH1-GOF CNS disease has not been established genetically in any model and is currently inferred from human neuropathology and ADAR1-driven surrogates in which MDA5 acts downstream.

verification.overall:
ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION SUMMARY — "neurons" angle, 24 claims checked against primary sources.

TALLY: 15 CONFIRMED, 8 OVERSTATED, 1 REFUTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE.

This is an unusually well-sourced claim set. I independently re-downloaded the brainrnaseq.org FPKM matrix and recomputed every cited gene: all ~50 numbers across claims 1, 2, 13, 22 and 23 reproduce exactly, and the cell-identity markers used to validate the file (Snap25, Cldn5, Cx3cr1, Gfap, Mbp) all check out. Numbers quoted from Fares et al. Table 1, Lazear, Rice 2020, Cho, Gilani, Wiley, Lacovich, Todo and Yoo were found verbatim in the sources. Several claims carried honest self-flagged limitations that I verified were genuine (I also could not extract per-cell-type brain nTPM from HPA; the Cho supplementary fold-changes are indeed not in the accessible text).

FINDINGS REQUIRING CORRECTION, in order of severity:

1. CLAIM 15 — FACTUAL ERROR (REFUTED). The viruses are swapped. In Chen et al. 2021, the MDA5/IFIH1-deficient child (P2, homozygous c.1641+1G>C) had ENTEROVIRUS-71 rhombencephalitis at 12 months; the TLR3-deficient child (P1) had ENTEROVIRUS-30 at 3.5 years. The claim reverses them. Confirmed three ways in the full text, including "P2 is homozygous for an essential splicing variant (c.1641+1G>C) of IFIH1" and the rescue experiment restoring resistance to EV71 in P2 cells. The scientific substance of the claim survives; the virus assignment does not.

2. CLAIM 19 — MIS-CITATION. PMID 25620203 is Jang et al., "Mutations in DDX58, which encodes RIG-I, cause atypical Singleton-Merten syndrome" — the wrong gene. The Rutsch 2015 IFIH1 Singleton-Merten paper is PMID 25620204. Separately, "41 previously unreported" refers to individuals, not mutations. All cohort statistics otherwise verified exactly, including the precise "26 of 27".

3. CLAIM 11 — OVERSTATED against the source's own body text. The abstract sentence quoted is verbatim, but the paper states "Syn1-Cre± MAVSfl/fl mice showed moderately and CX3CR1-CreER± MAVSfl/fl mice massively enhanced susceptibility to lethal VSV infection." Neuron-specific MAVS deletion DID produce a susceptibility phenotype; the claim's "not in neurons" is wrong. Astrocyte-specific deletion showed no phenotype, so that half holds. This matters because claim 11 was positioned as a decisive negative for neuronal RLR signalling.

4. CLAIM 1 — STATISTICALLY FRAGILE, the most important methodological finding here. The claim's headline assertion ("neurons are NOT the lowest", "neurons intermediate") rests on n=2 with a 4.65-fold spread between the two neuronal replicates (0.146 and 0.678). In replicate 1, neurons rank 5th of 7, BELOW astrocytes and OPC; in replicate 2 they rank 2nd. The neuron-vs-astrocyte-vs-OPC ordering is unresolved. Two further undisclosed caveats: cells were purified at postnatal day 7 (P17 for oligodendrocytes), i.e. developing brain with cell types compared across different ages, not adult "resting cortex"; and the 0.1 floor is an author-imposed threshold, making the "~20-fold range" a censored lower bound. What IS robust: endothelial cells clearly highest, oligodendrocytes at floor, and MDA5's narrow range versus STING's ~470-fold.

5. CLAIM 23 — PARTLY WRONG on rank. Neurons are NOT at the bottom for IFNAR1 (5th of 7, above both oligodendrocyte populations), and the "neurons lowest" STAT1 rank is not robust (neuronal replicate 2 exceeds both myelinating-OL replicates). The specific ratios quoted are exact.

6. CLAIM 3 — Three inaccuracies: the basal comparison used commercially purchased FOETAL PRIMARY astrocytes, not hiAstrocytes; the paper says astrocytes showed "strong" DDX58, not "moderate"; and "neurons lack robust innate immune signalling pathways" is a Discussion sentence citing prior literature, not the authors' own conclusion.

7. CLAIM 7 — Numbers perfect, framing overstated. The "enriched astrocyte" fraction is only 53.5% astrocytes and 35.7% neurons, and the authors explicitly attribute the gradient for 12 of 13 shared genes to astrocyte percentage in the culture. Calling this "the clearest head-to-head human neuron-vs-astrocyte number set" is too strong. Notably, the claim omits a directly relevant result from the same figure: basal MDA5 was significantly HIGHER in astrocytes than neurons (Fig. 7n) — a human baseline measurement that runs OPPOSITE to the mouse ranking the investigator leans on in claim 1.

8. CLAIM 17 — Author list fabricated in part: the paper is Yordy, Iijima, Huttner, Leib & Iwasaki, not "Yordy, Gao, Gonzalez & Iwasaki". Content is directionally right.

9. CLAIM 21 — Headline overreaches. Adar1 was deleted neuron-specifically but MDA5 deletion appears global, so the experiment does not establish that the sensing MDA5 is the neuron's own. Not "direct genetic proof that neuronal MDA5 is functional".

CROSS-CUTTING OBSERVATION FOR THE SCIENTIST: the claim set's central thesis — that neurons are MDA5-low and RLR-hypofunctional relative to glia and vasculature — survives scrutiny, but its strongest support is NOT the IFIH1 receptor numbers themselves. The Ifih1 cell-type ranking is statistically fragile (claim 1) and one human dataset puts astrocyte basal MDA5 ABOVE neurons while the mouse data put neurons above astrocytes (claims 7 vs 1). The robust, replicate-stable, multiply-sourced findings are: (a) neuronal MAVS is dramatically and reliably the lowest of any cortical cell type (claim 2); (b) MDA5 is functionally dispensable for cell-autonomous neuronal control of WNV (claim 10, verbatim-verified); (c) IFN-beta production in infected brain is glial, not neuronal (claim 12); (d) TLR3, not MDA5, is the non-redundant dsRNA sensor in human CNS neurons (claim 14). Conversely, three well-verified claims cut AGAINST a strong "neurons are MDA5-irrelevant" reading: neurons are competent ISG responders in vivo (claim 20), neuronal ADAR1 loss drives an MDA5-dependent interferonopathy (claim 21), and neuron-specific MAVS deletion does increase susceptibility (corrected claim 11). Note also that no claim in this set addresses multiple sclerosis or the user's GSE180759 dataset — this angle is entirely about baseline/infection biology, not MS.

research.dimension: Reference expression resources for IFIH1/MDA5 in the nervous system: per-cell-type and per-region values with units and assay type, plus cross-resource concordance of the CNS cell-type ranking

findings.claim: Human Protein Atlas single-cell consensus (154 cell types, scRNA-seq) ranks IFIH1 across neural cell types as: vascular endothelial 48.5 > Schwann 45.1 > microglia 26.7 > lymphatic endothelial 20.3 > Müller glia 16.0 > pericyte 11.9 > ependymal 10.1 > astrocyte 7.9 > OPC 7.5 > Bergmann glia 5.9 > oligodendrocyte 5.5 >> brain excitatory neuron 0.5 > brain inhibitory neuron 0.4 > other brain neuron 0.2 nCPM. Neurons are ~50-100x below vascular/myeloid cells.

Per-sample IFIH1 values — endothelial: 7.9 (47yo ctx), 5.1 (13yo ctx); microglia/macrophage: 6.0 (45yo), 4.3 (51yo), 5.1 (63yo); mature cortex astrocytes (8-63yo, n=12): 1.3, 1.8, 1.3, 2.0, 0.8, 2.4, 0.9, 2.0, 2.3, 1.5, 2.1, 2.0; hippocampal astrocytes: 1.3, 0.8, 1.1, 1.8; oligodendrocytes: 1.1, 1.3, 1.1, 1.3, 1.1; neuron (25yo ctx): 0.8. Note the brainrnaseq.org human CSV endpoint (fe-wp-dataset-124.csv) returned HTTP 504 on all attempts; the GEO supplementary table is the same underlying dataset.

findings.claim: In the same Brain RNA-Seq human dataset, astrocytes isolated from glioblastoma cores and peri-tumoral tissue carry ~4-5x more IFIH1 than healthy cortical astrocytes (mean 6.9, median 8.05 FPKM vs 1.70 FPKM), showing that astrocytic IFIH1 is strongly inducible even though its baseline is low.
findings.evidence: Zhang 2016 tumor-associated astrocyte samples (GSE73721), IFIH1 FPKM: 59yo tumor periphery 0.1, 59yo tumor core 9.6, 64yo tumor core 11.4, 65yo tumor core 6.5 (mean 6.9, median 8.05) vs 12 healthy mature cortical astrocyte samples mean 1.70 (range 0.8-2.4). The paralogue DDX58/RIG-I shows the same shift (tumor astro mean 5.80 vs healthy cortical astro 2.98), consistent with a coordinated ISG response rather than an IFIH1-specific artifact.

findings.claim: The MOUSE Brain RNA-Seq resource (Zhang 2014, brainrnaseq.org dataset 120) gives Ifih1 FPKM: endothelial 2.10/2.01 > microglia 0.60/0.48 > OPC 0.33/0.11 ≈ astrocyte 0.29/0.12 ≈ neuron 0.15/0.68 > myelinating and newly-formed oligodendrocytes 0.1/0.1 (at the dataset's detection floor). Mouse reproduces endothelial > microglia > astrocyte but, unlike human, does NOT put neurons clearly last and puts oligodendrocytes at the floor.
findings.evidence: Downloaded directly from https://brainrnaseq.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/fe-wp-dataset-120.csv (21,636 mouse genes x 14 samples, FPKM, floor 0.1). Ifih1 row: astrocytes 0.293204/0.118981; endothelial 2.099757/2.011976; microglia_macrophage 0.601787/0.480536; myelinating_oligodendrocyte 0.1/0.1; neurons 0.145805/0.677700; newly_formed_oligodendrocyte 0.1/0.1; opc 0.325703/0.108437. Ddx58 in the same samples is also endothelial-dominant (8.486/8.773 vs microglia 1.624/1.576, astrocytes 1.251/1.366). Spearman rho of mouse vs human resources over shared cell types = 0.60-0.70 (n=5-6, p>0.15), vs 0.96-1.00 among the human resources.

findings.claim: Allen Brain Map is the one resource that DISAGREES, and the disagreement is a statistical artifact of its summary metric, not biology: its per-cluster trimmed means report IFIH1 = 0.000 CPM in every single non-neuronal cluster in both human datasets — microglia, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, OPC, endothelial, pericytes and VLMC all exactly zero.
findings.evidence: Human M1 10x trimmed_means.csv (127 clusters): IFIH1 > 0 in only 3/127 clusters, all excitatory neurons — Exc L5 THEMIS VILL 1.7253, Exc L3-5 RORB LAMA4 0.7529, Exc L3 LAMP5 CARM1P1 0.1158. Micro L1-6 TYROBP CD74 = 0.0000; Endo L2-5 NOSTRIN SRGN = 0.0000; Astro L1-6 FGFR3 AQP1 = 0.0000; Oligo L2-6 OPALIN FTH1P3 = 0.0000; OPC L1-6 PDGFRA COL20A1 = 0.0000; VLMC L1-5 PDGFRA COLEC12 = 0.0000. Human Multiple Cortical Areas SMART-seq trimmed_means.csv (121 clusters): IFIH1 > 0 in only 5/121 clusters, again all excitatory (Exc L3 THEMIS PLA2G7 2.220, Exc L5-6 THEMIS THTPA 0.837, Exc L3 LINC00507 CTXN3 0.457, Exc L3-5 THEMIS ELOF1 0.404, Exc L3-4 RORB RPS3P6 0.061); Micro L1-6 C1QC = 0.000, Endo L2-5 CLDN5 = 0.000, Peri L1-6 MUSTN1 = 0.000, all Astro/Oligo/OPC/VLMC = 0.000. Mechanism: a 25% trimmed mean is identically zero whenever the transcript is detected in under ~25% of cells in the cluster; measured detection rates for IFIH1 are 8.3% in microglia and 23.1% in endothelial cells (Census), i.e. below that threshold. Allen's summary files therefore cannot be used to rank IFIH1 and should not be cited as evidence of absence.

findings.claim: GTEx bulk RNA-seq shows brain is one of the LOWEST-IFIH1 tissues in the body: all 13 brain regions rank 34th-54th of 54 tissues, with median TPM 0.91-4.28 against a whole-body tissue median of 7.03 and a maximum of 88.19 (EBV-transformed lymphocytes). Within brain, caudal regions are highest and cerebellum lowest.

findings.evidence: HPA brain page barChart data plus the downloadable rna_brain_hpa.tsv (193 subregions, TPM/pTPM/nTPM). Extremes among subregions, nTPM: cervical spinal cord dorsal horn 16.7 (highest in the whole brain), nucleus gracilis 15.5, nucleus tractus solitarii 11.7, nucleus cuneatus 11.4, dorsolateral tegmental area 10.6, dorsal motor vagal complex 10.2, area postrema 9.3, choroid plexus 9.5; lowest: flocculonodular lobe 2.1, cerebellar cortex 2.2, vermis 2.3, superior frontal gyrus 0.9 (prefrontal subregion series 0.8-2.1). FANTOM5 human CAGE (scaled tags per million): spinal cord 10.5, cerebral cortex 9.6, hippocampal formation 9.0, cerebellum 3.3.

findings.claim: Protein-level evidence in normal human brain is essentially negative and internally inconsistent, and HPA itself flags it as unreliable: mass-spec-based Deep Visual Proteomics reports IFIH1 intensity = 0 in brain neurons, astrocytes+neuropil and microglia+neuropil, while antibody IHC reports 'Neuronal cells: Medium' in cerebral cortex — the opposite of every RNA resource.
findings.evidence: HPA DVP (MS) brain panel, raw intensity: Neurons 0, Astrocytes and Neuropil 0, Microglia and Neuropil 0 (for comparison, the same panel gives Macrophages 2,720,714 and CD4 T-cells 1,258,735). HPA IHC knowledge-based annotation: cerebral cortex — Endothelial cells: Low, Glial cells: Not detected, Neuronal cells: Medium, Neuropil: Not detected; hippocampus — Glial cells: Not detected, Neuronal cells: Low; caudate — Glial cells: Not detected; cerebellum — cells in granular layer: Not detected. HPA's own data-reliability statement for IFIH1 reads verbatim: 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data.' Therefore the IHC 'Neuronal cells: Medium' call should not be used as evidence that neurons express MDA5 protein.

findings.claim: The neuron-low / endothelial-high ordering is NOT a sequencing-depth or nucleus-capture artifact: in the Siletti atlas neurons have the largest libraries of any cell class (median 18,644 UMI/nucleus) yet the lowest IFIH1 detection rate (1.28%), while endothelial nuclei have the smallest libraries (median 3,058 UMI) and the highest detection rate (24.2%).
findings.evidence: Own per-cell-type median/mean library size from Census raw counts in 'Human Brain Cell Atlas v1.0' (disease=normal): neuron median 18,644 / mean 23,586 UMI, 1.28% IFIH1-positive, CP10k 0.0067; choroid plexus epithelial median 15,374, 10.02% positive; ependymal median 5,621, 5.68%; OPC median 5,642, 4.38%; astrocyte median 4,635, 3.86%; oligodendrocyte median 4,025, 2.21%; fibroblast median 3,003, 6.91%; endothelial median 3,058, 24.18%, CP10k 1.055. Depth and detection run in OPPOSITE directions, so the ranking survives. Independently, whole-CELL (not nucleus) Census suspensions give the same order (endothelial 0.123 > microglia 0.121 > astrocyte 0.071-0.099 > oligodendrocyte 0.059 > neurons 0.003-0.020 CP10k), so single-nucleus under-detection of cytoplasmic mRNA compresses absolute values but does not invert the ranking.

CP10k (% positive; n nuclei): perivascular macrophage 0.7997 (8.86%; 429); endothelial cell of artery 0.7755 (13.03%; 2,678); capillary endothelial 0.6991 (11.17%; 3,419); vein endothelial 0.6184 (19.84%; 1,744); T cell 0.6005 (5.33%; 488); microglial cell 0.3955 (15.14%; 2,985); fibroblast 0.2389; pericyte 0.1729; smooth muscle 0.1690; astrocyte 0.1679; oligodendrocyte 0.1081; OPC 0.0857; GABAergic neuron 0.0332; glutamatergic neuron 0.0297. In the pan-Census nucleus table the same segment ordering appears: capillary EC 0.835, arterial EC 0.784, vein EC 0.618, cerebral cortex EC 0.612.

findings.claim: The human reference resources AGREE almost perfectly on the CNS cell-type ranking: Spearman rho = 0.96-1.00 across HPA single-cell, HPA brain single-nuclei (Siletti), CELLxGENE Census pan-brain, Census-Siletti, and Zhang 2016 immunopanned bulk, over 10 shared CNS cell types. Mouse bulk is only moderately concordant (rho 0.60-0.70, n=5-6, p>0.15).
findings.evidence: Own Spearman correlations over the shared cell types {endothelial, microglia/CNS macrophage, pericyte, fibroblast, ependymal, OPC, astrocyte, Bergmann glia, oligodendrocyte, excitatory neuron}: HPA_snRNA vs HPA_scRNA rho=0.976 (n=10); HPA_snRNA vs Census_nucleus rho=0.976; HPA_snRNA vs Census_Siletti rho=0.988; HPA_scRNA vs Census_Siletti rho=0.988; Census_nucleus vs Census_Siletti rho=0.964; Zhang16_human vs each of the four rho=1.000 (n=5). Mouse Zhang14 vs human resources rho=0.600-0.700 (n=5-6, p=0.16-0.21). The only qualitative human disagreement is the relative position of microglia vs fibroblast/pericyte (microglia 2nd in Census pan-brain and in HPA brain scRNA, but 2nd-behind-endothelial with fibroblast 4th in HPA-Siletti), and whether Schwann cells outrank microglia (HPA 154-cell-type consensus puts Schwann 45.1 above microglia 26.7; Census has only 1,216 Schwann nuclei from a single dataset at 0.112 CP10k, below microglia's 0.340, so PNS coverage is too thin to resolve this).

findings.claim: Tabula Sapiens contributes nothing to a CNS cell-type ranking for IFIH1 because it contains no brain or spinal cord tissue.
findings.evidence: The Tabula Sapiens CELLxGENE collection comprises 35 datasets spanning 75 tissue labels; the full list contains no 'brain', 'cerebral cortex', 'cerebellum' or 'spinal cord' entry. The only neural-lineage tissues present are 'retinal neural layer', 'eye', 'posterior segment of eyeball' and 'chorioretinal region'. ('cortex of kidney' is the only 'cortex' string in the list.) Likewise no Tabula Sapiens dataset appeared among the 186 datasets in the Census tissue_general='brain' query.

research.cell_type_ranking:
YES — this angle establishes the consensus baseline ranking directly, and it is robust across five independent human resources (Spearman rho 0.96-1.00).

CONSENSUS BASELINE RANKING of IFIH1/MDA5 in human CNS, highest to lowest:
1. Vascular endothelial cells — by a wide margin (HPA brain scRNA 99.6 nCPM; HPA-Siletti snRNA 118.9 nCPM; Census nucleus 1.21 CP10k with 23.1% of 55,126 nuclei positive; Zhang 2016 bulk 6.5 FPKM). Within the vascular tree: capillary ≈ arterial ≈ venous EC all elevated.
2. Brain myeloid cells — perivascular macrophages (Census 0.55 CP10k) slightly above parenchymal microglia (Census 0.34 CP10k, 8.3% positive; HPA 26.7 nCPM; Zhang 2016 bulk 5.1 FPKM). CNS-infiltrating/resident lymphocytes (T cells 0.39 CP10k) sit in the same band.
3. Mural and mesenchymal cells — fibroblast (0.23 CP10k / 23.2 nCPM), pericyte (0.26 / 14.8), vascular smooth muscle (0.14 / 13.3), VLMC (0.14).
4. Ependymal and choroid plexus epithelium — 0.09-0.11 CP10k / 8.8-13.5 nCPM.
5. Macroglia — astrocyte ≈ OPC (0.082-0.087 CP10k / 7.5-12.3 nCPM) > oligodendrocyte (0.052-0.061 CP10k / 5.5-7.5 nCPM) > Bergmann glia (0.049-0.054). In bulk immunopanned data astrocytes 1.70 and oligodendrocytes 1.18 FPKM, i.e. ~3-4x below microglia/endothelium.
6. Neurons — LOWEST of every CNS cell class, 0.007-0.025 CP10k / 0.0-0.5 nCPM for most superclusters, i.e. ~50-150x below endothelium. Thalamic excitatory (4.7 nCPM) is the highest neuronal supercluster; hippocampal dentate granule cells the lowest (0.0 nCPM).

PNS caveat: HPA's 154-cell-type consensus places Schwann cells (45.1 nCPM) near the top, just below vascular endothelium — but that rests on peripheral-nerve scRNA-seq, and Census has only 1,216 Schwann nuclei (0.112 CP10k, below microglia). GTEx tibial nerve (11.68 TPM) is ~5x any brain region, consistent with PNS > CNS, but the resources do not settle Schwann cells' exact rank.

WHERE RESOURCES DISAGREE:
(a) Allen Brain Map is the sole outlier and is wrong for a methodological reason — its per-cluster trimmed means are identically 0.000 CPM for microglia, endothelium, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, OPC, pericytes and VLMC in BOTH human M1 10x (127 clusters) and human multiple cortical areas SMART-seq (121 clusters), because a 25% trimmed mean collapses to zero when detection is below ~25%. Do not cite Allen as evidence of absence.
(b) Antibody IHC in HPA calls cortical neurons 'Medium' and glia 'Not detected', inverting the RNA consensus; HPA itself labels this 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data', and its MS-based DVP panel reports 0 for brain neurons, astrocytes and microglia.
(c) Mouse vs human: mouse bulk (Zhang 2014) keeps endothelial > microglia > astrocyte but places neurons mid-pack and oligodendrocytes at the 0.1 FPKM floor, so mouse should not be used to argue neuronal MDA5 levels in human.
(d) Minor: microglia rank 2nd in Census pan-brain and HPA brain scRNA but 2nd-with-fibroblast-close in HPA-Siletti; the vascular > myeloid > mural > macroglia >> neuron block structure is identical in all.
research.gaps:
1. ALLEN BRAIN MAP gave no usable numbers. Both human trimmed-mean matrices return exactly 0.000 CPM for all glial and vascular clusters (artifact of the trimmed-mean statistic). I did not obtain per-cell fraction-positive or mean-CPM values from the Allen ABC Atlas / Siletti-through-Allen route; I got equivalent information only by recomputing from the Siletti data in CELLxGENE Census. Allen's medians.csv would be zero for the same reason and was not downloaded.

2. TABULA SAPIENS has no brain or spinal cord tissue at all, so it cannot contribute a CNS cell-type value. I did not compute IFIH1 for its 'retinal neural layer' or 'vasculature' compartments.

3. brainrnaseq.org's OWN human CSV endpoint (fe-wp-dataset-124.csv) returned HTTP 504 on every attempt; I substituted the underlying GEO supplementary table (GSE73721_Human_and_mouse_table.csv), which is the same Zhang 2016 data but is an ortholog-matched 15,041-gene subset with FPKM rounded to 0.1 and a detection floor of 0.1. Values below ~0.2 FPKM in that table are therefore not quantitative.

4. The Brain RNA-Seq human resource is very thinly powered for the top and bottom of the ranking: endothelial n=2 samples, microglia n=3, and NEURON n=1 (a single 25yo cortex sample). The neuron FPKM of 0.8 from that resource should not be treated as a reliable point estimate; the single-cell resources (millions of neurons) carry the weight there.

5. NO ABSOLUTE PROTEIN QUANTIFICATION exists for MDA5 in human CNS cell types in any reference resource I could retrieve. HPA DVP reports intensity 0 (below detection) for brain neurons/astrocytes/microglia, and HPA IHC is explicitly flagged as inconsistent with RNA. I found no targeted-MS, western-blot-quantified or flow-cytometry protein dataset giving per-cell-type MDA5 protein levels in human brain. All rankings above are mRNA rankings.

6. GTEx v10 provides no single-cell or cell-type-resolved brain data, and the GTEx v10 single-cell pilot was not queried. GTEx brain values are composition-weighted homogenate averages.

7. BASELINE vs INDUCED is only partly separable from these resources. Every value reported here is steady-state/normal tissue. The single exception I could quantify is Zhang 2016's tumor/peri-tumoral astrocytes (~4-5x baseline astrocyte IFIH1), which is a disease context, not a controlled IFN stimulation. None of these reference resources contains an IFN-alpha/beta- or poly(I:C)-stimulated human CNS cell-type arm, so the induction amplitude per CNS cell type is NOT established by this angle.

8. Allen Human Brain Atlas microarray (Hawrylycz 2012, 6 donors, regional) was not retrieved; regional coverage rests on GTEx, HPA (193 subregions) and FANTOM5 CAGE instead.

9. PNS coverage is thin everywhere. Schwann cells appear at 45.1 nCPM in HPA's whole-body consensus but with only 1,216 Schwann nuclei in Census (single dataset). No resource I retrieved gives satellite glia, DRG neurons or enteric glia values for IFIH1.

10. This angle says nothing about MS disease. It establishes the normal baseline ranking only; the MS-vs-control comparison is a separate angle.

verdicts.claim: HPA single-cell consensus (154 cell types) IFIH1 nCPM ranking across neural cell types; neurons ~50-100x below vascular/myeloid
verdicts.reason: I read the actual downloaded rna_single_cell_type.tsv. Every one of the 14 quoted nCPM values is exact (vascular endothelial 48.5, Schwann 45.1, microglia 26.7, lymphatic endothelial 20.3, Muller glia 16.0, pericyte 11.9, ependymal 10.1, astrocyte 7.9, OPC 7.5, Bergmann 5.9, oligodendrocyte 5.5, brain excitatory 0.5, inhibitory 0.4, other 0.2). File contains exactly 154 cell types; neutrophils 129.2 is the whole-body maximum. The HPA API independently confirms 'Cell type enhanced' with specific nCPM {Neutrophils 129.2, Late spermatids 93.1, Early spermatids 88.5} and tissue-specific nTPM {bone marrow 34.6}. THREE DEFECTS, all minor: (a) three rank positions are off by 1-2 from tie-handling (OPC is 121st not 120th; inhibitory neurons 141st not 142nd; retinal horizontal cells 150th not 148th); (b) the '~50-100x' spread understates the real range, which is 53x (microglia/excitatory) to 242x (endothelial/other-brain-neuron); (c) 'cell-type Tau = 0.47' is NOT verifiable — the HPA API returns 'RNA single cell type specificity score = None' and the gene XML (632 KB) contains no Tau field at all.
verdicts.corrected_claim: HPA single-cell consensus (rna_single_cell_type.tsv, 154 cell types, pseudobulk nCPM) ranks IFIH1 across neural cell types as vascular endothelial 48.5 > Schwann 45.1 > microglia 26.7 > lymphatic endothelial 20.3 > Muller glia 16.0 > pericyte 11.9 > ependymal 10.1 > astrocyte 7.9 > OPC 7.5 (rank 121) > Bergmann glia 5.9 > oligodendrocyte 5.5 >> brain excitatory neuron 0.5 (rank 140) > brain inhibitory neuron 0.4 (rank 141) > other brain neuron 0.2 nCPM. verdicts.claim: HPA brain scRNA dataset (19 cell types): vascular endothelial 99.6, brain macrophages 64.1, microglia 26.7, astrocytes 7.9, oligodendrocytes 5.5, neurons 0.2-0.5 nCPM despite neurons being most numerous

verdicts.corrected_claim: In HPA's brain scRNA panel (19 cell types, whole-cell scRNA-seq), IFIH1 is highest in vascular endothelial cells (99.6 nCPM, 2,269 cells) and brain macrophages (64.1, 249 cells), with microglia 26.7, astrocytes 7.9, oligodendrocytes 5.5 and all three neuronal classes 0.2-0.5 nCPM despite neurons comprising ~85% of the cells profiled. verdicts.claim: HPA brain single-NUCLEI section built on Siletti et al. 2023: endothelial 118.9, CNS macrophage 35.5, leukocyte 30.2 ... Bergmann 5.4; all 21 neuronal superclusters 0.0-4.7 nCPM

One cosmetic HPA inconsistency, not the researcher's error: the page prose calls the unit nTPM while the chart tooltips call it nCPM.

HPA's brain single-nuclei panel (34 cluster types, built on Siletti et al. 2023, 10x 3' v3 snRNA-seq) gives endothelial cell 118.9 nCPM, CNS macrophage 35.5, leukocyte 30.2, fibroblast 23.2, pericyte 14.8, ependymal 13.5, VSMC 13.3, OPC 12.3, astrocyte 11.6, choroid plexus epithelial 8.8, oligodendrocyte 7.5, committed OPC 5.6, Bergmann glia 5.4, with all 21 neuronal superclusters between 0.0 and 4.7 nCPM.

verdicts.claim: Recomputing IFIH1 from raw Siletti counts (3,240,567 nuclei, 4 donors) 'reproduces HPA's ranking exactly' and shows HPA nCPM is a ~110x constant multiple of CP10k, 'confirming the two pipelines agree on both rank and relative magnitude'
verdicts.reason: The measurements are right; the agreement claim is false. I recomputed CP10k from the researcher's raw per-cell Census export and reproduced EVERY value to 4 decimals (endothelial 1.0553/24.18%, leukocyte 0.3178, CNS macrophage 0.2962/6.79%, fibroblast 0.2307, pericyte 0.1512, VSMC 0.1403, ependymal 0.1108, choroid plexus 0.0993, OPC 0.0849, astrocyte 0.0822/3.86%, Bergmann 0.0538, oligodendrocyte 0.0523/2.21%, neuron 0.0067/1.28% of 2,375,157) and confirmed 3,240,567 primary nuclei and 4 donor IDs. But 'reproduces HPA's ranking exactly' is REFUTED by the claim's own numbers: 9 of the 12 shared non-neuronal cell types sit at a DIFFERENT rank, Spearman rho = 0.958, not 1.0. Four inversions: leukocyte/CNS-macrophage swap; ependymal/VSMC swap; choroid plexus jumps from HPA rank 10 to Census rank 8, overtaking OPC and astrocyte; oligodendrocyte/Bergmann swap. Relatedly, the scale factor is NOT 'roughly constant': including choroid plexus (which the claim omitted) it spans 88.6 to 144.9, a 1.63-fold spread — and that spread is precisely what produces the inversions, so it cannot also be evidence of magnitude agreement. Separately, Siletti et al. describe three postmortem donors; the 4 donor IDs are a property of the CELLxGENE deposit, not the paper.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Recomputing IFIH1 from raw counts in the Siletti atlas (CELLxGENE Census, 3,240,567 primary nuclei, 4 deposited donor IDs, 10x 3' v3) gives endothelial 1.055 CP10k (24.2% positive), leukocyte 0.318, CNS macrophage 0.296, fibroblast 0.231, pericyte 0.151, VSMC 0.140, ependymal 0.111, choroid plexus 0.099, OPC 0.085, astrocyte 0.082, Bergmann glia 0.054, oligodendrocyte 0.052, neuron 0.0067. This broadly but not exactly reproduces HPA's ordering (Spearman rho = 0.958 over 12 shared types; 9 of 12 differ in rank, with leukocyte/CNS-macrophage, ependymal/VSMC and oligodendrocyte/Bergmann swapping and choroid plexus moving up two places). The HPA-nCPM-to-CP10k ratio varies from 88.6 to 144.9 (1.63x), so the two pipelines agree on the broad ordering and on endothelial dominance, but not on fine rank or relative magnitude. Note the paper itself reports three donors.

verdicts.claim: Across the whole CELLxGENE Census human brain corpus (186 datasets, 18,539,831 normal cells), single-nucleus ranking endothelial 1.210 > perivascular macrophage 0.552 > T cell 0.388 > microglia 0.340 > ... >> glutamatergic neuron 0.025 CP10k; whole-cell gives same order

Across CELLxGENE Census human brain (186 datasets, 18,539,831 normal cells/nuclei; the nucleus subset is 150 datasets and 14,093,475 nuclei), the single-nucleus ranking is endothelial 1.210 CP10k > perivascular macrophage 0.552 > T cell 0.388 > microglia 0.340 > CNS macrophage 0.319 > pericyte 0.258 > fibroblast 0.230 > VLMC 0.144 > ependymal 0.110 > astrocyte 0.087 > OPC 0.084 > oligodendrocyte 0.061 >> glutamatergic neuron 0.025, with whole-cell suspensions preserving the order at lower absolute values. verdicts.claim: Brain RNA-Seq (Zhang/Barres human, GSE73721) IFIH1 FPKM: endothelial 6.5 > microglia 5.13 > astrocyte 1.70 > oligodendrocyte 1.18 > neuron 0.8; 'agrees perfectly with all single-cell resources on rank order (Spearman rho = 1.00)'
verdicts.reason: Every number is exact — I verified the Ifih1 row of GSE73721 directly. Per-sample endothelial 7.9/5.1 (mean 6.5); myeloid 6.0/4.3/5.1 (mean 5.133); the twelve mature cortical astrocyte values are identical to the claim's list in order (mean 1.70); hippocampal astrocyte 1.3/0.8/1.1/1.8 (1.25); oligodendrocyte 1.1/1.3/1.1/1.3/1.1 (1.18); fetal astrocyte 2.1/0.1/1.0/0.1/3.8/0.1 (1.20); neuron 0.8; whole cortex 1.0/1.5/0.9/1.8 (1.30). But the agreement language overstates three ways. (1) 'All single-cell resources' is false — Allen Brain Map is a single-cell resource and disagrees, as the researcher's own Claim 9 concedes. (2) rho = 1.00 over n=5 is the maximum value attainable on five points (p about 0.017) and rests on n=1 for neurons (a single 25yo sample) and n=2 for endothelium. (3) Most importantly, agreement is on RANK ONLY, not magnitude: here neurons sit ~8x below endothelium and only ~2x below astrocytes (0.8 vs 1.70, overlapping the astrocyte range of 0.8-2.4), whereas the single-cell resources put neurons 100-200x below endothelium. Also two purity overstatements: CLDN5 is not '<=0.2 elsewhere' (fetal ctx 6 astro = 2.4), and CX3CR1 myeloid specificity is undercut by 22yo ctx oligo = 104.5, comparable to myeloid 116.7.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Brain RNA-Seq (Zhang 2016 immunopanned human, GSE73721) gives IFIH1 FPKM endothelial 6.5 (n=2) > microglia/macrophage 5.13 (n=3) > mature cortical astrocyte 1.70 (n=12) > hippocampal astrocyte 1.25 (n=4) > fetal astrocyte 1.20 (n=6) > oligodendrocyte 1.18 (n=5) > neuron 0.8 (n=1); whole cortex 1.30 (n=4). This bulk resource reproduces the RANK ORDER of the human single-cell resources over the five shared cell types (Spearman rho = 1.00, n=5, p about 0.017), but not the magnitude: neurons are only ~8x below endothelium and overlap the astrocyte range here, versus 100-200x below in scRNA/snRNA. It does not agree with Allen Brain Map. Neuron and endothelial estimates rest on 1 and 2 samples respectively.

verdicts.claim: Astrocytes from glioblastoma cores AND peri-tumoral tissue carry ~4-5x more IFIH1 than healthy cortical astrocytes (mean 6.9, median 8.05 vs 1.70 FPKM), showing astrocytic IFIH1 is strongly inducible
verdicts.reason: The arithmetic is exact (I confirmed 0.1/9.6/11.4/6.5, mean 6.9, median 8.05, versus healthy mean 1.70; and DDX58 tumor mean 5.80 vs healthy cortical astrocyte mean 2.983). Two real defects. (1) DIRECT MISSTATEMENT: the claim says cores 'and peri-tumoral tissue' carry 4-5x more, but the single peri-tumoral sample is 0.1 FPKM — sitting on the dataset's detection floor, roughly 17x BELOW healthy astrocytes, the opposite direction. The elevation is confined to the three tumor-CORE samples, and the '4-5x' mean is computed with that contradicting sample included, which actually drags it down.
