(2) 'Strongly inducible' is an inference the design cannot support: this is a cross-sectional comparison of immunopanned astrocytes from different donors in a glioblastoma microenvironment versus healthy cortex, with no interferon challenge, no paired baseline, n=3 cores versus 12 controls, and no p-value or statistical test reported anywhere. It demonstrates an association with tumor context, not induction. To the researcher's credit, purity markers in the same samples are reassuring (tumor-core SNAP25 1.4-11.4, MBP 3.9-9.3, CX3CR1 0.1-1.9), so myeloid or neuronal contamination is unlikely to explain it.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In GSE73721, astrocytes immunopanned from three glioblastoma CORES carry markedly more IFIH1 than the 12 healthy mature cortical astrocyte samples (9.6, 11.4 and 6.5 FPKM versus mean 1.70, range 0.8-2.4), an increase of roughly 4-7x per core sample. The single peri-tumoral sample is an exception at 0.1 FPKM, at the detection floor and below healthy astrocytes, so peri-tumoral tissue should NOT be included in the claim. DDX58/RIG-I shifts in the same direction (tumor 5.80 vs healthy 2.98), consistent with a coordinated ISG response rather than an IFIH1-specific artifact, and purity markers argue against contamination. No statistical test was performed (n=3 vs 12). This shows astrocytic IFIH1 is elevated in a glioblastoma microenvironment; it does not by itself demonstrate inducibility, which would require a paired interferon or dsRNA challenge.

verdicts.claim: Mouse Brain RNA-Seq (Zhang 2014, dataset 120) Ifih1 FPKM endothelial 2.10/2.01 > microglia 0.60/0.48 > OPC ~ astrocyte ~ neuron > oligodendrocytes at floor; mouse does NOT put neurons clearly last
verdicts.reason: I downloaded and parsed the same file and every value is exact to six decimals: astrocytes 0.293204/0.118981, endothelial 2.099757/2.011976, microglia_macrophage 0.601787/0.480536, myelinating oligodendrocyte 0.1/0.1, neurons 0.145805/0.677700, newly-formed oligodendrocyte 0.1/0.1, OPC 0.325703/0.108437; Ddx58 endothelial 8.485526/8.773187 vs microglia 1.623706/1.576394 and astrocytes 1.251449/1.365539. File shape is 21,636 genes x 14 samples as stated. I independently reproduced the rank correlations: mouse versus human over 5 shared types gives rho = 0.700 and over 6 types gives rho = 0.600, both with p > 0.15, exactly as claimed. The interpretive conclusion is correct and is the honest reading: mouse neuron mean (0.412) exceeds mouse astrocyte (0.206) and OPC (0.217), so neurons are not last. Two caveats the claim already half-flags: n=2 per cell type with neuron replicates differing 4.6-fold (0.146 vs 0.678), and 0.1 is a censoring floor, so 'oligodendrocytes at the floor' means not detected, not measured zero.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed as stated. Mouse Brain RNA-Seq (Zhang 2014, brainrnaseq dataset 120, n=2 replicates per cell type) gives Ifih1 FPKM endothelial 2.10/2.01 > microglia 0.60/0.48 > neuron 0.15/0.68 ~ OPC 0.33/0.11 ~ astrocyte 0.29/0.12 > myelinating and newly-formed oligodendrocytes at the 0.1 detection floor (i.e. not detected). Mouse reproduces endothelial > microglia > astrocyte but does not place neurons last, and rank concordance with the human resources is only moderate (Spearman rho 0.60-0.70, n=5-6, p > 0.15) versus 0.96-1.00 among human resources. Replicate spread is large (neuron replicates differ 4.6-fold), so the mid-rank ordering is not resolved.

verdicts.claim: Allen Brain Map disagrees, and the disagreement is an artifact of its trimmed-mean summary: IFIH1 = 0.000 CPM in every non-neuronal cluster in both human datasets
verdicts.reason: I parsed both trimmed_means.csv files myself. Human M1 10x (127 clusters): IFIH1 > 0 in exactly 3 clusters, all excitatory, at exactly the quoted values 1.7253087, 0.7529412, 0.115834706; and every named non-neuronal cluster is exactly 0.0000 (Micro L1-6 TYROBP CD74, Endo L2-5 NOSTRIN SRGN, Astro L1-6 FGFR3 AQP1, Oligo L2-6 OPALIN FTH1P3, OPC L1-6 PDGFRA COL20A1, VLMC L1-5 PDGFRA COLEC12). Multiple Cortical Areas SMART-seq (121 clusters): IFIH1 > 0 in exactly 5 clusters, all excitatory, at 2.220, 0.837, 0.457, 0.404, 0.061; Micro L1-6 C1QC, Endo L2-5 CLDN5, Peri L1-6 MUSTN1 and all Astro/Oligo/OPC/VLMC exactly 0.000. Both PMIDs are the correct papers (34616062 Bakken 2021 M1; 31435019 Hodge 2019 cortical areas). I also found INDEPENDENT support the researcher did not cite: in the M1 file the non-neuronal clusters have a nonzero trimmed mean for only 1,372-2,181 of 50,281 genes, versus 8,300-9,324 for the neuronal clusters (median 7,373 across all clusters) — so the collapse to zero is a global property of those clusters, not specific to IFIH1, which is exactly what the artifact hypothesis predicts. One limitation: I could not retrieve Allen primary documentation stating the trim is 25%-75%, so the specific numerical threshold in the mechanism is inferred rather than source-verified.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed as stated. Allen Brain Map's per-cluster trimmed means report IFIH1 = 0.000 in every non-neuronal cluster of both human datasets, with nonzero values in only 3/127 (M1 10x) and 5/121 (SMART-seq) clusters, all excitatory neurons. This is a property of the summary metric, not of the biology: a symmetric trimmed mean is identically zero whenever detection falls below the trim fraction, and measured IFIH1 detection is 8.3% in microglia and 23.1% in endothelial cells. Supporting this, the non-neuronal M1 clusters return a nonzero trimmed mean for only 1,372-2,181 of 50,281 genes versus 8,300-9,324 for neuronal clusters, i.e. the zeros are global to those clusters rather than IFIH1-specific. Allen's trimmed-mean files therefore cannot be used to rank IFIH1 or as evidence of absence. (The exact trim fraction is inferred; Allen's primary documentation was not retrievable.)

verdicts.claim: GTEx bulk RNA-seq: all 13 brain regions rank 34th-54th of 54 tissues, median TPM 0.91-4.28 vs whole-body tissue median 7.03 and max 88.19; caudal regions highest, cerebellum lowest
verdicts.reason: I queried the GTEx v10 API myself for ENSG00000115267.9 and every value matches to three decimals: Spinal_cord_cervical 4.277 (rank 34), Substantia_nigra 3.011 (40), Caudate 2.483 (42), Hypothalamus 2.430 (43), Amygdala 2.275 (44), Putamen 2.192 (45), Hippocampus 2.188 (46), Cortex 2.175 (47), Frontal_Cortex_BA9 2.167 (48), Nucleus_accumbens 1.967 (49), Anterior_cingulate 1.829 (51), Cerebellum 1.233 (52), Cerebellar_Hemisphere 0.910 (54 of 54). Top tissues confirmed: EBV-LCL 88.188, Spleen 16.853, Lung 13.564, Nerve_Tibial 11.815. The v8 cross-check is also exact (Spinal cord 4.300, Cortex 2.173, Cerebellar Hemisphere 0.956, EBV-LCL 87.030). All 13 brain regions do fall in ranks 34-54, cerebellar hemisphere is the single lowest of all 54 GTEx tissues, and the caudal-high gradient holds. ONE SMALL ERROR: the median of the 54 tissue medians is 6.97, not 7.03. The stated caveat that a bulk homogenate value is a composition-weighted average is correct and appropriately flagged.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed essentially as stated, with one correction: the whole-body median of the 54 GTEx tissue medians is 6.97 TPM, not 7.03. GTEx v10 bulk RNA-seq places all 13 brain regions at ranks 34-54 of 54 tissues (median TPM 0.910-4.277) against a maximum of 88.19 (EBV-transformed lymphocytes); cervical spinal cord is highest and cerebellar hemisphere is the lowest of all 54 GTEx tissues. Because this is polyA bulk RNA-seq of homogenate, the value is a cell-composition-weighted average.

verdicts.claim: HPA bulk brain RNA-seq agrees with GTEx on the caudal-high / cerebellum-low gradient, classifies IFIH1 'Low region specificity' (Tau 0.21), spinal cord 16.7 down to hippocampal formation 5.5 nTPM
verdicts.reason: The values are real but the headline conclusion is contradicted by the claim's own data. VERIFIED: all 13 consensus-region nTPM values are exact on the HPA brain page (spinal cord 16.7, medulla 15.5, pons 10.6, white matter 9.8, basal ganglia 9.5, choroid plexus 9.5, thalamus 9.3, hypothalamus 7.6, midbrain 7.6, cerebellum 7.3, amygdala 7.2, cerebral cortex 6.9, hippocampal formation 5.5); the HPA API confirms 'Low region specificity' and 'Detected in all'; the subregion extremes check out in rna_brain_hpa.tsv (cervical spinal cord dorsal horn 16.7 is the whole-brain maximum, nucleus gracilis 15.5, NTS 11.7, nucleus cuneatus 11.4, DLTA 10.6, dorsal motor vagal complex 10.2, choroid plexus 9.5, area postrema 9.3; lowest flocculonodular lobe 2.1, cerebellar cortex 2.2, vermis 2.3); and the cross-species numbers I could check are right (pig cerebellum 6.8, pig thalamus 4.0, mouse cerebellum 1.5, mouse thalamus 2.0). THREE DEFECTS: (1) 'Agrees with GTEx on the cerebellum-low gradient' is refuted by the claim's own list — HPA consensus puts cerebellum at 7.3, ABOVE amygdala 7.2, cerebral cortex 6.9 and hippocampal formation 5.5 (10th of 13, mid-pack), whereas GTEx ranks cerebellum and cerebellar hemisphere 52nd and 54th of 54, the lowest in the body. The two resources agree on caudal-high and disagree on cerebellum, because HPA's consensus region value tracks its highest subregion (cerebellar nuclei 7.3) while GTEx samples cerebellar cortex. (2) 'Superior frontal gyrus 0.9' does not exist in the cited rna_brain_hpa.tsv, whose 193 subregions have a MINIMUM of 2.1 and contain no 'superior frontal gyrus' row at all; the genuinely low prefrontal series (frontomarginal 1.0, ventromedial prefrontal 1.1, ventrolateral 1.3, dorsolateral 1.4, dorsomedial 1.7, frontopolar 2.1) is on the HPA web page from a different subregion set, so the claim merges two incompatible sources and quotes a value found in neither. (3) 'Tau = 0.21' is unverifiable — the HPA API returns 'RNA brain regional specificity score = None' and the gene XML has no Tau field.
verdicts.corrected_claim: HPA's bulk brain RNA-seq classifies IFIH1 as 'Low region specificity', 'Detected in all', with consensus regions spinal cord 16.7 > medulla oblongata 15.5 > pons 10.6 > white matter 9.8 > basal ganglia 9.5 = choroid plexus 9.5 > thalamus 9.3 > hypothalamus 7.6 = midbrain 7.6 > cerebellum 7.3 > amygdala 7.2 > cerebral cortex 6.9 > hippocampal formation 5.5 nTPM. It agrees with GTEx on the caudal-high gradient (cervical spinal cord dorsal horn 16.7 is the brain-wide subregion maximum) but DISAGREES on cerebellum, which HPA places mid-pack at the consensus level because its consensus tracks the highest subregion (cerebellar nuclei 7.3), even though HPA's own cerebellar-cortex subregions are the lowest in the brain (flocculonodular lobe 2.1, cerebellar cortex 2.2, vermis 2.3). In rna_brain_hpa.tsv the 193 subregions span 2.1-16.7 nTPM; the sub-2.0 prefrontal values (frontomarginal 1.0 to frontopolar 2.1) come from a different HPA subregion series, and no 'superior frontal gyrus 0.9' value could be located in either. The Tau value of 0.21 could not be confirmed.

verdicts.claim: Protein evidence in normal human brain is negative and internally inconsistent, and 'HPA itself flags it as unreliable': DVP mass-spec gives 0 in neurons/astrocytes/microglia while IHC calls 'Neuronal cells: Medium'
verdicts.reason: Every data point is exactly right; one characterisation is not. VERIFIED from the HPA pages: the DVP brain panel gives Neurons intensity 0, Astrocytes and Neuropil 0, Microglia and Neuropil 0 (all three tooltips read 'Intensity:0 Organ: Brain'); comparators Macrophages 2,720,714.2 and CD4 T-cells 1,258,734.8 confirmed, the former also via the HPA API field 'Protein cell type specific Intensity'. All four IHC annotations are verbatim: cerebral cortex 'Endothelial cells: Low, Glial cells: Not detected, Neuronal cells: Medium, Neuropil: Not detected'; hippocampus 'Glial cells: Not detected, Neuronal cells: Low'; caudate 'Glial cells: Not detected'; cerebellum 'Cells in granular layer: Not detected'. The sentence 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data.' appears verbatim. DEFECT: 'HPA itself flags it as unreliable' overstates. HPA's formal reliability score for IFIH1 IHC is 'Approved' — the third of four tiers (Enhanced > Supported > Approved > Uncertain), not 'Uncertain'. The low-consistency sentence is a standardised caveat, not a reliability downgrade. Minor second point: the Macrophage and CD4 T-cell comparators are lymph-node DVP samples, so the contrast is cross-organ rather than 'the same panel' in the brain sense. The claim's practical conclusion — that the IHC 'Neuronal cells: Medium' call should not be used as evidence neurons express MDA5 protein — remains well founded, resting on a single antibody (HPA002656) contradicted by DVP mass-spec and by every RNA resource.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Protein-level evidence for MDA5 in normal human brain is weak and internally inconsistent. HPA's Deep Visual Proteomics mass-spec panel reports intensity 0 in brain Neurons, Astrocytes and Neuropil, and Microglia and Neuropil (versus 2,720,714 in lymph-node macrophages and 1,258,735 in CD4 T-cells). Antibody IHC from a single antibody (HPA002656) reports the opposite pattern: cerebral cortex Neuronal cells Medium, Endothelial cells Low, Glial cells and Neuropil Not detected; hippocampus Neuronal cells Low, Glial cells Not detected; caudate Glial cells Not detected; cerebellum granular layer Not detected. HPA appends the standardised caveat 'Low consistency between antibody staining and RNA expression data', though its formal IHC reliability score for IFIH1 is 'Approved' (third of four tiers), not 'Uncertain'. Given the single antibody, the contradicting mass-spec result and the disagreement with every RNA resource, the IHC 'Neuronal cells: Medium' call should not be treated as evidence that neurons express MDA5 protein; no positive, cell-type-resolved protein evidence for MDA5 in normal human brain was found.

verdicts.claim: The neuron-low ordering is not a depth or nucleus-capture artifact: neurons have the largest libraries (median 18,644 UMI) yet lowest detection (1.28%), while endothelial nuclei have the smallest libraries (3,058) and highest detection (24.2%)
verdicts.reason: I recomputed per-cell-type median and mean library size and detection rate directly from the raw Census counts and every figure matches: neuron median 18,644 / mean 23,585 UMI with 1.28% positive and CP10k 0.0067; choroid plexus epithelial median 15,374 with 10.02%; ependymal 5,621 with 5.68%; OPC 5,642 with 4.38%; astrocyte 4,635 with 3.86%; oligodendrocyte 4,025 with 2.21%; fibroblast 3,003 with 6.90%; endothelial 3,058 with 24.18% and CP10k 1.055. The central argument is sound and survives: neurons have by far the deepest libraries (median 18,644, 3-6x every other cell class) and by far the lowest detection rate, so depth and detection genuinely run in opposite directions and the ranking cannot be a sequencing-depth artifact. The whole-cell Census cross-check in Claim 5 is also confirmed, so it is not a nucleus-capture artifact either. ONE FACTUAL ERROR that does not affect the argument: endothelial nuclei do NOT have the smallest libraries — leukocyte (1,990), CNS macrophage (2,454), VSMC (2,472) and pericyte (2,753) are all smaller than endothelial's 3,058.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The neuron-low / endothelial-high ordering is not a sequencing-depth or nucleus-capture artifact. In the Siletti atlas neurons have by far the largest libraries of any cell class (median 18,644 UMI/nucleus, mean 23,585) yet the lowest IFIH1 detection rate (1.28%), while endothelial nuclei are among the SMALLEST-library types (median 3,058, though leukocyte 1,990, CNS macrophage 2,454, VSMC 2,472 and pericyte 2,753 are smaller still) and have the highest detection rate (24.18%). Depth and detection therefore run in opposite directions. Independently, whole-cell Census suspensions preserve the same ordering, so single-nucleus under-capture of cytoplasmic mRNA compresses absolute values without inverting the ranking.

verdicts.claim: A vasculature-enriched CNS multiome dataset resolves the endothelial signal by vessel segment: perivascular macrophage 0.800 > arterial EC 0.776 > capillary EC 0.699 > vein EC 0.618 > T cell 0.601 > microglia 0.396 CP10k, and 'the same segment ordering appears' in pan-Census
verdicts.reason: The dataset exists and the cell types match, but the corroboration is circular and the ordering claim is self-contradicting. VERIFIED via the CELLxGENE API: the collection 'Brain vascular single-cell multi-omics elucidates disease risk associations' is a single 10x multiome snRNA dataset of 65,479 nuclei from 30 donors spanning Alzheimer disease, cognitive disorder and normal, in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex only, and its 14 cell-type labels are exactly the 14 in the claim. Subsetting to disease=normal plausibly yields the stated 21,155 nuclei / 10 donors. THREE DEFECTS: (1) The 'independent' pan-Census corroboration is CIRCULAR — the pan-Census nucleus row for vein endothelial cell is 0.6184 CP10k at 19.84% positive with n=1,744 from a SINGLE dataset, byte-identical to this multiome's vein EC figures, i.e. it is the same data; capillary EC in pan-Census (n=3,936 from 2 datasets) is ~87% the same nuclei. This cannot corroborate itself. (2) 'The same segment ordering appears' is contradicted by the claim's own two lists: the multiome gives arterial 0.776 > capillary 0.699, while pan-Census gives capillary 0.835 > arterial 0.784 — arterial and capillary swap. (3) The top five values (0.800, 0.776, 0.699, 0.618, 0.601) are separated by less than the noise floor: at median 2,075 UMI/nucleus they rest on roughly 38, 349, 382, 346 and 26 positive nuclei respectively, with no confidence intervals, so no vessel-segment ordering is actually resolved. The claim is scoped as CNS-wide vasculature but the tissue is DLPFC only.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In a single 10x multiome snRNA dataset of human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex vasculature (CELLxGENE collection 433700dc; 65,479 nuclei from 30 donors, of which ~21,155 nuclei from 10 donors are disease=normal; median ~2,075 UMI/nucleus), IFIH1 is concentrated in the vascular and myeloid compartment — perivascular macrophage 0.800, arterial EC 0.776, capillary EC 0.699, vein EC 0.618, T cell 0.601, microglia 0.396 CP10k — versus astrocytes 0.168, oligodendrocytes 0.108 and neurons 0.030-0.033. This independently reproduces the endothelial/myeloid-high, neuron-low ordering in a vasculature-enriched sample. It does NOT resolve a vessel-segment gradient: the arterial, capillary and vein values are separated by less than the sampling noise (26-382 positive nuclei each, no confidence intervals), and arterial and capillary swap order between this dataset and the pan-Census table. The pan-Census vein and capillary EC rows are drawn largely from this same dataset and therefore cannot serve as independent corroboration.

verdicts.claim: Human reference resources agree almost perfectly (Spearman rho 0.96-1.00) across HPA scRNA, HPA snRNA, Census pan-brain, Census-Siletti and Zhang 2016, over 10 shared CNS cell types
verdicts.reason: The arithmetic is correct — I reproduced rho = 0.976 for HPA_snRNA vs HPA_scRNA and rho = 0.988 for HPA_snRNA vs Census_Siletti by hand from the verified values, and rho = 0.60/0.70 for mouse. The overstatement is the word 'resources' and the implied independence. Of the five listed, only about three are independent measurements: (a) HPA brain snRNA and Census-Siletti are the SAME Siletti nuclei run through two pipelines — the researcher's own Claim 4 states this explicitly, so rho = 0.988 between them is a pipeline-concordance check, not cross-resource validation; (b) Census pan-brain CONTAINS the Siletti datasets, so Census_nucleus vs Census_Siletti (rho = 0.964) is partly self-correlation; (c) HPA's 154-cell-type consensus values for brain cell types are identical to its brain scRNA panel (microglia 26.7, astrocyte 7.9, OPC 7.5, oligodendrocyte 5.5, Bergmann 5.9 in both, as I verified), so Claims 1 and 2 are also one dataset. Additionally the Zhang16 rho = 1.000 is over n=5 with neurons represented by a single sample, and Claim 4's own full 12-type comparison gives rho = 0.958 with 9 of 12 ranks differing — lower than the 0.976-1.00 range advertised here, because the 10-type set used excludes leukocyte, VSMC and choroid plexus, which is where the inversions occur. The concession about microglia/fibroblast position and Schwann-cell coverage is fair and accurate.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The human reference data are highly concordant on the CNS cell-type ranking of IFIH1, but they constitute roughly three independent lines of evidence, not five: HPA whole-cell brain scRNA (which is also the source of the brain values in HPA's 154-cell-type consensus), the Siletti snRNA atlas (which reaches both HPA's single-nuclei panel and CELLxGENE Census, so those two agree at rho = 0.988 as a pipeline check rather than an independent replication), the broader Census pan-brain corpus (which contains Siletti), and Zhang 2016 immunopanned bulk. Across genuinely distinct measurements, Spearman rho is 0.958-0.976 over 10-12 shared cell types, with all resources placing endothelium first and neurons last. Zhang16's rho = 1.000 is over only 5 cell types with neurons represented by a single sample. Mouse bulk is only moderately concordant (rho 0.60-0.70, n=5-6, p > 0.15). Unresolved: microglia versus fibroblast/pericyte ordering, and whether Schwann cells outrank microglia (PNS coverage is too thin).

verdicts.claim: Tabula Sapiens contributes nothing to a CNS cell-type ranking for IFIH1 because it contains no brain or spinal cord tissue
verdicts.reason: I queried the CELLxGENE curation API for the Tabula Sapiens collection directly. It comprises exactly 35 datasets with 75 distinct tissue labels and 3,408,625 cells, suspension type 'cell' only. Filtering the 75 tissue labels for brain, cortex, cerebellum, cerebral, spinal, hippocampal and thalamic substrings returns exactly one hit: 'cortex of kidney' — precisely the caveat the claim itself anticipated. There is no brain, cerebral cortex, cerebellum or spinal cord entry. The dataset counts (35) and tissue-label count (75) match the claim exactly, and the assays are 10x 3' v3, 10x 5' v2, Smart-seq2 and Smart-seq3. I also confirmed from the researcher's own Census dataset listing that the tissue_general='brain' query returned 186 datasets, none of them Tabula Sapiens.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Confirmed as stated. The Tabula Sapiens CELLxGENE collection comprises 35 datasets and 3,408,625 cells across 75 tissue labels (whole-cell suspensions only), and contains no brain, cerebral cortex, cerebellum or spinal cord tissue — the only 'cortex' string in the tissue list is 'cortex of kidney'. The only neural-lineage tissues are retinal and ocular. It therefore contributes nothing to a CNS cell-type ranking for IFIH1.

verification.overall:
ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION SUMMARY — 16 claims checked against primary sources. Verdict: 10 CONFIRMED, 6 OVERSTATED, 0 REFUTED outright, 0 UNVERIFIABLE.

WHAT I DID. This was an unusually checkable claim set: the researcher left their raw intermediate files on disk, including a 155 MB per-cell CELLxGENE export with per-cell IFIH1 UMI counts and library sizes. Rather than only re-reading the cited pages, I independently RECOMPUTED the Census claims (4, 5, 13) from raw counts, re-queried the GTEx v10 API, re-fetched the live HPA brain page, re-parsed both Allen trimmed_means.csv files, re-extracted the GSE73721 and mouse brainrnaseq tables, and queried the CELLxGENE curation API for all three collections.

THE CORE FINDING SURVIVES, AND IS UNUSUALLY WELL SUPPORTED. IFIH1/MDA5 in human CNS is a vascular-endothelial and myeloid transcript with a near-absent neuronal baseline. This reproduces across genuinely independent measurements: HPA whole-cell brain scRNA (endothelial 99.6 vs neurons 0.2-0.5 nCPM), the Siletti snRNA atlas (endothelial 118.9 vs 21 neuronal superclusters at 0.0-4.7), 18.5 M cells of CELLxGENE Census (endothelial 1.210 vs glutamatergic neuron 0.025 CP10k), and Zhang 2016 immunopanned bulk (endothelial 6.5 vs neuron 0.8 FPKM). Claim 13's depth control is the strongest single piece of work here and I verified it fully from raw counts: neurons have the DEEPEST libraries of any cell class (median 18,644 UMI, 3-6x every other type) yet the LOWEST detection rate (1.28%), so the ordering cannot be a depth artifact. Claim 9's Allen-artifact diagnosis is also correct, and I found additional support the researcher did not cite — Allen's non-neuronal clusters return a nonzero trimmed mean for only 1,372-2,181 of 50,281 genes versus 8,300-9,324 for neuronal clusters, proving the zeros are a global property of those clusters rather than anything about IFIH1.

WHERE THE CLAIMS BREAK. The failures are not in the measurements — I could not find a single fabricated number in a primary-data claim — but in the language of agreement layered on top of them.

1. Claim 4 is self-refuting. It asserts the Census recomputation 'reproduces HPA's ranking exactly'. I reproduced every value to four decimals and then checked the ranking: 9 of 12 shared cell types sit at a DIFFERENT rank (Spearman rho = 0.958, not 1.0), with four clean inversions (leukocyte/CNS-macrophage, ependymal/VSMC, oligodendrocyte/Bergmann, and choroid plexus jumping two places). The companion assertion of a 'roughly constant scale factor' is contradicted by the same data: the ratio spans 88.6 to 144.9 (1.63x), and that spread is exactly what causes the inversions.

2. Claim 11 contradicts itself in a single sentence. It says HPA 'agrees with GTEx on the caudal-high / cerebellum-low gradient' and then lists cerebellum at 7.3 nTPM — ABOVE cerebral cortex (6.9) and hippocampal formation (5.5), 10th of 13 — while GTEx ranks cerebellum 52nd and cerebellar hemisphere 54th of 54 tissues, the lowest in the body. They agree on caudal-high and disagree on cerebellum. Separately, 'superior frontal gyrus 0.9' does not exist in the cited rna_brain_hpa.tsv, whose 193 subregions have a minimum of 2.1 and contain no such row; the real sub-2.0 prefrontal values come from a different HPA subregion series. This is the one claim where a quoted number could not be located in any source.

3. Claim 14's corroboration is circular. The pan-Census 'vein endothelial cell' row (0.6184 CP10k, 19.84% positive, n=1,744, one dataset) is byte-identical to the multiome's own vein EC figures — it IS the same dataset. And the two lists disagree on the very ordering being claimed (multiome arterial > capillary; pan-Census capillary > arterial). The vessel-segment gradient is not resolved; the top five values rest on 26-382 positive nuclei with no confidence intervals.

4. Claim 15 counts the same data more than once. Of five 'resources', HPA-snRNA and Census-Siletti are the same Siletti nuclei through two pipelines (Claim 4 says so), Census pan-brain contains Siletti, and HPA's 154-type consensus values for brain cell types are identical to its brain scRNA panel — so Claims 1 and 2 are one dataset too. There are about three independent human lines, not five.

5. Claim 7 makes an inducibility inference the design cannot bear, and misstates its own data: it says glioblastoma cores AND peri-tumoral tissue carry 4-5x more IFIH1, but the single peri-tumoral sample is 0.1 FPKM — on the detection floor, ~17x BELOW healthy astrocytes. The effect is confined to 3 tumour-core samples, with no IFN challenge, no paired baseline and no statistical test. This matters for the user's question because it is the one claim that speaks to inducibility, which the task brief explicitly asked to keep separate from baseline.

6. Claim 6's 'agrees perfectly with all single-cell resources' is false on its face (Allen is a single-cell resource and disagrees) and agreement is rank-only: in this bulk resource neurons sit ~8x below endothelium and overlap the astrocyte range, versus 100-200x below in scRNA.

TWO NUMBERS THAT ARE NOT IN ANY SOURCE. The Tau scores — cell-type Tau 0.47 (Claim 1) and brain-region Tau 0.21 (Claim 11) — are unverifiable. The HPA API returns 'specificity score = None' for every category and the 632 KB gene XML contains no Tau field. Both should be dropped unless separately sourced. All the accompanying categorical calls ('Cell type enhanced', 'Low region specificity', 'Detected in all') ARE confirmed via the API.

RELEVANCE TO THE USER'S ACTUAL QUESTION. For 'which neural cell types express MDA5', this claim set is a sound answer at the mRNA level and should be reported as: vascular endothelium first, CNS myeloid (microglia, perivascular/CNS macrophages) second, glia an order of magnitude lower, neurons effectively negative — with the important qualifier that this is baseline mRNA, that no positive cell-type-resolved PROTEIN evidence for MDA5 in normal human brain exists (Claim 12, correctly), and that the single IHC signal in neurons is contradicted by mass spectrometry and should not be cited. For the MS half of the user's question, note that NONE of these 16 claims addresses disease — they are all normal-tissue reference atlases, and the tumour-astrocyte result in Claim 7 is the only disease-adjacent datapoint and is the weakest claim in the set. Any MS-specific conclusion must come from the GSE180759/GSE138614/Absinta/Schirmer analyses elsewhere in this project, not from these atlases.

research.dimension: IFIH1/MDA5 in multiple sclerosis: genetic susceptibility (GWAS and candidate-gene) versus other autoimmune diseases, plus systemic (blood/PBMC/monocyte/CSF) expression and its behaviour under interferon-beta therapy

findings.claim: IFIH1 is NOT a genome-wide-significant multiple sclerosis susceptibility locus. In the definitive IMSGC 2019 genomic map (47,429 MS cases, 68,374 controls; 200 non-MHC autosomal variants, 1 chrX, 32 MHC variants), there is no associated variant anywhere in the IFIH1 region.
findings.evidence: I programmatically retrieved all associations for GWAS Catalog study GCST009597 (= IMSGC 2019, PMID 31604244) via the EBI REST API: 333 association records returned. Filtering variant coordinates for chromosome 2 between 160,000,000 and 165,000,000 bp (GRCh38) returned ZERO variants. IFIH1 spans chr2:162,267,079-162,318,703 (GRCh38, cytoband 2q24.2, per GTEx reference API). IFIH1 is therefore absent both from the 200 genome-wide-significant autosomal variants and from any prioritized-gene call at a 2q24 locus.

findings.claim: The GWAS Catalog contains zero multiple-sclerosis associations for any IFIH1 variant, while the same variants are genome-wide significant for at least six other autoimmune diseases.
findings.evidence: Direct EBI GWAS Catalog REST queries. rs1990760 (A946T, missense): 34 association records — type 1 diabetes (A allele OR 1.18 [1.11-1.23], p=2e-11; C allele OR 0.89 [0.86-0.91], p=2e-15; OR 1.2, p=2e-14), psoriasis (T allele OR 1.18 [1.12-1.25], p=1e-8; OR 1.19 [1.12-1.28], p=1e-7), SLE (T allele OR 1.15, p=4e-8; OR 1.17, p=3e-7), autoimmune thyroid disease (T OR 1.075, p=1e-14; C OR 0.94, p=7e-9; a third study p=9e-41), inflammatory bowel disease (G OR 1.095 [1.063-1.127], p=1e-9; G OR 1.066 [1.044-1.090], p=6e-9), selective IgA deficiency (T OR 1.43, p=4e-15) — and NOT ONE multiple sclerosis entry. rs3747517: 4 records — psoriasis (T OR 1.30 [1.22-1.37], p=1e-18; T OR 1.33 [1.23-1.45], p=3e-11), a cross-disease AS/Crohn/psoriasis/PSC/UC study (p=2e-9), anti-NMDAR encephalitis (C OR 1.55 [1.34-1.80], p=1e-8) — no MS. rs2068330: 1 record (cognitive domain measurement, p=3e-8) — no MS.

findings.claim: Open Targets Platform assigns IFIH1-multiple sclerosis an association score of 0.0162 supported by LITERATURE ONLY, with a genetic_association datatype score of exactly zero (the datatype is absent). This is 10-50x lower than IFIH1's scores for T1D, psoriasis, SLE, IBD and autoimmune thyroid disease, all of which carry substantial genetic evidence.
findings.evidence: GraphQL query to api.platform.opentargets.org for target ENSG00000115267 x disease MONDO_0005301: overall score 0.016216, datatypeScores = [{literature: 0.1334}] only — no genetic_association entry. By contrast, from the same API for IFIH1: Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome 7 score 0.821 (genetic_association 0.935); Singleton-Merten syndrome 1 score 0.779 (genetic 0.859); psoriasis 0.581 (genetic 0.757); type 1 diabetes 0.467 (genetic 0.721, literature 0.929); IBD 0.452 (genetic 0.721); SLE 0.405 (genetic 0.615); Hashimoto thyroiditis 0.407 (genetic 0.660); vitiligo 0.390 (genetic 0.614); autoimmune thyroid disease 0.365 (genetic 0.594). MS does not appear in IFIH1's top-30 associated diseases.

findings.claim: The only original positive MS report (Martinez 2008, Spanish) was driven by rs2068330, which lies in KCNH7 ~46-99 kb outside IFIH1, not by the IFIH1 missense variant rs1990760 — which was non-significant in that same study.
findings.evidence: Martinez et al., Eur J Hum Genet 2008;16(7):861-4. 412 MS patients + 535 ethnically matched controls, 4 SNPs (rs13422767, rs2111485, rs1990760, rs2068330), TaqMan MGB. rs2068330 G vs C: P=0.001, OR 0.73 (95% CI 0.60-0.88); allele counts controls 660 C (61.7%)/410 G (38.3%) vs MS 568 C (68.9%)/256 G (31.1%). rs1990760: P=0.07, OR 0.84 (0.70-1.02); controls 630 A (58.9%)/440 G (41.1%) vs MS 523 A (63%)/307 G (37%). The authors explicitly state that strong LD in the region 'hampered further localization of the etiologic gene' among IFIH1, GCA and KCNH7. GWAS Catalog genomic context places rs3747517 46,449 bp downstream of GCA and 99,093 bp from the next gene, i.e. the associated SNPs are intergenic relative to IFIH1's coding span.

findings.claim: The Martinez signal failed replication in a well-powered independent family-based French cohort: both rs1990760 and rs2068330 were null by TDT.
findings.evidence: Couturier et al., Eur J Hum Genet 2009;17(6):844-7. 591 French Caucasian MS trio families (412 female, 176 male probands), transmission/disequilibrium test. rs1990760: allele A transmitted 287 (51.6%) vs untransmitted 269 (48.4%), P=0.45. rs2068330: allele C transmitted 283 (52.4%) vs untransmitted 257 (47.6%), P=0.27. Haplotype analysis all P>0.30. No association after stratification for HLA-DRB1*1501 carriage. Reported power 79.5% at alpha=0.05 (87.3% at alpha=0.10) to detect genotype relative risks of 1.73 (homozygotes)/1.16 (heterozygotes).

findings.claim: The rare IFIH1 loss-of-function variant that most strongly protects against type 1 diabetes (rs35667974, Ile923Val) has no effect on MS risk, tested at 99% power in 3,037 cases and 10,657 controls.
findings.evidence: Bergamaschi et al., J Neuroimmunol 2010;221(1-2):112-4. 3,037 MS patients + 10,657 healthy controls from Italy and the UK; study explicitly reports 99% power to detect association at the 5% level for this rare variant. Conclusion: 'the nsSNP rs35667974/Ile923Val does not have a role in susceptibility to MS.' This is the direct MS test of the variant Nejentsev 2009 used to establish IFIH1 causality in T1D.

findings.claim: The largest IFIH1 meta-analysis to date finds the MS association with rs1990760 to be flatly null (OR 1.03), overturning an earlier smaller meta-analysis that had reported OR 1.181.
findings.evidence: Xiao et al., Front Immunol 2023;14:1051247 (35 studies, 70,966 cases / 124,509 controls overall). MS subgroup, rs1990760 A vs G allele model: OR = 1.03, 95% CI 0.93-1.14, p>0.05, from 7 studies with 5,674 MS cases and 11,163 controls. MS subgroup, rs3747517 C vs T: OR = 1.19, 95% CI 1.07-1.32, p=0.002, but from only 2 studies (1,679 cases / 1,666 controls). Overall autoimmune pooled: rs1990760 A OR 1.09 (1.01-1.17); rs3747517 C OR 1.24 (1.15-1.25); in Caucasians rs3747517 OR 1.29 (1.18-1.41). For contrast, T1D subgroup rs1990760 OR 1.12 (0.93-1.36) n.s. across 12 studies but rs3747517 OR 1.30 (1.11-1.52), p=0.001; SLE rs1990760 OR 1.08 (0.93-1.25) n.s., rs3747517 OR 1.19 (1.09-1.29), p<0.001. The earlier Cen et al., Autoimmunity 2013;46(7):455-62 meta-analysis reported MS T-allele OR 1.181 (1.062-1.313) but rested on only 2 MS comparisons, alongside T1D 1.184 (1.142-1.229), SLE 1.143 (1.073-1.217), RA 1.115 (1.004-1.239).

findings.claim: The residual MS candidate-gene signal for rs3747517 traces almost entirely to one Danish study whose nominal p-values do not survive correction for the 42 SNPs tested.
findings.evidence: Enevold et al., J Neuroimmunol 2009;212(1-2):125-31. 963 MS patients vs 960 controls, 42 SNPs across TLR1-10, NOD1-2, DDX58 and IFIH1. Reported: IFIH1-rs3747517 trend test P=0.002 and IFIH1-rs1990760 P=0.014. Bonferroni threshold for 42 tests is 0.05/42 = 0.00119, so rs1990760 clearly fails and rs3747517 (P=0.002) does not reach it either. The abstract presents these as 'support for previous findings' without multiple-testing correction. Two further cohorts are null: Varzari et al., J Neuroimmunol 2014;277(1-2):140-4, 716 German MS patients vs 706 controls, 18 SNPs in IFIH1/DDX58(RIG-I)/DHX58(LGP2)/MAVS(VISA) — 'did not reveal significant single-SNP associations with MS risk' (only two MAVS SNPs modestly linked to age of onset, plus a claimed combinatorial RIG-I/LGP2/IFIH1 effect). Wawrusiewicz-Kurylonek et al., Immunobiology 2020;225(1):151864 reported rs1990760 T allele MS OR = 1.36, p = 2.17e-02 in only 171 Polish MS patients vs 400 controls — nominal significance in a very small cohort, and in the same paper LADA gave OR 3.36, p=8.73e-07 and Graves' disease OR 1.34, p=7.02e-03.

findings.claim: In type 1 diabetes, by contrast, IFIH1 is an established CAUSAL gene with both a common missense variant and four independent rare protective variants; the direction is that reduced MDA5 function protects.
findings.evidence: Smyth et al., Nat Genet 2006;38(6):617-9: in 4,253 cases, 5,842 controls and 2,134 parent-child trios, the minor allele of rs1990760 A->G (A946T) had risk ratio 0.86 (95% CI 0.82-0.90) at P = 1.42e-10 — the sixth T1D locus identified. Nejentsev et al., Science 2009;324(5925):387-9: resequencing exons/splice sites of 10 candidate genes in pools of 480 patients / 480 controls, tested in >30,000 participants, found four rare IFIH1 variants each independently lowering T1D risk, odds ratios 0.51 to 0.74, P = 1.3e-3 to 2.1e-16; variants predicted to reduce IFIH1 expression or disrupt MDA5 structure. This is the archetypal demonstration that IFIH1 loss of function is protective in an autoimmune disease.

findings.claim: The only direct measurement of MDA5 transcript in MS patient blood versus healthy controls that I could locate reports MDA5 mRNA significantly DECREASED in MS — the opposite direction to the usual 'interferon signature' expectation — and shows IFN-beta-1a does NOT raise it at 6 months.
findings.evidence: Asadikaram et al., Biotechnol Appl Biochem 2021;68(2):267-271 (Epub 2020 May 25). Peripheral leukocytes from 30 newly diagnosed MS patients vs 35 healthy controls, RT-qPCR for MDA5 (IFIH1) and RIG-I (DDX58). 'mRNA levels of MDA5 and RIG-1 were significantly decreased in the MS patients in comparison to the healthy controls.' Repeat measurement 6 months after standard-dose IFN-beta-1a: 'IFN-beta 1a therapy leads to the upregulation of RIG-1, but not MDA5, in the total MS patients and the female group.' CAVEAT: small single-centre Iranian cohort; the abstract gives no fold-change, delta-Ct or p-value figures and I could not obtain the full text, so the effect size is unquantified. This is a single unreplicated study and should not be treated as settled.

findings.claim: IFIH1 is elevated at baseline specifically in the ~18% subgroup of untreated RRMS patients who carry a high endogenous type I interferon signature (MX1-high), and in that subgroup IFN-beta fails to induce it further — a pharmacodynamic ceiling effect.
findings.evidence: Hundeshagen et al., J Neuroinflammation 2012;9:140 (PMID 22727118). 61 RRMS patients, PBMC, Affymetrix HG-U133 A/B or Plus 2.0. MX1-high defined as baseline MX1 signal intensity >3,000 (two standard errors above the mean); 11 of 61 patients (18%) qualified. Baseline: 'Elevated transcript levels were found for cytoplasmic receptors (for example, IFIH1), TFs (for example, IRF7, IRF9 and STAT1)' in MX1-high vs MX1-low; the paper also names 'The receptors IFIH1, DDX58 and ZBP1, two ISGs (CXCL10, ISG20)'. Statistics: Wilcoxon rank-sum test, significance threshold P<0.01. After 1 month of IFN-beta, IFIH1 was significantly upregulated in MX1-low patients but remained unmodulated in MX1-high patients. Treatment arms: sc IFN-beta-1a n=12, sc IFN-beta-1b n=25, im IFN-beta-1a n=24. LIMITATION: the paper reports mean expression comparisons, not per-gene fold-changes, so no numeric fold-change for IFIH1 is available, and IFIH1 was not separately qPCR-validated.

findings.claim: IFIH1 is a durable, reproducible IFN-beta pharmacodynamic marker in MS blood: it is one of only 15 transcripts differentially expressed at every time point across a full year of IFN-beta-1b therapy.
findings.evidence: Serrano-Fernandez et al., Autoimmunity 2010;43(2):172-8 (PMID 19883335). Microarray monitoring of 18 IFNB1b-treated MS patients at four time points spanning 1 year. 'Fifteen markers were differentially expressed during all three time points and followed a consistent time course pattern: EIF2AK2, IFI6, IFI44, IFI44L, IFIH1, IFIT1, IFIT2, IFIT3, ISG15, MX1, OASL, RSAD2, SN [SIGLEC1], XAF1 and the marker 238704_at.' Expression changes were 'both early detectable and long lasting'. By contrast IL-8 was only a short-lasting marker and STAT1 changes were delayed. Independently corroborated by Nguyen et al., J Interferon Cytokine Res 2023;43(3):108-120 (PMID 36867172): in MS PBMC, long-term PEGylated IFN-beta-1a therapy 'increased expression of antiviral and immune-regulatory genes (IFIH1, TLR8, IRF5, TNFSF10 [TRAIL], STAT3, JAK2, IL15, and RB1)'; in the same study, 6 h after injection non-PEG IFN-beta-1a upregulated 136 genes and PEG-IFN-beta-1a 85, rising at 24 h to 476 and 598 genes respectively. NEITHER paper publishes a numeric fold-change for IFIH1 in its abstract.

findings.claim: IFIH1 is a genuine but mid-tier interferon-stimulated gene: across at least six independent MS / IFN-beta transcriptomic studies it falls below the reporting cutoff while IFI44L, IFIT1, MX1, RSAD2, ISG15 and the OAS genes clear it. Conclusions about 'the MS interferon signature' should not be assumed to include IFIH1.
findings.evidence: Documented absences, each checked against the paper: (1) van Baarsen et al., PLoS One 2008;3(4):e1927 (PMID 18382694), 16 + 30 RRMS patients, PBMC microarray at baseline/1/3/6 months — IFIH1 is not among the 126 differentially expressed genes nor the 28-gene IFN-induced cluster; their 15-gene predictive set is RSAD2, IFIT1, MX1, ISG15, EPSTI1, IRF7, LY6E, OAS1, OAS3, SERPING1, IFI44L, MT2A, TRIM22, SAMD9L, OAS2. (2) Singh et al., BMC Neurol 2015 (PMID 26589141, DOI 10.1186/s12883-015-0495-x), PBMC, 104 DEGs (87 up) in IFN-treated RRMS responders (n=10) vs untreated RRMS (n=25); IFIH1 absent; top genes at 1.8-2.9 log2FC are IFI44L, IFIT1, IFI44, IFIT3, MX1, ISG15, SIGLEC1, OAS3, OAS1; pathway enrichment IFN type 1 p=1.7e-16, IFN-beta signalling p=7.4e-08. (3) Malhotra et al., PLoS One 2013;8(4):e60994 — monocytes from 20 RRMS + 10 controls, 2,241 DEGs, IFIH1 not reported. (4) Khsheibun et al., PLoS One 2014;9(7):e102331 — 115 genes >2-fold induced by IFN-beta in MS B cells/LCLs, IFIH1 absent. (5) Waschbisch et al., PLoS One 2013;8(5):e62366 (PMID 23626809) — IFN-beta-1a 100 U/ml, 16 h, 3 donors; IFIH1 not reported; monocyte top hits DEFB1 31.8-fold (p=0.0001), TNFSF10 27.2-fold (p=0.003), CD80 26.9-fold, CXCL9 24.1-fold; T-cell top hits ZBP1 11.9-fold (p=0.001), TNFSF10 10-fold. (6) Ottoboni-type Interferome mapping study, Sci Rep 2017;7:9286 (PMID 28827704) — IFIH1 is not among the 21 concordantly dysregulated interferon-regulated genes in human MS blood nor the 100 validated RRMS IRGs (highlighted genes were NLRP3, ARRB1, CASP1, S100A9, MAF).

findings.claim: IFIH1 genotype does NOT predict clinical response to interferon-beta in MS: the one nominal signal (rs3747517) failed independent validation in a 1,385-patient two-stage pharmacogenomic study.
findings.evidence: Bustamante et al., Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2015;2(5):e154 (PMID 26445728). Screening phase: 384 SNPs genotyped in 830 MS patients classified as IFN-beta responders (n=416) vs non-responders (n=414). Seven SNPs advanced, including rs3747517 (IFIH1) at p=0.010. Validation cohort: 555 independent MS patients (281 responders, 274 non-responders) — 'None of these SNPs were significantly associated with IFN-beta response when genotyped in an independent cohort.' Combined analysis of all 1,385 patients retained only rs2277302 (PELI3, p=0.008) and rs832032 (GABRR3, p=0.006); IFIH1 dropped out. Concordantly, Enevold et al., Mult Scler 2010;16(8):942-9 (PMID 20595247) genotyped 42 pattern-recognition-receptor SNPs (including the IFIH1 SNPs) in 567 prospectively followed IFN-beta-treated RRMS patients and found 'no significant differences between interferon-beta responders and non-responders for any of the investigated single nucleotide polymorphisms'; the only signal surviving Bonferroni was TLR6-rs5743810 for neutralizing-antibody development in males (p=0.00002, corrected p=0.02) — not IFIH1.

findings.claim: There are essentially NO IFIH1/MDA5 data from MS cerebrospinal fluid. The two largest MS CSF single-cell studies do not report IFIH1 as differentially expressed, despite both finding altered type I interferon pathway activity.
findings.evidence: (1) CSF single-cell study, Brain 2024 (PMID 38038362, DOI 10.1093/brain/awad404): 96,732 CSF cells from 33 MS patients and 48 controls. The paper reports that 'activity in pathways responsible for controlling inflammatory and type 1 interferon responses are altered in multiple sclerosis in both T cells and myeloid cells' and highlights ZC3HAV1 (rs10271373_A, increased ZAP-L isoform usage in CD8+ T cells) and IFITM2 (rs1059091_A, reduced expression in CD8+ T cells) — IFIH1, DDX58, DHX58 and MAVS are not analysed or reported. (2) Schafflick et al., Nat Commun 2020;11:247 (PMID 31937773): IFIH1 appears only as a reference marker gene imported from a rodent study, with no MS-vs-control statistic. I found no study measuring MDA5 protein in MS CSF by any method (ELISA, Western, mass spectrometry).

findings.claim: Within peripheral blood, IFIH1 is a myeloid/innate gene: Human Protein Atlas assigns it to blood expression Cluster 40 'Monocytes - Innate immune response', with neutrophils the single enhanced cell type; plasmacytoid dendritic cells are conspicuously the LOWEST expressers among leukocytes.
findings.evidence: Human Protein Atlas record for ENSG00000115267 (queried 2026-09-19): 'RNA blood cell specificity' = Low immune cell specificity; 'RNA blood cell distribution' = Detected in all; 'Blood expression cluster' = Cluster 40: Monocytes - Innate immune response; 'RNA single cell type specificity' = Cell type enhanced with specific nCPM {Neutrophils: 129.2, Late spermatids: 93.1, Early spermatids: 88.5}; 'RNA tissue specificity' = Tissue enhanced, specific nTPM {bone marrow: 34.6}. HPA consensus immune-cell nTPM values for IFIH1: neutrophil 14.1; naive B-cell 12.5; non-classical monocyte 12.4; intermediate monocyte 12.2; memory B-cell 12.2; classical monocyte 11.3; myeloid DC 11.0; T-reg 10.0; MAIT T-cell 9.0; total PBMC 7.7; memory CD4 T-cell 7.7; memory CD8 T-cell 7.1; naive CD8 T-cell 6.6; naive CD4 T-cell 6.2; basophil 4.4; eosinophil 4.4; NK-cell 3.8; platelets 2.8; plasmacytoid DC 1.6. Activation strongly induces it: activated naive CD8 T-cell 84.2 and activated naive CD4 T-cell 70.7 nTPM, i.e. ~13x and ~11x over their resting counterparts. GTEx v8 median TPM for context: EBV-transformed lymphocytes 87.03, spleen 15.87, lung 13.43, whole blood 2.79 (whole blood is low because it is dominated by anucleate erythrocytes/platelets).

findings.claim: The MS interferon-signature literature localizes the pathogenic type I IFN signal to MONOCYTES, and links it to IFN-beta treatment failure — but the specific membership of IFIH1 in that monocyte signature is NOT established in the published record I could access.
findings.evidence: Comabella et al., Brain 2009;132(Pt 12):3353-65 (PMID 19741051). Genome-wide expression profiling of PBMC from 47 MS patients treated with IFN-beta >=2 years, classified responder/non-responder on clinical criteria; validation cohort n=30. Before treatment, non-responders overexpressed type I IFN-induced genes; on treatment those genes remained unaltered in non-responders but were strongly upregulated in responders. Functional work localized the defect to monocytes: selectively increased phosphorylated STAT1 and IFNAR1 expression in non-responder monocytes at baseline, increased monocyte type I IFN secretion after TLR4 stimulation, increased endogenous type I IFN production, and elevated myeloid dendritic cell activation. CAVEAT: the full gene list is paywalled and the abstract does not enumerate the signature genes, so I could not verify whether IFIH1 is among them. Do not cite Comabella 2009 as IFIH1 evidence without checking their supplementary tables.

findings.claim: The IFIH1 A946T variant rs1990760 is a powerful modifier of systemic interferon output and of circulating myeloid cell abundance, independent of any MS association — this is the quantitative reason it matters in other autoimmune diseases.
findings.evidence: GWAS Catalog associations for rs1990760 (EBI REST): interferon lambda-1 measurement p=7e-54 (beta CI 0.086-0.11); level of bone marrow stromal antigen 2 (BST2/tetherin) in blood p=1e-24 (beta CI 0.050-0.074); galectin-9 in blood p=2e-15 (beta CI 0.028-0.046); myeloid leukocyte count T allele p=7e-24 (beta CI 0.015-0.023); monocyte percentage of leukocytes T allele p=2e-15 and p=8e-16 (beta CI 0.011-0.019 and 0.014-0.023); leukocyte quantity p=6e-17; neutrophil count T allele p=2e-12, 5e-12, 1e-14, 3e-11; eosinophil count C allele p=7e-10. Counter-evidence on direct mRNA effect: (a) Pilotto/Canani-type qPCR study, PLoS One 2013;8(12):e83451 (PMID 24386202) found NO significant IFIH1 mRNA difference across rs1990760 genotypes in human mononuclear cells — GG 5.3 (1.4-6.8) AU (n=7), GA 6.6 (1.3-7.1) (n=13), AA 1.8 (1.3-6.7) (n=7), P=0.274, but n=26 total and therefore badly underpowered; (b) J Immunol 2024 (PMID 39373578, DOI 10.4049/jimmunol.2400344) genotyped 81 healthy donors (CC n=20, CT n=40, TT n=22) and found the T-allele = higher basal ISG effect ONLY in HEK293/beta-Lox5 overexpression systems, with no genotype-dependent ISG differences in primary PBMCs after CVB3 infection or poly(I:C)/LyoVec (except IFNA2). So the variant alters MDA5 protein signalling capacity more convincingly than IFIH1 transcript abundance.

findings.claim: The only MS genetic evidence implicating IFIH1 that survives modern scrutiny is a rare-variant burden signal at the level of a 62-gene inflammasome/interferon gene SET, not at the level of IFIH1 itself.
findings.evidence: Vidmar et al., Sci Rep 2019;9(1):9171 (PMID 31235738). Whole-exome sequencing of 319 probands (familial MS, sporadic MS, controls); 62 genes in the NLRP1/NLRP3 inflammasome regulatory network screened for rare pathogenic variation. Aggregate mutational burden was increased in MS patients at p = 0.00004, most pronounced for exceedingly rare variants with high predicted pathogenicity. IFIH1 is named as one of the contributing genes (grouped under 'response to infection with DNA viruses' alongside POLR3A and DHX58), together with NLRP1/3, CASP1, RIPK2, MEFV, TYK2 and PTPRC. CRITICAL CAVEAT: no gene-level statistic, odds ratio, variant list or p-value for IFIH1 alone is reported; the p=0.00004 is a gene-set burden statistic across 62 genes in a small exome cohort. This cannot be cited as an IFIH1-MS association.

research.cell_type_ranking: Yes, partially — this angle contributes two reference datasets I pulled directly from APIs, both of which bear on how CNS cell types should be ranked. (1) HPA single-nuclei human brain, IFIH1 nCPM per cluster (queried 2026-09-19, https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000115267-IFIH1/single+cell/brain): vascular endothelial cells c-14 104.1 (n=1533), c-23 95.6 (n=299), c-22 86.2 (n=437); macrophages c-26 64.1 (n=249); T-cells c-18 30.4 (n=999); microglia c-9 28.3 (n=2534), c-3 26.0 (n=4332), c-28 18.4 (n=133); B-cells c-31 23.8 (n=38); fibroblasts c-6 19.9 (n=3214); monocytes c-27 13.9 (n=136); choroid plexus epithelium c-1 12.6 (n=5057), c-19 12.4 (n=966); NK-cells c-24 11.0; pericytes c-17 10.7 (n=1166); ependymal cells c-7 10.2 (n=2779), c-20 9.6; astrocytes c-13 10.1, c-11 9.8, c-29 8.5, c-4 5.7; OPCs c-2 8.5 (n=5049), c-8 5.6; oligodendrocytes c-5 7.1, c-12 6.9, c-30 5.2, c-15 4.9, c-16 4.2, c-10 3.3; vascular smooth muscle c-25 4.9; Bergmann glia c-0 5.9; neurons overwhelmingly lowest — brain excitatory neurons 1.7-4.8, inhibitory neurons 1.9-2.1, and in the HPA aggregated neuronal categories 0.1-4.7 (medium spiny neuron 0.1, hippocampal CA4 0.1, hippocampal dentate gyrus 0.0, cerebellar inhibitory 0.2, upper-layer intratelencephalic 0.5). HPA formally calls IFIH1 'Cell type enhanced' in brain with the enhanced cell type being 'endothelial cell' at 118.9 nCPM. Implied CNS ranking: vascular endothelium > CNS/perivascular macrophages > infiltrating lymphocytes > microglia > fibroblasts/choroid plexus/pericytes/ependyma > astrocytes ~ OPC > oligodendrocytes >> neurons. (2) GTEx v8 bulk median TPM places all brain tissue at the bottom of the body-wide range — cervical spinal cord 4.30, substantia nigra 3.02, caudate 2.49, hypothalamus 2.46, amygdala 2.27, cortex 2.17, putamen 2.17, hippocampus 2.14, frontal cortex BA9 2.12, nucleus accumbens 1.96, anterior cingulate 1.82, cerebellum 1.24, cerebellar hemisphere 0.96 — versus spleen 15.87, lung 13.43, EBV-transformed lymphocytes 87.03. Two caveats for whoever assembles the final ranking: (a) the HPA brain values are single-NUCLEI, which systematically under-counts cytoplasm-resident transcripts and is known to deplete microglial signal, so microglia at ~26-28 nCPM is probably a floor, not a ceiling; (b) IFIH1 is an ISG, so any CNS cell-type ranking is inflammation-state-dependent — the activated-vs-resting T-cell contrast in the same HPA dataset (84.2 vs 6.6 nTPM for CD8) shows roughly an order of magnitude of state-driven swing, larger than most of the between-cell-type differences listed above.
research.gaps: Substantive gaps this angle could not close. (1) NO quantitative fold-change for IFIH1 induction by IFN-beta in MS patients anywhere in the accessible literature. The three papers that name IFIH1 as an IFN-beta-responsive gene in MS blood (Serrano-Fernandez 2010 PMID 19883335; Hundeshagen 2012 PMID 22727118; Nguyen 2023 PMID 36867172) all report it qualitatively or as a membership call; none publishes a fold-change, log2FC, delta-delta-Ct or p-value for IFIH1 specifically in their abstracts or accessible text. The best indirect anchor is OMIM's note that IFN-beta enhances MDA5 expression ~3-fold more than IFN-alpha, IFN-gamma or TNF in melanoma cells/skin fibroblasts — not MS, not blood, not a fold-induction over baseline. (2) NO MDA5 PROTEIN data in MS of any kind. I found no Western blot, flow cytometry, ELISA or mass-spectrometry quantification of MDA5 protein in MS PBMC, monocytes, serum, CSF or brain. Every MS finding above is mRNA. (3) NO CSF IFIH1 data. Both large MS CSF single-cell datasets (Brain 2024, PMID 38038362, 96,732 cells; Nat Commun 2020, PMID 31937773) report type I IFN pathway alteration without reporting IFIH1, and I could not determine whether IFIH1 was tested and non-significant versus filtered out before testing — that distinction requires their supplementary differential-expression tables, which I could not retrieve. (4) The Comabella 2009 Brain monocyte IFN signature gene list (PMID 19741051) is paywalled; I could not verify whether IFIH1 is a member, so the single most-cited 'monocyte type I IFN signature in MS' result cannot currently be claimed as IFIH1 evidence. (5) The Asadikaram 2021 finding of DECREASED MDA5 in MS leukocytes (PMID 32311159) — the only direct MS-vs-control MDA5 measurement I located, and a direction-reversing one — is a single small unreplicated study whose effect size I could not obtain; it needs the full text and independent replication before being weighted. (6) No eQTLGen / BLUEPRINT cis-eQTL statistic for rs1990760 on IFIH1 expression in whole blood or sorted monocytes was retrievable through the APIs available here, so the mechanistic step from MS-irrelevant genotype to expression remains unquantified. (7) I did not verify from primary supplementary data whether IFIH1 appears among the 551 prioritized susceptibility genes in IMSGC 2019 by non-positional means (e.g. a distal regulatory link); I established only that no genome-wide-significant variant lies within 2.5 Mb of the gene, which makes prioritization essentially impossible but does not formally exclude it. (8) Effect sizes for rs3747517 in MS come from a 2-study meta-analysis subgroup whose two constituent studies I could not both identify by PMID; one is almost certainly Enevold 2009.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 is NOT a genome-wide-significant MS locus in IMSGC 2019 (GCST009597); filtering the 333 association records for chr2:160,000,000-165,000,000 (GRCh38) returned ZERO variants; IFIH1 absent from the 200 GWS autosomal variants and from any prioritized-gene call at 2q24.
verdicts.reason: I re-ran the query. GCST009597 does return 333 associations, but the chr2:160-165Mb filter does NOT return zero: rs2052401 sits at chr2:162,105,535 (p=2e-07, OR 1.0669, genomeWide=false, author-reported gene DPP4, closest genes LOC101929532/GCG/EIF3EP2, ~161 kb from IFIH1). Two further evidentiary errors: (a) GCST009597's own recorded initialSampleSize is 14,802 cases / 26,703 controls plus 74,299 replication individuals — the 47,429/68,374 figure is the Science paper's total, not this accession's; (b) only 195 of the 333 records are p<5e-8, not the 200+1+32=233 the claim implies the record contains. The 'absent from any prioritized-gene call' half was never actually tested: the 551-gene list is a supplementary table, and the claim's own method (association API only) cannot reach it. I confirmed IFIH1, DPP4 and '2q24' are absent from the IMSGC 2019 main text (PMC7241648), which supports but does not establish the gene-level claim.
verdicts.corrected_claim: IFIH1 is not a genome-wide-significant MS susceptibility locus. In GWAS Catalog study GCST009597 (IMSGC 2019, PMID 31604244; paper total 47,429 cases / 68,374 controls; 200 non-MHC autosomal + 1 chrX + 32 MHC variants), the 333 catalogued associations include exactly one variant in chr2:160-165Mb: rs2052401 at chr2:162,105,535, which is sub-genome-wide (p=2e-07, OR 1.0669, flagged genomeWide=false), is assigned by the authors to DPP4, and lies ~161 kb from IFIH1 (chr2:162,267,079-162,318,703). No genome-wide-significant variant maps to IFIH1, and IFIH1 is not named in the paper's main text. Whether IFIH1 appears in the supplementary 551-gene prioritization list was not checked.

verdicts.claim: The GWAS Catalog contains zero MS associations for any IFIH1 variant, while the same variants are genome-wide significant for at least six other autoimmune diseases.
verdicts.reason: I independently re-queried all three EBI endpoints. rs1990760: exactly 34 records, zero MS. Every quoted statistic matches: T1D OR 1.18 p=2e-11, OR 0.89 p=2e-15, OR 1.2 p=2e-14; psoriasis OR 1.18 p=1e-8 and OR 1.19 p=1e-7; SLE OR 1.15 p=4e-8 and OR 1.17 p=3e-7; autoimmune thyroid disease OR 1.0752687 p=1e-14, OR 0.94 p=7e-9, third study p=9e-41; IBD OR 1.095 p=1e-9 and OR 1.066 p=6e-9; selective IgA deficiency OR 1.4285715 p=4e-15. rs3747517: exactly 4 records (psoriasis OR 1.30 [1.22-1.37] p=1e-18; psoriasis OR 1.33 [1.23-1.45] p=3e-11; AS/Crohn/psoriasis/PSC/UC p=2e-09; anti-NMDAR encephalitis OR 1.55 [1.34-1.80] p=1e-08), zero MS. rs2068330: exactly 1 record (cognitive domain measurement, p=3e-08), zero MS. Six distinct autoimmune diseases reach genome-wide significance, as stated.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands as worded. Caveat for the reader: absence from the GWAS Catalog reflects what curators have indexed, not a formal test of the null, and the catalog indexes only genome-wide-significant/curated hits — candidate-gene MS studies of these SNPs exist and are simply not catalogued.

verdicts.claim: Open Targets assigns IFIH1-MS a score of 0.0162 from LITERATURE ONLY with genetic_association exactly zero/absent; 10-50x lower than IFIH1's scores for T1D, psoriasis, SLE, IBD and autoimmune thyroid disease.
verdicts.reason: I re-ran the GraphQL query against api.platform.opentargets.org for ENSG00000115267 x MONDO_0005301 and got score 0.016216232095068214 with datatypeScores = [{literature: 0.13337235223792707}] and no genetic_association entry — exact match. All comparator figures verified to 3-4 decimal places in the same API call: AGS7 0.8214 (genetic 0.9348), Singleton-Merten 1 0.7793 (genetic 0.8595), psoriasis 0.5813 (genetic 0.757), T1D 0.4667 (genetic 0.7212, literature 0.9293), IBD 0.4521 (genetic 0.721), SLE 0.4046 (genetic 0.6145), Hashimoto 0.4065 (genetic 0.6598), vitiligo 0.3899 (genetic 0.614), AITD 0.3646 (genetic 0.5943). MS does not appear in IFIH1's top 40 of 715 associated diseases. The stated ratios compute to 22-36x, inside the claimed 10-50x band.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands as worded. Note for interpretation: the Open Targets literature score of 0.1334 is text-mining co-occurrence, so it reflects that IFIH1 and MS are discussed together, not that any measurement links them.

verdicts.claim: The only original positive MS report (Martinez 2008) was driven by rs2068330, which lies in KCNH7 ~46-99 kb outside IFIH1, not by rs1990760, which was non-significant in that same study.
verdicts.reason: The core assertion checks out. The PubMed abstract confirms rs2068330 G vs C P=0.001, OR 0.73 (0.6-0.88), 412 MS + 535 controls, 4 SNPs, TaqMan MGB, and the LD statement verbatim. I could not reach the paywalled full text, but Xiao 2023's Table 2 reproduces Martinez's rs1990760 genotype counts (MS 170/183/62; controls 188/254/93), which yield exactly the claim's allele counts (controls 630 A / 440 G; MS 523 A / 307 G) and, on my own recomputation, OR 0.8405 and chi-square p=0.0673 — matching 'OR 0.84, P=0.07'. The same method on rs2068330 gives OR 0.7255, p=0.00105. So the numbers are sound. The POSITIONAL evidence is wrong. Per the GWAS Catalog genomic context, rs2068330 (chr2:162,380,880) is 62,196 bp from IFIH1, not '~46-99 kb'; it sits at distance 0 inside KCNH7 with GCA the closest gene at 5,484-9,285 bp. The 46,449 and 99,093 bp figures the claim cites belong to rs3747517 and are its distances to GCA and KCNH7 — not to IFIH1. And rs3747517 (chr2:162,272,314) and rs1990760 (chr2:162,267,541) both have distance 0 to IFIH1, i.e. they are INSIDE the gene, so 'the associated SNPs are intergenic relative to IFIH1's coding span' is false.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The positive signal in Martinez 2008 (PMID 18285833) came from rs2068330 (G vs C, P=0.001, OR 0.73 [0.60-0.88]), not from the IFIH1 missense variant rs1990760, which was non-significant in the same 412 MS / 535 control cohort (OR 0.84, P≈0.07; allele counts controls 630 A / 440 G, MS 523 A / 307 G). rs2068330 (chr2:162,380,880) lies within KCNH7, 62.2 kb from IFIH1, with GCA the nearest gene (~5.5-9.3 kb). The authors state that strong LD 'hampered further localization of the etiologic gene' among IFIH1, GCA and KCNH7. Note that rs1990760 and rs3747517 are both located within IFIH1 itself, so no general statement that 'the associated SNPs are intergenic relative to IFIH1' is available.

verdicts.claim: The Martinez signal failed replication in a well-powered independent family-based French cohort: both rs1990760 and rs2068330 were null by TDT.
verdicts.reason: I retrieved the PMC full text (PMC2947096) and every number matches verbatim: rs1990760 transmitted 287 A (51.6%) vs untransmitted 269 A (48.4%), P=0.45; rs2068330 transmitted 283 C (52.4%) vs untransmitted 257 C (47.6%), P=0.27; 591 French Caucasian trio families with 412 women and 176 men (three of unknown sex, F/M 2.3:1); no association after HLA-DRB1*1501 stratification; power 79.5% at alpha=0.05 and 87.3% at alpha=0.10, assuming genotype relative risks 1.73 (homozygotes) / 1.16 (heterozygotes). The three haplotypes with frequency >5% gave p=0.47, 0.32 and 0.55, consistent with 'all P>0.30'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands as worded, with the small precision that the smallest haplotype p-value is 0.32 (A-C 0.47, G-G 0.32, G-C 0.55), and that the quoted power is the study's own stated figure for the specific genotype relative risks 1.73/1.16, not a general power claim.

verdicts.claim: The rare IFIH1 loss-of-function variant most strongly protecting against T1D (rs35667974, Ile923Val) has no effect on MS risk, tested at 99% power in 3,037 cases and 10,657 controls.
verdicts.reason: The PubMed abstract (PMID 20116863) supports every element verbatim: 3,037 MS patients and 10,657 healthy controls from Italy and the UK; rs35667974/Ile923Val chosen because it 'displayed the strongest effect in T1D and was also shown to lead to a loss of IFIH1 function in an in vitro study'; 'This study has 99% power to demonstrate an association at the 5% level with this rare variant'; conclusion 'the nsSNP rs35667974/Ile923Val does not have a role in susceptibility to MS.' It is correctly framed as the direct MS test of a Nejentsev 2009 variant.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands as worded. One qualification the abstract requires: the '99% power' is the authors' stated power to detect an association 'at the 5% level' but no effect size is specified in the abstract, so the power figure cannot be re-derived from what is published there.

verdicts.claim: The largest IFIH1 meta-analysis (Xiao 2023) finds the MS association with rs1990760 flatly null (OR 1.03), overturning Cen 2013's OR 1.181.
verdicts.reason: The headline number is exact — I found the row in the PMC full text (PMC10327432): 'A vs. G MS Random 5674/11163(7) 1.03(0.93~1.14) >0.05'. Cen 2013's figures are also exact (MS T-allele OR 1.181 [1.062-1.313] from 2 MS comparisons; T1D 1.184, SLE 1.143, RA 1.115), as are Xiao's overall figures and the T1D/SLE contrasts. But the framing misrepresents the paper twice. First, Xiao explicitly states: 'it should be pointed out that HT had a low power to detect a significant association depending on the model and MS was also underpowered for the recessive and allelic models' — the OR 1.03 IS the allelic model, so this is an underpowered null presented as a refutation. Second, the same meta-analysis's own conclusion for MS is positive: 'After stratifying by diseases, T1D, SLE, and MS suggested a significant positive correlation (OR=1.30...; OR=1.19...; OR=1.19, 95% CI: 1.07~1.32; respectively, in the allele model)' for rs3747517. The claim does report the rs3747517 MS result (OR 1.19 [1.07-1.32], p=0.002, 2 studies, 1,679/1,666 — all verified) but subordinates it and then calls 'the MS association' null.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the largest IFIH1 meta-analysis (Xiao 2023, PMID 37426657; 35 studies, 70,966 cases / 124,509 controls), the MS subgroup shows no association for rs1990760 (A vs G, OR 1.03, 95% CI 0.93-1.14, p>0.05, 7 comparisons, 5,674 cases / 11,163 controls) — but the authors themselves flag the MS analysis as underpowered in the allelic model. In the SAME meta-analysis, MS IS significantly associated with rs3747517 (C vs T, OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.07-1.32, p=0.002, 2 comparisons, 1,679 cases / 1,666 controls), which the authors list alongside T1D and SLE as a significant positive correlation. So Xiao 2023 overturns Cen 2013's rs1990760 MS estimate specifically; it does not report a null 'MS association' for IFIH1 overall.

verdicts.claim: The residual MS candidate-gene signal for rs3747517 traces almost entirely to one Danish study whose nominal p-values do not survive correction for the 42 SNPs tested.
verdicts.reason: The arithmetic and the source quotes are all correct. Enevold 2009 (PMID 19450885): 963 MS vs 960 controls, 42 SNPs across TLR1-10/NOD1-2/DDX58/IFIH1, rs3747517 P=0.002 and rs1990760 P=0.014, presented as 'support for previous findings' with no correction; 0.05/42=0.00119, so both fail. Varzari 2014 (PMID 25288302): 716 vs 706, 18 SNPs in IFIH1/RIG-I/LGP2/VISA, 'did not reveal significant single-SNP associations with MS risk', two VISA SNPs with age of onset, combinatorial claim — verbatim. Wawrusiewicz-Kurylonek 2020 (PMID 31733941): MS OR 1.36 p=2.17e-02 in 171 MS vs 400 controls, LADA OR 3.36 p=8.73e-07, GD OR 1.34 p=7.02e-03 — verbatim. But 'traces almost entirely to one Danish study' is wrong. Xiao 2023's Table 2 shows the pooled rs3747517 MS estimate rests on TWO cohorts, and from the raw genotypes I computed allelic ORs of 1.25 for Enevold and 1.11 for Varzari — i.e. the very study the claim cites as null counter-evidence has a same-direction point estimate; it is null through lack of power, not through opposite direction. The claim also omits the most powerful negative result available: IMSGC 2009 (Genes Immun 10:11-14, PMID 18987646) tested rs1990760 among 7 T1D SNPs in 2,369 trios + 5,737 cases + 10,296 controls and found only CLEC16A and CD226 associated.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The MS candidate-gene signal for IFIH1 rests on nominally significant results that do not survive multiple-testing correction. Enevold 2009 (963 MS vs 960 controls, 42 SNPs) reported rs3747517 P=0.002 and rs1990760 P=0.014 against a Bonferroni threshold of 0.00119, and presented them as 'support for previous findings' without correction. Wawrusiewicz-Kurylonek 2020 reported MS OR 1.36, p=2.17e-02 in only 171 Polish MS cases vs 400 controls. Varzari 2014 (716 vs 706) reported no significant single-SNP association, though its rs3747517 allelic point estimate (OR ≈ 1.11, computed from published genotypes) is in the same direction as Enevold's (OR ≈ 1.25), and these two cohorts together supply Xiao 2023's pooled MS estimate. Separately, IMSGC 2009 (PMID 18987646) tested rs1990760 in 2,369 trios plus 5,737 cases and 10,296 controls and found no MS association.

verdicts.claim: In T1D, IFIH1 is an established causal gene with a common missense variant plus four independent rare protective variants; reduced MDA5 function protects.
verdicts.reason: Both abstracts match verbatim. Smyth 2006 (PMID 16699517): 'In 4,253 cases, 5,842 controls and 2,134 parent-child trio genotypes, the risk ratio for the minor allele of the nsSNP rs1990760 A --> G (A946T) was 0.86 (95% confidence interval = 0.82-0.90) at P = 1.42 x 10(-10)' and 'a sixth type 1 diabetes (T1D) locus'. Nejentsev 2009 (PMID 19264985): resequenced exons/splice sites of 10 candidate genes in pools of 480 patients / 480 controls, tested in over 30,000 participants, 'four rare variants that lowered T1D risk independently of each other (odds ratio = 0.51 to 0.74; P = 1.3 x 10(-3) to 2.1 x 10(-16))', and 'This finding firmly establishes the role of IFIH1 in T1D.'
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands, with one wording correction: Nejentsev's abstract says the four rare variants 'are predicted to alter the expression and structure of IFIH1', not specifically to reduce it. The loss-of-function-protects direction is firmly established for the rare variants but is NOT established for the common rs1990760 A946T — Taylor et al. 2024 (PMID 39373578) report the T1D risk allele 946T as a GAIN of function (elevated basal type I IFN and ISG expression in overexpression systems, increased ATPase activity in vitro), so the two variant classes should not be pooled into a single directional statement.

verdicts.claim: The only direct measurement of MDA5 transcript in MS blood vs healthy controls reports MDA5 mRNA significantly DECREASED in MS, and IFN-beta-1a does NOT raise it at 6 months.
verdicts.reason: The abstract (PMID 32311159) supports every element verbatim: peripheral leukocytes of 30 new MS cases and 35 healthy controls, real-time PCR for MDA5 and RIG-1, measurement repeated 6 months after standard-dose IFN-beta-1a; 'mRNA levels of MDA5 and RIG-1 were significantly decreased in the MS patients in comparison to the healthy controls'; 'IFN-beta 1a therapy leads to the upregulation of RIG-1, but not MDA5, in the total MS patients and the female group.' I also independently ran targeted PubMed searches (IFIH1 AND multiple sclerosis AND expression: 6 hits; MDA5 AND multiple sclerosis: 8 hits) and found no other direct MDA5-transcript MS-vs-healthy-control blood measurement, which supports the scoping claim. The claim's own caveats — small single-centre Iranian cohort, no fold-change/delta-Ct/p-value in the abstract, full text not obtained, single and unreplicated — are all accurate and appropriately stated.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands as worded, including its caveats. Two additions for the scientist: the effect size is entirely unquantified (no fold-change, delta-Ct or p-value is retrievable without the full text), and 'newly diagnosed' MS patients means treatment-naive at baseline, so the decrease is a baseline property and not an interferon-induced one.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 is elevated at baseline in the ~18% MX1-high subgroup of untreated RRMS patients, and in that subgroup IFN-beta fails to induce it further (pharmacodynamic ceiling).
verdicts.reason: I pulled the PMC full text (PMC3464734) and every methodological detail matches verbatim: 'We set a cut-off at 3,000, which was two standard errors above the mean'; MX1 signal intensities ranged 875-11,588; 11 of 61 patients qualified as MX1-high (18%); 'Wilcoxon rank-sum test... Expression differences with P-values below 0.01 were considered statistically significant'; and the exact quote 'Elevated transcript levels were found for cytoplasmic receptors (for example, IFIH1), TFs (for example, IRF7, IRF9 and STAT1)'. IFIH1 is one of only 11 of 56 pathway genes significantly elevated at baseline in MX1-high. The induction result is supported: '25 of the 56 genes were found to be significantly modulated in MX1-low patients... The upregulated genes comprised all the 11 genes that were significantly elevated in the MX1-high patient group at baseline', while 'The pathway expression profile of those [MX1-high] patients was not significantly influenced by subcutaneous IFN-beta therapy.'
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands, with two corrections. First, the post-treatment comparison was restricted to subcutaneously treated patients only — n=7 MX1-high vs n=30 MX1-low, not 11 vs 50 — because the 24 intramuscular-IFN-beta-1a patients were excluded from the expression comparison by design; the 18% (11/61) figure applies only to the baseline classification. Second, the claim's second quote ('The receptors IFIH1, DDX58 and ZBP1, two ISGs (CXCL10, ISG20)') comes from the section on PREDICTED ISGF3 transcription-factor binding sites in promoter regions, not from a list of measured expression differences. As the claim states, no per-gene fold-change for IFIH1 is published and IFIH1 was not among the 14 genes re-measured by qPCR.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 is a durable IFN-beta pharmacodynamic marker in MS blood: one of only 15 transcripts differentially expressed at every time point across a full year of IFN-beta-1b therapy.
verdicts.reason: The Serrano-Fernandez abstract (PMID 19883335) contains the gene list verbatim, including IFIH1: 'Fifteen markers were differentially expressed during all three time points and followed a consistent time course pattern: EIF2AK2, IFI6, IFI44, IFI44L, IFIH1, IFIT1, IFIT2, IFIT3, ISG15, MX1, OASL, RSAD2, SN, XAF1 and the marker 238704_at', from 18 IFNB1b-treated MS patients at four time points spanning 1 year, with 'Expression changes were both early detectable and long lasting', IL-8 short-lasting and STAT1 delayed. Nguyen 2023 (PMID 36867172) also matches verbatim: 'Long-term PEG-IFN-beta-1a therapy increased expression of antiviral and immune-regulatory genes (IFIH1, TLR8, IRF5, TNFSF10 [TRAIL], STAT3, JAK2, IL15, and RB1)', and the gene counts 136 and 85 at 6 h, 476 and 598 at 24 h. Neither abstract publishes a numeric fold-change for IFIH1, exactly as the claim concedes.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands, with two precisions. The paper says the 15 markers were differentially expressed 'during all three time points' — four sampling points across a year giving three post-baseline comparisons, so 'at every time point' should read 'at all three post-baseline time points'. And Nguyen's IFIH1 finding is specific to long-term PEGylated IFN-beta-1a, not to IFN-beta in general. No fold-change for IFIH1 is published in either study, so its rank within the pharmacodynamic response is unquantified.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 is a mid-tier ISG: across at least six MS/IFN-beta transcriptomic studies it falls below the reporting cutoff while IFI44L, IFIT1, MX1, RSAD2, ISG15 and OAS genes clear it.
verdicts.reason: The substantive absence finding survives — I searched the full texts and IFIH1 (and MDA5) appear nowhere in van Baarsen 2008 (PMC2271130), Gurevich 2015 (PMC4654830), Henig 2013 (PMC3633862) or Srinivasan 2017 (PMC5566335). Every number I could check was exact (126 genes, 28-gene IFN cluster; 104 DEGs of which 87 up and 17 down, IFN type 1 p=1.7E-16, IFN-beta signalling p=7.4E-08, top genes at 2.9-1.8 log2FC = IFI44L, IFIT1, IFI44, IFIT3, MX1, ISG15, SIGLEC1, OAS3, OAS1; DEFB1 31.8-fold p=0.0001, TNFSF10 27.2-fold p=0.003 with T-cell 10-fold, ZBP1 T-cell 11.9-fold p=0.001, 100 U/ml IFN-beta-1a for 16 h in 3 donors; 21 core transcripts, 100 validated IRGs). But three of the six citations are misattributed. PMID 26589141 is Gurevich et al., not 'Singh et al.'. PMID 23626809 / PLoS One 8:e62366 is Henig et al. (issue 4, April 23), not 'Waschbisch et al., 8(5)' — and its design is TNF-alpha-primed monocytes and T cells then exposed to IFN-beta, a co-stimulation experiment the claim omits entirely. PMID 28827704 is Srinivasan et al., Sci Rep 2017;7:8981 — '7:9286' is the DOI suffix mistaken for an article number, and 'Ottoboni-type' names no author on the paper. Also, all four DEG lists live in supplementary tables I could not screen, so the absences are confirmed for main text and figures only; and I did not verify Malhotra 2013 or Khsheibun 2014.
verdicts.corrected_claim: IFIH1 is a genuine but mid-tier interferon-stimulated gene in MS blood. In the main text and figures of four MS/IFN-beta transcriptomic studies I checked — van Baarsen 2008 (PLoS One 3:e1927, PMID 18382694), Gurevich 2015 (BMC Neurol 15:240, PMID 26589141), Henig 2013 (PLoS One 8:e62366, PMID 23626809; TNF-alpha-primed monocytes and T cells + IFN-beta-1a 100 U/ml, 16 h, 3 donors) and Srinivasan 2017 (Sci Rep 7:8981, PMID 28827704) — IFIH1 is never named, while IFI44L, IFIT1, IFI44, IFIT3, MX1, ISG15, RSAD2, SIGLEC1 and the OAS genes are. The supplementary DEG tables were not screened, so this is an absence from what each paper reports, not proof of absence from each DEG list. Conclusions about 'the MS interferon signature' should not be assumed to include IFIH1.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 genotype does NOT predict clinical response to IFN-beta in MS; the one nominal signal (rs3747517) failed validation in a 1,385-patient two-stage study.
