verdicts.reason: Bustamante 2015 (PMID 26445728) matches verbatim on every point: 384 polymorphisms in 830 MS patients (416 responders / 414 nonresponders); seven SNPs advanced including rs3747517 (IFIH1) at p=0.010; validation cohort of 555 patients (281 responders / 274 nonresponders); 'None of these SNPs were significantly associated with IFN-beta response when genotyped in an independent cohort of patients'; combined analysis of all 1,385 retained only rs2277302 (PELI3, p=0.008) and rs832032 (GABRR3, p=0.006), so IFIH1 drops out. The authors' own conclusion is that the findings 'do not support an association'. Enevold 2010 (PMID 20595247) also matches: 42 pattern-recognition-receptor SNPs in 567 prospectively followed IFN-beta-treated RRMS patients, 'There were no significant differences between interferon-beta responders and non-responders for any of the investigated single nucleotide polymorphisms', with TLR6-rs5743810 in males the only signal surviving Bonferroni (p=0.00002, corrected p=0.02) and that for neutralizing-antibody development, not response.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands as worded. One small precision: Enevold 2010's abstract lists the 42-SNP panel by gene family rather than enumerating it, so 'including the IFIH1 SNPs' rests on the panel being the same one described in Enevold 2009 (TLR1-10, NOD1-2, DDX58, IFIH1) — a reasonable but indirect inference.

verdicts.claim: There are essentially NO IFIH1/MDA5 data from MS CSF; the two largest MS CSF single-cell studies do not report IFIH1 as differentially expressed despite both finding altered type I IFN pathway activity.
verdicts.reason: I searched both full texts directly. In Ban et al., Brain 2024 (PMC10834244), the strings IFIH1, MDA5, DDX58, DHX58 and MAVS return zero hits across the entire article. The paper does report 96,732 CSF cells, the type 1 interferon pathway alteration in T cells and myeloid cells, and both eQTLs verbatim: 'the risk allele rs10271373_A increasing expression of... ZC3HAV1 and rs1059091_A reducing the expression of... IFITM2' in CD8+ T cells, with 'increased usage of the ZAP-L isoform in individuals that carry the multiple sclerosis risk allele (rs10271373_A)'. In Schafflick et al. 2020 (PMC6959356), IFIH1 appears exactly once, in Methods: 'We extracted marker genes from a rodent study (NLRC5, IL12RB1, PSMB9, TAP1, TAP2, IFIH1, IRF7, and ZBP1)' — precisely as the claim describes, with no MS-vs-control statistic.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands on substance, with three corrections. The Brain 2024 comparison group is 48 patients with OTHER NEUROLOGICAL DISEASES (n=48,057 cells), not healthy controls — the 33 MS patients contributed 48,675 cells. The absence of IFIH1/DDX58/DHX58/MAVS is confirmed for the full article text, but supplementary eQTL and DE tables were not screened, so 'not analysed' should read 'not reported'. And 'the two largest MS CSF single-cell studies' is an unverified superlative — Schafflick's MS-vs-control scRNA-seq rests on only 4 MS and 4 control donors. The claim that no study has measured MDA5 protein in MS CSF by ELISA, Western or mass spectrometry remains an unverified negative.

verdicts.claim: In blood IFIH1 is a myeloid/innate gene: HPA Cluster 40 'Monocytes - Innate immune response', neutrophils the single enhanced cell type, pDCs the lowest expressers; activation raises it ~13x and ~11x in naive CD8 and CD4 T cells.
verdicts.reason: Every individual number is exact — I reproduced all of them. HPA JSON for ENSG00000115267 returns 'Low immune cell specificity', 'Detected in all', 'Cluster 40: Monocytes - Innate immune response', specific nCPM {Neutrophils 129.2, Late spermatids 93.1, Early spermatids 88.5}, tissue specific nTPM {bone marrow 34.6}. All 18 immune-cell nTPM values match exactly (neutrophil 14.1, naive B-cell 12.5, non-classical monocyte 12.4, intermediate monocyte 12.2, memory B-cell 12.2, classical monocyte 11.3, myeloid DC 11.0, T-reg 10.0, MAIT 9.0, total PBMC 7.7, memory CD4 7.7, memory CD8 7.1, naive CD8 6.6, naive CD4 6.2, basophil 4.4, eosinophil 4.4, NK 3.8, pDC 1.6). GTEx v8 matches exactly (EBV-lymphocytes 87.03, spleen 15.87, lung 13.43, whole blood 2.79). Three errors in the interpretation. (i) HPA lists THREE enhanced cell types, not one — the claim's own evidence quotes all three then says 'neutrophils the single enhanced cell type'. (ii) 'IFIH1 is a myeloid/innate gene' contradicts HPA's own classification of 'Low immune cell specificity / Detected in all': naive B-cells (12.5) outrank every monocyte subset (11.3-12.4). (iii) The activation fold-changes are wrong by 3.5-4.5x. The values 84.2 and 70.7 come from the Schmiedel dataset, whose matched RESTING values are naive CD8 23.7 and naive CD4 29.5 — giving 3.6x and 2.4x. The claim divided Schmiedel activated TPM by HPA-consensus resting nTPM (6.6 and 6.2), a cross-dataset comparison.
verdicts.corrected_claim: IFIH1 is broadly expressed across leukocytes with low cell-type specificity. HPA classifies it 'Low immune cell specificity', 'Detected in all', blood expression Cluster 40 'Monocytes - Innate immune response', RNA single cell type 'Cell type enhanced' in three types (Neutrophils 129.2, Late spermatids 93.1, Early spermatids 88.5 nCPM) and tissue enhanced in bone marrow (34.6 nTPM). Consensus immune-cell nTPM span only ~9-fold across leukocytes: neutrophil 14.1, naive B-cell 12.5, non-classical monocyte 12.4, intermediate monocyte 12.2, memory B-cell 12.2, classical monocyte 11.3, myeloid DC 11.0, T-reg 10.0, MAIT 9.0, total PBMC 7.7, memory CD4 7.7, memory CD8 7.1, naive CD8 6.6, naive CD4 6.2, basophil 4.4, eosinophil 4.4, NK 3.8, plasmacytoid DC 1.6 (lowest). Naive B-cells outrank all monocyte subsets, so the pattern is not specifically myeloid. Within the Schmiedel dataset, activation raises IFIH1 ~3.6x in naive CD8 T cells (23.7 to 84.2) and ~2.4x in naive CD4 T cells (29.5 to 70.7). GTEx v8 medians: EBV-transformed lymphocytes 87.03, spleen 15.87, lung 13.43, whole blood 2.79 TPM.

verdicts.claim: The MS interferon-signature literature localizes the pathogenic type I IFN signal to MONOCYTES and links it to IFN-beta treatment failure, but IFIH1's membership in that monocyte signature is NOT established in the accessible record.
verdicts.reason: Comabella 2009 (PMID 19741051) supports every element of the evidence verbatim: genome-wide expression profiling of PBMC from 47 MS patients treated with IFN-beta for a minimum of 2 years classified responder/non-responder on clinical criteria, with a 30-patient validation cohort; 'Before treatment, interferon-beta responders and non-responders were characterized by differential expression of type I interferon-induced genes with overexpression of the type interferon-induced genes in non-responders. Upon treatment the expression of these genes remained unaltered in non-responders, but was strongly upregulated in responders'; 'a selective increase in phosphorylated STAT1 levels and interferon receptor 1 expression in monocytes of non-responders at baseline'; 'increased monocyte type I interferon secretion upon innate immune stimuli via toll-like receptor 4, by increased endogenous production of type I interferon, and by an elevated activation status of myeloid dendritic cells'. The abstract does not enumerate the signature genes, so the claim's caveat — do not cite Comabella 2009 as IFIH1 evidence without checking the supplementary tables — is correct and is the right epistemic call.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Claim stands as worded. Two framing precisions: Comabella 2009 characterises this type I IFN signature as a marker of IFN-beta treatment non-response, not as 'pathogenic' in the disease-causing sense; and the genome-wide profiling was done on whole PBMC, with monocyte localisation established afterwards by targeted functional assays (phospho-STAT1, IFNAR1, TLR4-stimulated secretion), so the signature itself is a bulk-PBMC measurement.

verdicts.claim: rs1990760 A946T is a powerful modifier of systemic interferon output and circulating myeloid cell abundance, independent of MS; the variant alters MDA5 signalling capacity more than IFIH1 transcript abundance.
verdicts.reason: Every cited number is exact. The GWAS Catalog associations verify: interferon lambda-1 measurement p=7e-54, BST2 in blood p=1e-24, galectin-9 p=2e-15, myeloid leukocyte count p=7e-24, monocyte percentage p=2e-15 and p=8e-16, leukocyte quantity p=6e-17, neutrophil count p=2e-12/5e-12/1e-14/3e-11, eosinophil count p=7e-10. The qPCR values are verbatim from PMC3873949: 'G/G (n = 7): 5.3 (1.4-6.8), G/A (n = 13): 6.6 (1.3-7.1), A/A (n = 7): 1.8 (1.3-6.7) AU; P = 0.274'. The J Immunol 2024 details are verbatim too: 81 healthy donors, '20 non-risk/non-risk (CC), 40 risk/non-risk (CT), and 22 risk/risk (TT)' — the paper's own counts, which sum to 82 — HEK-Blue IFN-alpha/beta reporter and beta-Lox5 overexpression lines, and 'no statistically significant difference in the expression of any gene analyzed in response to CVB3 infection, except for IFNA2', with no poly(I:C) differences either. The problems are interpretive. 'Powerful modifier' misreads the effect sizes: the blood-count betas are 0.015-0.023 SD units, i.e. tiny effects with huge p-values from UK-Biobank-scale samples. 'Systemic interferon output' mislabels the strongest signal: interferon lambda-1 is a TYPE III interferon, not the type I interferon MDA5-MAVS signalling induces. The myeloid leukocyte count beta is recorded as a DECREASE while monocyte percentage increases, which the claim does not reconcile. And the qPCR counter-evidence was measured in 26 TYPE 1 DIABETES PATIENTS, not unselected 'human mononuclear cells' — in the same paper IFIH1 mRNA differed by hypertension status (p=0.036), so the cells were not a neutral background. First author is Bouças, not 'Pilotto'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: rs1990760 (A946T) is robustly but weakly associated with circulating interferon-pathway protein levels and blood-cell indices, independent of MS: interferon lambda-1 (a type III interferon) p=7e-54 (beta 0.098), BST2/tetherin p=1e-24, galectin-9 p=2e-15, plus myeloid leukocyte count p=7e-24, monocyte percentage p=2e-15/8e-16 and neutrophil count p=1e-14 — all with betas of only ~0.015-0.023 SD units, so the associations are highly significant but small. Evidence that the variant changes IFIH1 TRANSCRIPT abundance is weak: Bouças et al. 2013 (PMID 24386202) found no genotype difference in mononuclear cells from 26 T1D patients (GG 5.3, GA 6.6, AA 1.8 AU; P=0.274, badly underpowered). Evidence that it changes MDA5 PROTEIN function is stronger but confined to artificial systems: Taylor et al. 2024 (PMID 39373578) found elevated basal type I IFN and ISG expression and increased ATPase activity only in HEK-Blue and beta-Lox5 overexpression models, with no genotype-dependent ISG differences in primary PBMCs from 81 healthy donors after CVB3 or poly(I:C) (IFNA2 the sole exception).

verdicts.claim: The only MS genetic evidence implicating IFIH1 that survives modern scrutiny is a rare-variant burden signal at the level of a 62-gene inflammasome/interferon gene SET, not IFIH1 itself.
verdicts.reason: Every factual element of the evidence is verbatim correct. Vidmar 2019 (PMID 31235738): whole exome sequencing of 319 probands comprising familial MS, sporadic MS and controls; 62 genes in the NLRP1/NLRP3 inflammasome regulatory network; 'We demonstrate an increased (p = 0.00004) variant burden among MS patients which was most pronounced for the exceedingly rare variants with high predicted pathogenicity'; and IFIH1 named exactly where the claim says — 'genes involved in response to infection with DNA viruses (POLR3A, DHX58, IFIH1)' alongside NLRP1/3, CASP1, RIPK2, MEFV, TYK2 and PTPRC. The claim's critical caveat is also correct: no gene-level statistic, odds ratio, variant list or p-value for IFIH1 alone is reported. The headline is what fails. A 319-proband exome study with no replication, no gene-level statistic and a set-level p-value across 62 genes does not 'survive modern scrutiny' better than the candidate-gene literature the claim dismisses elsewhere; and by the claim's own concession it 'cannot be cited as an IFIH1-MS association', which contradicts calling it evidence 'implicating IFIH1'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Vidmar 2019 (PMID 31235738) reports an increased burden of exceedingly rare, high-predicted-pathogenicity variants in MS patients across a 62-gene inflammasome regulatory network (whole exome sequencing of 319 probands; aggregate burden p = 0.00004), and lists IFIH1 among the contributing genes. No gene-level statistic, odds ratio, variant list or p-value for IFIH1 alone is reported, the cohort is small, and there is no replication — so this does not constitute evidence implicating IFIH1 in MS, and should be cited only as a gene-set-level finding. Note also that the source paper groups IFIH1 under 'response to infection with DNA viruses', which is biologically incorrect: MDA5 is a cytoplasmic sensor of long double-stranded RNA.

verification.overall:
VERDICT COUNTS: 10 CONFIRMED, 9 OVERSTATED, 0 REFUTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE.

The researcher's central thesis — that IFIH1/MDA5 is NOT an established MS susceptibility gene, in sharp contrast to T1D, psoriasis, SLE, IBD and autoimmune thyroid disease — survives adversarial checking and is well supported. The database work (claims 2, 3) reproduced exactly when I re-ran the queries independently, and the full-text verifications (claims 5, 11, 15) matched verbatim down to individual allele counts and cut-off values. This is unusually careful work by the standards of this exercise.

However, nine claims overstate what their sources support. The recurring failure modes:

1. ABSENCE OVERSTATED INTO A ZERO (claim 1, the highest-stakes error). "chr2:160-165Mb returned ZERO variants" is false — rs2052401 sits at chr2:162,105,535 in GCST009597 (p=2e-07, OR 1.0669, genomeWide=false, author-assigned to DPP4, ~161 kb from IFIH1). The conclusion survives, the stated evidence does not. Also GCST009597's recorded sample is 14,802/26,703 + 74,299 replication, not the paper's 47,429/68,374; and only 195 of the 333 records are p<5e-8.

2. CROSS-DATASET FOLD-CHANGE (claim 16). The "~13x and ~11x" T-cell activation induction was computed by dividing Schmiedel activated TPM (84.2, 70.7) by HPA-consensus resting nTPM (6.6, 6.2). Within the Schmiedel dataset the matched resting values are 23.7 and 29.5, giving 3.6x and 2.4x — the claim inflates by 3.5-4.5x. Claim 16 also calls IFIH1 "a myeloid/innate gene" when HPA itself says "Low immune cell specificity / Detected in all" and naive B-cells (12.5 nTPM) outrank every monocyte subset.

3. POSITIONAL FIGURES ATTACHED TO THE WRONG SNP (claim 4). The "46-99 kb outside IFIH1" numbers are rs3747517's distances to GCA and KCNH7. rs2068330 is 62,196 bp from IFIH1. Critically, rs3747517 and rs1990760 both have distance 0 to IFIH1 — they are INSIDE the gene — so "the associated SNPs are intergenic relative to IFIH1's coding span" is false.

4. SELECTIVE READING OF A META-ANALYSIS (claim 7). Xiao 2023's MS rs1990760 OR 1.03 is exact, but the paper explicitly writes "MS was also underpowered for the recessive and allelic models," and in the same paper's own words "T1D, SLE, and MS suggested a significant positive correlation" for rs3747517 (MS OR 1.19, 95% CI 1.07-1.32, p=0.002). Calling "the MS association" flatly null inverts the authors' conclusion.

5. THREE WRONG AUTHOR/CITATION ATTRIBUTIONS (claim 13). PMID 26589141 is Gurevich et al., not "Singh et al." PMID 23626809 is Henig et al., PLoS One 8(4):e62366, not "Waschbisch et al., 8(5)" — and its design is TNF-alpha-primed cells plus IFN-beta, a co-stimulation experiment the claim omits. PMID 28827704 is Srinivasan et al., Sci Rep 7:8981, not "7:9286" (that is the DOI suffix) and not "Ottoboni-type". The absence finding itself held up: I confirmed IFIH1 appears nowhere in the full text of all four papers I could retrieve.

SIGNIFICANT EVIDENCE GAP the researcher missed: IMSGC 2009, Genes Immun 10:11-14 (PMID 18987646) tested rs1990760 among seven T1D SNPs in 2,369 MS trio families plus 5,737 cases and 10,296 controls and found only CLEC16A (p=1.6e-16) and CD226 (p=5.4e-08) associated. This is the best-powered direct negative test of the common IFIH1 variant in MS and appears in none of the 19 claims — it strengthens the overall thesis considerably.

CAVEAT ON ALL "ABSENT FROM" CLAIMS (1, 13, 15): I could verify absence from main texts, figures and abstracts only. Supplementary DEG and eQTL tables were not screened. "Not reported" is defensible; "not present in the gene list" is not.

MOST IMPORTANT NOTE FOR THE USER'S ACTUAL QUESTION: the user asked which NERVOUS SYSTEM cell types express MDA5 and where it changes in MS. Not one of these 19 claims addresses that. All 19 concern MS genetics, peripheral blood and IFN-beta pharmacodynamics. Relevant data I retrieved in passing, which the ms-genetics angle does not cover: HPA brain single-nuclei IFIH1 is "Cell type enhanced" in ENDOTHELIAL CELLS (118.9 nCPM), with microglia 26.7, oligodendrocytes 12.3/7.5, astrocytes 11.6/7.9 and neurons 0.1-0.8 nCPM; the HPA single-cell group comparison gives glial cells 45.1 vs neuronal cells 0.5 nCPM; GTEx v8 bulk brain regions are uniformly low (cervical spinal cord 4.30, substantia nigra 3.02, cortex 2.17, cerebellar hemisphere 0.96 TPM) against spleen 15.87 and lung 13.43. These are healthy-baseline human values, not MS. The MS-vs-control cell-type question in CNS tissue remains, on the evidence gathered here, unanswered — claim 15 confirms IFIH1/DDX58/DHX58/MAVS appear nowhere in the largest MS CSF single-cell study, and no MS brain-tissue single-nucleus data on IFIH1 was examined by this angle at all. That is the gap to fill next.

research.dimension: MDA5/IFIH1 measured directly in multiple sclerosis brain tissue (IHC, bulk transcriptomics, single-nucleus/spatial transcriptomics of MS lesions)

findings.claim: IFIH1 is significantly UPREGULATED in OLIGODENDROCYTES in human subcortical MS lesions versus control white matter — this is the single strongest published, cell-type-resolved differential-expression result for IFIH1 in MS brain that I could locate.
findings.evidence: Lerma-Martin et al. 2024 Nat Neurosci, Supplementary Table 6 ('STable_6_Cell_type_DEG', pseudobulk DESeq2 per cell type, 49,888 rows). I parsed the published .xlsx directly. IFIH1 rows: (1) cell_type=OL, contrast=CAvsCtrl (chronic active lesion vs control): baseMean=132.96, log2FC=+0.9050, lfcSE=0.2923, stat=3.096, p=1.963e-3, padj=1.218e-2. (2) cell_type=OL, contrast=CIvsCtrl (chronic inactive vs control): baseMean=132.96, log2FC=+1.0947, lfcSE=0.3189, stat=3.433, p=5.968e-4, padj=4.697e-3. (3) cell_type=MC (myeloid cells), CIvsCtrl: baseMean=39.18, log2FC=+0.9501, p=3.637e-2, padj=0.1155 (NOT significant). (4) cell_type=TC (T cells), CAvsCI: baseMean=11.43, log2FC=-0.9642, p=6.036e-4, padj=4.211e-2. IFIH1 does NOT appear for AS (astrocytes), OPC, NEU (neurons), EC (endothelial), BC (B cells) or SC in any of the three contrasts. IFIH1 is absent from STable_3_Cell_type_markers, STable_4_Cell_subtype_markers, STable_5_ASC_markers and STable_7_Niche_DEG (i.e. not a marker gene, and not a spatial-niche DEG). Dataset: 12 subcortical MS lesions from 6 donors + 7 controls, paired snRNA-seq + 10x Visium. Supplementary file used: https://static-content.springer.com/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41593-024-01796-z/MediaObjects/41593_2024_1796_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx

findings.claim: In the same Lerma-Martin 2024 cell-type DEG table, the whole cytosolic dsRNA-sensing/ISG module moves UP specifically in oligodendrocytes, while the classic ISGs MX1 and IFI44L move DOWN in endothelial cells and astrocytes — i.e. the MS interferon shift is cell-type-directional, not uniform.
findings.evidence: From STable_6_Cell_type_DEG (same file, same DESeq2 pipeline): DDX58 (RIG-I) OL CAvsCtrl log2FC=+0.544, padj=1.63e-3; OL CIvsCtrl log2FC=+0.469, padj=1.47e-2 (baseMean 320.9, i.e. ~2.4x higher baseline than IFIH1's 132.96). EIF2AK2 (PKR) OL CAvsCtrl log2FC=+0.513, padj=2.08e-3 (baseMean 504.8). IRF7 OL CAvsCtrl log2FC=+2.999, padj=1.39e-2; IRF7 AS CAvsCtrl log2FC=+1.213, padj=7.83e-3. IFIT1 OL CIvsCtrl log2FC=+1.190, padj=2.06e-2. B2M OL CIvsCtrl log2FC=+1.926, padj=1.36e-2. Opposite direction: MX1 EC CAvsCtrl log2FC=-1.536, padj=0.031 and CIvsCtrl log2FC=-1.878, padj=0.0162; IFI44L AS CAvsCtrl log2FC=-1.561, padj=0.0227; IFI44L EC CAvsCtrl log2FC=-1.999, padj=0.0259. MAVS goes DOWN in AS (CIvsCtrl -0.650, padj=0.0359), EC (CIvsCtrl -0.929, padj=4.32e-6), MC (CIvsCtrl -0.605, padj=0.0052) and OL (CIvsCtrl -0.656, padj=7.82e-4). DHX58/LGP2 and ISG15 are absent from the table entirely.

findings.claim: IFIH1 is significantly upregulated in ACTIVE and CHRONIC ACTIVE white-matter lesions of progressive MS versus control white matter in bulk RNA-seq, whereas its paralogues DDX58 (RIG-I) and DHX58 (LGP2) are NOT changed in any lesion type.
findings.evidence: Own reanalysis of the author-deposited edgeR result tables in GEO GSE138614 (Elkjaer et al. 2019, Acta Neuropathol Commun 7:205; 73 MS WM areas from 10 progressive-MS patients vs 25 control WM areas). IFIH1 (ENSG00000115267): active lesion vs control WM logFC=+0.558, logCPM=4.023, LR=8.740, P=3.114e-3, FDR=0.0209; chronic active vs control WM logFC=+0.478, logCPM=3.789, LR=10.221, P=1.388e-3, FDR=7.279e-3; remyelinating lesion vs control WM logFC=+0.604, P=0.0116, FDR=0.0608 (trend); inactive lesion vs control WM logFC=+0.313, P=0.0945, FDR=0.213 (NS); NAWM vs control WM logFC=+0.201, P=0.111, FDR=0.450 (NS). Same tables, DDX58 (ENSG00000107201): FDR=0.550 (AL), 0.217 (CA), 0.911 (IL), 0.981 (NAWM), 0.533 (RL) — never significant. DHX58 (ENSG00000108771): FDR 0.99, 0.34, 0.78, 0.68, 0.98 — never significant. Absolute level logCPM 3.74-4.02 = ~13-16 CPM. Files: https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE138nnn/GSE138614/suppl/GSE138614_WM_vs_{AL,CA,IL,NAWM,RL}.txt.gz . Caveat: this group has a retracted earlier companion paper (Retraction Note, PMC6704544); the 2019 7:205 paper is the standing publication and the GEO tables are the deposited versions.

findings.claim: IFIH1 is a named, statistically significant DEG in a published MS-brain bulk RNA-seq study: it is among the most significant genes upregulated in foamy active lesions of poorly remyelinating MS donors compared with efficiently remyelinating donors.
findings.evidence: Chen JQA et al., Brain 2025;148(6):2201-2217, doi 10.1093/brain/awae414. Verbatim from the Results: 'The most significant DEGs upregulated in ALs foamy of PRDs included SNX3, IFIT1, IFIT3, MOCS2, EIF2AK2 and IFIH1.' Design: Netherlands Brain Bank cohort n=239 stratified into efficiently remyelinating donors (ERD, n=21) and poorly remyelinating donors (PRD, n=19); bulk RNA-seq of 96 dissected samples — remyelinated lesions, active lesions non-foamy, active lesions foamy, and NAWM. 502 DEGs at FDR<0.05 in ALs foamy ERD vs PRD (vs only 17 in RLs and 8 in ALs non-foamy, 0 in NAWM). Note the co-listed genes IFIT1, IFIT3, EIF2AK2 are all type-I-IFN/dsRNA-response genes, i.e. IFIH1 appears here as part of an interferon signature, not in isolation. Data: GEO GSE283092.

findings.claim: Own reanalysis of GSE283092 raw counts confirms IFIH1 is expressed at ~14-15 CPM in MS NAWM and rises ~1.4-1.8-fold in lesions, with the largest and most significant rise in FOAMY ACTIVE lesions; the ERD-vs-PRD contrast the paper highlights is directionally reproducible but only p=0.14 by a simple unpaired test.
findings.evidence: Own analysis of GSE283092_allCounts.orig.tab.gz (96 samples, 61,541 genes, median library 26.9M) with sample annotation from the GEO series matrix. IFIH1 (ENSG00000115267) median CPM by group: ERD NAWM 14.37 (n=27), PRD NAWM 15.18 (n=20), ERD RL 18.55 (n=14), PRD RL 20.26 (n=7), ERD AL non-foamy 20.62 (n=7), PRD AL non-foamy 18.01 (n=7), ERD AL foamy 22.12 (n=7), PRD AL foamy 29.24 (n=7, mean 41.27, max 78.47). Pooled: NAWM median 14.42 (n=47) vs all lesions 20.27 (n=49), Mann-Whitney z=-4.52, p=6.2e-6. Paired lesion vs SAME-DONOR NAWM (Wilcoxon signed-rank on log2 ratios): foamy active lesions median FC=1.79, n=13, p=0.0015; remyelinated lesions FC=1.36, n=20, p=0.0009; non-foamy active lesions FC=1.21, n=13, p=0.152. Comparison genes, same paired test in foamy active lesions: DDX58 FC=1.24 p=0.016; MX1 FC=2.07 p=0.0019; CSF1R FC=1.63 p=0.0046; GFAP FC=1.68 p=0.0024; MBP FC=0.48 p=0.0015. ERD vs PRD within AL foamy (unpaired Mann-Whitney on my CPMs): IFIH1 22.12 vs 29.24, FC=1.32, p=0.142 — I could NOT reproduce the paper's FDR<0.05 with a naive nonparametric test; the authors used a covariate-adjusted DE model, so the discrepancy is methodological, and my paired lesion-vs-NAWM result is the more robust statement.

findings.claim: NEGATIVE FINDING: IFIH1/MDA5 does not appear anywhere in the published output of Absinta et al. 2021 Nature (GSE180759) — not in any marker-gene list, differential-expression list, WGCNA module, or drug-target table. Neither do DDX58, DHX58, MX1, ISG15, IFIT1, STAT1, IRF7, OAS1, TLR3 or EIF2AK2.
findings.evidence: I downloaded and parsed Supplementary Table file 41586_2021_3892_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx, which contains all 13 supplementary tables: 'Table of content', S1, S2_IHC, S3_ALL, S4_IMM, S5_OL, S6_OPC, S7_AST, S8_peripheral immune, S9_WGCNA, S10 Drugs_MIMS-foamy, S11 Drugs_MIMS-iron, S12_IMM_by_location, S13_VAS. The workbook contains 4,091 unique shared strings of which 3,445 are gene-symbol-like. Positive controls present: FTL, FTH1, C1QA, CD163, SPP1, GFAP, IFITM3, B2M, HLA-A. Absent: IFIH1, DDX58, DHX58, MX1, ISG15, IFI44L, STAT1, IRF7, OAS1, TLR3, EIF2AK2, IFIT1. The MOESM5 source-data file (Extended Fig 10 quantifications) likewise contains none. Conclusion: the MIMS-foamy / MIMS-iron microglia signatures and the lymphocyte-microglia-astrocyte axis reported by Absinta 2021 are not built on RLR/ISG genes, and this paper provides no published evidence for or against IFIH1 change in MS lesions.

findings.claim: Own reanalysis of the raw GSE180759 (Absinta 2021) count matrix shows IFIH1 IS detectable but very sparse, and ranks LYMPHOCYTES > VASCULAR CELLS > MYELOID/IMMUNE >> ASTROCYTES > OLIGODENDROCYTES > OPC ~ NEURONS in MS/control white matter.
findings.evidence: Own analysis of GSE180759_expression_matrix.csv.gz (66,432 nuclei x 30,559 genes, raw UMI) joined to GSE180759_annotation.txt (5 pathology regions, 7 cell classes); per-nucleus total UMI computed over the full matrix. IFIH1 mean counts-per-10,000 (and % nuclei with >=1 UMI): lymphocytes 0.394 (7.39%, n=406); vascular_cells 0.322 (6.79%, n=1,708); immune/myeloid 0.294 (5.85%, n=5,432); astrocytes 0.089 (2.02%, n=8,211); oligodendrocytes 0.059 (1.68%, n=45,697); OPC 0.028 (1.01%, n=2,175); neurons 0.027 (0.96%, n=2,803). Within oligodendrocytes by region: control WM 0.032 CP10K (0.96% detected, n=4,264) < chronic active lesion edge 0.050 (1.11%, n=12,658) ~ chronic inactive edge 0.050 (1.15%, n=11,193) < MS periplaque WM 0.079 (2.59%, n=17,563) — i.e. a 1.6-2.5x rise over control, directionally matching Lerma-Martin's OL result. Reference genes in the same matrix: MX1 immune 0.542 vs oligodendrocytes 0.005 (~100x myeloid-skewed); DDX58 lymphocytes 0.779 > vascular 0.439 > immune 0.385 > OPC 0.343 > astrocytes 0.251 > oligodendrocytes 0.196 > neurons 0.118; MAVS is far more uniform (0.28-0.66 across all classes). Caveat: snRNA-seq under-samples low-abundance cytoplasmic transcripts, so these are relative, not absolute, levels, and the per-cell-type means are not statistically tested here.

findings.claim: NEGATIVE FINDING: IFIH1 is absent from every supplementary table of Schirmer et al. 2019 Nature, including the cell-type-specific MS-vs-control DE list (3,277 rows) and the 11,071-gene lesion-stage list — even though its paralogues DDX58 and DHX58 and several ISGs ARE in the lesion-stage list, all declining from early to late lesion.
findings.evidence: I parsed 41586_2019_1404_MOESM1_ESM.xlsx (Supplementary Tables 1-7). Supplementary Table 3 (cell_type / gene_ID / gene_name / FC / FDR; MS vs control DE per cell type, 3,277 rows): no IFIH1; the only ISG present is ISG15, exclusively in 'Endo cells' (FC=1.217, FDR=1.39e-99). Supplementary Table 5 (ensembl/gene/pval/qval/n_expr/exp_early/exp_late/direction; 11,071 genes ordered along lesion stage): DDX58 q=3.81e-2, exp_early=0.222, exp_late=0.135, direction=-1; DHX58 q=1.42e-3, early 0.0909, late 0.0135, direction=-1; IFIT1 q=5.63e-3, early 0.478, late 0.0808, direction=-1; IFIT3 q=3.54e-7, direction=-1; STAT1 q=4.20e-2, early 0.481, late 0.152, direction=-1; ISG15 q=3.32e-3, direction=-1; B2M q=3.40e-7, direction=-1. Neither the string 'IFIH1' nor 'ENSG00000115267' occurs anywhere in the workbook (72,062 unique strings, 23,043 gene-like). So IFIH1 fell below Schirmer's expression/detection filter in 48,919 nuclei of MS cortex+subcortical WM — an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence of change.

findings.claim: NEGATIVE FINDING: IFIH1 and all RLR/ISG genes are absent from every supplementary table of Jakel et al. 2019 Nature (GSE118257, MS white matter oligodendrocyte heterogeneity).
findings.evidence: I parsed all six supplementary Excel files (41586_2019_903_MOESM3..8_ESM.xlsx), covering OPC, COP, Oligo1-6, ImOlG/imOLG, Astrocytes1-2 marker and DE sheets. Largest file (MOESM5) contains 2,442 unique gene-like symbols. IFIH1: absent from all six. DDX58, DHX58, MAVS, MX1, IFIT1, IFIT3, STAT1, IRF7, OAS1, EIF2AK2: absent from all six. ISG15 appears once (MOESM5) and B2M twice. The paper's oligodendrocyte-state signatures therefore carry no information about MDA5.

findings.claim: NEGATIVE FINDING: there is no published immunohistochemistry or protein-level measurement of MDA5 in human multiple sclerosis brain tissue.
findings.evidence: PubMed query ((MDA5[tiab] OR IFIH1[tiab]) AND (brain[tiab] OR CNS[tiab] OR cerebral[tiab]) AND (immunohistochemistry[tiab] OR immunostaining[tiab] OR immunofluorescence[tiab])) returns exactly 1 record: PMID 36457126, 'An AGS-associated mutation in ADAR1 catalytic domain results in early-onset and MDA5-dependent encephalopathy with IFN pathway activation in the brain' (J Neuroinflammation 2022) — a mouse Adar1 model, not MS, not human. Broader query ((IFIH1 OR MDA5) AND multiple sclerosis) in PubMed returns 22 records, none of which is a brain-tissue expression study: the set is dominated by SNP-association genetics (rs1990760 etc.), peripheral-blood IFN-beta pharmacogenomics, and reviews. Europe PMC full-text queries combining IFIH1 with 'MS lesion'/'white matter lesion'/'demyelinated lesion' (37 hits) and with snRNA-seq terms (17 hits) surfaced no MS-brain IHC either. Conclusion: all direct MS-brain evidence for MDA5 is transcript-level only.

findings.claim: The only protein-level (IHC) data on MDA5 in primate CNS come from an SIV encephalitis model, not MS: MDA5 protein is CONSTITUTIVELY expressed in neurons in uninfected brain and is undetectable in perivascular macrophages and astrocytes, becoming strongly induced in those glial/myeloid compartments only on infection.
findings.evidence: Rhesus macaque SIV study (J Infect Dis 2011;204:1104, doi 10.1093/infdis/jir469). Uninfected brain IHC: RIG-I and MDA5 'undetectable in perivascular macrophages and astrocytes, while being constitutively expressed in neurons'. Infected brain: both 'clearly induced in perivascular macrophages and astrocytes' while 'maintained in neurons'. qPCR: MDA5 mRNA induced ~20.7-fold by day 4 post-infection vs 4.2-fold for RIG-I; MDA5 ~21-fold induction in white matter by day 7. Grey matter had higher basal levels of both with minimal infection-driven change. Caveat: macaque, infectious not autoimmune, and IHC baseline 'undetectable' in glia conflicts with transcript-level detection of IFIH1 in human astrocytes/microglia — likely a sensitivity issue, so this should be weighted as suggestive for the neuron-high baseline claim, not decisive.

findings.claim: Peripheral-blood MDA5 in MS moves in the OPPOSITE direction to MS brain lesion tissue, so blood data must not be used as a proxy for CNS IFIH1.
findings.evidence: Asadikaram et al. 2021, Biotechnol Appl Biochem 68(2):267-271 (PMID 32311159): qRT-PCR of peripheral leukocytes from 30 newly diagnosed MS patients vs 35 healthy controls — 'mRNA levels of MDA5 and RIG-1 were significantly decreased in the MS patients in comparison to the healthy controls'; after 6 months of IFN-beta-1a, RIG-I was upregulated but MDA5 was NOT (no effect-size numbers given in the abstract; the paper reports significance only). Contrast: Hundeshagen et al. 2012, J Neuroinflammation 9:140 (PMID 22727118): in the 11/61 MS patients with an elevated endogenous type-I-IFN signature (MX1-high), 'pathogen receptors (for example, TLR7, RIG-I and IFIH1) ... were also expressed more strongly' in PBMC, attributed to ISGF3 overactivity. So in blood IFIH1 tracks the patient's systemic IFN tone rather than MS status per se.

findings.claim: In MS white-matter bulk tissue, IFIH1 abundance tracks immune-cell and astrocyte content and is inversely related to myelin content — consistent with the lesion signal being driven by infiltrating/activated immune cells plus glia rather than by neurons.
findings.evidence: Own Spearman correlation of log2(CPM+1) across all 96 GSE283092 MS white-matter samples: IFIH1 vs PTPRC/CD45 rho=+0.592 (p=1.1e-12); vs CD3E rho=+0.570 (p=1.8e-11); vs TYROBP rho=+0.568 (p=2.1e-11); vs C1QB rho=+0.523 (p=2.6e-9); vs GFAP rho=+0.519 (p=3.9e-9); vs MS4A1 rho=+0.515 (p=5.7e-9); vs MX1 rho=+0.487 (p=6.6e-8); vs CSF1R rho=+0.429 (p=4.1e-6); vs AQP4 rho=+0.338 (p=5.1e-4); vs P2RY12 rho=+0.294 (p=2.9e-3); NEGATIVE vs MBP rho=-0.620 (p=1.7e-14) and PLP1 rho=-0.467 (p=3.0e-7); essentially flat vs CLDN5 rho=+0.034 (p=0.74) and weakly negative vs SNAP25 rho=-0.202 (p=0.045). Caveat: these are cross-sample correlations in bulk tissue and are confounded by lesion state (all markers shift together with demyelination), so they indicate co-variation, not cell-of-origin.

findings.claim: IFIH1 is reported as differentially expressed in progressive-MS patient-derived induced neural stem cells in vitro — but this is NOT brain tissue and must be kept separate from the lesion data.
findings.evidence: Neuron 2025, 'Integrated omics reveals disease-associated radial glia-like cells with epigenetically dysregulated interferon response in multiple sclerosis' (PMID 41075785, PMC12834227). Fibroblasts from healthy controls and progressive-MS (PMS) donors were directly reprogrammed to induced neural stem cells (iNSCs). Bulk transcriptomics showed DE transcripts ISG15, IFIT1, SERPINE1; GSEA on DE transcripts identified pathways enriched in PMS iNSCs including 'IFN-alpha/-beta signalling (IFIT2 and OASL)' and 'response to cytokine (IFIH1 and STAT6)', plus IFN-associated TFs IRF-8, IRF-5, IRF-2. No fold-change or p-value for IFIH1 itself is given in the text; it is cited as a leading-edge gene of an enriched gene set (Figure 1C; Table S2). The paper's headline cell type is a disease-associated radial-glia-like cell with an epigenetically dysregulated interferon response.

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of stimulated human astrocyte transcriptomes nominates IFIH1 as one of five hub genes of the astrocyte inflammatory response — establishing astrocytes as IFIH1-inducible, though the stimuli were not MS-derived.
findings.evidence: Front Cell Neurosci 2026 (PMID 42591297, PMC13461556): robust rank aggregation across 11 RNA-seq datasets, 153 samples (91 stimulated, 62 control) of astrocytes exposed to TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta, palmitic acid, SARS-CoV-2, Borrelia burgdorferi. 130 DEGs (125 up, 5 down). STRING/Cytoscape PPI network of 33 immune/inflammation nodes, 200 edges, average node degree 12.1, clustering coefficient 0.711, PPI enrichment p<1.0e-16; the five hub nodes by combined degree + betweenness centrality were CXCL10, DDX58, IFIH1, IL1B, TLR3. The authors emphasise 'the consistent upregulation of the cytosolic sensors DDX58 (RIG-I) and IFIH1 (MDA5) across diverse non-viral inflammatory contexts', which they interpret as astrocyte 'antiviral mimicry'. Caveat: cultured astrocytes (iPSC-derived, fetal and primary), no MS tissue, no per-gene fold-change reported for IFIH1 in the abstract or the text I could extract.

research.cell_type_ranking:
YES — this angle contributes two directly measured CNS rankings, which must be read separately because one is baseline abundance and one is disease-responsiveness.

(A) BASELINE per-nucleus IFIH1 abundance in human MS/control white matter (my own reanalysis of GSE180759, Absinta 2021; 66,432 nuclei; mean counts-per-10K, % nuclei detected):
lymphocytes 0.394 (7.4%) > vascular/endothelial 0.322 (6.8%) > myeloid/microglia-macrophage 0.294 (5.9%) >> astrocytes 0.089 (2.0%) > oligodendrocytes 0.059 (1.7%) > OPC 0.028 (1.0%) ~ neurons 0.027 (1.0%).
So within CNS tissue the CNS-resident cell with the highest IFIH1 is the microglia/macrophage compartment; astrocytes are ~3x lower; oligodendrocytes, OPCs and neurons are the lowest. Non-parenchymal lymphocytes and vascular cells outrank all glia.

(B) DISEASE-RESPONSIVE ranking — which cell type's IFIH1 actually CHANGES in MS (Lerma-Martin 2024 Nat Neurosci, published pseudobulk DESeq2):
1. OLIGODENDROCYTES — the only cell type with significant IFIH1 upregulation: +0.91 log2FC in chronic active lesions (padj 0.012) and +1.09 in chronic inactive lesions (padj 0.0047). DDX58, EIF2AK2, IRF7, IFIT1 and B2M move up in the same cell type, so this is a coherent dsRNA-sensing/IFN program in oligodendrocytes.
2. Myeloid cells — same direction (+0.95 log2FC, chronic inactive vs control) but padj 0.116, not significant.
3. T cells — IFIH1 LOWER in chronic active than chronic inactive lesions (-0.96, padj 0.042).
4. Astrocytes, OPCs, neurons, endothelial, B cells — no significant IFIH1 change reported.

(C) These two rankings are not contradictory: oligodendrocytes have LOW baseline IFIH1 but are the most numerous nucleus in white matter (45,697/66,432 = 69% of nuclei in GSE180759; 64,834/103,780 = 62% in Lerma-Martin), so they carry the statistical power, and their fold-change is real (my GSE180759 reanalysis independently shows oligodendrocyte IFIH1 rising from 0.032 CP10K in control WM to 0.050 at lesion edges and 0.079 in periplaque WM).

(D) One protein-level caveat that cuts against a glia-first ranking: in uninfected macaque brain MDA5 protein IHC was constitutive in NEURONS and undetectable in perivascular macrophages and astrocytes (doi 10.1093/infdis/jir469). Human transcript data put neurons lowest. This mRNA/protein and human/macaque conflict is unresolved and should be flagged in any final ranking.

(E) Bulk-tissue anchor for absolute level: IFIH1 sits at ~13-16 CPM in control/normal-appearing white matter (logCPM 3.74-4.02 in GSE138614; median 14.4 CPM in GSE283092 NAWM), rising to ~20-29 CPM in lesions. That is a low-to-moderately expressed gene — roughly 1/1000 of GFAP and 1/700 of PLP1 in the same samples.
research.gaps:
1. NO PROTEIN DATA AT ALL in human MS brain. Zero immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, western blot or proteomic measurement of MDA5 in MS lesions exists in the indexed literature. Every claim above about MS brain is mRNA. Nobody has shown which cells in an MS lesion actually contain MDA5 protein, nor whether the transcript rise translates to protein.

2. NO SPATIAL LOCALISATION. IFIH1 is absent from Lerma-Martin's spatial niche DEG table (STable_7) despite being significant in their cell-type table, so even the one dataset with 10x Visium does not place IFIH1 in the rim vs core vs perivascular niche. No RNAscope/in-situ for IFIH1 in MS tissue was found.

3. TWO KEY DATASETS COULD NOT BE CHECKED. (a) Macnair et al. 2025 Neuron 113:396-410 (PMID 39708806, 632,000 nuclei / 156 samples, the largest MS snRNA-seq resource) is paywalled and not in PMC; its supplementary factor gene lists could not be retrieved, so whether IFIH1 loads on any of their glial-response factors is UNKNOWN. (b) Feng/Simons et al. 2025 Immunity 58:2989 (PMID 41167189), the snRNA-seq + MERFISH chronic-active-lesion atlas that explicitly reports 'inflamed microglia displaying an interferon response' at the lesion rim, is also paywalled — IFIH1 could not be checked in exactly the paper most likely to contain it. These are the two highest-value remaining targets.

4. THE ISG-vs-BASELINE CONFOUND IS NOT RESOLVED BY ANY MS BRAIN STUDY. IFIH1 is itself an ISG. Nothing I found separates 'this cell type constitutively holds more MDA5' from 'this cell type is currently sitting in more interferon'. In Lerma-Martin the oligodendrocyte IFIH1 rise travels with IRF7 (+3.0), IFIT1 (+1.19) and B2M (+1.93) in the same cells, which argues the oligodendrocyte signal is induced, not constitutive — but no one has measured IFIH1 in sorted, unstimulated human CNS cell types alongside MS tissue to settle it.

5. STATISTICAL FRAGILITY OF THE PUBLISHED RESULTS. The Lerma-Martin IFIH1 result rests on 6 MS donors / 12 lesions and padj values of 0.005-0.012 within a 49,888-row table. The Elkjaer FDRs (0.0073-0.021) come from a group with a retracted companion paper. The Chen/Brain 2025 IFIH1 claim is a text mention I could not back with a per-gene fold-change or FDR (the DEG tables are not in the PMC supplementary), and my own unpaired test of their deposited counts gave p=0.14 for the exact contrast they report. No single result is individually strong; the case rests on three independent cohorts agreeing on direction.

6. NO ABSOLUTE PROTEIN OR TRANSCRIPT COPY NUMBER PER CELL TYPE. I have CPM for bulk tissue and CP10K for nuclei, but no TPM-per-purified-cell-type figure for human CNS from MS tissue, and no comparison to the immune-cell baseline (e.g. pDC, monocyte) that would tell a reader whether 'high for a glial cell' is high in absolute terms.

7. NO LONGITUDINAL OR ACTIVITY-STRATIFIED DATA in the snRNA-seq studies. Elkjaer's bulk data show IFIH1 rises in active and chronic active lesions but NOT in inactive lesions or NAWM (FDR 0.21 and 0.45), implying the change tracks inflammatory activity; Lerma-Martin's oligodendrocyte result is, confusingly, slightly LARGER in chronic INACTIVE than chronic active lesions. This bulk/single-nucleus discrepancy about which lesion stage matters is unexplained.

8. MOUSE/EAE EVIDENCE NOT COVERED by this angle, and the one CNS MDA5 IHC study found is macaque SIV encephalitis, not MS — cross-species and cross-disease extrapolation is doing unacknowledged work in every prior claim about 'MDA5 in the CNS'.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 is significantly UPREGULATED in OLIGODENDROCYTES in human subcortical MS lesions versus control white matter (Lerma-Martin 2024 STable_6) — strongest cell-type-resolved DE result for IFIH1 in MS brain.
verdicts.reason: I re-downloaded the Springer supplementary file myself; it is byte-identical to the copy used (md5 d4433e525e704c617e0f3c979286ce01). All four IFIH1 rows match to every reported digit: OL CAvsCtrl baseMean=132.9643, log2FC=0.904969786, lfcSE=0.292319, stat=3.09582, p=1.9627e-3, padj=1.21782e-2; OL CIvsCtrl log2FC=1.094652, padj=4.69657e-3; MC CIvsCtrl padj=0.11551 (NS); TC CAvsCI log2FC=-0.964198, padj=4.21137e-2. Table has exactly 49,888 data rows. IFIH1 confirmed absent from STable_3 (27 rows), STable_4 (84), STable_5 (365) and STable_7 (2,515). BUT four material problems the claim does not disclose: (1) the cited PMID 39443718 is WRONG — that PMID is 'Eating disorder debut cases during COVID-19 lockdown in adults' (Eur Eat Disord Rev 2025). Correct is PMID 39501036 / PMC11614744, Nat Neurosci 27:2354-2365. (2) STable_6 is PRE-FILTERED at nominal p<0.062 (max p in table = 0.0619), so IFIH1's absence for AS/OPC/NEU/EC means 'not nominally significant', not 'tested and null'. (3) BC, SC and TC have ONLY the CAvsCI contrast in the table — there is no vs-control contrast for them at all, so 'does not appear for BC or SC in any of the three contrasts' is vacuous for those types. (4) The cohort is described wrongly: STable_1 shows 12 MS samples from 8 donors (not 6) plus 7 controls; and the pseudobulk DEG rests only on the snRNA-seq subset (STable_2 'Batch snRNA-seq'): 6 CA samples from 5 donors, 4 CI samples from just 2 donors, 6 controls. The strongest IFIH1 result (CIvsCtrl, padj=4.7e-3) therefore rests on 2 MS donors. Also, IFIH1/MDA5 occurs ZERO times in the paper's own text (PMC11614744) — this is an unremarked supplementary-table result, not a finding the authors report.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the published supplementary DEG table of Lerma-Martin et al. 2024 (Nat Neurosci 27:2354-2365; PMID 39501036, NOT 39443718), IFIH1 is significantly upregulated in oligodendrocytes in both chronic active (log2FC=+0.905, padj=1.22e-2) and chronic inactive (log2FC=+1.095, padj=4.70e-3) subcortical MS lesions versus control white matter, by pseudobulk DESeq2. It is not significant in myeloid cells (padj=0.116) and is down in T cells between lesion types (CAvsCI log2FC=-0.964, padj=4.21e-2). This is an unremarked supplementary-table result — IFIH1 is never mentioned in the paper itself. Caveats: the table is pre-filtered at p<0.062, so absence in astrocytes/OPC/neurons/endothelium means 'not nominally significant', not 'unchanged'; B/stromal/T cells have no versus-control contrast at all; and the snRNA-seq pseudobulk behind these numbers comprises only 6 chronic-active samples (5 donors), 4 chronic-inactive samples (2 donors) and 6 controls.

verdicts.claim: The whole cytosolic dsRNA-sensing/ISG module moves UP specifically in oligodendrocytes, while MX1 and IFI44L move DOWN in endothelial cells and astrocytes — the MS interferon shift is cell-type-directional, not uniform.
verdicts.reason: Every individual number is exact (I verified all of them in the byte-verified file): DDX58 OL CAvsCtrl +0.543879/padj=1.63198e-3 and CIvsCtrl +0.468568/padj=1.47359e-2, baseMean=320.94; EIF2AK2 OL CAvsCtrl +0.513160/padj=2.07951e-3, baseMean=504.82; IRF7 OL CAvsCtrl +2.998609/padj=1.39477e-2 and AS CAvsCtrl +1.213413/padj=7.82869e-3; IFIT1 OL CIvsCtrl +1.190207/padj=2.05639e-2; B2M OL CIvsCtrl +1.925867/padj=1.35501e-2; MX1 EC -1.535852/padj=0.030982 and -1.877828/padj=0.0161691; IFI44L AS -1.561017/padj=0.0227411 and EC -1.998610/padj=0.0259353; MAVS AS/EC/MC/OL CIvsCtrl all negative with the stated padj. DHX58 and ISG15 are indeed absent from the whole table. But the HEADLINE is contradicted by the claim's own evidence: MAVS — the obligate adaptor through which MDA5 and RIG-I signal, i.e. the core of the 'cytosolic dsRNA-sensing module' — is significantly DOWN in oligodendrocytes (CIvsCtrl log2FC=-0.656, padj=7.82e-4), the very same cell type and contrast in which IFIH1 is up. So the module does not move up as a unit in OL. Further counter-examples in the same table: STAT1's only appearance is DOWN (OPC CIvsCtrl -0.793); OAS1 is down in OPC (both contrasts); EIF2AK2 is DOWN in OPC (CIvsCtrl -0.636, padj=0.0374) while up in OL. Separately, 'MX1 and IFI44L move DOWN in endothelial cells and astrocytes' implies both genes in both cell types: MX1 has NO astrocyte row anywhere in the table (only EC, plus an UP row in T cells, CAvsCI +1.410), and only IFI44L is down in both AS and EC.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the Lerma-Martin cell-type DEG table the interferon/dsRNA-sensing response is cell-type-directional rather than uniform: in oligodendrocytes the sensors and effectors IFIH1 (+0.905), DDX58 (+0.544), EIF2AK2 (+0.513), IRF7 (+2.999) and IFIT1 (+1.190) are significantly up, whereas classic ISGs fall in vascular and astrocytic compartments (MX1 in endothelium -1.536/-1.878; IFI44L in astrocytes -1.561 and endothelium -1.999). The move is NOT a coherent whole-module shift, however: MAVS, the adaptor required for MDA5/RIG-I signalling, is significantly DOWN in oligodendrocytes themselves (-0.656, padj=7.8e-4) as well as in astrocytes, endothelium and myeloid cells, and STAT1, OAS1 and EIF2AK2 are down in OPC. MX1 is not reported in astrocytes at all. DHX58/LGP2 and ISG15 are absent from the table entirely.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 is significantly upregulated in active and chronic active WM lesions of progressive MS vs control WM in GSE138614 bulk RNA-seq, whereas DDX58 and DHX58 are NOT changed in any lesion type.
verdicts.reason: I parsed all five author-deposited edgeR tables myself. Every figure is exact: IFIH1 (ENSG00000115267.5) AL logFC=0.558094, logCPM=4.02261, LR=8.73967, P=3.1136e-3, FDR=0.0209408; CA logFC=0.478441, logCPM=3.78855, LR=10.2214, P=1.38819e-3, FDR=7.27914e-3; RL logFC=0.603736, P=0.0116481, FDR=0.0608235; IL logFC=0.313115, P=0.0944516, FDR=0.213326; NAWM logFC=0.200943, P=0.110586, FDR=0.449957. DDX58 FDRs 0.550/0.217/0.911/0.981/0.533 and DHX58 FDRs 0.9917/0.3373/0.7773/0.6821/0.9846 — never significant, exactly as stated and in the stated AL/CA/IL/NAWM/RL order. I also checked the retraction caveat: PubMed and Europe PMC records for PMID 31829262 carry NO 'Retracted Publication' or 'Expression of Concern' publication type and commentCorrectionList is null, so the standing 2019 paper is clean — the researcher's caveat was appropriately worded. Abstract confirms 73 MS WM areas vs 25 control WM areas. Two limits worth noting: effect sizes are modest (logFC 0.478-0.558 = 1.39-1.47x, at ~13-16 CPM), and the paralogue-specificity does NOT generalise — in GSE283092 I found DHX58 significantly UP in remyelinated lesions (paired FC=1.38, p=0.0022) and non-foamy active lesions (FC=1.28, p=0.013).
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the author-deposited edgeR tables of GSE138614 (Elkjaer 2019, Acta Neuropathol Commun 7:205; 73 MS WM areas vs 25 control WM areas), IFIH1 is significantly up versus control white matter in active lesions (logFC=+0.558, FDR=0.021) and chronic active lesions (logFC=+0.478, FDR=7.3e-3), a trend in remyelinating lesions (FDR=0.061), and not significant in inactive lesions or NAWM. In this dataset DDX58 and DHX58 are not significant in any lesion type. Effects are modest (~1.4-1.5x at ~13-16 CPM). The paralogue-specificity is dataset-specific, not a general property: in GSE283092 DHX58 rises significantly in remyelinated and non-foamy active lesions by paired testing. The standing 2019 paper carries no retraction or expression-of-concern flag.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 is a named, statistically significant DEG in Chen et al. Brain 2025 — among the most significant genes upregulated in foamy active lesions of poorly remyelinating MS donors vs efficiently remyelinating donors.
verdicts.reason: The quoted sentence is verbatim-exact in the full text (PMC12129743): 'The most significant DEGs upregulated in ALs foamy of PRDs included SNX3, IFIT1, IFIT3, MOCS2, EIF2AK2 and IFIH1.' IFIH1 occurs exactly once in the whole paper. The surrounding text confirms the DEG counts precisely: 'RLs (17 DEGs) and ALs non-foamy (8 DEGs) between ERDs and PRDs (FDR < 0.05)' and 'a more distinct difference ... in ALs foamy (502 DEGs)'; and for NAWM, 'the NAWM did not show differences between the donor groups'. Cohort confirmed: NBB n=239 stratified into ERD n=21 and PRD n=19; bulk RNA-seq of RLs, ALs non-foamy, ALs foamy and NAWM. I independently confirmed GSE283092 holds exactly 96 samples. PubMed metadata confirms Brain 148:2201-2217, PMID 39718981. The claim correctly notes this is a PRD-vs-ERD contrast (MS vs MS), not MS vs control, and correctly notes IFIH1 appears alongside IFIT1/IFIT3/EIF2AK2 as part of an interferon signature.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Chen JQA et al., Brain 2025;148(6):2201-2217 (PMID 39718981) states verbatim that 'The most significant DEGs upregulated in ALs foamy of PRDs included SNX3, IFIT1, IFIT3, MOCS2, EIF2AK2 and IFIH1' — the single mention of IFIH1 in the paper. This is a poorly-remyelinating-vs-efficiently-remyelinating donor contrast within MS (not MS vs control), in foamy active lesions, where 502 genes reached FDR<0.05 versus 17 in remyelinated lesions, 8 in non-foamy active lesions and none in NAWM (ERD n=21, PRD n=19, from NBB n=239; 96 bulk RNA-seq samples, GEO GSE283092). No per-gene fold-change or FDR for IFIH1 is given in the text. IFIH1 appears as one member of a type-I-IFN/dsRNA-response cluster.

verdicts.claim: Own reanalysis of GSE283092 raw counts: IFIH1 ~14-15 CPM in MS NAWM rising ~1.4-1.8x in lesions, largest in foamy active lesions; ERD-vs-PRD directionally reproducible but only p=0.14.
verdicts.reason: I independently reran this from the raw count matrix and series matrix and reproduced the group medians to the decimal: ERD NAWM 14.37 (n=27), PRD NAWM 15.18 (n=20), ERD RL 18.55 (n=14), PRD RL 20.26 (n=7), ERD AL non-foamy 20.62 (n=7), PRD AL non-foamy 18.01 (n=7), ERD AL foamy 22.12 (n=7), PRD AL foamy 29.24 (n=7, mean 41.27, max 78.47) — all eight exact. Pooled NAWM median 14.42 (n=47) vs lesions 20.27 (n=49), Mann-Whitney z=-4.518, p=6.34e-6 (claim: z=-4.52, p=6.2e-6). Matrix confirmed 61,541 genes, 96 samples, median library 26,946,756 = 26.9M — exact. Paired Wilcoxon on log2 ratios reproduces directionally and in magnitude, with small p-value differences attributable to exact vs approximate Wilcoxon: foamy active FC=1.82 p=2.4e-4 (claim 1.79, p=0.0015); remyelinated FC=1.38 p=3.5e-4 at n=21 (claim 1.36, p=0.0009, n=20 — one pair difference, from the two dual-labelled NAWM samples); non-foamy FC=1.22 p=0.19 (claim 1.21, p=0.152), NS either way. Comparison genes reproduce: DDX58 1.26/p=0.0061, MX1 2.12/p=4.9e-4, CSF1R 1.64/p=0.033, GFAP 1.65/p=7.3e-4, MBP 0.49/p=2.4e-4. ERD vs PRD in AL foamy: 22.12 vs 29.24, FC=1.322, Mann-Whitney p=0.165 (claim 1.32, p=0.142) — same conclusion, not significant. The honest statement that the naive nonparametric test does not reproduce the paper's FDR<0.05 is correct and appropriately attributed to the authors' covariate-adjusted model.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Independent reanalysis of GSE283092 (96 samples, 61,541 genes, median library 26.9M) confirms IFIH1 sits at ~14-15 CPM in MS NAWM and rises in lesions: pooled NAWM median 14.42 vs lesions 20.27 (Mann-Whitney p=6.3e-6). Paired against same-donor NAWM, IFIH1 rises 1.8-fold in foamy active lesions (n=13, p<0.001) and 1.4-fold in remyelinated lesions (n=21, p<0.001), but not significantly in non-foamy active lesions (1.2-fold, p=0.19). Within foamy active lesions, PRD exceeds ERD 29.24 vs 22.12 CPM (1.32-fold) but this is not significant by an unpaired nonparametric test (p=0.14-0.17); the paper's FDR<0.05 comes from a covariate-adjusted model. The paired lesion-vs-NAWM result is the more robust statement. Note the rise is not IFIH1-specific — MX1 rises 2.1-fold and GFAP 1.7-fold in the same samples.

verdicts.claim: NEGATIVE: IFIH1/MDA5 does not appear anywhere in the published output of Absinta et al. 2021 Nature (GSE180759), nor do DDX58, DHX58, MX1, ISG15, IFIT1, STAT1, IRF7, OAS1, TLR3 or EIF2AK2.
verdicts.reason: I parsed both supplementary workbooks. 41586_2021_3892_MOESM4_ESM.xlsx contains exactly the 13 tables plus a table of contents as listed (S1, S2_IHC, S3_ALL, S4_IMM, S5_OL, S6_OPC, S7_AST, S8_peripheral immune, S9_WGCNA, S10 Drugs_MIMS-foamy, S11 Drugs_MIMS-iron, S12_IMM_by_location, S13_VAS). Across all sheets IFIH1, DDX58, DHX58, MX1, ISG15, IFIT1, IFIT3, STAT1, IRF7, OAS1, TLR3, EIF2AK2, IFI44L and MAVS are all absent, while the positive controls FTL, FTH1, C1QA, CD163, SPP1, GFAP, IFITM3, B2M and HLA-A are all present — so the search was correctly specified and would have found these genes had they been there. MOESM5 (Extended Fig 10 source data, 9 sheets) contains none of them either. My unique-string count (3,803 after stripping) differs trivially from the claimed 4,091 raw shared strings — a deduplication difference, not a substantive one. One scope limit: I could not independently extract text from the main-article PDFs to confirm the body text, so my verification covers the supplementary tables and source data, which is what the claim is scoped to.
verdicts.corrected_claim: IFIH1/MDA5 is absent from every supplementary table and the Extended Data source-data file of Absinta et al. 2021 Nature (PMID 34497421), as are DDX58, DHX58, MX1, ISG15, IFIT1, IFIT3, STAT1, IRF7, OAS1, TLR3, EIF2AK2, IFI44L and MAVS, while positive controls (FTL, FTH1, C1QA, CD163, SPP1, GFAP, IFITM3, B2M, HLA-A) are present. The MIMS-foamy/MIMS-iron microglial signatures are therefore not built on RLR/ISG genes and the paper offers no published evidence either way on IFIH1 in MS lesions. This is an absence from curated, thresholded output lists, which is weaker than a tested null result.

verdicts.claim: Own reanalysis of raw GSE180759 counts: IFIH1 is detectable but sparse and ranks LYMPHOCYTES > VASCULAR > MYELOID/IMMUNE >> ASTROCYTES > OLIGODENDROCYTES > OPC ~ NEURONS; within oligodendrocytes it rises 1.6-2.5x over control WM.
verdicts.reason: I recomputed this end-to-end from GSE180759_expression_matrix.csv.gz with per-nucleus totals over the full matrix and reproduced every value exactly: lymphocytes 0.394 CP10K / 7.39% / n=406; vascular_cells 0.322 / 6.79% / n=1,708; immune 0.294 / 5.85% / n=5,432; astrocytes 0.089 / 2.02% / n=8,211; oligodendrocytes 0.059 / 1.68% / n=45,697; OPC 0.028 / 1.01% / n=2,175; neurons 0.027 / 0.96% / n=2,803. Oligodendrocytes by region also exact: control WM 0.032 / 0.96% / n=4,264; chronic active edge 0.050 / 1.11% / n=12,658; chronic inactive edge 0.050 / 1.15% / n=11,193; periplaque WM 0.079 / 2.59% / n=17,563. Reference genes exact too: MX1 immune 0.542 vs OL 0.005; DDX58 0.779/0.439/0.385/0.343/0.251/0.196/0.118 in the stated order; MAVS 0.277-0.661 across classes. Two metadata errors: the matrix holds 29,432 genes, not 30,559, and there are 66,431 nuclei, not 66,432 (that is the annotation line count including its header). One important confound the claim does not state: control white matter comes from 3 donors (11_69, 12_002, 14_043) that contribute NO MS tissue, while all MS regions come from 5 entirely different donors — so the oligodendrocyte 'rise over control' is wholly between-donor, unbalanced and untested. Also the highest oligodendrocyte value is periplaque WM (0.079), not the lesion edge, which is the opposite of a lesion-gradient expectation. I checked the depth confound and it does not explain the ranking: lymphocytes have the LOWEST median UMI (1,688) yet the highest detection rate, so if anything their top rank is conservative.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In raw GSE180759 snRNA-seq (66,431 nuclei, 29,432 genes), IFIH1 is detectable but very sparse and ranks lymphocytes 0.394 CP10K (7.4% of nuclei) > vascular 0.322 (6.8%) > myeloid/immune 0.294 (5.9%) >> astrocytes 0.089 (2.0%) > oligodendrocytes 0.059 (1.7%) > OPC 0.028 (1.0%) ~ neurons 0.027 (1.0%). This ordering is not a sequencing-depth artefact (lymphocytes have the lowest median UMI yet the highest detection). Within oligodendrocytes, IFIH1 is 1.6x higher at chronic active and chronic inactive lesion edges and 2.5x higher in periplaque white matter than in control white matter — directionally consistent with Lerma-Martin's oligodendrocyte result, but this comparison is untested statistically and fully confounded by donor, since the 3 control-WM donors contribute no MS tissue and the 5 MS donors no control tissue. The peak being in periplaque rather than lesion-edge white matter argues against a simple lesion gradient. snRNA-seq under-samples low-abundance cytoplasmic transcripts, so these are relative, not absolute, levels.

verdicts.claim: NEGATIVE: IFIH1 is absent from every supplementary table of Schirmer et al. 2019 Nature, though DDX58, DHX58 and several ISGs are in the lesion-stage list, all declining from early to late lesion.
verdicts.reason: I parsed 41586_2019_1404_MOESM1_ESM.xlsx directly. Row counts are exact: Supplementary Table 3 has 3,277 data rows, Supplementary Table 5 has 11,071. Neither 'IFIH1' nor 'ENSG00000115267' occurs anywhere in the workbook (72,064 unique strings in my parse vs 72,062 claimed — a trivial stripping difference). Every quoted Table 5 value is exact: DDX58 q=3.81299e-2, early 0.222222, late 0.134680, direction -1; DHX58 q=1.42186e-3, early 0.0909091, late 0.0134680, -1; IFIT1 q=5.63376e-3, early 0.478114, late 0.0808081, -1; IFIT3 q=3.54368e-7, -1; STAT1 q=4.19740e-2, early 0.481481, late 0.151515, -1; ISG15 q=3.31728e-3, -1; B2M q=3.40096e-7, -1. Table 3's ISG15 in 'Endo cells' is exact: FC=1.216774, FDR=1.3929e-99. One trivial internal inconsistency: B2M is also present in Table 3 in six cell types and is interferon-responsive, so 'the only ISG present is ISG15' holds only if B2M is not counted as an ISG — yet claim 2 does count B2M in its ISG module. The claim's own closing caveat (absence of evidence, not evidence of absence of change) is the correct reading.
verdicts.corrected_claim: IFIH1 and its Ensembl ID are absent from every supplementary table of Schirmer et al. 2019 Nature (PMID 31316211), including the 3,277-row cell-type MS-vs-control DE list and the 11,071-gene lesion-stage list — it fell below the detection/expression filter in 48,919 nuclei. Its paralogues and several ISGs are present in the lesion-stage list and all decline from early to late lesion: DHX58 q=1.4e-3, DDX58 q=3.8e-2, IFIT1 q=5.6e-3, IFIT3 q=3.5e-7, ISG15 q=3.3e-3, STAT1 q=4.2e-2, B2M q=3.4e-7. In the cell-type DE list the only ISG is ISG15, in endothelial cells (FC=1.217, FDR=1.4e-99), with B2M additionally up in six cell types. This is an absence of evidence about IFIH1, not evidence that IFIH1 is unchanged.

verdicts.claim: NEGATIVE: IFIH1 and all RLR/ISG genes are absent from every supplementary table of Jäkel et al. 2019 Nature (GSE118257).
verdicts.reason: I parsed all six supplementary workbooks (41586_2019_903_MOESM3-8_ESM.xlsx). IFIH1 is absent from all six, as are DDX58, DHX58, MAVS, MX1, IFIT1, IFIT3, STAT1, IRF7, OAS1 and EIF2AK2. ISG15 appears only in MOESM5 and B2M only in MOESM5 and MOESM6 — matching the claim. MOESM5 is the largest (24 sheets, 2,454 unique strings in my parse vs the claimed 2,442 gene-like symbols — consistent given headers are included in mine). One correction that strengthens rather than weakens the finding: the claim describes coverage as 'OPC, COP, Oligo1-6, ImOlG/imOLG, Astrocytes1-2', but MOESM5 in fact also covers Neuron1-5, Microglia_Macrophages, Pericytes, Endothelial cells1-2, Immune cells, Macrophages and Vascular smooth muscle, so the negative spans far more cell types than stated.
verdicts.corrected_claim: IFIH1 is absent from all six supplementary Excel files of Jäkel et al. 2019 Nature (PMID 30747918, GSE118257), as are DDX58, DHX58, MAVS, MX1, IFIT1, IFIT3, STAT1, IRF7, OAS1 and EIF2AK2; ISG15 appears once and B2M twice. The sheets span not only the oligodendroglial and astrocyte populations but also neurons, microglia/macrophages, pericytes, endothelium, immune cells and vascular smooth muscle, so this paper's cell-state signatures carry no information about MDA5 across any of those types. As with all such lists, this is absence from curated marker/DE output, not a tested null.

verdicts.claim: NEGATIVE: there is no published immunohistochemistry or protein-level measurement of MDA5 in human multiple sclerosis brain tissue.
verdicts.reason: I reran both PubMed queries through E-utilities and reproduced the counts exactly: the IHC query returns exactly 1 record, PMID 36457126, and the broad '(IFIH1 OR MDA5) AND multiple sclerosis' query returns exactly 22 records, including 32311159 and 22727118 as stated. I confirmed PMID 36457126 is indeed a CRISPR mouse Adar1 D1113H model — 'we established a mutant mouse model', with IHC/ISH on mouse brain — so it is mouse, not MS, not human, as claimed. I then ran four additional independent queries designed to break the negative ('MDA5 AND multiple sclerosis AND (autopsy OR post-mortem OR lesion)' = 1 hit, a review; 'IFIH1 AND demyelination AND protein' = 15; '(MDA5 OR IFIH1) AND (oligodendrocyte OR microglia OR astrocyte) AND human brain' = 13; 'MDA5[tiab] AND (western blot OR protein expression) AND brain[tiab]' = 2). None is a human MS brain-tissue protein/IHC study: the hits are mouse AGS models, in-vitro astrocyte/endothelial work, a JEV endothelial study, the SIV macaque paper, and reviews. Standard limitation: a keyword-search negative cannot be exhaustive, since a paper could report MDA5 IHC without those terms in title/abstract.
verdicts.corrected_claim: No published immunohistochemistry or other protein-level measurement of MDA5 in human multiple sclerosis brain tissue could be located across six independent PubMed/Europe PMC query formulations; the only CNS MDA5 IHC records retrieved are a mouse Adar1 Aicardi-Goutières model (PMID 36457126) and an SIV-infected macaque study (PMID 21881126). All direct MS-brain evidence for MDA5 is therefore transcript-level only. This is a bounded search negative, not proof of non-existence.

verdicts.claim: The only protein-level (IHC) data on MDA5 in primate CNS come from an SIV encephalitis model: MDA5 protein is constitutively expressed in neurons in uninfected brain, undetectable in perivascular macrophages and astrocytes, and strongly induced in those compartments on infection.
verdicts.reason: The scientific content is verbatim-confirmed from the full text, but the species is WRONG. The paper (Co JG, Witwer KW, Gama L, Zink MC, Clements JE; J Infect Dis 2011;204(7):1104-1114; PMID 21881126) used PIGTAILED macaques — 'Fifty-three pigtailed macaques (Macaca nemestrina) were intravenously inoculated with SIV/DeltaB670' — not rhesus macaques as the claim states. Everything else checks out verbatim: uninfected brain, 'RIG-I and MDA5 was undetectable in perivasular macrophages and astrocytes, while being constitutively expressed in neurons'; infected brain, 'RIG-I and MDA5 were clearly induced in perivascular macrophages and astrocytes. Expression of both proteins was maintained in neurons'. qPCR confirmed: at day 4, 'RIG-I levels increased 4.2-fold, while MDA5 levels increased 20.7-fold'; white matter MDA5 'reaching a peak of 21-fold induction by 7 days postinfection'. Grey/white contrast confirmed verbatim: 'gray matter had higher basal levels of expression of both proteins, but there was little change in expression of either protein during SIV infection'. The claim's own caveats (macaque, infectious not autoimmune, IHC 'undetectable' in glia conflicting with transcript-level detection, weight as suggestive only) are appropriate and I endorse them. I could not independently establish the exclusivity assertion ('the only protein-level data in primate CNS'), so that part remains unverified.
verdicts.corrected_claim: The principal protein-level (IHC) data on MDA5 in primate CNS come from an SIV encephalitis model in PIGTAILED macaques (Macaca nemestrina), not rhesus (Co et al., J Infect Dis 2011;204:1104-1114; PMID 21881126). In uninfected brain, RIG-I and MDA5 were undetectable by IHC in perivascular macrophages and astrocytes while constitutively expressed in neurons; on infection both were clearly induced in perivascular macrophages and astrocytes and maintained in neurons. MDA5 mRNA rose 20.7-fold by day 4 versus 4.2-fold for RIG-I, with a ~21-fold white-matter peak at day 7, while grey matter had higher basal levels of both with little infection-driven change. Weight this as suggestive only for a neuron-high protein baseline: it is a non-primate-autoimmune infectious model in a different species, and the 'undetectable' glial baseline conflicts with clear transcript-level detection of IFIH1 in human astrocytes and microglia, most likely an antibody-sensitivity floor.

verdicts.claim: Peripheral-blood MDA5 in MS moves in the OPPOSITE direction to MS brain lesion tissue, so blood data must not be used as a proxy for CNS IFIH1.
verdicts.reason: Both underlying quotes are verbatim-correct. Asadikaram (PMID 32311159, Biotechnol Appl Biochem 2021): 'mRNA levels of MDA5 and RIG-1 were significantly decreased in the MS patients in comparison to the healthy controls', with 30 new MS cases vs 35 controls in peripheral leukocytes by RT-PCR, and 'IFN-β 1a therapy leads to the upregulation of RIG-1, but not MDA5'. Hundeshagen (PMID 22727118, J Neuroinflammation 2012): 'pathogen receptors (for example, TLR7, RIG-I and IFIH1) and transcription factors were also expressed more strongly, which could be attributed to an overactivity of ISGF3', in 11 of 61 patients with high endogenous IFN activity. But the headline inference does not follow. (1) It rests on a single small study with no effect sizes reported, in one population, in a low-profile journal. (2) Hundeshagen actually shows IFIH1 UP in an MS subset — the SAME direction as brain — so the two blood studies disagree with each other, rather than blood disagreeing with brain. (3) Hundeshagen's contrast is MS-high-IFN vs MS-low-IFN, not MS vs healthy control, so it is not a like-for-like counterpart to Asadikaram. (4) Decisively, no study has measured IFIH1 in blood and brain in the same individuals, so 'moves in the opposite direction' is an inference stitched across non-comparable cohorts, compartments, assays and contrasts. The claim's own closing sentence — that in blood IFIH1 tracks systemic IFN tone rather than MS status — is the defensible version.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Peripheral-blood IFIH1/MDA5 in MS is inconsistent across the two available studies and cannot be used as a proxy for CNS IFIH1. One small study (n=30 MS vs 35 controls, peripheral leukocytes, qRT-PCR; PMID 32311159) reports MDA5 and RIG-I mRNA significantly DECREASED in MS versus healthy controls, with IFN-beta-1a raising RIG-I but not MDA5; no effect sizes are given. A separate PBMC microarray study (PMID 22727118) reports IFIH1 expressed more strongly in the 11 of 61 MS patients with a high endogenous type-I-IFN signature, attributed to ISGF3 overactivity — i.e. UP, but in an MS-subset-vs-MS-subset comparison, not MS vs control. Blood IFIH1 therefore appears to track a patient's systemic interferon tone rather than MS status per se. No study has measured IFIH1 in blood and brain in the same individuals, so no directional comparison between the two compartments is actually established.

verdicts.claim: In MS white-matter bulk tissue, IFIH1 abundance tracks immune-cell and astrocyte content and is inversely related to myelin content — consistent with the lesion signal being driven by infiltrating/activated immune cells plus glia rather than by neurons.
verdicts.reason: I recomputed all fifteen Spearman correlations from the raw GSE283092 counts and every rho matches to three decimals: PTPRC +0.592, CD3E +0.570, TYROBP +0.568, C1QB +0.523, GFAP +0.519, MS4A1 +0.515, MX1 +0.487, CSF1R +0.429, AQP4 +0.338, P2RY12 +0.294, MBP -0.620, PLP1 -0.467, CLDN5 +0.034, SNAP25 -0.202. My p-values are systematically somewhat larger than those quoted (e.g. PTPRC 2.2e-10 vs 1.1e-12; MBP 1.6e-11 vs 1.7e-14; CD3E 1.4e-9 vs 1.8e-11), suggesting the claim used a more liberal p computation, but every correlation remains significant at the stated threshold except CLDN5, and the two borderline calls (CLDN5 p=0.74 NS, SNAP25 p=0.048) reproduce. Two interpretive cautions: 'driven by' is causal language that cross-sample bulk correlation cannot support — the researcher's own caveat says exactly this — and the correlation with MX1 (+0.487), a pure interferon-stimulated gene with no cell-type meaning, is as strong as the correlations with cell-type markers, so IFIH1 may be tracking interferon tone as much as cellular composition.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Across the 96 bulk MS white-matter samples of GSE283092, IFIH1 co-varies positively with leucocyte and glial markers (PTPRC rho=+0.59, CD3E +0.57, TYROBP +0.57, C1QB +0.52, GFAP +0.52, MS4A1 +0.52, CSF1R +0.43, AQP4 +0.34, P2RY12 +0.29), negatively with myelin genes (MBP -0.62, PLP1 -0.47), is flat against endothelium (CLDN5 +0.03, NS) and weakly negative against neurons (SNAP25 -0.20). These are cross-sample correlations in bulk tissue in which every marker shifts together with demyelination, so they demonstrate co-variation, not cell of origin and not causation. Note that IFIH1 correlates with the pure ISG MX1 (+0.49) about as strongly as with any cell-type marker, so the signal is equally consistent with IFIH1 tracking local interferon tone as with it tracking immune-cell content.

verdicts.claim: IFIH1 is reported as differentially expressed in progressive-MS patient-derived induced neural stem cells in vitro — but this is NOT brain tissue and must be kept separate from the lesion data.
verdicts.reason: IFIH1 occurs exactly once in the full text (PMC12834227), and the sentence does not say IFIH1 is differentially expressed. Verbatim: 'Gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) on DE transcripts identified several pathways enriched in the PMS iNSCs, including gene sets associated with IFN-alpha/-beta signaling (IFIT2 and OASL), response to stress (NLRP2 and CLU), response to cytokine (IFIH1 and STAT6), lipid metabolic process (ID2 and ANXA1), and TFs associated with IFN signaling (IRF-8, IRF-5, and IRF-2)'. So IFIH1 is named only as an illustrative member of an enriched gene set, not as an individually significant DEG — GSEA set membership is not the same as per-gene differential expression, and the individually-named DE transcripts are ISG15, IFIT1 and SERPINE1, not IFIH1. The claim's own evidence block states this correctly ('No fold-change or p-value for IFIH1 itself is given in the text; it is cited as a leading-edge gene of an enriched gene set'), so the error is confined to the headline wording. The in-vitro framing, the fibroblast-to-iNSC reprogramming design and the disease-associated radial-glia-like headline cell type are all confirmed in the text.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In Neuron 2025 (PMID 41075785), IFIH1 is named once, as an example member of the GSEA-enriched 'response to cytokine' gene set in progressive-MS patient-derived induced neural stem cells — not as an individually significant differentially expressed gene (the named DE transcripts are ISG15, IFIT1 and SERPINE1). No fold-change or p-value for IFIH1 is reported. This is fibroblast-derived iNSCs in vitro, not brain tissue, and must be kept separate from lesion data; it supports only the weak statement that IFIH1 sits within an interferon/cytokine-response programme that is epigenetically and transcriptionally elevated in PMS-derived iNSCs.

verdicts.claim: A meta-analysis of stimulated human astrocyte transcriptomes nominates IFIH1 as one of five hub genes of the astrocyte inflammatory response — establishing astrocytes as IFIH1-inducible, though the stimuli were not MS-derived.
verdicts.reason: Every reported figure is verbatim-confirmed in the full text (PMC13461556): '11 RNA-Seq datasets, encompassing a total of 153 samples (91 stimulated, and 62 controls)'; '130 differentially expressed genes (DEGs), including 125 upregulated and 5 downregulated'; 'a subnetwork of 33 nodes'; 'comprised 33 nodes and 200 interaction edges with an average node degree of 12.1, a cluster coefficient of 0.711'; PPI enrichment p<1.0e-16; and 'Network analysis revealed five hub nodes, CXCL10, DDX58, IFIH1, IL-1beta, and TLR3'. The hub criterion is confirmed as 'top 15% of the distribution for both degree and betweenness centrality'. The interpretive sentence is verbatim: 'A remarkable finding of this meta-analysis is the consistent upregulation of the cytosolic sensors DDX58 (RIG-I) and IFIH1 (MDA5) across diverse non-viral inflammatory contexts'. Astrocyte sources confirmed as iPSC-derived, fetal and primary. Two qualifications: the stimulus list also includes FBS alongside the six named; and the paper itself explicitly warns that 'the candidate hub nodes identified based on network connectivity should not be interpreted as drivers of astrocyte inflammatory responses and have not been independently experimentally validated', so 'establishing' is stronger than a topology-based nomination with no per-gene effect size warrants.
verdicts.corrected_claim: A robust-rank-aggregation meta-analysis of 11 RNA-seq datasets (153 samples: 91 stimulated, 62 control) of cultured human astrocytes (iPSC-derived, fetal and primary) exposed to TNF-alpha, IL-6, IL-1beta, palmitic acid, FBS, SARS-CoV-2 and Borrelia burgdorferi found 130 DEGs (125 up, 5 down) and nominates IFIH1 as one of five topological hub nodes (with CXCL10, DDX58, IL1B, TLR3) in a 33-node, 200-edge PPI network (mean degree 12.1, clustering 0.711, enrichment p<1e-16) (PMID 42591297). The authors highlight consistent upregulation of DDX58 and IFIH1 across diverse non-viral inflammatory contexts, indicating astrocytes can induce IFIH1. Caveats: cultured astrocytes only, no MS tissue, no per-gene fold-change reported for IFIH1, and the authors explicitly state the hub nodes are not to be read as drivers and were not experimentally validated.

verification.overall:
ADVERSARIAL VERIFICATION SUMMARY — 15 claims checked against primary sources. I re-downloaded the Lerma-Martin supplementary file (byte-identical, md5 d4433e525e704c617e0f3c979286ce01), parsed all supplementary workbooks myself, and independently re-ran three of the researcher's own reanalyses end-to-end from raw data.

VERDICTS: 11 CONFIRMED, 4 OVERSTATED, 0 REFUTED, 0 UNVERIFIABLE.

WHAT HELD UP REMARKABLY WELL. The quantitative work is unusually solid. I reproduced from raw data, to the reported decimal place: (a) all four Lerma-Martin IFIH1 rows and ~30 comparison-gene rows; (b) all five GSE138614 edgeR rows for IFIH1/DDX58/DHX58; (c) all eight GSE283092 IFIH1 group medians, the pooled Mann-Whitney z=-4.518, and the 26.9M median library size; (d) all fifteen GSE283092 Spearman rho values to three decimals; (e) every single GSE180759 value — seven cell-type means, seven detection percentages, seven cell counts, four region values, and the MX1/DDX58/MAVS reference profiles. The four negative findings (Absinta, Schirmer, Jäkel, no-human-MS-IHC) all verified, including reproducing both PubMed query counts exactly (1 and 22). I could not refute a single substantive quantitative assertion.

ERRORS FOUND THAT MATTER.
1. WRONG PMID (claims 1, 2). PMID 39443718 is "Eating disorder debut cases during COVID-19 lockdown in adults" (Eur Eat Disord Rev). Lerma-Martin 2024 Nat Neurosci 27:2354-2365 is PMID 39501036 / PMC11614744. The DOI was correct; the PMID must be corrected before this goes anywhere.
2. WRONG SPECIES (claim 11). The SIV study used PIGTAILED macaques (Macaca nemestrina), not rhesus.
3. SELF-CONTRADICTORY HEADLINE (claim 2). "The whole cytosolic dsRNA-sensing module moves UP in oligodendrocytes" is contradicted by the claim's own data: MAVS — the adaptor MDA5 signals through — is significantly DOWN in oligodendrocytes (log2FC=-0.656, padj=7.8e-4), same cell type, same contrast. STAT1, OAS1 and EIF2AK2 are also down in OPC. Also MX1 has no astrocyte row at all, so "MX1 and IFI44L down in endothelium and astrocytes" overstates.
4. GSEA SET MEMBERSHIP SOLD AS DIFFERENTIAL EXPRESSION (claim 14). The Neuron 2025 paper names IFIH1 once, as an illustrative member of an enriched "response to cytokine" gene set. Its actual named DE transcripts are ISG15, IFIT1, SERPINE1.
5. CROSS-STUDY INFERENCE SOLD AS A FINDING (claim 12). "Blood moves opposite to brain" rests on one small study (n=30/35, no effect sizes); the second cited study shows IFIH1 UP in an MS subset — same direction as brain — and is an MS-vs-MS contrast. No study has measured both compartments in the same people.

UNDISCLOSED CAVEATS I ADDED (these change how strong claim 1 is).
