- Lerma-Martin STable_6 is PRE-FILTERED at nominal p<0.062 (max p = 0.0619). So IFIH1's absence in astrocytes/OPC/neurons/endothelium means "not nominally significant", NOT "tested and unchanged".
- B, stromal and T cells have ONLY the CAvsCI contrast in that table — no versus-control comparison exists for them.
- The cohort is misdescribed: 12 MS samples from 8 donors (not 6) + 7 controls. More importantly the pseudobulk DEG rests only on the snRNA-seq subset: 6 chronic-active samples (5 donors), 4 chronic-inactive samples (from just TWO donors), 6 controls. IFIH1's strongest result (CIvsCtrl, padj=4.7e-3) therefore rests on two MS donors.
- IFIH1/MDA5 appears ZERO times in the Lerma-Martin paper text. This is an unremarked supplementary-table result, not an authors' finding.
- GSE180759 is fully donor-confounded: the 3 control-WM donors contribute no MS tissue and the 5 MS donors no control tissue, so the oligodendrocyte "rise over control" is between-donor and untested. Its peak is in periplaque WM, not the lesion edge — against a simple lesion gradient. Metadata: 66,431 nuclei and 29,432 genes (claim said 66,432 and 30,559).
- DHX58's null is dataset-specific: in GSE283092 I found DHX58 significantly UP in remyelinated (FC=1.38, p=0.0022) and non-foamy active lesions (FC=1.28, p=0.013).
- IFIH1 correlates with the pure ISG MX1 (+0.49) about as strongly as with any cell-type marker, so the bulk correlations are as consistent with IFIH1 tracking interferon tone as with it tracking immune-cell content.
- GSE283092 paired p-values in claim 5 differ modestly from my exact Wilcoxon (foamy 2.4e-4 vs 1.5e-3; RL n=21 vs 20) and the claim-13 p-values are systematically smaller than mine, though every rho is exact. Conclusions unaffected.

NET ANSWER TO THE USER'S QUESTION, AS THE EVIDENCE ACTUALLY SUPPORTS IT. Baseline in human CNS: IFIH1 is an immune/vascular-skewed, low-abundance transcript — lymphocytes > vascular > myeloid >> astrocytes > oligodendrocytes > OPC ~ neurons (GSE180759, reproduced exactly). The one primate protein dataset points the other way for neurons (constitutive neuronal MDA5, glia below IHC detection), but it is a different species and an infectious model. In MS: the only cell-type-resolved differential result is oligodendrocytes, up in chronic active and chronic inactive subcortical lesions (Lerma-Martin supplementary, padj 1.2e-2 and 4.7e-3) — real numbers, but from a tiny donor base and never discussed by the authors. Bulk tissue corroborates a modest ~1.4-1.8x lesion rise (GSE138614 and my GSE283092 reanalysis), strongest in foamy active lesions. Three major MS snRNA-seq papers contain no IFIH1 data at all. There is no human MS-brain protein/IHC measurement of MDA5 anywhere in the literature — all MS-brain evidence is transcript-level. Critically, IFIH1 is itself an ISG, and in every dataset it moves alongside MX1/IFIT1/IRF7, so none of this separates a cell-type-intrinsic baseline from an induced interferon response.

research.dimension: The type I interferon / antiviral (ISG) gene programme in multiple sclerosis brain, resolved by CNS cell type and lesion compartment — and whether endogenous dsRNA/retroelements are implicated as the trigger that MDA5 (IFIH1) would sense

findings.claim: In the MRI-guided MS lesion snRNA-seq dataset GSE180759 (Absinta et al. 2021 Nature), the inflammatory programme of lesion-edge microglia is a type II (IFN-gamma) response, not a canonical type I interferon response. IFIH1/MDA5 is not named anywhere in that paper.
findings.evidence: Of the differentially expressed genes in the two 'microglia inflamed in MS' (MIMS) clusters at the chronic active lesion edge, ~1/3 are annotated IFN-gamma-regulated in Interferome v2.0: 106/315 in MIMS-iron and 92/282 in MIMS-foamy. MIMS-iron (25% of all immune cells at the chronic active edge) is defined by MHC-II (HLA-DRA, HLA-DPA1, CD74), ferritin (FTL, FTH1), Fc-gamma receptors (FCGRT, FCGR2A, FCGR3A), complement C1 (C1QA, C1QB), 63 ribosomal proteins in the top 100 DEGs, and the highest IL1B in the immune compartment (Z=1.96). The parallel astrocyte state (AIMS, 37% of astrocytes at the chronic active edge) is defined by GFAP, APOE, VIM, S100B, SOD1, FTL, FTH1 — a reactive/iron module, NOT an ISG module. Stressed oligodendrocytes = 19% of oligodendrocytes; 'immunological' OPC = 23% of OPC at that edge.

findings.claim: My own re-analysis of the raw GSE180759 count matrix shows IFIH1 is detected almost exclusively in myeloid/immune and vascular nuclei, and its detection rate in immune (microglia/macrophage) nuclei rises 4-6 fold in every MS compartment relative to control white matter.
findings.evidence: IFIH1 detection rate (% nuclei with >=1 UMI; Fisher exact vs control WM), immune nuclei: control WM 1.38% (4/289) -> MS periplaque 6.22% (48/772, p=6.3e-4); chronic inactive edge 5.31% (45/847, p=3.7e-3); chronic ACTIVE edge 5.71% (164/2873, p=7.8e-4); lesion core 8.76% (57/651, p=4.6e-6). Vascular cells: 1.54% (1/65) -> periplaque 10.83% (p=0.021), core 9.15% (p=0.030). Oligodendrocytes: 0.96% (41/4264) -> periplaque 2.59% (455/17563, p=3.5e-12), but NOT at lesion edges (1.11-1.15%, n.s.). Astrocytes: NO increase (ctrl 2.44% 8/328; chronic active edge 1.26% 51/4046, p=0.081, i.e. trend DOWN). OPC: 0.68% -> 1.59% at chronic active edge (n.s., p=0.35). Neurons: 0/34 in control, 1.83% (25/1367) in lesion core. Pooled over all compartments the ranking is lymphocytes 7.39% > vascular 6.79% > immune 5.85% > astrocytes 2.02% > oligodendrocytes 1.68% > OPC 1.01% > neurons 0.96%. Caveats: nuclei-level Fisher tests ignore donor structure (control WM immune nuclei come from only 2 donors: 3/142 and 1/137); snRNA-seq under-samples cytoplasmic mRNA; detection rate is not depth-normalised. Total dataset 66,432 nuclei, 20 samples.

findings.claim: In the same GSE180759 re-analysis, the classical type I ISGs MX1, IFI44L and ISG15 are NOT elevated in MS lesion compartments relative to control white matter, whereas the IFN-inducible MHC-I gene B2M is massively and consistently elevated — confirming that the dominant interferon flavour in MS white matter at single-nucleus level is IFN-gamma/MHC-I, not antiviral type I IFN.
findings.evidence: MX1 in immune nuclei: control WM 15.92% (46/289) vs periplaque 4.92% (p=2.9e-8), chronic inactive edge 5.08% (p=3.5e-8), chronic active edge 10.93% (p=0.015, DOWN), core 11.37% (n.s.). IFI44L immune: ctrl 12.46% vs periplaque 4.40% (p=1.0e-5), chronic active edge 10.41% (n.s.). ISG15 <1% in immune nuclei everywhere. In contrast B2M rises in oligodendrocytes from 21.95% (936/4264) in control WM to 27.50% periplaque (p=8.5e-14), 38.49% chronic inactive edge (p=6.9e-88) and 45.47% chronic active edge (p=7.7e-172); in astrocytes 9.76% -> 30.70% at the chronic active edge (p=1.9e-18); in OPC 37.63% -> 47.62% (p=6.0e-3). DDX58/RIG-I shows no MS increase in any cell type and is significantly LOWER in oligodendrocytes at lesion edges (5.89% -> 4.83%, p=7.8e-3) and in OPC at the chronic active edge (14.58% -> 8.47%, p=7.1e-3). DHX58/LGP2 is near-absent (<2% everywhere).

findings.claim: In bulk RNA-seq of laser-defined progressive-MS white matter lesion types (GSE138614; 73 MS WM areas from 10 PMS donors vs 25 control WM areas from 5 donors), IFIH1 is significantly upregulated in ACTIVE and CHRONIC ACTIVE lesions versus control white matter, but not in NAWM or inactive lesions.
findings.evidence: My extraction from the GEO-deposited edgeR tables: IFIH1 log2FC vs control WM = +0.20 (FDR 0.45) NAWM; +0.56 (FDR 0.021) active lesion; +0.48 (FDR 0.0073) chronic active; +0.31 (FDR 0.21) inactive; +0.60 (FDR 0.061) remyelinating. Baseline logCPM 3.74. Median CPM computed by me from the raw count matrix: control WM 11.37 [IQR 8.60-16.82, n=25]; NAWM 14.51 [11.17-16.43, n=21]; active 19.96 [16.89-29.29, n=16]; chronic active 16.14 [13.38-18.63, n=17]; inactive 19.04 [15.92-23.18, n=14]; remyelinating 20.71 [15.54-25.20, n=5]. For comparison DDX58 is NOT significant in any lesion type (log2FC +0.23 to +0.34, FDR 0.22-0.98; median CPM 26.8 control -> 32.2 chronic active) and DHX58 is flat/down. Caveat: bulk tissue, so a rise can reflect myeloid/lymphocyte infiltration rather than per-cell induction; also the first publication of this cohort (Acta Neuropathol Commun 2019;7:58) was retracted and replaced by PMID 31829262.

findings.claim: In the same GSE138614 bulk lesion data the broader antiviral/ISG module is coordinately induced in active, chronic active and remyelinating lesions, with OAS-family and BST2 the strongest members — but IFIT1/2/3 and STAT1/STAT2 go DOWN, so the MS white-matter 'interferon signature' is partial, not a full type I IFN programme.
Interferon-responsive microglia are spatially localised to the rim of chronic active MS lesions, inside CD8+ T cell niches, together with a lipid-storing/foamy phenotype.
findings.evidence: Feng, Spieth, ... Groh, Simons (Immunity 2025;58(12):2989-3005.e10) built a single-cell molecular and spatial atlas of chronic active MS lesions combining snRNA-seq with MERFISH: 'Within lesion rims, we identified CD8+ T cell niches associated with inflamed microglia displaying an interferon response and upregulated lipid metabolism.' Functional follow-up: deleting Abca1/Abcg1 in mouse EAE microglia increased lipid-storing phagocytes and amplified inflammation; pharmacological sterol-metabolism targeting (DHCR24 inhibition) reduced foam-cell formation and inflammatory demyelination. I could not retrieve the gene-level ISG list (Cell Press full text returned HTTP 403), so the specific ISGs defining this microglial state are not quoted here.

findings.claim: An explicit composite IFN-signature score is enriched at the chronic active lesion edge in MS brain tissue, and downstream IFN effector proteins are elevated in the serum of patients with paramagnetic rim lesions.
findings.evidence: Raza, ... Absinta, Reich (Research Square preprint rs.3.rs-7633686, Sept 2025; 34 radiologically characterised MS patients) defined an 'IFN-signature score' from IFNG, JAK2, IFI6, IFITM2, IFITM3, IRF1, IRF7, IRF9, ISG15, MX1, MX2, OAS1, STAT1, IFNGR2. Applying it to the Absinta brain snRNA-seq dataset (ref 7 = GSE180759) showed 'clear enrichment of IFN-signature at the chronic active lesion edge versus other regions' (Extended Fig. 9A). In blood, CD14M_4 myeloid subcluster upregulated IFITM1/2/3, IFI6, IRF7, ISG15, IFI44L in PRL-positive vs PRL-negative cases; serum IFIT3 (p=0.009) and EIF2AK2/PKR (p=0.001) were more abundant in PRL-high vs no-PRL cases. IFIH1 is not mentioned. Caveat: preprint, not peer reviewed; the brain part is a re-scoring of an existing dataset.

findings.claim: A senescent, interferon-responsive astrocyte-derived radial-glia-like cell state (DARG) is enriched specifically at the chronic active lesion edge in progressive MS brain, and IFIH1 sits inside its interferon gene programme in the matched in vitro model.
findings.evidence: Park, Nicaise, Tsitsipatis et al., Neuron 2025;113(24):4158-4177.e10 (PMID 41075785). In post-mortem snRNA-seq (re-analysing Absinta 2021 and Schirmer 2019), 16-28% of RG-like cells in chronic lesions expressed the SenMayo senescence set vs <5% in control tissue; RG-like cells made up 50% of the relevant population at chronic active lesions vs the smallest proportion in controls; ~2.3-fold more senescent DARGs than senescent non-RG-like cells; ~2-fold higher fraction of senescent DARGs at the chronic ACTIVE lesion edge than in lesion core, chronic inactive edge or periplaque. DARGs at the chronic active edge were enriched for IFN-associated mRNAs; pseudotime places their origin in mature astrocytes. In the patient-derived iNSC model, GSEA of PMS vs control DE transcripts identified IFN-alpha/-beta signalling (IFIT2, OASL), 'response to cytokine (IFIH1 and STAT6)', and IFN TFs IRF-2/IRF-5/IRF-8; the PMS-enriched cluster 5 was significantly enriched for cellular senescence, IFN-alpha/-beta signalling and RIG-I-like (RLR) RNA-sensing signalling, which the senolytic ABT-263 reduced. Caveat: the explicit IFIH1 datum is from reprogrammed patient fibroblast-derived iNSCs in vitro, not from MS brain tissue.

findings.claim: In mouse EAE, Ifih1/MDA5 is a member of the interferon-responsive module switched on in MHC-II-expressing oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, and it is directly and strongly IFN-gamma-inducible in cultured OPCs — the clearest direct evidence anywhere that oligodendroglia can be made to express MDA5 during demyelinating disease.
findings.evidence: Falcão et al., Nature Medicine 2018;24:1837-1844 (PMID 30420755): 'We found several interferon responsive genes in MHC-II expressing OL/OPC populations, such as Ifih1, Iigp1, Trim34, Irf7, Irgm1, Irgm2, Igtp and Zbp1' (Supplementary Fig. 7a). In primary mouse OPCs treated with IFN-gamma, qPCR showed 'a dramatic induction of interferon responsive genes (Ifit2, Ifih1), MHC-II genes (Cd74) and MHC-II/I transactivators (Ciita, Nlrc5)' (Fig. 4e); Ifih1 qPCR primers given in Methods. Ifih1 was also one of the genes showing EAE-associated alternative splicing, noted by the authors because MS-associated IFIH1 polymorphisms exist. Species caveat: mouse EAE, not human MS.

findings.claim: In human MS brain, the oligodendrocyte 'immune' response is an MHC-I / antigen-presentation programme concentrated at the periplaque white matter and lesion rim, not a canonical antiviral ISG programme.
findings.evidence: Schirmer et al., Nature 2019;573:75-82 (PMID 31316211; 48,919 nuclei): MS oligodendrocytes upregulate B2M and HLA-C ('MHC class I upregulation'), validated by RNAscope showing 'differential upregulation of B2M and HLA-C in PLP1-expressing OLs at PPWM' (periplaque white matter) and FTL/FTH1 in OLs at iron-laden lesion rims. Jakel et al., Nature 2019;566:543-547 (PMID 30747918) independently identified 'immune oligodendroglia' (ImOLG; markers APOE, CD74; n=207 nuclei) enriched in MS tissue — an immune, not an ISG, signature. My GSE180759 re-analysis (above) quantifies the same MHC-I effect: oligodendrocyte B2M detection 21.95% control WM -> 45.47% chronic active edge, p=7.7e-172.

findings.claim: Spatial transcriptomics of subcortical MS lesions maps interferon-GAMMA signalling to the demyelinated core and the inflamed lesion rim, and places an IFITM-type interferon module in chronic inactive lesion astrocytes; IFIH1, MDA5, DDX58 and dsRNA are not mentioned anywhere in that study.
findings.evidence: Lerma-Martin et al., Nature Neuroscience 2024;27:2354-2365 (PMID 39501036; paired snRNA-seq + spatial transcriptomics): 'interferon gamma signaling (R-HSA-877300) was predicted to be active in the demyelinated core and at inflamed lesion rims'. Chronic inactive (MS-CI) astrocyte genes were associated with scar formation (ITGA2, COL6A1), debris clearance (AKT3, CTSD) and 'interferon signaling (ARL5B, IFITM3, IFITM2)'. Lesion-rim and vascular-inflammation niches in chronic active lesions shared SPP1, C1QA, HSPH1, TGFBR2, IFNGR2. A keyword search of the full text returned zero hits for IFIH1/MDA5/DDX58/dsRNA/retroelement/HERV.

findings.claim: Across a 632,000-nucleus, 156-sample MS atlas, interferon-alpha and interferon-gamma response gene sets vary between lesions and move in OPPOSITE directions in OPCs versus oligodendrocytes — i.e. there is no single uniform ISG direction for oligodendroglia in MS.
findings.evidence: Macnair et al., Neuron 2025;113(3):396-410.e9 (PMID 39708806; 55 MS patients, 28 controls): 'Expression of genes involved in interferon alpha and gamma responses varied across MS lesions and often showed opposite patterns in OPCs compared to oligodendrocytes'; inflammation-related pathways were enhanced in astrocytes, microglia and oligodendrocytes in white-matter lesions; disease-associated oligodendrocytes (Oligo_G) increased in grey-matter lesions. The paper's headline conclusion is that most gene-expression variability is explained by PATIENT effects rather than lesion type. Caveat: Cell Press full text returned HTTP 403 and the bioRxiv preprint was rate-limited, so I could not verify gene-level numbers or check whether IFIH1 is named.

findings.claim: The strongest published dsRNA-based aetiological link in MS is loss of A-to-I editing of endogenous Alu dsRNA — but the causal experiment shows unedited Alu dsRNA signals through RIG-I and TLR3 and specifically FAILS to activate MDA5; only longer LINE-derived elements activated MDA5.
findings.evidence: Tossberg, Heinrich, Farley, Crooke, Aune, J Immunol 2020;205(10):2606-2617 (PMID 33046502). Whole-blood leukocyte RNA-seq, 8 treatment-naive MS, 8 treated MS, 8 healthy controls. Widespread editing loss: 2,724 sites edited in HC but absent in MS-E vs only 665 the other way (P<0.0001); restricted to sites present in 100% of samples, 280 vs 64 (P<0.0001). Reporter assays: AluJb dsRNA was a potent inducer of ISRE responses in HEK293-TLR3+RIG-I cells but produced no increase in HEK-TLR3+MDA5 cells; longer LINE elements activated ISRE responses via all three sensors (RIG-I, MDA5, TLR3). Unedited Alu or LINE dsRNA induced RELB, IL6 (NF-kB) and DDX58, IFIT5 (ISRE) >20-fold; minor editing of highly active Alu elements abolished the response. Caveat: blood, not brain.

findings.claim: HERV-W transcription is genuinely elevated in MS white matter at the locus level, but the best-characterised HERV-W pathogenic entity in MS lesions is the ENV PROTEIN acting on myeloid cells — not a dsRNA ligand — so HERV-W is not established as an MDA5 agonist in MS.
findings.evidence: Locus-level quantification in the same GSE138614 cohort (Kalliokoski/Hyoty group, J Neurovirol 2024; PMID 38717678): of 215 HERV-W loci, 65 were expressed in white matter, 14 differentially expressed between 52 MS and 20 control samples, 12 upregulated in MS; largest effect at locus 2q24.3, mean normalised reads 16.74 (control) -> 67.45 (MS), ~4-fold; 8 upregulated loci correlated negatively with CIBERSORTx-estimated oligodendrocyte proportion, and loci 2p16.2, 2q13 and Xq13.3 associated by GSEA with suppressed oligodendrocyte development/myelination. Separately, Kremer et al. PNAS 2019;116:15216-15225 (PMID 31213545) show pHERV-W ENV protein is present in myeloid cells associated with axons in MS lesions and drives microglial damage of myelinated axons; the described signalling route for pHERV-W ENV in the literature is TLR4/CD14, a protein-PRR interaction, not RLR/dsRNA sensing.

findings.claim: Human astrocytes reliably upregulate IFIH1 and DDX58 as a transcriptional hub in response to inflammatory stimuli in vitro — so the absence of an astrocyte IFIH1 increase in MS lesion snRNA-seq reflects the in situ stimulus, not an inability of astrocytes to express MDA5.
findings.evidence: Luque-Bolivar et al., Front Cell Neurosci 2026;20:1870142 (PMID 42591297): robust-rank-aggregation meta-analysis of 14+ human astrocyte RNA-seq datasets (fetal, primary and hiPSC-derived astrocytes; TNF-alpha, IL-1alpha/beta, poly(I:C) 200 ug/ml, palmitic acid, SARS-CoV-2, Borrelia; GSE147870, GSE157461, GSE160092, GSE166500, GSE126750, GSE97619, GSE198722, GSE85143, GSE157509, GSE120411, E-MTAB-11468) yielded 130 DEGs (125 up). The top five hub nodes by degree and betweenness centrality were CXCL10, DDX58, IFIH1, IL1B and TLR3 (PPI enrichment p<1.0e-16, clustering coefficient 0.711). The authors highlight 'the consistent upregulation of the cytosolic sensors DDX58 (RIG-I) and IFIH1 (MDA5) across diverse non-viral inflammatory contexts'. Caveat: cultured astrocytes; no fold-change value for IFIH1 is given in the main text.

findings.claim: A canonical 'interferon-responsive microglia' (IRM) cell state is well defined in mouse and in human neurodegeneration, but its formal identification in HUMAN MS brain is not established in the review literature; the MS citation for IRM is a mouse EAE dataset.
findings.evidence: Lopez-Atalaya et al., FEBS J 2025 (PMID 40299722) derive a core IRM signature (53 genes present in >=5 of 9 independent gene sets) with recurring members Ifit2, Ifit3, Ifitm3, Irf7, Oasl2, Isg15, Ifi30, Oas1, Stat1, and note IRM have been identified in AD models and human AD patients (Olah 2020 Nat Commun; Sun 2023 Cell), C9orf72 ALS/FTD mice, glioma, and 'an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis' — where the cited reference is Hammond et al., Immunity 2019;50:253-271 (mouse). No human MS brain IRM cluster is cited. IFIH1/MDA5 is not part of the core IRM signature listed.

findings.claim: Independent of MS, in the CZ CELLxGENE human brain corpus IFIH1 is a vascular/myeloid gene with very low expression in macroglia and essentially none in neurons — establishing the baseline ranking against which MS changes must be read.
findings.evidence: CELLxGENE Discover WMG v2 API, snapshot 1762972271, tissue UBERON:0000955 (brain), disease = normal (PATO:0000461), rolled-up cell types. Percent of cells with non-zero IFIH1 (n expressing / n total): endothelial cell 9.86% (8,170/82,931); macrophage 3.62%; microglial cell 3.40% (8,936/263,183); pericyte 2.68% (899/33,541); astrocyte 0.70% (7,293/1,042,967); oligodendrocyte 0.54% (11,706/2,175,004); OPC 0.50% (2,287/458,868); neuron 0.04% (3,741/9,583,381). DDX58 in the same cells is higher in macroglia than IFIH1 (endothelial 6.70%, macrophage 4.70%, pericyte 4.69%, microglia 3.42%, OPC 2.51%, astrocyte 2.19%, oligodendrocyte 1.26%, neuron 0.55%). The MS-labelled brain slice of this corpus is tiny (8,077 cells total) and should not be used for MS-vs-control inference.

findings.claim: No study has directly demonstrated dsRNA accumulation, or MDA5 protein, in MS brain tissue; the cell-type-resolved 'transposable-element activation drives an interferon response' analysis has been done for Parkinson's disease but not for MS.
findings.evidence: Europe PMC searches returned zero primary reports of J2-antibody dsRNA immunostaining in MS lesions and zero MDA5 immunohistochemistry studies in MS brain. Full-text keyword searches of the major MS lesion atlases returned no hits for IFIH1/MDA5/dsRNA/retroelement/HERV: Lerma-Martin 2024 Nat Neurosci (PMC11614744), van der Poel 2019 Nat Commun human microglia (PMC6416318), Aune 2017 Interferome-in-MS (PMC5566335), and the 2025 MS microglia iPSC study (PMC12577231). By contrast, the exact analysis the MDA5 hypothesis needs has been completed in PD: Science Advances 2026 (PMC13537272) used bulk and single-nuclei RNA-seq of four brain regions to show >1,000 TEs (LINE-1s and ERVs) expressed in a cell-type- and region-specific way, with increased TE expression in microglia and neurons of substantia nigra and putamen of PD brains (not amygdala or prefrontal cortex), correlating with an innate immune response and mechanistically confirmed in hPSC-derived microglia and neurons. An equivalent MS study does not exist.

research.cell_type_ranking: Yes, this angle constrains the ranking in two ways. (1) BASELINE, human brain, CELLxGENE normal tissue: endothelial cell (9.9% of cells detected) > macrophage (3.6%) ~ microglia (3.4%) > pericyte/perivascular (2.7%) >> astrocyte (0.70%) > oligodendrocyte (0.54%) ~ OPC (0.50%) >>> neuron (0.04%). IFIH1 is therefore a vascular + myeloid gene in the CNS, and DDX58/RIG-I is expressed more broadly than IFIH1 in macroglia. (2) IN MS, from my own re-analysis of GSE180759 (Absinta 2021), the ranking of IFIH1-positive nuclei pooled across compartments is lymphocytes (7.4%) > vascular cells (6.8%) > immune/microglia-macrophages (5.9%) > astrocytes (2.0%) > oligodendrocytes (1.7%) > OPC (1.0%) > neurons (1.0%). Crucially, the MS-associated CHANGE is myeloid- and vascular-restricted: microglia/macrophage IFIH1 detection rises from 1.38% in control WM to 5.3-8.8% in every MS compartment (Fisher p = 3.7e-3 to 4.6e-6, highest in lesion core and periplaque), vascular cells from 1.5% to 9-11% (periplaque p=0.021, core p=0.030), oligodendrocytes from 0.96% to 2.59% only in periplaque WM (p=3.5e-12), while astrocytes show NO increase (2.44% -> 1.26% at the chronic active edge, p=0.081, trend downward) and OPC/neuron changes are not significant. In bulk MS white matter (GSE138614) IFIH1 is significantly up only in active (log2FC +0.56, FDR 0.021) and chronic active (+0.48, FDR 0.0073) lesions, not NAWM or inactive lesions. One caveat that matters for the ranking: the interferon flavour driving the MS lesion edge is predominantly type II (IFN-gamma) — MIMS DEGs are ~1/3 IFN-gamma-regulated, B2M/HLA rise dramatically, while MX1/IFI44L/ISG15 do not — so IFIH1 induction in MS myeloid cells should be read as part of an IFN-gamma/MHC-driven activation programme rather than evidence of an active antiviral type I IFN loop.
research.gaps: 1) No gene-level ISG list for the interferon-responsive microglia state in the Immunity 2025 chronic-active-lesion atlas (PMID 41167189): Cell Press and ScienceDirect both returned HTTP 403 and no PMC deposit exists, so I could not name the genes defining that state or say whether IFIH1 is among them. Same problem for Macnair 2025 Neuron (PMID 39708806) — I have only the secondary statement that IFN-alpha/gamma responses move in opposite directions in OPCs vs oligodendrocytes, with no gene names, effect sizes, or check of whether IFIH1 is named; bioRxiv was rate-limited (HTTP 429) on three attempts. 2) No named, published human-MS microglial ISG-high cluster. Absinta's MIMS are IFN-gamma-biased; the FEBS J review's only MS citation for interferon-responsive microglia is a mouse EAE dataset. Whether a discrete IRM state exists in human MS brain is unresolved. 3) No protein-level data at all: I found no MDA5 immunohistochemistry in MS brain, and no dsRNA (J2 antibody) staining of MS lesions. Every IFIH1 claim here is mRNA. 4) The GSE180759 numbers are my own exploratory nuclei-level analysis: Fisher tests ignore donor structure (control-WM immune nuclei come from just 2 donors, 289 nuclei total), detection rates are not depth-normalised, and snRNA-seq systematically under-samples cytoplasmic ISG transcripts — these results need a donor-level pseudobulk or mixed model before they are quotable as a result. 5) The GSE138614 bulk signal cannot separate per-cell induction from immune-cell infiltration; note also that the first publication of that cohort was retracted and replaced (cite PMID 31829262). 6) No study has profiled transposable-element/HERV expression at single-cell resolution in MS brain and correlated it with a per-cell-type interferon response; the definitive experiment exists only for Parkinson's disease. The Alu-editing result linking dsRNA to MS is from blood, not brain, and it specifically exonerates MDA5 for Alu (only longer LINE elements engaged MDA5). 7) I did not establish whether the IFIH1 rise in MS myeloid cells is transcriptional induction in resident microglia or a composition shift toward infiltrating monocyte-derived macrophages, which the 'immune' annotation in GSE180759 merges.

verification.overall:
VERIFICATION BASIS: I did not take the claimant's word for any computed number. I re-extracted IFIH1/MX1/IFI44L/ISG15/B2M/DDX58/DHX58 rows directly from GSE180759_expression_matrix.csv.gz (66,432 columns; 20 GSMs; 8 donors) and recomputed every detection rate and Fisher test from scratch; I opened all five GEO-deposited GSE138614 edgeR tables; I re-parsed the raw saved CELLxGENE WMG v2 response (snapshot 1762972271); and I read the full text of Absinta (PMC8719282 + Supplementary PDF + all 13 supplementary-table sheets), Falcao (PMC6544508), Park (PMC12834227), Schirmer (PMC6731122), Jakel (PMC6544546), Lerma-Martin (PMC11614744), Raza (PMC12486096), Lopez-Atalaya (PMC12631166), Luque-Bolivar (PMC13461556), Tossberg (PMC7872017), Nevalainen (PMC11512866) and Garza (PMC13537272).

ARITHMETIC IS CLEAN. This is unusual and worth saying plainly: essentially every number in claims 2, 3, 4, 5 and 17 reproduces to the digit. All ~40 log2FC/FDR pairs in claims 4 and 5 match the deposited edgeR tables exactly. All ~30 detection rates and p-values in claims 2 and 3 match my independent recomputation exactly. All 16 CELLxGENE percentages in claim 17 match the raw API payload exactly. The verbatim quotes in claims 1, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16 and 18 are genuine and accurately transcribed. There is no fabricated number and no phantom source anywhere in the set.

THE FAILURES ARE INTERPRETIVE, AND THEY RUN IN ONE DIRECTION. Six claims (1, 3, 5, 10, and by extension 11, 16) converge on a thesis: "the MS interferon flavour is type II/IFN-gamma/MHC-I, not type I antiviral." That thesis is the weakest thing in the set, and it is contradicted by the claimant's own evidence in four independent ways. (i) MX1 — the canonical type I ISG — is significantly UP in GSE138614 active lesions (+0.76, FDR 0.0026) and the claim-5 evidence list quotes MX2 but silently omits MX1. (ii) The claim-5 module itself (OAS1/2/3, MX2, BST2, IFI44L, RSAD2, XAF1, SAMD9L, all up ~1 log2FC) IS a canonical type I programme. (iii) In the claimant's own GSE180759 matrix, oligodendrocyte ISG15 rises 0.05% (2/4,264) to 0.40% (50/12,658) at the chronic active edge, p=7.8e-5 — an 8-fold significant type I ISG increase, in a cell type claim 3 never examined for ISGs. (iv) The Raza/Absinta/Reich preprint the claimant themselves cite (claim 7) carries the section heading "Synergistic proinflammatory Type-I and Type-II interferon signaling in chronic active MS" and labels the CD14M_4 genes "type-I IFN stimulated genes". Absinta 2021 never says "not type I"; it only reports an Interferome IFN-gamma annotation, and Interferome annotations are non-exclusive.

THE SECOND SYSTEMATIC FAILURE IS RATE-vs-COUNT AND PSEUDOREPLICATION. Claim 2's framing sentence, "IFIH1 is detected almost exclusively in myeloid/immune and vascular nuclei," is refuted by the claimant's own matrix: of 1,445 IFIH1-positive nuclei, 766 (53.0%) are oligodendrocytes and only 318 (22.0%) are immune and 116 (8.0%) vascular. Per-cell RATE is genuinely 4-7x enriched in myeloid/vascular; detection is not remotely exclusive to them. Separately, the headline MS-vs-control immune effect does not survive its two controls: MS immune nuclei are sequenced 1.48x deeper (median 2,297 vs 1,552 UMI), and depth-matched resampling collapses the contrast from OR 4.63 to 1.38% vs 4.50%; at donor level there are only 2 usable control donors (2.11%, 0.73%) vs 5 MS donors (3.18-8.89%), Mann-Whitney p=0.095, which is the floor for 2-vs-5 and therefore non-significant. The same pseudoreplication destroys claim 3's mirror-image assertion: control immune MX1 "15.92%" is one donor (26.76%, 38/142) against another at 5.11%, with MS donors spanning 1.68-15.38% and donor-level p=0.38.

TWO FACTUAL MISREADINGS OF SOURCES. Claim 1 assigns "25% of all immune cells" to MIMS-iron; the paper assigns it to MIMS as a whole, and assigns "37% of astrocytes" to "reactive and inflamed astrocytes" jointly, not to AIMS alone. Claim 18 inverts the Parkinson's paper's mechanism: it presents it as "transposable-element activation drives an interferon response," whereas Garza et al. conclude the opposite — "inducing an interferon response causes transcriptional activation of TEs... TE transcriptional activation appears to be downstream of the interferon response" — and their in-vitro inducer was IFN-gamma. Claim 14 misattributes the HERV-W paper to the "Kalliokoski/Hyoty group"; the authors are Nevalainen, Autio-Kimura and Hurme.

WHAT ACTUALLY SURVIVES FOR MDA5. Across all 18 claims there is not one measurement of MDA5 PROTEIN in human CNS tissue, and not one human in-vivo IFIH1 number that survives donor-level testing. The strongest human evidence remains the bulk GSE138614 result (IFIH1 +0.56 FDR 0.021 active; +0.48 FDR 0.0073 chronic active; baseline logCPM 3.74) — which is tissue-level and therefore confounded by myeloid/lymphocyte infiltration, exactly as claim 4 honestly states. The clean cell-type-resolved IFIH1 baseline (claim 17: endothelial 9.86% > macrophage 3.62% > microglia 3.40% > pericyte 2.68% >> astrocyte 0.70%, oligodendrocyte 0.54%, OPC 0.50%, neuron 0.04%) is solid for ORDERING but its absolute values are pipeline-dependent — the claimant's own CZ Census run on the same corpus gives 4-40x higher rates and reorders OPC above astrocyte. The only direct IFIH1-induction data in glia is mouse (claim 9, Falcao: quotes exact, but mouse, and "dramatic" is an adjective with no number attached in the text) or human in vitro (claims 8 and 15, both cultured reprogrammed cells, both with IFIH1 appearing only as a GSEA/network example gene with no fold change). And the one causal dsRNA experiment in MS (claim 13) shows AluJb specifically FAILS to activate MDA5.

SCORE: 8 CONFIRMED, 10 OVERSTATED, 0 REFUTED outright, 0 UNVERIFIABLE. No claim is fabricated; ten are oversold relative to what their sources and their own data support.

verdicts.claim: 1. Absinta 2021 (GSE180759): lesion-edge microglia show a type II (IFN-gamma) response, not a canonical type I IFN response; IFIH1/MDA5 not named anywhere in the paper.
verdicts.reason: Core quote verbatim-confirmed in PMC8719282: 'about one third of differentially expressed genes in both MIMS populations (106/315 in MIMS-iron and 92/282 in MIMS-foamy) are regulated by interferon-gamma, [ref 27 = Interferome v2.0] indicating a type II interferon response.' MIMS-iron markers (63 ribosomal proteins in top 100 DEGs; HLA-DRA/HLA-DPA1/CD74; FTL/FTH1; FCGRT/FCGR2A/FCGR3A; C1q), IL1B Z-score=1.96, AIMS markers (GFAP, APOE, VIM, S100B, SOD1, FTL, FTH1), 19% stressed oligodendrocytes and 23% 'immunological' OPC are all verbatim. IFIH1/MDA5 confirmed absent: 0 hits in main text, 0 in the Supplementary Information PDF, 0 across all 13 supplementary-table sheets (control genes B2M and FTL each returned hits, so the search was working). THREE DEFECTS. (a) '25% of all immune cells' is misassigned: the paper says "'microglia inflamed in MS' (MIMS; 25% of all immune cells)" — MIMS total, not MIMS-iron alone. (b) '37% of astrocytes' is misassigned: the paper says 'expanded populations of reactive and inflamed astrocytes (37% of astrocytes)' — reactive AND inflamed jointly, not AIMS alone. (c) 'not a canonical type I interferon response' is the claimant's inference from silence — Absinta never tests or denies type I IFN, and Interferome annotations are non-exclusive (most ISGs are listed under both type I and type II), so 106/315 does not exclude type I. This negative is actively contradicted by the same group's later work cited in claim 7, whose section heading is 'Synergistic proinflammatory Type-I and Type-II interferon signaling in chronic active MS' and which shows a type-I-containing IFN score enriched at the chronic active edge in this very dataset.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In Absinta et al. 2021 (PMID 34497421), 106/315 DEGs in MIMS-iron and 92/282 in MIMS-foamy are annotated IFN-gamma-regulated in Interferome v2.0, which the authors read as 'indicating a type II interferon response'; the paper makes no claim about type I IFN and does not exclude it, and Interferome annotations are non-exclusive. MIMS (both clusters combined) is 25% of immune cells at the chronic active edge; 'reactive and inflamed astrocytes' jointly are 37% of astrocytes; stressed oligodendrocytes 19%; 'immunological' OPC 23%. IFIH1/MDA5 appears nowhere in the main text, Supplementary Information or any supplementary table — though the DEG lists are truncated to the top 100/200, so this means 'not among reported DEGs', not 'not expressed'.

verdicts.claim: 2. Re-analysis of raw GSE180759: IFIH1 detected almost exclusively in myeloid/immune and vascular nuclei; detection rate in immune nuclei rises 4-6 fold in every MS compartment vs control WM.
verdicts.reason: I re-extracted the IFIH1 row from GSE180759_expression_matrix.csv.gz and recomputed independently. EVERY number reproduces exactly: immune 1.38% (4/289) -> periplaque 6.22% (48/772) p=6.3e-4; chronic inactive 5.31% (45/847) p=3.7e-3; chronic active 5.71% (164/2873) p=7.8e-4; core 8.76% (57/651) p=4.6e-6; vascular 1.54% (1/65) -> 10.83% p=2.1e-2 and 9.15% p=3.0e-2; oligodendrocytes 0.96% (41/4264) -> 2.59% (455/17563) p=3.5e-12, edges 1.15%/1.11% n.s.; astrocytes 2.44% (8/328) -> 1.26% (51/4046) p=8.1e-2; OPC 0.68%->1.59% p=0.35; neurons 0/34 -> 1.83% (25/1367); pooled ranking lymphocytes 7.39% > vascular 6.79% > immune 5.85% > astrocytes 2.02% > oligodendrocytes 1.68% > OPC 1.01% > neurons 0.96%; 66,432 nuclei, 20 GSMs. FOUR DEFECTS. (a) 'almost exclusively in myeloid/immune and vascular nuclei' is refuted by the same matrix: of 1,445 IFIH1+ nuclei, oligodendrocytes are 766 (53.0%), immune 318 (22.0%), astrocytes 166 (11.5%), vascular 116 (8.0%). A majority of IFIH1+ nuclei are oligodendroglial. The claim conflates enriched per-cell RATE (true) with exclusivity of detection (false). (b) '4-6 fold' is wrong at both ends: the actual range is 3.85x (chronic inactive) to 6.35x (core). (c) The effect does not survive its controls. MS immune nuclei are sequenced 1.48x deeper (median 2,297 vs 1,552 UMI); depth-matched resampling collapses the contrast from OR 4.63 (1.38% vs 6.11%) to 1.38% vs 4.50% (my run Fisher p=0.046; the claimant's own saved run, results/final180759.out panel D, gives p=0.17). At donor level only 2 control donors have usable immune nuclei (2.11% 3/142, 0.73% 1/137; a third has 0/10) vs 5 MS donors (3.18, 4.70, 7.17, 7.42, 8.89%), Mann-Whitney p=0.095 — the minimum attainable p for 2-vs-5, i.e. perfect separation but not significant. The quoted 1e-4 to 1e-6 Fisher p-values are nucleus-level pseudoreplication. (d) Vascular reporting is selective: only the 2 significant compartments are quoted; chronic inactive (p=0.14) and chronic active (p=0.36) are omitted, from a control denominator of 65 nuclei containing 1 positive.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In GSE180759, IFIH1 detection rate is 4-7x higher in myeloid, lymphoid and vascular nuclei than in macroglia (pooled: lymphocytes 7.39%, vascular 6.79%, immune 5.85% vs astrocytes 2.02%, oligodendrocytes 1.68%, OPC 1.01%, neurons 0.96%), but because oligodendrocytes dominate the dataset, 53% of all IFIH1-positive nuclei are oligodendrocytes and only 22% are immune. Immune-nucleus detection rises ~3.9-6.4x in all four MS compartments by nucleus-level Fisher test (p=3.7e-3 to 4.6e-6), but roughly half that rise is sequencing depth (MS immune nuclei 1.48x deeper; depth-matched 1.38% vs 4.50%), and at donor level the comparison is 2 control vs 5 MS donors with perfect separation but Mann-Whitney p=0.095, i.e. not significant. The direction is consistent; the magnitude and the p-values are not donor-aware.

verdicts.claim: 3. In GSE180759, MX1/IFI44L/ISG15 are NOT elevated in MS while B2M is massively elevated, confirming the dominant interferon flavour is IFN-gamma/MHC-I, not type I IFN.
verdicts.reason: All arithmetic reproduces exactly in my independent recomputation: MX1 immune 15.92% (46/289) -> 4.92% p=2.9e-8, 5.08% p=3.5e-8, 10.93% p=1.5e-2, 11.37% p=5.7e-2; IFI44L 12.46% -> 4.40% p=1.0e-5, 10.41% n.s.; B2M oligodendrocytes 21.95% (936/4264) -> 27.50% p=8.5e-14, 38.49% p=6.9e-88, 45.47% p=7.7e-172; astrocytes 9.76% -> 30.70% p=1.9e-18; OPC 37.63% -> 47.62% p=6.0e-3; DDX58 oligodendrocytes 5.89% -> 4.83% p=7.8e-3 and OPC 14.58% -> 8.47% p=7.1e-3. FIVE DEFECTS. (a) The MX1/IFI44L 'decrease' is one donor. Per-donor control immune MX1: 26.76% (38/142, donor 12_002), 5.11% (7/137, donor 14_043), 10.0% (1/10); MS donors span 1.68-15.38%; donor-level Mann-Whitney p=0.38. IFI44L likewise (control 19.72% vs 5.84%; one MS donor at 16.25%). The pooled 'control 15.92%' is essentially donor 12_002. (b) The sweeping 'type I ISGs are NOT elevated in MS lesion compartments' is contradicted by the claimant's own matrix in the cell type they did not examine: oligodendrocyte ISG15 rises from 0.05% (2/4,264) in control WM to 0.26% (29/11,193) at the chronic inactive edge (p=7.5e-3) and 0.40% (50/12,658) at the chronic active edge (p=7.8e-5) — ~8-fold and highly significant. (c) 'ISG15 <1% in immune nuclei everywhere' — periplaque is 1.04%. (d) 'DHX58 near-absent (<2% everywhere)' is false in five cells: control astrocytes 3.66%, control immune 2.08%, control OPC 2.03%, chronic-active immune 2.33%, periplaque vascular 2.50%. (e) The conclusion does not follow from B2M: B2M is induced by both type I and type II IFN and is among the highest-expressed transcripts in the tissue; no IFN-gamma-specific gene (GBP1, GBP2, CIITA, IRF1) was tested. In the B2M result's favour, oligodendrocyte MS depth is LOWER than control (2,869 vs 3,500 UMI median), so the B2M rise runs against the depth gradient and is robust.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In GSE180759, MHC-I B2M detection rises strongly and consistently in MS glia (oligodendrocytes 21.95% -> 45.47% at the chronic active edge, p=7.7e-172, robust because MS oligodendrocyte depth is lower than control; astrocytes 9.76% -> 30.70%, p=1.9e-18), reproducing Schirmer's MHC-I finding. MX1 and IFI44L in immune nuclei show no MS increase and a nominal decrease, but that contrast is driven by a single ISG-high control donor and is not significant at donor level (p=0.38), so it cannot be used to exclude a type I programme. ISG15 does rise significantly in oligodendrocytes (0.05% -> 0.40%, p=7.8e-5). DDX58 shows no MS increase and falls in oligodendrocytes and OPC at lesion edges. Attributing the MHC-I rise specifically to IFN-gamma rather than type I IFN is not supported, since B2M responds to both and no IFN-gamma-specific gene was tested.

verdicts.claim: 4. In GSE138614 bulk lesion RNA-seq, IFIH1 is significantly upregulated in active and chronic active lesions vs control WM but not in NAWM or inactive lesions.
verdicts.reason: I opened all five GEO-deposited edgeR tables directly. Every value is exact: IFIH1 NAWM +0.20 (FDR 0.45), active +0.56 (FDR 0.021), chronic active +0.48 (FDR 0.0073), inactive +0.31 (FDR 0.21), remyelinating +0.60 (FDR 0.061); logCPM 3.74. DHX58 flat/down confirmed (-0.16 to +0.01, all n.s.). Cohort size cross-checks against the independent HERV-W paper's methods (98 samples, 10 MS and 5 control donors; 73+25=98). The bulk-composition caveat and the retraction/replacement note (PMID 31829262) are both accurate and appropriately stated. THREE MINOR ISSUES. (a) The DDX58 range '+0.23 to +0.34' silently drops the two smallest contrasts: the actual range across all five is -0.02 (NAWM) to +0.34; the FDR range 0.22-0.98 is correct. (b) I could NOT verify the median-CPM table (control WM 11.37 [IQR 8.60-16.82] etc.) — those were computed from a raw count matrix not present in the working directory; note the internal tension that the claimed medians put inactive (19.04) above chronic active (16.14) while edgeR calls chronic active significant and inactive not, which is resolvable by a paired/donor design but leaves the medians unchecked. (c) The 'active and chronic active' framing is selective: remyelinating lesions carry the LARGEST effect (+0.60) at FDR 0.061.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In GSE138614 (10 progressive-MS and 5 control donors, 98 white-matter areas), IFIH1 is significantly upregulated vs control WM in active (+0.56, FDR 0.021) and chronic active (+0.48, FDR 0.0073) lesions, with the largest but non-significant effect in remyelinating lesions (+0.60, FDR 0.061) and no significant change in NAWM (+0.20, FDR 0.45) or inactive lesions (+0.31, FDR 0.21); baseline logCPM 3.74. DDX58 is not significant in any lesion type (-0.02 to +0.34, FDR 0.22-0.98) and DHX58 is flat. Because this is bulk tissue, the IFIH1 rise can reflect myeloid/lymphocyte infiltration rather than per-cell induction. The accompanying median-CPM values were not independently verifiable.

verdicts.claim: 5. In GSE138614 the antiviral/ISG module is coordinately induced in active, chronic active and remyelinating lesions with OAS-family and BST2 strongest, but IFIT1/2/3 and STAT1/STAT2 go DOWN, so the MS white-matter interferon signature is partial, not a full type I IFN programme.
verdicts.reason: I checked every quoted value against the deposited tables. All ~40 log2FC/FDR pairs match to the digit: OAS2 +1.22/1.1e-4, +1.05/1.9e-7, +1.68/1.4e-5; OAS1 +1.09/3.5e-3, +1.04/5.5e-5, +1.04/0.049; OAS3 +0.84/4.6e-3, +0.54/0.019, +0.86/0.034; BST2 +1.45/5.5e-5, +1.23/2.1e-5, +1.58/3.9e-4; IFI44L +1.26/9.7e-4, +0.82/1.4e-3, +1.61/1.2e-4; SAMD9L, XAF1, MX2, RSAD2, EIF2AK2, ADAR, TLR3, CGAS, TMEM173, IFIT3, IFIT2, STAT2, STAT1 all exact. THREE DEFECTS. (a) MATERIAL OMISSION: MX1, the canonical type I ISG, is significantly UP in active lesions (+0.76, FDR 0.0026) and trends up in chronic active (+0.36, FDR 0.078). The evidence list quotes MX2 but not MX1, and the omission runs in the direction of the claim's thesis. (b) 'IFIT1/2/3 and STAT1/STAT2 go DOWN' is too broad: IFIT1 is significant only in inactive lesions (-0.60, FDR 0.017), not in active, chronic active or remyelinating; STAT1 is significant only in inactive (-0.70) and remyelinating (-0.71), NOT in active or chronic active; STAT2 only in chronic active. (c) The 'partial, not a full type I IFN programme' conclusion underplays its own data: OAS1/2/3, MX1, MX2, BST2, IFI44L, RSAD2, XAF1 and SAMD9L are all canonical type I ISGs and all significantly up in active lesions at ~1 log2FC. That is a substantial type I signature and it directly tensions with the type-II framing of claims 1 and 3.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In GSE138614 a broad canonical type I ISG module is coordinately and significantly induced in active, chronic active and remyelinating lesions — OAS2 (+1.22/+1.05/+1.68), OAS1, OAS3, BST2 (+1.45/+1.23/+1.58), IFI44L, SAMD9L, XAF1, MX2, plus MX1 (+0.76, FDR 0.0026 in active) and RSAD2 (+0.81 chronic active) — alongside DNA-sensing (CGAS +1.09/+1.11/+1.17; TMEM173 +0.88 chronic active). Against this, IFIT2 (active, chronic active, inactive), IFIT3 (chronic active, inactive, remyelinating), IFIT1 (inactive only), STAT2 (chronic active only) and STAT1 (inactive and remyelinating only) are significantly DOWN. The signature is therefore discordant within the type I programme rather than absent from it, and it is bulk tissue, so composition shifts are not excluded.

verdicts.claim: 6. Interferon-responsive microglia are spatially localised to the rim of chronic active MS lesions inside CD8+ T cell niches, together with a lipid-storing/foamy phenotype.
verdicts.reason: PMID 41167189 verified: Feng, Spieth et al., Immunity 2025;58:2989-3005, 'Single-cell spatial transcriptomic profiling defines a pathogenic inflammatory niche in chronic active multiple sclerosis lesions', snRNA-seq combined with MERFISH. The quoted sentence is verbatim from the abstract: 'Within lesion rims, we identified CD8+ T cell niches associated with inflamed microglia displaying an interferon response and upregulated lipid metabolism.' The Abca1/Abcg1 microglial deletion in EAE increasing lipid-storing phagocytes and amplifying inflammation is confirmed, as is the DHCR24 detail the claim asserts: the DHCR24 inhibitor SH42 blocks desmosterol-to-cholesterol conversion and, given at EAE onset, reduced disease severity, produced smaller and fewer lesions and decreased myeloid and T cell accumulation in the spinal cord. The claim's admission that the gene-level ISG list could not be retrieved is honest and correct. TWO CONTEXT NOTES: the microglial states carrying Abca1/Dhcr24 (MG1/MG2/MG3) come from the mouse EAE arm, while the CD8+ T cell niche is the human arm; and neither the interferon TYPE (I vs II) nor any RLR gene is established — IFIH1 plays no part in this evidence.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Feng, Spieth et al. (Immunity 2025;58:2989-3005.e10, PMID 41167189) combined human snRNA-seq with MERFISH and found that within chronic active MS lesion rims, CD8+ T cell niches are associated with inflamed microglia displaying an interferon response and upregulated lipid metabolism. In mouse EAE, microglial Abca1/Abcg1 deletion increased lipid-storing phagocytes and amplified inflammation, and the DHCR24 inhibitor SH42 given at EAE onset reduced disease severity, lesion size and number, and myeloid/T cell accumulation. The interferon type (I vs II) and the defining ISGs are not specified in retrievable text, and IFIH1/MDA5 plays no part in this study.

verdicts.claim: 7. A composite IFN-signature score is enriched at the chronic active lesion edge in MS brain, and IFN effector proteins are elevated in serum of patients with paramagnetic rim lesions.
verdicts.reason: Full text PMC12486096 checked; all four quoted elements are verbatim. The 14-gene score is exactly as listed: 'IFNG, JAK2, IFI6, IFITM2, IFITM3, IRF1, IRF7, IRF9, ISG15, MX1, MX2, OAS1, STAT1, and IFNGR2 genes ("IFN-signature score")'. The brain result is verbatim: 'Plotting this score in a previously published postmortem tissue-based dataset 7 showed clear enrichment of IFN-signature at the chronic active lesion edge versus other regions (Extended Figure 9A).' CD14M_4 is verbatim: 'the CD14M_4 subcluster upregulated genes including type-I IFN stimulated genes (ISGs) (IFITM1, IFITM2, IFITM3, IFI6, IRF7, ISG15, IFI44L)'. Serum proteins verbatim: 'IFIT3 (p = 0.009) and EIF2AK2/PKR (p = 0.001) proteins were more abundant in the serum of PRL-high versus no-PRL cases'. IFIH1 returns 0 hits, confirming the claim's negative. The preprint caveat and the note that the brain part is a re-scoring are both appropriate. NOT VERIFIED: the '34 radiologically characterised MS patients' figure, and that reference 7 is specifically GSE180759 (the text says only 'a previously published postmortem tissue-based dataset 7'). IMPORTANT OMISSION BY THE CLAIM: this source's section heading is 'Synergistic proinflammatory Type-I and Type-II interferon signaling in chronic active MS', it explicitly labels the CD14M_4 genes 'type-I IFN stimulated genes', and it describes serum IFIT3 as 'induced by type-I IFN signaling' — so it argues for BOTH interferon types at the chronic active edge, cutting directly against the type-II-only framing of claims 1 and 3.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Raza et al. (Research Square rs.3.rs-7633686; PMC12486096) defined a 14-gene IFN-signature score (IFNG, JAK2, IFI6, IFITM2, IFITM3, IRF1, IRF7, IRF9, ISG15, MX1, MX2, OAS1, STAT1, IFNGR2) and, applying it to a previously published post-mortem snRNA-seq dataset, reported 'clear enrichment of IFN-signature at the chronic active lesion edge versus other regions'. In blood, CD14M_4 upregulated type-I ISGs (IFITM1/2/3, IFI6, IRF7, ISG15, IFI44L) in PRL-positive cases, and serum IFIT3 (p=0.009) and EIF2AK2/PKR (p=0.001) were higher in PRL-high vs no-PRL. The paper's own framing is 'Synergistic proinflammatory Type-I and Type-II interferon signaling in chronic active MS' — i.e. it supports type I AND type II, not type II alone. IFIH1 is not mentioned. Preprint, not peer reviewed; the brain result is a re-scoring of an existing dataset.

verdicts.claim: 8. A senescent, interferon-responsive astrocyte-derived radial-glia-like state (DARG) is enriched at the chronic active lesion edge in progressive MS, and IFIH1 sits inside its interferon gene programme in the matched in vitro model.
verdicts.reason: Full text PMC12834227 checked; the brain findings are verbatim-confirmed. 'A proportion (16%-28%) of total RG-like cells—which we termed disease-associated RG-like cells (DARGs)—in chronic lesions showed non-zero expression of the SenMayo gene set, whereas <5% of RG-like cells with the same features were identified in control tissues'; '~2.3-fold increase in the proportion of senescent DARGs (vs. senescent non-RG-like cells)'; '~2-fold increase in the fraction of senescent DARGs in the edge of chronic active lesions'; 'DARGs in chronic active lesions also showed enriched IFN-associated mRNAs'; cluster 5 showed 'significant enrichment of genes associated with cellular senescence, IFN-alpha/-beta signaling, and retinoic acid-inducible gene I (RIG-I) signaling for RNA sensing'; ABT-263 'significantly reduced the expression of transcripts involved in senescence, inflammation, IFN-alpha/-beta, and RIG-I signaling' (the authors call this a senomorphic, not senolytic, effect); 'This analysis identifies the emergence of DARGs from mature astrocytes'. THE DEFECT IS THE IFIH1 PLACEMENT. The paper's sentence is: 'gene sets associated with IFN-alpha/-beta signaling (IFIT2 and OASL), response to stress (NLRP2 and CLU), response to cytokine (IFIH1 and STAT6)...'. IFIH1 is an example gene of the generic 'response to cytokine' GO set, paired with STAT6 (an IL-4/IL-13 factor) — it is NOT in the IFN-alpha/-beta set, which is exemplified by IFIT2 and OASL. So 'IFIH1 sits inside its interferon gene programme' misplaces it. IFIH1 is named exactly once in the paper, as a GSEA leading-edge example in bulk RNA-seq of PMS vs control iNSCs, with no fold change and no p-value; iNSCs are reprogrammed patient skin fibroblasts in culture, not DARGs and not brain. NOT VERIFIED: 'RG-like cells made up 50% of the relevant population at chronic active lesions', and that pseudotime specifically (rather than module correlation) establishes the mature-astrocyte origin.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Park, Nicaise, Tsitsipatis et al. (Neuron 2025;113:4158-4177.e10, PMID 41075785) identified disease-associated radial-glia-like cells (DARGs) in post-mortem progressive-MS brain: 16-28% of RG-like cells in chronic lesions expressed the SenMayo senescence set vs <5% in controls, with ~2.3-fold more senescent DARGs than senescent non-RG-like cells and ~2-fold more at the chronic active lesion edge than elsewhere, and DARGs at that edge enriched for IFN-associated mRNAs. In the patient-derived iNSC model, the PMS-enriched cluster 5 was enriched for senescence, IFN-alpha/-beta and RIG-I-like RNA-sensing signalling, which ABT-263 reduced (a senomorphic effect). IFIH1 is named once, as an example gene of the generic 'response to cytokine' GO set (paired with STAT6) in bulk RNA-seq of cultured PMS iNSCs — not within the IFN-alpha/-beta set, and with no fold change or p-value reported.

verdicts.claim: 9. In mouse EAE, Ifih1/MDA5 is part of the interferon module in MHC-II-expressing oligodendrocyte-lineage cells and is directly and strongly IFN-gamma-inducible in cultured OPCs — the clearest direct evidence anywhere that oligodendroglia can express MDA5 during demyelinating disease.
verdicts.reason: Full text PMC6544508 checked; both quotes are verbatim exact. 'We found several interferon responsive genes in MHC-II expressing OL/OPC populations, such as Ifih1, Iigp1, Trim34, Irf7, Irgm1, Irgm2, Igtp and Zbp1 (Supplementary Fig. 7a).' And: 'we observed a dramatic induction of interferon responsive genes (Ifit2, Ifih1) MHC-II genes (Cd74) and MHC-II and I transactivators (Ciita, Nlrc5) (Fig. 4e). Thus, our results indicate that MHC-II genes induction in EAE OL lineage cells is possibly mediated by IFNgamma.' The Ifih1 qPCR primers are present in Methods (F: ATGTCTTGGACACTTGCTTCG, R: CTGACTCATTCCCGCTGTTT). The splicing statement is verbatim: '...the myelin genes Mbp, Mobp, Pdgfa and the Ifih1 gene, in which MS-associated polymorphisms have been found'. THREE CALIBRATION NOTES. No numeric fold change for Ifih1 exists in the text — 'dramatic' is the authors' adjective and the value lives only in Fig. 4e. MDA5 PROTEIN was never measured. The in-vivo component is co-membership in a scRNA-seq gene list, not a quantified induction, and the quantified induction is in cultured OPCs stimulated with IFN-gamma, which is not 'during demyelinating disease'. 'Clearest direct evidence anywhere' is an unverifiable superlative.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Falcao et al. (Nat Med 2018;24:1837-1844, PMID 30420755) report Ifih1 among interferon-responsive genes in MHC-II-expressing mouse OL/OPC populations in EAE (Supplementary Fig. 7a), and qPCR showing 'a dramatic induction' of Ifit2 and Ifih1 alongside Cd74, Ciita and Nlrc5 in primary mouse OPCs treated with IFN-gamma (Fig. 4e); Ifih1 also showed EAE-associated alternative splicing. No fold-change value is given in the text and MDA5 protein was not measured. This is the clearest published evidence that oligodendroglia can be induced to transcribe Ifih1 — but it is mouse, the quantified induction is in cell culture, and it is mRNA only.

verdicts.claim: 10. In human MS brain the oligodendrocyte 'immune' response is an MHC-I/antigen-presentation programme concentrated at periplaque white matter and lesion rim, not a canonical antiviral ISG programme.
verdicts.reason: Full texts PMC6731122 and PMC6544546 checked; the positive half is verbatim-confirmed. Schirmer: 'MHC class I upregulation (B2M, HLA-C)'; 'Note differential upregulation of B2M and HLA-C in PLP1-expressing OLs at PPWM (right; yellow arrowheads...)'; 'FTL and FTH1 upregulation in PLP1-expressing OLs at iron-laden lesions rims'; 48,919 nuclei confirmed twice in text. Jakel: 'APOE and CD74 for immune oligodendroglia (imOLG)'; nImOLG=207; 'Oligo2, Oligo3, Oligo5 and imOLGs were enriched' in MS. My independent GSE180759 recomputation reproduces the B2M numbers exactly (oligodendrocytes 21.95% 936/4264 -> 45.47% at the chronic active edge, p=7.7e-172), and that result is robust because MS oligodendrocyte sequencing depth is LOWER than control (median 2,869 vs 3,500 UMI), so it runs against the depth gradient. THE DEFECT: 'not a canonical antiviral ISG programme' is an argument from silence. Neither Schirmer nor Jakel tested or excluded ISGs — IFIH1 simply returns 0 hits in both full texts, which is absence of mention, not evidence of absence. Worse, the claimant's own GSE180759 re-analysis contradicts it: oligodendrocyte ISG15 rises from 0.05% (2/4,264) in control WM to 0.40% (50/12,658) at the chronic active edge, p=7.8e-5.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Schirmer et al. (Nature 2019;573:75-82, PMID 31316211; 48,919 nuclei) show MS oligodendrocytes upregulate MHC class I (B2M, HLA-C), validated by RNAscope at periplaque white matter, with FTL/FTH1 at iron-laden lesion rims; Jakel et al. (Nature 2019;566:543-547) independently identified MS-enriched 'immune oligodendroglia' (ImOLG; APOE, CD74; n=207). GSE180759 reproduces the MHC-I effect (oligodendrocyte B2M 21.95% -> 45.47%, p=7.7e-172, robust to depth). Neither paper tested antiviral ISGs, so their silence is not evidence against an ISG programme — and in GSE180759 oligodendrocyte ISG15 does rise significantly (0.05% -> 0.40%, p=7.8e-5) at the chronic active edge.

verdicts.claim: 11. Spatial transcriptomics of subcortical MS lesions maps IFN-gamma signalling to the demyelinated core and inflamed rim and places an IFITM interferon module in chronic inactive lesion astrocytes; IFIH1/MDA5/DDX58/dsRNA are not mentioned.
verdicts.reason: Full text PMC11614744 checked; all three quotes are verbatim. 'Conversely, interferon gamma signaling (R-HSA-877300) was predicted to be active in the demyelinated core and at inflamed lesion rims.' 'MS-CI AS genes were associated with functions related to scar formation (ITGA2, COL6A1), debris clearance (AKT3, CTSD) and interferon signaling (ARL5B, IFITM3, IFITM2).' And the niche genes: 'inflammation (SPP1, C1QA, HSPH1), interferon signaling and tissue remodeling (TGFBR2, IFNGR2)'. Keyword scan confirms 0 hits for IFIH1, MDA5, DDX58, dsRNA, retroelement and HERV in the full text. TWO CALIBRATION NOTES. 'Predicted to be active' is a Reactome pathway inference on spatial transcriptomic data, not a measurement of IFN-gamma protein or activity; the claim's 'maps interferon-GAMMA signalling to' is a shade stronger than the source. And the keyword absence was checked against the PMC full text only — the study's supplementary differential-expression tables were not searched, so 'not mentioned anywhere in that study' is a stronger negative than what was actually tested.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Lerma-Martin et al. (Nat Neurosci 2024;27:2354-2365, PMID 39501036) report that interferon gamma signalling (Reactome R-HSA-877300) was PREDICTED by pathway inference to be active in the demyelinated core and at inflamed lesion rims; chronic inactive astrocyte genes included an interferon module (ARL5B, IFITM3, IFITM2) alongside scar formation and debris clearance; lesion-rim and vascular-inflammation niches shared SPP1, C1QA, HSPH1, TGFBR2, IFNGR2. A keyword search of the PMC full text returns zero hits for IFIH1, MDA5, DDX58, dsRNA, retroelement or HERV, though the supplementary DE tables were not searched.

verdicts.claim: 12. Across a 632,000-nucleus, 156-sample MS atlas, IFN-alpha and IFN-gamma response gene sets move in opposite directions in OPCs versus oligodendrocytes.
verdicts.reason: The bibliographic frame and headline are confirmed from the Europe PMC abstract: Neuron 2025;113:396-410.e9; 'we analyzed 632,000 single-nucleus RNA sequencing profiles from 156 brain tissue samples of MS and control donors'; 'Most gene expression variability was instead explained by patient effects'. But the key quoted sentence is NOT in the abstract, and the claimant never retrieved the body text — every local Macnair file is empty or an error (macnair_pre.pdf = 17 bytes, macnair_pmc.txt = 0 bytes, macnair.xml = a Europe PMC 404 JSON), consistent with their stated 403. I recovered the sentence second-hand via web search of the Cell page: 'In white matter lesions (WMLs), expression of genes involved in interferon alpha and gamma responses varied across multiple sclerosis lesions and often showed opposite patterns in OPCs compared to oligodendrocytes.' The claim DROPS the scope qualifier 'In white matter lesions (WMLs)' and generalises it to the whole atlas, which is what makes the headline overstated. Cell Press full text returned 403 to me as well, so this remains second-hand. NOT VERIFIED: '55 MS patients, 28 controls'; 'inflammation-related pathways enhanced in astrocytes, microglia and oligodendrocytes in white-matter lesions'; 'Oligo_G increased in grey-matter lesions'; and whether IFIH1 is named anywhere.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Macnair et al. (Neuron 2025;113:396-410.e9, PMID 39708806; 632,000 nuclei, 156 samples) report that IN WHITE MATTER LESIONS specifically, expression of interferon alpha and gamma response genes varied across MS lesions and often showed opposite patterns in OPCs compared to oligodendrocytes; the paper's headline conclusion is that most gene-expression variability is explained by patient effects rather than lesion type. The interferon sentence could only be obtained second-hand (Cell Press returns HTTP 403), the donor counts were not verified, and whether IFIH1 is named is unknown.

verdicts.claim: 13. The strongest dsRNA-based aetiological link in MS is loss of A-to-I editing of Alu dsRNA, but the causal experiment shows unedited Alu signals through RIG-I and TLR3 and specifically fails to activate MDA5; only longer LINE-derived elements activated MDA5.
verdicts.reason: Full text PMC7872017 checked; the load-bearing negative is verbatim: 'We did not find an increase in ISRE-responses in HEK-TLR3 + MDA5 cells compared to HEK-TLR3 cells suggesting that AluJb does not activate MDA5.' Supporting: 'AluJb dsRNA... was a potent inducer of ISRE-responses in HEK293-TLR3 + RIG-I cells compared to HEK-TLR3 and HEK-TLR3 + MDA5 cells.' The LINE result is verbatim: 'We found that this L1P1 dsRNA element activated ISRE-responses in HEK-TLR3, HEK-TLR3 + RIG-I, and HEK-TLR3 + MDA5 reporter cells.' Editing numbers exact: '2,724 nucleotide sites that were A-to-I edited in genomes of the HC cohort but were not A-to-I edited in genomes from the MS-E cohort... only 665... (P<0.0001, chi2)'; '280 editing sites present in 100% of HC samples and absent from MS samples and only 64 editing sites present in 100% of MS samples'. n=8 treatment-naive MS, 8 treated MS, 8 HC, whole blood leukocytes, all confirmed. '>20-fold' for RELB, IL6, DDX58, IFIT5 confirmed. THREE CALIBRATIONS. 'Longer LINE elements' (plural) rests on ONE element, L1P1. Generalising from a single AluJb element in an overexpression reporter system to 'unedited Alu dsRNA' as a class overreaches the authors' own hedge ('suggesting'). The >20-fold inductions were in THP-1 and HMC3 cell lines, which the claim omits. 'The strongest published dsRNA-based aetiological link in MS' is an unverifiable superlative. The blood-not-brain caveat is correctly stated.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Tossberg et al. (J Immunol 2020;205:2606-2617, PMID 33046502) found widespread loss of A-to-I editing in MS whole-blood leukocytes (2,724 sites edited in HC but not MS vs 665 the reverse, P<0.0001; restricted to sites in 100% of samples, 280 vs 64, P<0.0001; n=8/8/8). In HEK293 reporter assays a single element, AluJb, was a potent ISRE inducer via RIG-I but the authors 'did not find an increase in ISRE-responses in HEK-TLR3 + MDA5 cells... suggesting that AluJb does not activate MDA5'; a single LINE element, L1P1, activated ISRE via TLR3, RIG-I and MDA5. Unedited Alu or LINE dsRNA induced RELB, IL6, DDX58 and IFIT5 >20-fold in THP-1 and HMC3 cells. Blood, not brain; the Alu-does-not-activate-MDA5 result comes from one element in an overexpression reporter.

verdicts.claim: 14. HERV-W transcription is elevated in MS white matter at the locus level, but the best-characterised HERV-W pathogenic entity is the ENV protein acting on myeloid cells, not a dsRNA ligand, so HERV-W is not established as an MDA5 agonist in MS.
verdicts.reason: Full text PMC11512866 checked; every number is exact. Same GSE138614 cohort confirmed ('white matter brain samples sourced from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) database (GSE138614)'). '52 were from the patients with MS, and 20 samples were extracted from controls without neurological disease' — exact. 215 HERV-W loci analysed, 65 with detectable expression, 14 differentially expressed, 12 upregulated in MS — all exact. 'The highest fold change in the difference of means was observed in case of HERV-W locus 2q24.3, where the expression was four-fold higher in the MS samples (16.74 vs 67.45 reads)' — exact. Eight upregulated loci negatively correlated with CIBERSORTx-estimated oligodendrocyte proportions, and GSEA associating 2p16.2, 2q13 and Xq13.3 with suppressed oligodendrocyte development/myelination — both exact. Kremer PNAS 2019 confirmed: pHERV-W ENV is present in myeloid cells associated with axons in MS lesions, induces a degenerative microglial phenotype that structurally damages myelinated axons, and signals through TLR4; no mention of dsRNA, RIG-I, MDA5 or IFIH1. ONE ERROR: the paper is by Nevalainen T, Autio-Kimura A and Hurme M (Tampere), not the 'Kalliokoski/Hyoty group'. Minor: the claim says 'TLR4/CD14'; only TLR4 is established in the source I could check.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Nevalainen, Autio-Kimura and Hurme (J Neurovirol 2024, PMID 38717678) re-quantified HERV-W at locus level in the GSE138614 cohort (52 MS vs 20 control samples): of 215 loci, 65 were expressed, 14 differentially expressed, 12 upregulated in MS, largest at 2q24.3 (16.74 -> 67.45 mean normalised reads, four-fold); 8 upregulated loci correlated negatively with CIBERSORTx oligodendrocyte proportion and 2p16.2, 2q13 and Xq13.3 associated by GSEA with suppressed oligodendrocyte development/myelination. Separately, Kremer et al. (PNAS 2019;116:15216-15225) showed pHERV-W ENV protein in myeloid cells associated with axons in MS lesions, driving microglial damage to myelinated axons via TLR4. No study links HERV-W to RLR/dsRNA sensing in MS, so HERV-W is not established as an MDA5 agonist.

verdicts.claim: 15. Human astrocytes reliably upregulate IFIH1 and DDX58 as a transcriptional hub in response to inflammatory stimuli in vitro, so the absence of an astrocyte IFIH1 increase in MS lesion snRNA-seq reflects the in situ stimulus, not an inability of astrocytes to express MDA5.
verdicts.reason: The paper is real and the quotes are verbatim (PMC13461556, PMID 42591297, Front Cell Neurosci, fncel-20-1870142): '130 DEGs... including 125 upregulated and 5 downregulated'; 'Based on these criteria, five primary nodes were identified: CXCL10, DDX58, IFIH1, IL-1B, and TLR3'; and 'A remarkable finding of this meta-analysis is the consistent upregulation of the cytosolic sensors DDX58 (RIG-I) and IFIH1 (MDA5) across diverse non-viral inflammatory contexts, including stress induced by palmitic acid and systemic pro-inflammatory cytokine exposure.' FOUR DEFECTS. (a) 'Hub' is a PPI-network topology property — degree and betweenness centrality among 33 immune/inflammation nodes — not a measure of how reliably or how strongly a gene is upregulated. 'Reliably upregulate... as a transcriptional hub' imports a meaning the network analysis does not carry, and the claim itself concedes no fold change is given. (b) The claim's own stimulus list includes poly(I:C) 200 ug/ml and SARS-CoV-2; poly(I:C) is the canonical direct MDA5 ligand and SARS-CoV-2 is a virus, so those datasets cannot support a statement about 'non-viral inflammatory contexts' — the paper's 'non-viral' wording covers palmitic acid and cytokines. (c) The 'so...' clause is pure inference: no source tests whether the in-situ stimulus explains the absent astrocyte IFIH1 rise in MS. This converts an absence of evidence into a mechanistic explanation. (d) The '14+ datasets' count and the accession list were not verified.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Luque-Bolivar et al. (Front Cell Neurosci 2026;20:1870142, PMID 42591297) performed a robust-rank-aggregation meta-analysis of human astrocyte RNA-seq datasets, yielding 130 DEGs (125 up), and identified CXCL10, DDX58, IFIH1, IL-1B and TLR3 as the top five hub nodes by degree and betweenness centrality in a PPI network built from 33 immune/inflammation-related DEGs. The authors state that DDX58 and IFIH1 are consistently upregulated across inflammatory contexts including palmitic acid and cytokine exposure, but report no fold change or p-value for IFIH1, and some contributing datasets used poly(I:C) or SARS-CoV-2, which are direct viral/dsRNA stimuli. Cultured astrocytes only. Whether this explains the absence of an astrocyte IFIH1 increase in MS lesion snRNA-seq is untested speculation.

verdicts.claim: 16. A canonical interferon-responsive microglia (IRM) state is well defined in mouse and human neurodegeneration, but its formal identification in human MS brain is not established in the review literature; the MS citation for IRM is a mouse EAE dataset.
verdicts.reason: Full text PMC12631166 checked; the quotes are verbatim. 'The inset box highlights the core IRM gene signature, consisting of IRM marker genes identified in >=5 gene sets, totalling 53 genes.' And: 'IRM have also been identified in other neurodegenerative conditions, including ALS/FTD in C9orf72 mutant mice [171], an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis (MS) [143], and glioma [175].' Reference 143 is confirmed as Hammond TR et al. 2019, a mouse lifespan/injury scRNA-seq study. AD models and human AD patients are cited as stated. IFIH1 returns 0 hits in the full text. TWO DEFECTS. (a) The 53-gene core signature lives in a FIGURE inset (Fig. 4 UpSet plot), so a full-text keyword search cannot establish that IFIH1 is absent from it — it establishes only that IFIH1 is not discussed in the prose. The recurring-member list quoted in the claim (Ifit2, Ifit3, Ifitm3, Irf7, Oasl2, Isg15, Ifi30, Oas1, Stat1) is likewise figure-derived and could not be verified from text. (b) More importantly, a review not citing a human MS IRM cluster is evidence about the review's citation practice, not about the field — and the claimant's own claim 6 (Feng/Spieth, Immunity 2025) describes exactly such a state, 'inflamed microglia displaying an interferon response', in human chronic active MS lesion rims. The negative is self-contradicted within this claim set.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Lopez-Atalaya and Bhojwani-Cabrera (FEBS J 2025, PMID 40299722) derive a core IRM signature of 53 genes present in >=5 of 9 independent gene sets and cite IRM in AD models and human AD patients, C9orf72 ALS/FTD mice, glioma, and 'an experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis model of multiple sclerosis', for which the cited reference is the mouse study Hammond et al. 2019. This review cites no human MS brain IRM cluster, and IFIH1 is not discussed in its text — but the 53-gene list is figure-only so IFIH1's absence from it is unverified, and a human MS lesion-rim interferon-responsive microglial state has since been described by Feng, Spieth et al. (Immunity 2025).

verdicts.claim: 17. In the CZ CELLxGENE human brain corpus IFIH1 is a vascular/myeloid gene with very low expression in macroglia and essentially none in neurons.
verdicts.reason: I re-parsed the saved raw WMG v2 API payload directly (snapshot_id 1762972271, exactly as the claim states; tissue UBERON:0000955; disease PATO:0000461; rolled-up cell types). Every figure reproduces exactly. IFIH1: endothelial cell 9.86% (8,170), macrophage 3.62% (14,215), microglial cell 3.40% (8,936/263,183), pericyte 2.68% (899/33,541), astrocyte 0.70% (7,293/1,042,967), oligodendrocyte 0.54% (11,706/2,175,004), OPC 0.50% (2,287/458,868), neuron 0.04% (3,741). DDX58: endothelial 6.70%, macrophage 4.70%, pericyte 4.69%, microglia 3.42%, OPC 2.51%, astrocyte 2.19%, oligodendrocyte 1.26%, neuron 0.55% — all exact, and DDX58 is indeed higher than IFIH1 in every macroglial type. The MS-labelled brain slice is ~7,900-8,100 cells, confirming it is too small for MS-vs-control inference. ONE CALIBRATION THE CLAIM SHOULD CARRY: the absolute rates are pipeline-dependent. The claimant's own CZ CELLxGENE Census computation over the same corpus (out_census_baseline_all.csv, nucleus suspensions) gives astrocyte 3.40%, oligodendrocyte 2.45%, OPC 3.67%, endothelial 23.11%, CNS macrophage 7.85% and neuron 1.55% — 4-40x higher, and it reorders OPC above astrocyte. The vascular/myeloid > macroglia > neuron ORDERING is stable across both pipelines; the absolute percentages are not. So 'essentially none in neurons' rests on one pipeline's 0.04% and becomes 1.55% under the other, and snRNA-seq detection rate is not evidence of absent expression.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the CZ CELLxGENE WMG v2 human brain corpus (snapshot 1762972271, disease = normal, rolled up), IFIH1 detection ranks endothelial cell 9.86% > macrophage 3.62% > microglial cell 3.40% > pericyte 2.68% >> astrocyte 0.70% > oligodendrocyte 0.54% > OPC 0.50% >> neuron 0.04%, with DDX58 higher than IFIH1 in every macroglial type (oligodendrocyte 1.26%, astrocyte 2.19%, OPC 2.51%, neuron 0.55%). The vascular/myeloid-over-macroglia-over-neuron ordering is reproducible, but absolute detection rates are pipeline-dependent — the CZ Census on the same corpus gives 4-40x higher values (neuron 1.55%, oligodendrocyte 2.45%, endothelial 23.11%) — so 'essentially none in neurons' should be read as low detection in one pipeline, not absent expression. The MS-labelled brain slice (~8,000 cells) is too small for MS-vs-control inference.

verdicts.claim: 18. No study has demonstrated dsRNA accumulation or MDA5 protein in MS brain tissue; the cell-type-resolved 'transposable-element activation drives an interferon response' analysis has been done for Parkinson's disease but not MS.
verdicts.reason: THE NEGATIVES HOLD. My own Europe PMC searches support them: the tightest query, TITLE:"multiple sclerosis" AND ABSTRACT:(IFIH1 OR MDA5), returns 11 records, all genetic-association or blood-transcriptome studies (Enevold 2009 PRR polymorphisms; IFIH1-GCA-KCNH7 locus; type I IFN activity in MS subsets; inflammasome rare variants; IFNB1b time-course; RLR polymorphisms in German MS). No MS brain-tissue MDA5 immunohistochemistry and no J2-antibody dsRNA staining of MS lesions surfaced. Local keyword scans confirm 0 hits for IFIH1/MDA5/DDX58/dsRNA in PMC11614744, PMC6416318, PMC5566335 and PMC12577231. THE DEFECT IS A DIRECTIONAL MISREPRESENTATION OF THE PD PAPER. PMC13537272 is Garza et al., Sci Adv 2026, 'Activation of transposable elements is LINKED TO a region- and cell type-specific interferon response in Parkinson's disease' (PMID 42685224). Its abstract confirms 'Increased TE expression was found in microglia and neurons in the substantia nigra and putamen of PD brains, but not amygdala or prefrontal cortex, compared to controls. This TE activation correlated with an innate immune response in the same brain regions.' But its mechanistic conclusion is the OPPOSITE of what the claim asserts: 'Our mechanistic in vitro modeling, which uses hPSC-derived microglia and DA neurons, confirmed that inducing an interferon response causes transcriptional activation of TEs. Therefore, TE transcriptional activation appears to be downstream of the interferon response.' The in-vitro inducer was IFN-gamma (5 ng/ml, 48 h) — type II. So the paper is not an instance of 'transposable-element activation drives an interferon response'; it argues TEs are downstream of IFN. Also, the '>1,000 TEs' figure was not confirmed at that exact threshold.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Targeted Europe PMC searches return no primary report of J2-antibody dsRNA immunostaining in MS lesions and no MDA5 immunohistochemistry in MS brain; the 11 records with 'multiple sclerosis' in the title and IFIH1/MDA5 in the abstract are all genetic-association or blood studies. Full-text keyword searches of the major MS lesion atlases return no hits for IFIH1/MDA5/dsRNA/retroelement/HERV. In Parkinson's disease, Garza et al. (Sci Adv 2026, PMC13537272, PMID 42685224) did the cell-type- and region-resolved TE analysis: LINE-1s and ERVs were expressed cell-type- and region-specifically, with increased TE expression in microglia and neurons of substantia nigra and putamen but not amygdala or prefrontal cortex, correlating with an innate immune response — but their hPSC-derived microglia and DA neuron experiments established the reverse causal direction, that inducing an interferon response (with IFN-gamma) activates TEs, so 'TE transcriptional activation appears to be downstream of the interferon response'. No equivalent MS study exists.

research.dimension: MDA5/IFIH1 and dsRNA sensing in demyelination, oligodendrocytes, and animal models of MS (EAE, cuprizone, Theiler's virus, ADAR1/AGS models)

findings.claim: In purified mouse cortical cell types at homeostasis, Ifih1 mRNA is NOT detectable in oligodendrocytes (both myelinating and newly-formed), and is highest in endothelial cells, then microglia. Rank: endothelial >> microglia > neurons ≈ OPC ≈ astrocyte >> oligodendrocyte (at floor).
findings.evidence: Brain RNA-Seq purified-cell-type FPKM table (Zhang et al. 2014 mouse cortex data, downloaded from brainrnaseq.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/fe-wp-dataset-120.csv; 2 replicates per cell type; 0.1 = imputed detection floor). Ifih1 FPKM: endothelial 2.100 / 2.012; microglia-macrophage 0.602 / 0.481; neurons 0.146 / 0.678; OPC 0.326 / 0.108; astrocytes 0.293 / 0.119; newly-formed oligodendrocyte 0.100 / 0.100 (floor); myelinating oligodendrocyte 0.100 / 0.100 (floor). For comparison in the same table, Ddx58/RIG-I: endothelial 8.486 / 8.773; OPC 2.391 / 1.826; microglia 1.624 / 1.576; astrocytes 1.251 / 1.366; myelinating OL 0.100 / 0.156. Dhx58/LGP2: microglia 2.143 / 1.155; endothelial 0.722 / 0.498; astrocytes 0.417 / 0.267; myelinating OL 0.162 / 0.153. Tlr3: astrocytes 16.492 / 8.626; endothelial 9.034 / 8.787; OPC 2.827 / 0.893; microglia 2.622 / 2.588; myelinating OL 0.100 / 0.373. Sanity-check markers in the same file behave correctly (Cx3cr1 microglia 473.2 / 506.2; Mbp myelinating OL 115330 / 75465).

findings.claim: MAVS (the shared RLR adaptor) IS robustly expressed in mouse oligodendrocytes even though Ifih1 is not — so the oligodendrocyte signalling machinery downstream of MDA5 is present while the sensor itself is essentially absent at baseline.
