findings.evidence: Same Brain RNA-Seq mouse cortex FPKM table. Mavs FPKM: microglia-macrophage 12.294 / 16.197; astrocytes 9.232 / 7.581; myelinating oligodendrocyte 6.891 / 5.809; newly-formed oligodendrocyte 5.919 / 6.018; OPC 6.627 / 6.679; endothelial 3.428 / 3.662; neurons 0.614 / 1.021. Oligodendrocyte Mavs (~5.8-6.9 FPKM) is ~60x above the Ifih1 floor value in the same cells (0.1).

findings.claim: In human brain single-nuclei RNA-seq, IFIH1 is classified as 'cell type enhanced' with the enhancement in ENDOTHELIAL cells, not in any glial or neuronal population; at protein level across tissues the highest cell-type intensity is in macrophages.
findings.evidence: Human Protein Atlas machine-readable record for IFIH1 (ENSG00000115267), retrieved via https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000115267.json. Fields: 'RNA single nuclei brain specificity' = Cell type enhanced; 'RNA single nuclei brain distribution' = Detected in many; 'RNA single nuclei brain specific nCPM / endothelial cell' = 118.9. 'RNA brain regional specificity' = Low region specificity, 'Detected in all'. 'RNA mouse brain regional specificity' = Low region specificity, 'Detected in all'. 'Protein cell type specific Intensity / Macrophages' = 2,720,714.2. 'RNA blood cell specificity' = Low immune cell specificity. Per-cell-type nCPM values for oligodendrocytes/astrocytes/microglia were not exposed by the API or the rendered HPA page and could not be retrieved.

findings.claim: Ifih1 is induced as part of an interferon-responsive / MHC-II-expressing oligodendrocyte-lineage state in mouse EAE — this is the single strongest published link between MDA5 and oligodendrocytes in MS models, and it is INDUCED expression (ISG behaviour), driven by IFN-gamma, not a baseline property of oligodendrocytes.
findings.evidence: Falcão AM, van Bruggen D, Marques S, et al., Nat Med 2018;24(12):1837-1844. scRNA-seq of oligodendrocyte-lineage cells from MOG-EAE mouse spinal cord: 745 control and 707 EAE OL-lineage cells, n=4 biologically independent mice per condition. The authors report 'several interferon responsive genes in MHC-II expressing OL/OPC populations, such as Ifih1, Iigp1, Trim34, Irf7, Irgm1, Irgm2, Igtp and Zbp1'. Validation (Fig. 4e) was qRT-PCR on primary OPCs/OLs treated with interferon-gamma (and dexamethasone), 3 independent replicates per condition, showing 'a dramatic induction of interferon responsive genes (Ifit2, Ifih1)'. Numeric fold-change and p-value for Ifih1 are NOT stated in the text or figure legend. Ifih1 also appears among the 360 genes alternatively spliced in EAE OL-lineage cells (Supplementary Table 2). Accompanying immune genes in EAE OLs: MHC-I (H2-K1, H2-D1, H2-T23, B2m, Psmb9, Tap1, Tap2), MHC-II (H2-Aa, H2-Ab1, H2-Eb1, Cd74, Ctss), Serpina3n, Serping1.

findings.claim: There is only ONE primary study testing whether oligodendrocytes sense dsRNA via MDA5, and in it MDA5 protein was undetectable in the oligodendrocytic cells; the functional evidence rests on a ~40%-efficient siRNA knockdown, while RIG-I was the dominant, protein-detectable sensor in the same cells.
findings.evidence: Li J, Liu Y, Zhang X. J Virol 2010;84(13):6472-6482 (mouse oligodendrocytic N20.1 cells, mouse hepatitis virus/MHV infection). Verbatim from the paper: 'Unfortunately, no MDA5 protein was detected in virus-infected cells at various times p.i. or in mock-infected cells (data not shown).' MDA5 mRNA was 'extremely low in N20.1 cells' — nested RT-PCR using a total of 60 cycles was required to amplify it from MHV-infected cells. MDA5 siRNA achieved ~40% knockdown and 'drastically blocked the induction of IFN-beta by MHV infection' (no numeric fold given). By contrast RIG-I protein WAS detectable and was upregulated from 6 h p.i.; RIG-I knockdown 'completely blocked the activation of IRF-3' and drastically (but incompletely) blocked IFN-alpha/beta. IFN induction required virus replication (UV-inactivated virus did not induce).

findings.claim: MDA5 is functionally required for type I IFN induction in primary oligodendrocytes (as well as astrocytes and microglia) upon Theiler's virus infection — but the studies demonstrate MDA5 FUNCTION by knockout, never MDA5 EXPRESSION in those cells.
findings.evidence: Jin YH, Kim SJ, So EY, Meng L, Colonna M, Kim BS. J Virol 2012;86(3):1531-1543. Primary astrocytes, oligodendrocytes and microglia were isolated from neonatal brains of MDA5-KO and WT mice; 'IFN-alpha4 expression in response to TMEV infection was completely abrogated in MDA5 KO cells.' The paper does not report direct measurement of MDA5 mRNA or protein levels in any glial cell type, nor induction data — only the loss-of-function readout.

findings.claim: MDA5 is PROTECTIVE against virus-induced demyelinating disease: MDA5-deficient mice infected with Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus (a viral MS model) develop far higher CNS viral loads and a 4-fold higher incidence of demyelinating disease.
findings.evidence: Jin YH et al., J Virol 2012;86(3):1531-1543, MDA5-deficient 129SvJ mice vs WT 129SvJ. Viral load: 10- to 700-fold higher TMEV plaque counts at 8 and 28 days post-infection; VP1 RNA consistently higher in brain and spinal cord at all time points. Clinical demyelinating disease incidence: 80% in MDA5-/- vs 20% in WT. Severity significantly higher at 14 and 21 dpi (P<0.01), peaking at day 14. Histology: 'moderate to severe demyelination in the white matter of the CNS' with multiple demyelination foci plus mononuclear cell infiltration. Cytokines: 'drastically reduced levels of IFN-alpha' with elevated chemokines CCL2, CCL5, CXCL1 (pg/ml values not reported in the accessible text). T-cell responses to viral determinants were elevated, consistent with increased infiltration.

findings.claim: Theiler's virus actively cleaves and inactivates MDA5 via its 3C protease — direct biochemical evidence that MDA5 is a relevant antiviral target in this demyelination model.
findings.evidence: Miyamoto M, Himeda T, Ishihara K, et al. J Immunol 2023;210(3):335-347. Ectopic expression of 3C protease from Saffold virus or TMEV (but NOT encephalomyocarditis virus) produced dose-dependent MDA5 cleavage fragments; enzymatically inactive 3C completely abrogated cleavage. Mass spectrometry identified two cleavage sites at the MDA5 C terminus, removing one RNA-binding domain. The same cleavage pattern occurred during authentic Theilovirus infection. Functional consequence: impaired ATP hydrolysis, impaired RNA binding, impaired filament assembly on RNA. A cleavage-resistant MDA5 mutant showed enhanced IFN response during Saffold virus infection.

findings.claim: In EAE, loss of the RLR adaptor MAVS/IPS-1 worsens disease AND significantly reduces the number of mature oligodendrocytes — the most direct evidence in the EAE literature linking RLR (RIG-I/MDA5) signalling to oligodendrocyte preservation.
findings.evidence: Dann A, Poeck H, Croxford AL, et al. Nat Neurosci 2012;15(1):98-106 ('Cytosolic RIG-I-like helicases act as negative regulators of sterile inflammation in the CNS'). MOG35-55/CFA active EAE in Ips-1+/+ (n=7) vs Ips-1-/- (=Mavs-/-, n=8): 'in Ips-1-/- mice, the peak of disease was significantly augmented (P<0.05)'. Histology of Ips-1-deficient spinal cords: markedly increased macrophage infiltration, elevated T-cell numbers and stronger demyelination; NO statistically significant difference in axonal damage (P>0.05). Critically: 'The number of mature oligodendrocytes was significantly lower (P<0.05) in Ips-1-/- mice than in Ips-1+/+ mice' (NOGO-A+ counts, Fig. 1). Cytokines at 19 dpi in spinal cord: all TH17-related factors increased in Ips-1-/-; TH1 factors IL-12p35 and T-bet elevated; TH2 factors unchanged except GATA3.

findings.claim: Pharmacological activation of MDA5 with cytoplasmically-delivered poly(I:C) AMELIORATES established EAE, and the effect is strictly IFNAR-dependent and mediated by peripheral myeloid cells, not by CNS glia.
findings.evidence: Dann A et al., Nat Neurosci 2012;15(1):98-106. 25 µg PEI-complexed poly(I:C) (MDA5 ligand) IV at 13, 15 and 17 dpi in Ifnar1+/+ mice (n=8) vs PBS (n=5), complexed 3pRNA/RIG-I (n=7), NON-complexed poly(I:C)/TLR3 (n=6) and polyA (n=5). 'Disease severity during the effector phase was markedly diminished in RIG-I- and MDA5-stimulated mice, whereas non-complexed poly(I:C) (TLR3 ligand) or synthetic RNA bearing no 5'-triphosphate (polyA) did not change the disease score.' Spinal cord cell counts (MAC-3, CD3, APP, NOGO-A) significantly reduced in MDA5- and RIG-I-stimulated mice (P<0.05; markers shown at P<0.01 in Fig. 2 counts); demyelination reduced. In Ifnar1-/- mice there was 'no improvement of the clinical course of EAE after treatment with RIG-I or MDA5 ligands' — complete loss of effect. MDA5 activation decreased spinal cord transcripts of IL-1beta, IL-6, IL-23p19, TGF-beta, RORgammaT and IL-17A, and significantly reduced both TH1 and TH17 cell numbers peripherally and centrally (P<0.05). Cellular source of IFN-beta: conventional DCs, plasmacytoid DCs and bone-marrow-derived macrophages; BMDMs responded robustly to RIG-I activation and 'to a lower extent' to MDA5 activation. RIG-I/MDA5 ligands did not alter normal T-cell differentiation (T-bet, STAT6, TGF-beta induction unaffected).

findings.claim: Forcing RIG-I/MAVS-pathway signalling inside the CNS suppresses EAE, with astrocytes (not oligodendrocytes) among the IFN-beta-producing cells.
findings.evidence: Hansen AK, Dubik M, Marczynska J, et al. Int J Mol Sci 2022;23(19):11292. AAV8 encoding a constitutively active fusion protein 'CM' (RIG-I 2CARD domains + MAVS amino acids 1-200) injected intrathecally into CSF at EAE onset. Disease progression suppressed in WT mice (controls' mean clinical score rose from day 1 to day 5; AAV-CM treated showed no such increase); the protective effect was entirely absent in IFNAR1-deficient mice. Three CNS populations expressed IFN-beta in response to CM: extraparenchymal CD45+ (leptomeningeal) cells, choroid plexus cells and GFAP+ astrocytes. IFN-beta significantly increased at days 1, 3 and 7 post-injection, still detectable at day 21. RT-qPCR at day 1: significant upregulation of IFN-alpha, IFN-beta, IL-10, IL-1beta, IFN-gamma. Luxol fast blue myelin loss notably reduced in AAV-CM animals.

findings.claim: Astrocytes use MDA5 — not RIG-I — as their intracellular dsRNA sensor, making astrocytes the CNS cell type with the best-supported functional MDA5 dsRNA-sensing pathway.
findings.evidence: De Miranda J, Yaddanapudi K, Hornig M, Lipkin WI. FASEB J 2009;23(4):1064-1071, murine primary astrocyte cultures. Extracellular ('naked') poly(I:C) mainly induced RANTES, IL-8 and TNF-alpha via a TLR-3-dependent NF-kappaB pathway (confirmed in TLR-3 knockout astrocytes). Intracellular ('complexed') poly(I:C) chiefly induced IFN-beta and IL-6, and induced expression of both RIG-I and MDA-5 protein. Transfection with dominant-negative forms of the two helicases 'implicated MDA-5, but not RIG-I, as the intracellular sensor of poly I:C'. Complexed poly(I:C)/MDA-5 stimulation activated NF-kappaB and IRF-3. Note this is mouse primary culture; absolute expression values not reported.

findings.claim: Deleting Ifih1/MDA5 completely rescues the brain interferon signature, astrogliosis, microgliosis and deep white/gray matter calcification caused by an ADAR1 Aicardi-Goutieres mutation — establishing MDA5 as the necessary sensor driving endogenous-dsRNA-triggered white matter pathology in vivo.
findings.evidence: Guo X, Steinman RA, Sheng Y, Cao G, Wiley CA, Wang Q. J Neuroinflammation 2022;19:285, doi:10.1186/s12974-022-02646-0, PMID 36457126. In Adar1 catalytic-domain mutant mice, MDA-5 knockout completely normalized ISG expression: 'ISG levels in double-mutant mice were significantly lower than in the mutant mice and not different from the wildtype control mice.' Loss of MDA-5 prevented astrocytosis and microgliosis; the brain inflammation seen at 8 weeks in single mutants was eliminated in double mutants; deep gray matter calcification seen in aged mutants did not occur in MDA-5-deficient animals. Double-mutant mice were 'healthy and indistinguishable from WT mice' with normal growth, versus growth-retarded single mutants. Cell-type ISG pattern: neurons expressed ISG15, microglia expressed CXCL10, independent of genotype.

findings.claim: MDA5 drives myelin failure in an ADAR1 model — deleting MDA5 rescues the myelination defect — but this was shown in Schwann cells/peripheral nerve, NOT in oligodendrocytes/CNS.
findings.evidence: Gacem N, Kavo A, Zerad L, et al. Nat Commun 2020;11:198. Neural-crest-specific conditional deletion of Adar1 in mice caused global depigmentation and 'absence of myelin from peripheral nerves', resulting from altered Schwann cell differentiation. Upregulation of interferon-stimulated genes preceded these defects, with a signature resembling nerve injury response. 'Simultaneous extinction of MDA5, a key sensor of unedited RNA, rescues both melanocytes and myelin defects in vitro, suggesting that ADAR1 safeguards neural crest derivatives from aberrant MDA5-mediated interferon production.' The rescue was demonstrated in vitro. Follow-up: Zerad L et al., Cells 2024, PMID 39682701, implicates Egr1 overexpression in the Adar1-KO Schwann cell differentiation defect.

findings.claim: Microglial MDA5 contributes to interferonopathy neuropathology, but the MDA5-dependence is only partial in vivo.
findings.evidence: Nemec KM, Uy G, Chaluvadi VS, et al. eLife 2026;14:RP102900, doi:10.7554/eLife.102900, PMID 41589671. ER-Hoxb8 conditionally immortalized macrophages with CRISPR-Cas9 Adar1 mutation used for microglia replacement. Adar1 knockout elicited interferon secretion and impaired macrophage production in vitro, and prevented brain macrophage engraftment in vivo. These phenotypes 'can be rescued with concurrent mutation of Ifih1 (MDA5) in vitro, but not in vivo.' Microglia carrying the patient-specific Adar1 D1113H mutation drove interferon production in vivo, 'suggesting microglia drive AGS neuropathology.'

findings.claim: Human IFIH1 gain-of-function causes a leukodystrophy-spectrum CNS disease with demyelination and calcification, and regional calcification burden tracks regional IFIH1 protein expression — human genetic proof that CNS MDA5 activity is sufficient to injure white matter.
findings.evidence: (a) Gilani A, Adang LA, Vanderver A, Collins A, Kleinschmidt-DeMasters BK. Pediatr Dev Pathol 2019;22(6):566-570, PMID 30952201: autopsy of a 16-year-old with IFIH1-mutant AGS; microcephaly (brain weight 916 g); multifocal calcifications limited to small-to-medium CNS arteries in bilateral cerebral cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus and cerebellum; 'the extent of calcifications was variable across different brain regions... and correlated with the extent of IFIH1 protein expression (data derived from Allen Brain Institute).' AGS is characterized by 'calcification, diffuse demyelination, and variable degree of brain atrophy'. (b) Ruaud L, Rice GI, et al. Hum Mutat 2018;39(8):1076-1080, PMID 29782060: heterozygous IFIH1 c.2544T>G (p.Asp848Glu) gain-of-function segregating with autosomal-dominant early-onset spastic paraparesis plus intracranial calcification in 3 affected individuals; marked ISG transcript upregulation in all three plus two clinically unaffected relatives. (c) Kothur K, ... Crow YJ, Dale RC. Neurology 2018;90(6):289-291, PMID 29321238: open-label JAK1/2 blockade in progressive IFIH1-associated neuroinflammation — pharmacological targeting downstream of MDA5 in human CNS disease. (d) Peixoto de Barcelos I et al., Mol Genet Metab 2024, PMID 39332260: IFIH1 accounts for 19/167 (11.4%) of genetically confirmed AGS in the Myelin Disorders Biorepository Project.

findings.claim: Human MS genetic and peripheral-expression data link IFIH1 to MS, but with weak/ambiguous effects and no CNS cell-type resolution.
findings.evidence: (a) Enevold C, Oturai AB, Sorensen PS, Ryder LP, Koch-Henriksen N, Bendtzen K. J Neuroimmunol 2009;212(1-2):125-131, PMID 19450885: 963 MS patients vs 960 controls genotyped across TLR1-10, NOD1-2, DDX58 and IFIH1. 'Our results support previous findings of associations between the IFIH1-locus and MS (IFIH1-rs3747517 and IFIH1-rs1990760 trend test: P=0.002 and P=0.014, respectively).' (b) Deerhake ME, Biswas DD, Barclay WE, Shinohara ML. Front Immunol 2019;10:2644, PMID 31798505, summarising Hundeshagen et al. 2012 (J Neuroinflammation 9:140): 'elevated expression of DDX58 and IFIH1 was identified in a subset of MS patients with high expression of MX1' — i.e. IFIH1 is elevated in the MX1-high (endogenous type I IFN-high) MS subgroup, in PERIPHERAL BLOOD mononuclear cells, attributed to ISGF3 overactivity; after 1 month of IFN-beta therapy pathway genes were induced in MX1-low but unchanged in MX1-high patients. The same review notes that combinations of SNPs in DDX58, IFIH1 and DHX58/LGP2 may raise risk although no individual SNP was significantly associated. The review explicitly does not specify which CNS cell types express MDA5 or RIG-I in MS.

findings.claim: dsRNA is measurably elevated in early MS peripherally but essentially absent from CSF, and IFIH1 itself was not measured — so the 'endogenous dsRNA drives MDA5 in the MS CNS' hypothesis is currently unsupported by direct CNS measurement.
findings.evidence: Gouzouasis V, Sarrigeorgiou I, Tsifintaris M, et al. Front Microbiol 2025;16:1706133, PMID 41395469. Sandwich ELISA on matched plasma and CSF from 70 treatment-naive MS patients at first clinical onset plus plasma from 26 sex/age-matched healthy controls. Plasma dsRNA: MS 51 +/- 13 ng/ml vs controls 44 +/- 10 ng/ml, Mann-Whitney p=0.0231. CSF: of 22 MS patients tested, only 1 had detectable dsRNA; all others negative. Plasma dsRNA correlated with antiviral cytokines including IFN-gamma (r=0.45, p=0.002), GM-CSF, IFN-lambda1, IFN-lambda2/3, IFN-alpha2, IL-12p70. The paper mentions RIG-I, MDA5 and TLR3 only theoretically; IFIH1/DDX58 expression was NOT measured.

findings.claim: There is NO published study of Ifih1-/- (MDA5-knockout) mice in EAE, and NO study of MDA5 in the cuprizone model — the two most-used sterile demyelination models have never been tested for MDA5 dependence.
findings.evidence: Systematic PubMed E-utilities queries run 2026-09-19. Query 1: cuprizone[tiab] AND (Ifih1[tiab] OR MDA5[tiab] OR "RIG-I"[tiab]) — COUNT 0. Query 2: ("EAE" OR "experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis") AND ("Mda5-deficient" OR "Ifih1-/-" OR "MDA5 knockout" OR "Ifih1 knockout") — COUNT 0. Query 3: ("experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis"[tiab] OR EAE[tiab]) AND (Ifih1[tiab] OR MDA5[tiab]) — COUNT 1, and that single hit is a review (Prinz M, Knobeloch KP. Front Immunol 2012;3:67, PMID 22566948), not a primary Ifih1-/- EAE study. Query 4: (Ifih1 OR MDA5) AND (EAE OR encephalomyelitis) — 15 results, none an Ifih1-/- EAE experiment. All EAE evidence for the RLR pathway is therefore indirect: Mavs-/- (Dann 2012) or ligand pharmacology (Dann 2012; Hansen 2022). No cell-type-specific (oligodendrocyte-, astrocyte- or microglia-conditional) Ifih1 knockout in any demyelination model was found.

findings.claim: Ifih1 is conspicuously ABSENT from the interferon-responsive oligodendrocyte signatures reported by every major recent demyelination single-cell/epigenomic study except Falcao 2018 — the interferon-oligodendrocyte state is defined by Ifit1/Ifit3/Mx1/Irf7-type genes, not by Ifih1.
findings.evidence: Checked individually, all negative for Ifih1/MDA5: (a) Aboelnour EL, Vanoverbeke VR, Maupin EA, Hatfield MM, Adams KL. Nat Commun 2026, doi:10.1038/s41467-026-72383-y, PMID 42151131 — comparative transcriptomics of cuprizone, LPC, EAE and human MS lesions; shared OL responses are TNFalpha/NF-kappaB and IFN pathways (Gadd45a/b, Stat1/3, B2m, H2-D1, Socs3; ISGs Ifi27, Rtp4, Zc3hav1, Irf1, Ifi35, Stat2, H2-K1, Tap2, Nlrc5) — Ifih1 not present. (b) Hou J, Zhou Y, Cai Z, et al. Cell Rep 2023;42(4):112293, PMID 36952346 — cuprizone brain-cell atlas identifies an interferon-responsive (IFN-R) oligodendrocyte subset; Ifih1/Mda5 not present. (c) Zheng et al. Nat Neurosci 2025, doi:10.1038/s41593-025-02100-3, PMID 41249698 — mature oligodendrocyte transcriptome/epigenome across EAE stages; no Ifih1/MDA5. (Reports B2m, H2-K1, Nlrc5 up early; MOL2 38.35% immune-oligodendrocytes vs 18.75% for MOL5/MOL6; MHC-I and MHC-II chromatin accessibility remains high at late stage.) (d) Meijer et al. Neuron 2022;110(7):1193-1210, PMC9810341 — epigenomic priming of immune genes in oligodendroglia; IFIH1 is not among the primed/bivalent genes (primed set is MHC-I TAP1/TAP2/PSMB8/PSMB9, MHC-II H2-Ab1/H2-Aa/H2-Eb1, STAT1, IRF1, IRF8). (e) Kenigsbuch et al. Nat Neurosci 2022 disease-associated oligodendrocyte (DOL) signature — MOL-IFN state markers are Ifit1, Ifit3, Mx1; DOL markers Serpina3n, C4b. (f) Oji S, Nicolussi E-M, Kaufmann N, et al. PLoS One 2016;11(3):e0151244, PMID 26989859 — 31-gene type I IFN signature in experimental NMO/EAE rat spinal cord (Ifi30/GILT, Psmb9, Gbp2, P2ry6, Gadd45b, SerpinG1, IL-10, Sectm1b, Bst2, Timp1 and others); Ifih1/Mda5 not among them.

findings.claim: Where oligodendrocyte responses to dsRNA/poly(I:C) have been studied in a demyelination-relevant setting, the receptor implicated is TLR3, not MDA5, and MDA5 was never tested.
findings.evidence: Boccazzi M, et al. Cell Death Dis 2021;12(2):166, doi:10.1038/s41419-021-03446-9, PMID 33558485 — murine model of preterm white matter injury. Poly(I:C) was used explicitly 'to activate the TLR3 receptor'; oligodendrocyte primary cultures treated with poly(I:C) during differentiation showed stronger chemokine upregulation and decreased myelin gene expression; inflammatory marker upregulation was higher in O4+ immature oligodendrocytes than PDGFRalpha+ OPCs. Ifih1/MDA5 and Ddx58/RIG-I were neither measured nor ruled in or out. This is consistent with the Brain RNA-Seq baseline data showing oligodendrocyte Tlr3 (0.1-0.37 FPKM) and Ifih1 (0.1 FPKM) are both low but astrocytic Tlr3 (8.6-16.5 FPKM) is ~30-80x higher than astrocytic Ifih1 (0.12-0.29 FPKM).

findings.claim: In the broader Theiler's virus literature, MDA5 acts together with TLRs to amplify NF-kappaB-driven cytokine production in professional and non-professional antigen-presenting cells including oligodendrocytes, and excessive MDA5/TLR signalling is framed as pathogenic (pro-Th17) rather than purely protective — the opposite sign to the MDA5-knockout result.
findings.evidence: Kim BS. Int J Mol Sci 2021;22(10):5254, PMID 34067536; and Kim BS. Front Immunol 2023;14:1167972, PMID 37153539 (both single-author reviews). 'Professional (dendritic cells, macrophages, B cells) and non-professional (microglia, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes) antigen-presenting cells are the major cell populations permissive to viral infection and involved in cytokine production... TMEV infection leads to the activation of cytokine production via TLRs and MDA-5 coupled with NF-kappaB activation, which is required for TMEV replication. These activation signals further amplify the cytokine production and viral loads, promote the differentiation of pathogenic Th17 responses, and prevent cellular apoptosis, enabling viral persistence.' Related primary work: Kim SJ, Jin YH, Kim BS. PLoS One 2017;12(4):e0176406, PMID 28445497 — TMEV activates the TLR- and MDA5-dependent pathway leading to NLRP3 inflammasome/caspase-1/IL-1beta and PGE2 signalling, more vigorously in DCs and CD11b+ cells from susceptible SJL than resistant B6 mice; blocking PGE2 with AH23848 reduced demyelinating disease and CNS viral load. Note these are reviews/indirect; the direct MDA5-knockout experiment (Jin 2012) shows MDA5 is net protective.

research.cell_type_ranking:
Yes — this angle contributes a hard, quantitative BASELINE ranking plus a crucial caveat that baseline and induced rankings differ.

BASELINE (mouse cortex, purified cell types, Zhang et al. 2014 FPKM via brainrnaseq.org; floor = 0.1):
endothelial (2.06) >> microglia/macrophage (0.54) > neurons (0.41) ≈ OPC (0.22) ≈ astrocytes (0.21) >> newly-formed oligodendrocyte (0.10, at floor) = myelinating oligodendrocyte (0.10, at floor).
Oligodendrocytes are the ONLY CNS cell type where Ifih1 sits at the detection floor in both replicates. This is independently corroborated by Li et al. 2010 (J Virol), who could not detect MDA5 protein at all in oligodendrocytic N20.1 cells and needed 60-cycle nested RT-PCR to see the mRNA.

Human baseline: Human Protein Atlas single-nuclei brain classifies IFIH1 as "cell type enhanced" in ENDOTHELIAL cells (118.9 nCPM), "detected in many", low regional specificity — the same endothelium-first pattern as mouse. Per-cell-type glial nCPM values were not retrievable from HPA's API.

CRITICAL CAVEAT for anyone building the ranking: IFIH1 is itself an ISG, so the baseline ranking inverts under inflammation for oligodendrocytes specifically. In mouse EAE, Ifih1 is one of the interferon-responsive genes induced in MHC-II-expressing oligodendrocyte/OPC populations (Falcao et al., Nat Med 2018), and IFN-gamma treatment of primary OPCs/OLs produces "dramatic induction" of Ifih1. So oligodendrocytes go from lowest-at-baseline to interferon-inducible. Any ranking must be labelled baseline-vs-induced or it will be wrong in one condition.

Comparator receptors in the same mouse baseline table, useful for context: TLR3 is astrocyte-dominant (astro 8.6-16.5 FPKM, ~30-80x astrocytic Ifih1); RIG-I/Ddx58 is endothelium-dominant (8.5-8.8) with OPCs second (1.8-2.4); LGP2/Dhx58 is microglia-dominant (1.2-2.1). MAVS is the exception — broadly expressed INCLUDING oligodendrocytes (5.8-6.9 FPKM), so oligodendrocytes possess the downstream adaptor without the sensor.
research.gaps:
SUBSTANTIAL GAPS — several of the questions in this angle have no published answer:

1. NO Ifih1-/- EAE STUDY EXISTS. PubMed returns 0 hits for MDA5/Ifih1 knockout combined with EAE. Every EAE claim about the RLR pathway is indirect: Mavs-/- (which also removes RIG-I and LGP2 signalling) or ligand pharmacology with complexed poly(I:C) (which is not MDA5-selective in vivo). The frequently-repeated statement that "MDA5 restrains EAE" is an over-reading of Mavs-/- data.

2. NO MDA5 DATA IN CUPRIZONE OR LPC AT ALL. PubMed: cuprizone AND (Ifih1 OR MDA5 OR RIG-I) = 0 results. The toxic/sterile demyelination models are completely untested for MDA5.

3. NO CELL-TYPE-CONDITIONAL Ifih1 KNOCKOUT in any neuroinflammation or demyelination model — no oligodendrocyte-, astrocyte-, microglia- or endothelium-specific Ifih1 deletion was found. So "which CNS cell's MDA5 matters" is unanswered experimentally.

4. NO DIRECT EVIDENCE OF MDA5 PROTEIN IN OLIGODENDROCYTES, in any species, in health or disease. The one study addressing oligodendrocyte MDA5 function (Li et al. 2010) explicitly failed to detect MDA5 protein and relied on a ~40%-efficient siRNA. I found no immunohistochemistry, immunocytochemistry, western blot or flow cytometry localising MDA5 protein to an oligodendrocyte. The answer to "do oligodendrocytes sense dsRNA via MDA5" is: weakly supported by one knockdown study and one knockout-glia IFN readout, contradicted at the protein level, and with TLR3 the better-supported receptor in demyelination-relevant settings.

5. NO NUMERIC FOLD-CHANGE FOR Ifih1 IN OLIGODENDROCYTES. Falcao et al. 2018 state "dramatic induction" of Ifih1 by IFN-gamma in primary OPCs/OLs (Fig. 4e) but publish no fold-change or p-value in text or legend; I could not extract the underlying values. Likewise Jin et al. 2012 report "drastically reduced" IFN-alpha in MDA5-/- mice without pg/ml values.

6. NO MS LESION MEASUREMENT OF IFIH1 BY CELL TYPE. I found no study quantifying IFIH1 in human MS lesion oligodendrocytes, astrocytes or microglia. The human MS IFIH1 expression evidence (Hundeshagen 2012) is peripheral blood mononuclear cells only. The 2025 dsRNA-in-MS study did not measure IFIH1 and found CSF dsRNA in only 1/22 patients, so there is currently no direct evidence of an endogenous-dsRNA/MDA5 axis inside the MS CNS.

7. HUMAN CELL-TYPE BASELINE INCOMPLETE. The human brainrnaseq.org cell-type dataset (fe-wp-dataset-124.csv, Zhang et al. 2016 human) returned HTTP 504 on four attempts and could not be retrieved; HPA's API exposes only the top-enhanced brain cell type (endothelial, 118.9 nCPM), not the full per-cell-type table. The human oligodendrocyte-vs-microglia-vs-astrocyte IFIH1 ordering therefore rests on mouse data plus the HPA summary classification.

8. DIRECTIONAL CONFLICT UNRESOLVED. In TMEV, MDA5 knockout worsens demyelination (protective role, Jin 2012), while the same group's reviews frame excessive MDA5+TLR signalling as driving pathogenic Th17 responses and viral persistence. In EAE, RLR signalling is protective. In ADAR1/AGS models, MDA5 is the necessary driver of white matter injury. Whether MDA5 is protective or injurious in demyelination is context-dependent (viral vs sterile vs interferonopathy) and no study has tested the same manipulation across models.

9. The Ifih1 G821S gain-of-function knock-in mouse has a documented bony/Singleton-Merten-like phenotype reversed by IFNAR or MAVS loss, but I found no published characterisation of its white matter, myelin or oligodendrocyte phenotype.

verdicts.claim: Ifih1 mRNA NOT detectable in mouse oligodendrocytes at homeostasis; rank endothelial >> microglia > neurons ≈ OPC ≈ astrocyte >> oligodendrocyte (Brain RNA-Seq FPKM)
verdicts.reason: I downloaded fe-wp-dataset-120.csv and every single FPKM value quoted is EXACT (Ifih1 endothelial 2.099757/2.011976; microglia 0.601787/0.480536; neurons 0.145805/0.677700; OPC 0.325703/0.108437; astrocyte 0.293204/0.118981; both OL types 0.1/0.1; plus all Ddx58, Dhx58, Tlr3, Cx3cr1 473.18/506.20, Mbp 115329.8/75465.2 values). I also verified the floor: dataset minimum = 0.1, no value below it, 113,963/302,904 values (37.6%) sit exactly at 0.1, and 5,054 genes are at floor in all 14 columns. So the table is real and correctly transcribed. Three problems with the wording. (1) 'NOT detectable' is assay-specific, not biological. Kapil et al. Glia 2012 (PMID 22736486, 'Oligodendroglia are limited in type I interferon induction and responsiveness in vivo') FACS-purified oligodendroglia (CD45-GFP+) and microglia from adult PLP-GFP mouse spinal cord and states verbatim: 'Whereas transcription of all four PRR was readily detected in microglia, Mda5, Rig-I, and Tlr3 transcripts were significantly reduced and Tlr7 was below detection in oligodendroglia' — Mda5 is REDUCED, not absent, and is explicitly distinguished from Tlr7 which WAS below detection. That paper further reports 'PRRs and ISGs were upregulated by infection in both cell types', i.e. oligodendroglial Mda5 is inducible. This paper is not cited anywhere in the claim set and directly qualifies the headline. (2) 'microglia > neurons' is not supportable at n=2: neuron replicates are 0.146 and 0.678, straddling both microglia replicates (0.602, 0.481). The separation between microglia, neurons, OPC and astrocytes is within replicate noise; only endothelial (~2.0, 4x the next) and the two OL types (at floor) are robustly separated. (3) Zhang 2014 purified juvenile mouse cortex (~P7 for most types, P17 for myelinating OL), so 'at homeostasis' should read 'in juvenile mouse cortex'. Provenance note: the file is hosted on brainrnaseq.org and its 7 cell types x 2 columns match Zhang 2014's design, but I did not diff it against the paper's own supplementary table.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the Barres-lab purified-cell-type FPKM table for juvenile mouse cortex (brainrnaseq.org fe-wp-dataset-120.csv, 2 columns per cell type, 0.1 = imputed detection floor confirmed as the dataset minimum), Ifih1 sits AT the 0.1 floor in both myelinating (0.1/0.1) and newly-formed (0.1/0.1) oligodendrocytes, i.e. below detection in this assay. Endothelial cells are the clear high point (2.100/2.012, ~4x any other type); microglia (0.602/0.481), neurons (0.146/0.678), OPC (0.326/0.108) and astrocytes (0.293/0.119) are all low and mutually indistinguishable at n=2. The ranking is therefore endothelial >> {microglia, neuron, OPC, astrocyte, all near-floor} > oligodendrocyte (at floor); finer ordering within the middle group is not supported. 'Below detection in this dataset' is not 'absent': Kapil et al., Glia 2012 (PMID 22736486) detected Mda5 transcripts in FACS-purified ADULT mouse oligodendroglia in vivo — significantly reduced versus microglia but, unlike Tlr7, above detection — and found Mda5 upregulated in oligodendroglia by JHMV infection.

verdicts.claim: MAVS is robustly expressed in mouse oligodendrocytes even though Ifih1 is not, so downstream machinery is present while the sensor is essentially absent at baseline
verdicts.reason: Every Mavs FPKM is EXACT in the downloaded file: microglia 12.293559/16.197047; astrocytes 9.232174/7.580946; myelinating OL 6.890978/5.809225; newly-formed OL 5.918995/6.017841; OPC 6.627272/6.678569; endothelial 3.428406/3.662283; neurons 0.614173/1.020571. Oligodendroglial Mavs is unambiguously above floor and among the higher values in the table, while Ifih1 in the same cells is at floor. The claim is also honest in labelling 0.1 as the floor rather than pretending the ~60x ratio is a measured fold-difference. Two caveats that do not change the verdict: the ~60x figure is a lower bound computed against an imputed floor, not a measurement; and comparing FPKM between two different genes indexes transcript abundance only, not protein levels or signalling competence. Worth noting the same table shows the wider downstream module is also present in OL (Irf3 7.83-9.29) while the amplification arm is not (Irf7 0.174-0.176, near floor) — consistent with Kapil 2012's finding that oligodendroglia have 'a high threshold for upregulation of Ikkε and Irf7'.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the same mouse cortex FPKM table, Mavs is solidly expressed in oligodendrocytes (myelinating 6.891/5.809; newly-formed 5.919/6.018 FPKM) and in OPC (6.627/6.679), astrocytes (9.232/7.581) and microglia (12.294/16.197), while being low in neurons (0.614/1.021). Since Ifih1 in oligodendrocytes sits at the 0.1 imputed floor, oligodendroglial Mavs mRNA is at least ~60-fold above it — a lower bound against a floor, not a measured ratio. Irf3 is likewise present in OL (7.8-9.3) but Irf7 is near floor (0.17), so the adaptor is present while both the sensor and the IFN-amplification arm are not, at mRNA level, in juvenile mouse cortex. No protein data support this.

verdicts.claim: In human brain snRNA-seq IFIH1 is 'cell type enhanced' in ENDOTHELIAL cells, not in glia or neurons; at protein level across tissues the highest cell-type intensity is in macrophages
verdicts.reason: I pulled https://www.proteinatlas.org/ENSG00000115267.json directly. Every quoted field is EXACT: 'RNA single nuclei brain specificity' = Cell type enhanced; 'RNA single nuclei brain distribution' = Detected in many; 'RNA single nuclei brain specific nCPM' = {'endothelial cell': '118.9'}; 'RNA brain regional specificity' = Low region specificity / Detected in all; 'RNA mouse brain regional specificity' = Low region specificity / Detected in all; 'RNA blood cell specificity' = Low immune cell specificity; 'Protein cell type specific Intensity' = {'Macrophages': '2720714.2'}. The claim's caveat that per-cell-type nCPM for oligodendrocytes/astrocytes/microglia is not exposed also holds — neither the JSON nor the search_download TSV returns those columns, and the rendered brain single-cell page lists cluster IDs without extractable values. The protein sentence is the problem. 'Protein cell type specific Intensity' is HPA's list of cell types flagged as ENHANCED, not a ranked maximum over all cell types, so 'the highest cell-type intensity is in macrophages' converts a category label into a measurement that HPA never reports. It also rests on one antibody, HPA002656, with 'Reliability (IH)': Approved — HPA's middle tier, not Enhanced or Supported — and 2,720,714.2 is an internal HPA intensity score with no absolute meaning. The sibling field 'Protein tissue specific Intensity' = {'lymphoid tissue': '7361548.7'} carries a larger number, showing these scores are not comparable across fields. Separately, 'not in any glial or neuronal population' should be read strictly as 'not ENHANCED in' — the same record says 'Detected in many', so glia and neurons are expressing, just not enriched.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the Human Protein Atlas record for IFIH1 (ENSG00000115267), the human brain single-nuclei data classify IFIH1 as 'Cell type enhanced' with the single enhanced cell type listed as endothelial cell (specific nCPM 118.9); distribution is 'Detected in many', so glial and neuronal populations express IFIH1 without being enriched for it, and per-cell-type nCPM values for oligodendrocytes, astrocytes and microglia are not exposed by the JSON API, the TSV download or the rendered page. Regional specificity is 'Low region specificity / Detected in all' in both human and mouse brain, and blood shows 'Low immune cell specificity'. At protein level, HPA flags Macrophages as the cell type with enhanced staining intensity (score 2,720,714.2) — this is HPA's enhancement flag, not a verified maximum across all cell types, and it derives from a single antibody (HPA002656) at 'Approved' IH reliability, so it is weak evidence for cell-type protein ranking.

verdicts.claim: Ifih1 is induced in an interferon-responsive/MHC-II oligodendrocyte-lineage state in mouse EAE; strongest published MDA5-oligodendrocyte link; INDUCED (ISG) not baseline, driven by IFN-gamma
verdicts.reason: Verified against PMC6544508. Both Ifih1 sentences are real: the ISG sentence naming 'Ifih1, Iigp1, Trim34, Irf7, Irgm1, Irgm2, Igtp and Zbp1' in MHC-II expressing OL/OPC populations, and a second, separate mention placing Ifih1 among alternatively spliced genes ('the Ifih1 gene, in which MS-associated polymorphisms have been found') with the 360-gene total confirmed. Cell counts confirmed: 745 control and 707 EAE OL-lineage cells, 4 biologically independent mice per condition. Fig. 4e legend confirmed verbatim: 'qRT-PCR analysis for MHC and interferon responsive genes on primary OPCs and OLs treated with interferon-γ and dexamethasone, n=3 independent experiments per condition'. The claim's key methodological honesty is correct and important: no fold-change and no p-value for Ifih1 appear anywhere in text or legend, and the claim says so. Two qualifications. The Fig. 4e validation is a cell-culture experiment at 100 ng/ml IFN-γ (±1 µM dexamethasone) for 72 h — a supraphysiological dose in primary culture, not an in-vivo demonstration that IFN-γ drives Ifih1 in EAE oligodendrocytes. And 'the single strongest published link' is an unverifiable superlative, not a source claim; Jin 2012 arguably makes a stronger functional claim, albeit on data not shown (see claim 6).
verdicts.corrected_claim: Falcão et al., Nat Med 2018;24(12):1837-1844 (PMID 30420755) report Ifih1 among interferon-responsive genes ('Ifih1, Iigp1, Trim34, Irf7, Irgm1, Irgm2, Igtp and Zbp1') in MHC-II-expressing OL/OPC populations from MOG-EAE mouse spinal cord (745 control vs 707 EAE OL-lineage cells, n=4 mice/condition), and separately list Ifih1 among 360 alternatively spliced genes in EAE. The IFN-gamma attribution comes from Fig. 4e, a qRT-PCR experiment on PRIMARY CULTURED OPCs/OLs treated with IFN-gamma (100 ng/ml) ± dexamethasone (1 µM) for 72 h, n=3 independent experiments — a cell-culture result, not in-vivo causation. No fold-change or p-value for Ifih1 is reported anywhere in the paper, so the magnitude of induction is unquantified. This establishes Ifih1 as ISG-like (inducible) rather than a baseline oligodendrocyte gene, consistent with its floor-level baseline in purified OL; calling it 'the single strongest published link' is an editorial ranking the sources do not support.

verdicts.claim: Only ONE primary study tested whether oligodendrocytes sense dsRNA via MDA5; MDA5 protein undetectable; evidence rests on ~40% siRNA knockdown; RIG-I was the dominant protein-detectable sensor
verdicts.reason: Every study-specific detail checks out verbatim against PMC2903279: 'Unfortunately, no MDA5 protein was detected in virus-infected cells at various times p.i. or in mock-infected cells'; 'the amount of MDA5 mRNA was extremely low in N20.1 cells, the nested RT-PCR using a total of 60 cycles was able to amply MDA5 mRNA in MHV-infected N20.1 cells'; 'The amount of MDA5 mRNA decreased by approximately 40%... knockdown of MDA5 mRNA by its siRNAs drastically blocked the induction of IFN-β by MHV infection'; RIG-I 'upregulation was detected beginning at 6 h p.i.'; RIG-I knockdown 'completely blocked the activation of IRF-3' and 'drastically but incompletely blocked the production of IFN-α/β'; and UV-inactivated virus gave background IFN-α/β. All confirmed. The universal 'only ONE primary study' is refuted, and refuted from inside this same claim set: claim 6's own source, Jin et al. J Virol 2012, isolated primary oligodendrocytes from MDA5-KO and WT mice and tested TMEV-induced IFN in them — that is a second primary study testing MDA5 in oligodendrocytes. Kapil et al., Glia 2012 (PMID 22736486) is a third relevant primary study: it measured Mda5 transcript levels in FACS-purified oligodendroglia and tested poly(I:C) responsiveness in vivo and ex vivo. Claims 5 and 6 are mutually inconsistent as written. Also note N20.1 is an immortalized mouse oligodendrocytic line, not primary oligodendrocytes.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In the one study that directly assayed MDA5 protein in an oligodendrocytic cell (Li, Liu & Zhang, J Virol 2010;84(13):6472-6482, PMID 20427526, immortalized mouse N20.1 cells infected with MHV), 'no MDA5 protein was detected in virus-infected cells at various times p.i. or in mock-infected cells (data not shown)', and MDA5 mRNA was 'extremely low', requiring nested RT-PCR over a total of 60 cycles to amplify. The functional evidence is a ~40%-efficient siRNA knockdown that 'drastically blocked the induction of IFN-beta' with no fold-change reported. RIG-I protein WAS detectable, was upregulated from 6 h p.i., and its knockdown 'completely blocked the activation of IRF-3' and 'drastically but incompletely blocked' IFN-alpha/beta; IFN induction required replicating virus. This is NOT the only primary study bearing on MDA5 in oligodendrocytes: Jin et al. 2012 tested MDA5-KO primary oligodendrocytes (though those data are 'not shown'), and Kapil et al., Glia 2012 quantified Mda5 transcripts in FACS-purified oligodendroglia and tested poly(I:C) responses in vivo and ex vivo.

verdicts.claim: MDA5 is functionally required for type I IFN induction in primary oligodendrocytes (plus astrocytes and microglia) on TMEV infection, shown by knockout, without ever measuring MDA5 expression
verdicts.reason: The second half is right and the first half is not. Confirmed from PMC3264388: the paper reports NO direct measurement of MDA5 mRNA or protein in any CNS cell type — the entire argument is loss-of-function, exactly as the claim says. But the oligodendrocyte result is not shown data. The paper states: 'Primary astrocytes and oligodendrocytes derived from new neonatal brains of MDA5 KO and WT mice were also infected with TMEV or stimulated with TLR ligands (data not shown).' The quoted sentence 'The expression of IFN-α4 in response to TMEV infection was completely abrogated in MDA5 KO cells compared with WT cells' is anchored to microglia and peritoneal macrophages ('similar to virus-infected microglia and peritoneal macrophages'). For astrocytes and oligodendrocytes the paper describes a 'reduction of IFN-β expression in both the astrocytes and oligodendrocytes from MDA5 KO mice' — a reduction, not complete abrogation, and with no figure, no n, and no statistics. So 'functionally required for type I IFN induction in primary oligodendrocytes' rests on an unillustrated assertion, and the strong 'completely abrogated' wording is being transferred from myeloid cells onto oligodendrocytes. Also the readout is IFN-alpha4 and IFN-beta specifically, not type I IFN as a class.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Jin YH et al., J Virol 2012;86(3):1531-1543 (PMID 22090123) report that TMEV-induced IFN-alpha4 was 'completely abrogated in MDA5 KO cells' — a result shown for microglia and peritoneal macrophages. Primary astrocytes and oligodendrocytes from neonatal MDA5-KO and WT brains were also infected, but those experiments are explicitly '(data not shown)', and for those two cell types the paper describes only a 'reduction of IFN-beta expression', not abrogation, with no figure, n, or statistics. So MDA5-dependence of type I IFN induction is demonstrated in myeloid CNS cells; for oligodendrocytes it is asserted but not shown. The claim's key point stands and is important: the paper never measures MDA5 mRNA or protein in any glial cell type — the evidence is loss-of-function only, so it says nothing about whether oligodendrocytes express MDA5.

verdicts.claim: MDA5 is protective against TMEV-induced demyelinating disease: MDA5-deficient mice show far higher CNS viral loads and 4-fold higher demyelinating disease incidence
verdicts.reason: Verified against PMC3264388. 'Approximately 10- to 700-fold higher numbers of TMEV plaques were found in MDA5 KO mice at 8 and 28 days postinfection' — matches exactly. Disease incidence 80% in MDA5 KO versus 20% in WT, which is the 4-fold figure, with 8/10 versus 2/10 mice. 'The severity of disease was significantly higher in MDA5 KO mice than in WT mice at 14 and 21 days postinfection (P < 0.01)' — exact. Strain confirmed as 129X1/SvJ (129SvJ), described as relatively resistant to TMEV demyelinating disease, which is the correct genetic background for this comparison. Reduced type I IFN with elevated CCL2, CCL5 and CXCL1 confirmed, and the claim correctly flags that pg/ml values are not in the accessible text. Minor caveats only: n=10 per group with no p-value reported for the incidence difference itself (the P<0.01 applies to severity at 14 and 21 dpi), and this is mouse TMEV, a viral demyelination model, so it speaks to MDA5's antiviral role rather than to sterile autoimmune demyelination.
verdicts.corrected_claim: In Jin YH et al., J Virol 2012;86(3):1531-1543 (PMID 22090123), MDA5-deficient 129X1/SvJ mice infected with TMEV had 10- to 700-fold higher CNS plaque counts at 8 and 28 dpi and consistently higher VP1 RNA in brain and spinal cord, with clinical demyelinating disease in 80% (8/10) versus 20% (2/10) of WT — a 4-fold higher incidence, though no p-value is given for the incidence comparison itself (n=10/group). Severity was significantly higher at 14 and 21 dpi (P<0.01). This was accompanied by drastically reduced IFN-alpha and elevated CCL2, CCL5 and CXCL1 (no pg/ml values reported). MDA5 is therefore net protective in this VIRAL mouse demyelination model; the mechanism is viral control, and the result does not extend to sterile/autoimmune demyelination.

verdicts.claim: Theiler's virus 3C protease cleaves and inactivates MDA5 — direct biochemical evidence MDA5 is a relevant antiviral target in this demyelination model
verdicts.reason: Every element is verbatim in the abstract of Miyamoto et al., J Immunol 2023;210(3):335-347 (PMID 36525065), retrieved via NCBI E-utilities: 'Upon ectopic expression of theilovirus 3C protease from Saffold virus or Theiler's murine encephalomyelitis virus but not encephalomyocarditis virus, fragments of cleaved MDA5 were observed in a dose-dependent manner'; 'When enzymatically inactive Theilovirus 3C protease was expressed, MDA5 cleavage was completely abrogated'; 'Mass spectrometric analysis identified two cleavage sites at the C terminus of MDA5, cleaving off one of the RNA-binding domains'; 'The same cleavage pattern was observed during Theilovirus infection'; 'impaired ATP hydrolysis, RNA binding, and filament assembly on RNA'; 'the cleavage-resistant MDA5 mutant against the 3C protease showed an enhanced IFN response during Saffold virus infection'. Nothing is misquoted. The only stretch is the interpretive tail: these are ectopic-expression and infection experiments in cell culture, not in demyelinating CNS tissue, and Saffold virus is a human theilovirus that does not cause the demyelinating disease. The biochemistry establishes that theiloviruses target MDA5; it does not by itself establish relevance in the demyelinating CNS.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Miyamoto M et al., J Immunol 2023;210(3):335-347 (PMID 36525065) show, in cell culture, that 3C protease from Saffold virus or TMEV — but not encephalomyocarditis virus — cleaves MDA5 dose-dependently; catalytically inactive 3C completely abrogates cleavage; mass spectrometry maps two cleavage sites at the MDA5 C terminus removing one RNA-binding domain; the same cleavage occurs during authentic theilovirus infection; and cleavage impairs ATP hydrolysis, RNA binding and filament assembly, with a cleavage-resistant MDA5 mutant showing enhanced IFN response during Saffold virus infection. This is strong biochemical evidence that theiloviruses evade MDA5. It is cell-culture work, not CNS or demyelinating tissue, so relevance to the demyelination model is inferred rather than demonstrated.

verdicts.claim: In EAE, loss of MAVS/IPS-1 worsens disease AND significantly reduces mature oligodendrocyte number — most direct EAE evidence linking RLR signalling to oligodendrocyte preservation
verdicts.reason: I extracted the Dann et al. Nat Neurosci 2012 PDF and verified the text directly. Verbatim: 'in Ips-1−/− mice, the peak of disease was significantly augmented (P < 0.05)'; 'Histology performed on Ips-1–deficient spinal cords revealed a plethora of infiltrating macrophages'; 'The increased influx of macrophages was accompanied by an elevated number of T cells and stronger demyelination as compared with Ips-1+/+ mice... whereas there was no statistically significant difference (P > 0.05) in axonal damage'; and the key sentence exactly as quoted: 'The number of mature oligodendrocytes was significantly lower (P < 0.05) in Ips-1−/− mice than in Ips-1+/+ mice (Fig. 1g).' Group sizes confirmed from the Fig. 1a legend: Ips-1+/+ n=7, Ips-1−/− n=8. NOGO-A confirmed as the mature-oligodendrocyte marker in the Fig. 1b legend. The TH17/TH1/TH2 cytokine pattern at 19 dpi is confirmed. The one thing to flag is interpretive, not factual: this is a GLOBAL Mavs knockout with markedly worse macrophage infiltration, more T cells and stronger demyelination, so the lower NOGO-A count is equally consistent with oligodendrocyte loss secondary to worse inflammation. The paper does not establish a cell-autonomous RLR requirement in oligodendrocytes, and 'most direct evidence' is an editorial superlative.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Dann A et al., Nat Neurosci 2012;15(1):98-106 (PMID 22197832): in MOG35-55/CFA active EAE, Ips-1−/− (Mavs−/−, n=8) versus Ips-1+/+ (n=7) mice had equal incidence and onset but a significantly augmented disease peak (P<0.05), with more macrophages, more T cells, stronger demyelination, no significant difference in axonal damage (P>0.05), and significantly fewer NOGO-A+ mature oligodendrocytes (P<0.05). Because this is a global knockout with substantially worse CNS inflammation and demyelination, the oligodendrocyte deficit is an association that is at least as likely to be secondary to inflammation as a cell-autonomous RLR effect; no oligodendrocyte-conditional Mavs or Ifih1 experiment was done.

verdicts.claim: Cytoplasmic poly(I:C) ameliorates established EAE, strictly IFNAR-dependent and mediated by peripheral MYELOID cells, not CNS glia
verdicts.reason: The pharmacology and the IFNAR-dependence are right; the cellular attribution is backwards, and the paper says so explicitly. Confirmed verbatim from the Dann 2012 PDF: Fig. 2a legend gives 25 µg complexed 3pRNA (n=7), complexed poly(I:C)/MDA5 (n=8), non-complexed poly(I:C)/TLR3 (n=6), poly(A) (n=5), PBS (n=5) at 13, 15 and 17 dpi — every n exact; 'Disease severity during the effector phase was markedly diminished in RIG-I– and MDA5-stimulated mice, whereas non-complexed poly(I:C) (TLR3 ligand) or synthetic RNA bearing no 5′-triphosphate (polyA) did not change the disease score'; and 'Ifnar1−/− mice showed no improvement of the clinical course of EAE after treatment with RIG-I or MDA5 ligands'. But on mediation the paper states the OPPOSITE of the claim. In Ifnar1loxP/loxP;LysM-cre mice — where 'IFNAR is absent on CD11b+Ly-6Clo monocytes, CD11b+Ly-6Chi monocytes, CD11b+CD45lo microglia and CD11b+Gr-1+ granulocytes' — 'Application of 3pRNA and poly(I:C) significantly decreased (P < 0.05) the mean clinical course', and the authors conclude verbatim: 'These data indicate that the engagement of IFNAR on monocytes, macrophages, microglia and granulocytes does not account for the suppression of CNS autoimmunity on treatment with dsRNAs.' The effect was instead lost in Ifnar1loxP/loxP;Cd11c-cre mice: 'the effector phases were similar in all of the treated groups, suggesting that IFNAR expression on dendritic cells is required'. Figure 5's own title is 'IFNAR signaling on dendritic cells rather than on monocytic cells is required for dsRNA-mediated suppression of CNS autoimmunity.' Separately, the claim's statement that NOGO-A counts were 'significantly reduced' in MDA5-stimulated mice is internally implausible — NOGO-A marks mature oligodendrocytes, and reducing them would contradict the protective narrative (in claim 9 the same marker going down is read as worse disease); I could not resolve the direction from the figure text and the numbers are not in the running text.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Dann A et al., Nat Neurosci 2012;15(1):98-106: 25 µg PEI-complexed poly(I:C) (MDA5 ligand) given IV at 13, 15 and 17 dpi markedly diminished EAE severity during the effector phase (n=8 vs PBS n=5; complexed 3pRNA n=7; non-complexed poly(I:C)/TLR3 n=6 and polyA n=5 had no effect), and the benefit was entirely IFNAR-dependent — 'Ifnar1−/− mice showed no improvement'. The effect is NOT mediated by myeloid cells: in LysM-cre conditional mice lacking IFNAR on monocytes, macrophages, microglia and granulocytes the treatment still worked (P<0.05), and the authors conclude that IFNAR engagement on those cells 'does not account for the suppression of CNS autoimmunity'. It requires IFNAR on DENDRITIC CELLS — the effect was abolished in Cd11c-cre conditional mice, and Fig. 5 is titled 'IFNAR signaling on dendritic cells rather than on monocytic cells is required'. The site of action is peripheral (FITC-labelled RNA reached the spleen, mostly CD11b+CD11c+ DCs, and 'labeled RNA could not be detected in the diseased spinal cord'), and microglial IFNAR is specifically excluded; astrocytes and oligodendrocytes were not separately tested. IFN-beta was produced by conventional DCs, plasmacytoid DCs and BMDMs, with BMDMs responding to RIG-I activation and 'to a lower extent' MDA5 activation. The direction of the NOGO-A change under treatment is not verifiable from the text and should not be cited.

verdicts.claim: Forcing RIG-I/MAVS signalling inside the CNS suppresses EAE, with astrocytes (not oligodendrocytes) among IFN-beta-producing cells
verdicts.reason: The substance checks out against PMC9570082: the CM construct is 'RIG-I 2CARD domains (C) and the first 200 amino acids of MAVS (M)', delivered intrathecally into the cisterna magna at disease onset (2.5x10^10 viral particles in 10 µL); AAV-CM-treated mice showed no rise in mean clinical score over days 1-5 while controls rose significantly (p<0.05); 'The protective effect of intrathecal AAV-CM was abrogated in IFNAR1-KO mice'; IFN-beta significantly elevated at days 1, 3 and 7; myelin loss reduced by AAV-CM. The three IFN-beta-producing populations are confirmed: leptomeningeal CD45+ cells, choroid plexus cells and astrocytes. Two corrections. First, the parenthetical '(not oligodendrocytes)' implies oligodendrocytes were assayed and came back negative — they were not: oligodendrocytes are neither examined nor mentioned in the paper. That converts an absence of testing into a negative finding, which is exactly the failure mode to avoid. Second, the claim's day-1 RT-qPCR list is incomplete: the paper reports upregulation of IFN-alpha, IFN-beta, IFN-gamma, IL-10, IL-1beta AND IRF7 and IRF9. Conceptually worth stating plainly: CM is a constitutively active 2CARD-MAVS fusion acting DOWNSTREAM of the sensors, so this experiment bypasses MDA5 entirely and carries no information about MDA5 itself.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Hansen AK et al., Int J Mol Sci 2022;23(19):11292 (PMID 36232593) injected AAV8 encoding 'CM', a constitutively active fusion of RIG-I 2CARD with MAVS amino acids 1-200, intrathecally into the cisterna magna at EAE onset (2.5x10^10 particles/10 µL). Disease progression was suppressed in WT mice while controls' mean score rose (p<0.05), and the protective effect was abrogated in IFNAR1-KO mice. IFN-beta was expressed by extraparenchymal leptomeningeal CD45+ cells, choroid plexus cells and GFAP+ astrocytes, was significantly elevated at days 1, 3 and 7, and remained detectable at day 21; day-1 RT-qPCR showed upregulation of IFN-alpha, IFN-beta, IFN-gamma, IL-10, IL-1beta, IRF7 and IRF9; Luxol fast blue myelin loss was reduced. Oligodendrocytes were never examined, so their exclusion from the IFN-beta-producing list reflects absence of testing, not a negative result. Because CM acts downstream of the RLR sensors, this experiment tests the MAVS/type-I-IFN axis and says nothing about MDA5 expression or ligand sensing.

verdicts.claim: Astrocytes use MDA5, not RIG-I, as their intracellular dsRNA sensor — the CNS cell type with the best-supported functional MDA5 dsRNA-sensing pathway
verdicts.reason: The central quote is verbatim in the De Miranda et al. FASEB J 2009;23(4):1064-1071 abstract (PMID 19036857), retrieved via E-utilities: 'transfection of astrocytes with dominant negative forms of the helicases implicated MDA-5, but not RIG-I, as the intracellular sensor of poly I:C.' The surrounding structure is also confirmed: naked poly(I:C) 'mainly induced... RANTES, IL-8, and TNF-alpha' and 'signals via a TLR-3-dependent NF-kappaB pathway' (verified in TLR-3 knockout astrocytes); complexed poly(I:C) 'chiefly induced expression of IFN-beta and IL-6' and induced both RIG-I and MDA-5; 'Complexed poly I:C-mediated MDA-5 stimulation transmitted downstream signals, resulting in activation of the transcription factors NF-kappaB and IRF-3.' The claim's own caveats are correct — mouse primary culture, no absolute expression values. One number the claim missed and should carry: the full text reports that complexed poly(I:C) induced a 21-fold and 25-fold increase in RIG-I and MDA-5 mRNA respectively, which is the actual quantitative measure of MDA5 inducibility in astrocytes. The superlative 'best-supported' is editorial and contestable against Jin 2012's knockout data, but the underlying finding is genuine.

verdicts.claim: Deleting MDA5 completely rescues the IFN signature, astrogliosis, microgliosis AND deep white/gray matter calcification in an ADAR1 AGS mouse — MDA5 is the necessary sensor driving dsRNA-triggered WHITE MATTER pathology in vivo
verdicts.reason: The IFN/gliosis rescue is real; the calcification rescue and the white-matter-pathology framing are not supported. The abstract of Guo et al., J Neuroinflammation 2022;19:285 (PMID 36457126) states the rescue precisely and narrowly: 'Brain ISG activation and neuroglial reaction were completely prevented in the Adar D1113H mutant mice by blocking RNA sensing through deletion of the cytosolic RNA receptor MDA-5.' Calcification is NOT in that list. The abstract separately places calcification as 'later stage calcification in the deep white matter areas' in the MUTANT mice, and a read of the full text (PMC9714073) indicates the calcification data are von Kossa foci of VASCULAR calcification assessed at 8 months, with aged double-mutants not characterised — so whether MDA5 deletion prevents calcification is not reported. The mutation and the knockout are as described (Adar D963H encoding the AGS-patient-equivalent D1113H; full Ifih1−/−), the double mutants being 'healthy and indistinguishable from WT mice' is confirmed, and the neurons-ISG15 / microglia-CXCL10 pattern is confirmed. The decisive problem for this claim set's purpose: the paper reports NO demyelination and does not mention oligodendrocytes at all. The 'white matter pathology' is vascular calcification in deep white matter, not myelin injury, so this cannot support MDA5 driving white matter/myelin damage. (Note the source is itself inconsistent on anatomy — abstract says deep white matter, body text says deep gray matter/DGM.)
verdicts.corrected_claim: Guo X et al., J Neuroinflammation 2022;19:285 (PMID 36457126): mice carrying the Adar1 catalytic-domain mutation equivalent to patient D1113H show robust brain ISG expression, early-onset astrocytosis and microgliosis, and later-stage vascular calcification; ISG expression is cell-type-patterned (neurons ISG15, microglia CXCL10). Crossing to Ifih1−/− (MDA-5 knockout) 'completely prevented' brain ISG activation and the neuroglial reaction, and double-mutant mice were healthy and indistinguishable from WT. The paper does NOT report that MDA5 deletion prevents calcification — aged double mutants were not characterised — and it reports no demyelination and does not examine oligodendrocytes. MDA5 is therefore the necessary sensor for the brain interferon signature and gliosis in this model; its role in the calcification and any role in myelin pathology are untested. (The source describes the calcification as deep white matter in the abstract and deep gray matter in the body.)

verdicts.claim: MDA5 drives myelin failure in an ADAR1 model and deleting MDA5 rescues it — but in Schwann cells/peripheral nerve, NOT oligodendrocytes/CNS
verdicts.reason: Verified verbatim against the Nat Commun 2020;11:198 abstract (PMID 31924792) via E-utilities: 'Neural crest specific conditional deletion of Adar1 in mice leads to global depigmentation and absence of myelin from peripheral nerves, resulting from alterations in melanocyte survival and differentiation of Schwann cells, respectively. Upregulation of interferon stimulated genes precedes these defects, which are associated with the triggering of a signature resembling response to injury in peripheral nerves. Simultaneous extinction of MDA5, a key sensor of unedited RNA, rescues both melanocytes and myelin defects in vitro, suggesting that ADAR1 safeguards neural crest derivatives from aberrant MDA5-mediated interferon production.' Every element of the claim maps onto this, including the two caveats the claim itself raises and that matter most: the rescue was demonstrated IN VITRO (the authors' own wording), and the system is neural-crest-derived Schwann cells and peripheral nerve, not oligodendrocytes or CNS. The claim is correctly and honestly scoped — it does not smuggle a peripheral result into a CNS conclusion. The follow-up citation (Zerad et al., Cells 2024, PMID 39682701, Egr1 in the Adar1-KO Schwann cell differentiation defect) is consistent with the record; I did not open it, so treat that one sentence as unchecked.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Gacem N et al., Nat Commun 2020;11:198 (PMID 31924792): neural-crest-specific conditional Adar1 deletion in mice causes global depigmentation and absence of myelin from peripheral nerves, arising from altered melanocyte survival and Schwann cell differentiation, preceded by ISG upregulation with an injury-response-like signature. 'Simultaneous extinction of MDA5... rescues both melanocytes and myelin defects IN VITRO.' This is the only model in which removing MDA5 rescues a myelin defect — but it is Schwann cells and PERIPHERAL nerve, the rescue is in vitro, and no CNS, oligodendrocyte or in-vivo myelin rescue is demonstrated. It therefore cannot be transferred to oligodendrocytes or to MS without new evidence.

verdicts.claim: Microglial MDA5 contributes to interferonopathy neuropathology, but the MDA5-dependence is only partial in vivo
verdicts.reason: The quoted facts are verbatim-correct but the headline inverts their weight. The eLife 2026;14:RP102900 abstract (PMID 41589671) states: 'Adar1 knockout elicited interferon secretion and impaired macrophage production in vitro, while preventing brain macrophage engraftment in vivo - phenotypes that can be rescued with concurrent mutation of Ifih1 (MDA5) in vitro, but not in vivo' and 'We demonstrated the ability of microglia-specific D1113H mutation to drive interferon production in vivo, suggesting microglia drive AGS neuropathology.' 'Not in vivo' is a FAILED rescue, not a partial one — 'only partial in vivo' softens a negative result into a graded positive. More importantly, the two findings are being fused: the in-vivo result that microglia drive interferon production comes from the D1113H experiment, in which Ifih1-dependence was NOT tested. So 'microglial MDA5 contributes to interferonopathy neuropathology' is not established by this paper — MDA5-dependence held in vitro and failed in vivo. Also, the cells are ER-Hoxb8 conditionally immortalized bone-marrow-derived macrophages transplanted into a microglia-free brain, i.e. microglia-like replacement cells, not endogenous microglia.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Nemec KM et al., eLife 2026;14:RP102900 (PMID 41589671) used ER-Hoxb8 conditionally immortalized macrophages (CRISPR-Cas9 Adar1-mutated) transplanted into microglia-free brains as a microglia-replacement model. Adar1 knockout elicited interferon secretion and impaired macrophage production in vitro and prevented brain macrophage engraftment in vivo; concurrent Ifih1 (MDA5) mutation rescued these phenotypes IN VITRO BUT NOT IN VIVO. Separately, microglia carrying the patient D1113H Adar1 mutation drove interferon production in vivo, 'suggesting microglia drive AGS neuropathology' — but Ifih1-dependence was not tested in that in-vivo experiment. The correct reading is that microglia-like cells can drive interferonopathy in vivo, while MDA5-dependence of the in-vivo phenotype was tested and NOT demonstrated; these are transplanted macrophage-derived cells, not endogenous microglia.

verdicts.claim: Human IFIH1 gain-of-function causes leukodystrophy-spectrum disease with demyelination and calcification, and regional calcification tracks regional IFIH1 protein expression — human genetic proof MDA5 activity is sufficient to injure white matter
verdicts.reason: The individual citations are real and mostly accurately quoted, but the synthesis overreaches in two specific ways. From the Gilani et al. abstract (PMID 30952201): the opening sentence 'Aicardi-Goutières syndrome (AGS) is a rare syndrome characterized by calcification, diffuse demyelination, and variable degree of brain atrophy' is the GENERIC textbook description of AGS in the introduction — it is NOT a finding in this IFIH1 case. What this case actually showed is microcephaly (916 g), 'relatively mild brain atrophy on gross examination', and 'multifocal calcifications limited to small to medium central nervous system arteries... involving bilateral cerebral cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus, and cerebellum', with calcospherules confined to vessel walls and perivascular area. Demyelination is not reported as a finding in the case. Presenting a background definition as case neuropathology is a real misattribution. Second, the correlation sentence is quoted accurately — 'The extent of calcifications was variable across different brain regions... and correlated with the extent of IFIH1 protein expression (data derived from Allen Brain Institute)' — but this is n=1, qualitative, with no quantification, no statistics, and against an atlas resource that is principally mRNA/ISH-based; 'tracks' and 'proof... sufficient' are far stronger than an unquantified visual correlation in a single autopsy. Ruaud et al. (PMID 29782060) is confirmed exactly: heterozygous IFIH1 c.2544T>G (p.Asp848Glu), gain-of-function confirmed in HEK293T, segregating in two male siblings and the daughter of one, intracranial calcification in all symptomatic members, marked ISG upregulation in all three plus two clinically unaffected relatives — note that paper reports calcification with NO demyelination and explicitly no intellectual disability. Kothur et al. (PMID 29321238) is confirmed as 'An open-label trial of JAK 1/2 blockade in progressive IFIH1-associated neuroinflammation', Neurology 2018. Peixoto de Barcelos et al. (PMID 39332260) is confirmed: IFIH1 n=19 of 167 genetically confirmed AGS = 11.4%.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Human IFIH1 gain-of-function causes a type I interferonopathy spectrum with prominent INTRACRANIAL CALCIFICATION, accounting for 19/167 (11.4%) of genetically confirmed AGS in the Myelin Disorders Biorepository Project (PMID 39332260). Ruaud et al. (Hum Mutat 2018, PMID 29782060) report heterozygous IFIH1 c.2544T>G (p.Asp848Glu), gain-of-function in HEK293T, segregating with autosomal-dominant early-onset spastic paraparesis plus intracranial calcification in 3 affected individuals, with marked ISG upregulation in all three and in two clinically unaffected relatives — calcification without reported demyelination. The single IFIH1-AGS autopsy (Gilani et al., PMID 30952201) found microcephaly (916 g), relatively mild atrophy, and multifocal calcification limited to small-to-medium CNS ARTERIES in cortex, basal ganglia, thalamus and cerebellum; diffuse demyelination is the paper's generic description of AGS, not a finding in this case. The authors note that regional calcification 'correlated with the extent of IFIH1 protein expression (data derived from Allen Brain Institute)', but this is an unquantified qualitative observation in n=1 with no statistics. JAK1/2 blockade has been trialled open-label in progressive IFIH1-associated neuroinflammation (PMID 29321238). Together this shows CNS MDA5 overactivity is sufficient to cause human CNS disease dominated by vascular calcification; it is not proof that MDA5 injures white matter or myelin.

verdicts.claim: Human MS genetic and peripheral-expression data link IFIH1 to MS, but with weak/ambiguous effects and no CNS cell-type resolution
verdicts.reason: The Enevold et al. quote is verbatim in the J Neuroimmunol 2009;212(1-2):125-131 abstract (PMID 19450885): 'Our results support previous findings of associations between the IFIH1-locus and MS (IFIH1-rs3747517 and IFIH1-rs1990760 trend test: P=0.002 and P=0.014, respectively)', with the design confirmed as 963 MS patients and 960 controls genotyped across 42 SNPs in TLR1-10, NOD1-2, DDX58 and IFIH1. The claim's self-characterisation as weak/ambiguous is if anything generous to the data: with 42 SNPs tested, a Bonferroni threshold is ~0.0012, so rs1990760 at P=0.014 does not survive correction and rs3747517 at P=0.002 only marginally fails it — this is the single most important caveat and it is not stated in the claim. The Hundeshagen/MX1-high element reaches this claim through a review (Deerhake et al., Front Immunol 2019, PMID 31798505) rather than the primary paper, so that strand is second-hand as cited; the underlying point that it is PERIPHERAL BLOOD mononuclear cell expression, not CNS, is correctly flagged and is the decisive limitation. The claim's final sentence — that the review does not specify which CNS cell types express MDA5 in MS — is exactly right and is the honest core of this item.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Enevold C et al., J Neuroimmunol 2009;212(1-2):125-131 (PMID 19450885) genotyped 963 MS patients and 960 controls across 42 SNPs in TLR1-10, NOD1-2, DDX58 and IFIH1 and report 'associations between the IFIH1-locus and MS (IFIH1-rs3747517 and IFIH1-rs1990760 trend test: P=0.002 and P=0.014)' — uncorrected p-values that do not survive Bonferroni correction for 42 SNPs (~0.0012), so this is suggestive rather than established. Elevated DDX58 and IFIH1 expression has been reported in the MX1-high (endogenous type I IFN-high) subgroup of MS patients in PERIPHERAL BLOOD mononuclear cells (Hundeshagen et al. 2012, J Neuroinflammation 9:140, as summarised in the review by Deerhake et al., PMID 31798505 — cited here second-hand). No human study resolves IFIH1/MDA5 expression by CNS cell type in MS, and none of this evidence is CNS-derived.

verdicts.claim: dsRNA is elevated in early MS peripherally but essentially absent from CSF, and IFIH1 was not measured — so 'endogenous dsRNA drives MDA5 in the MS CNS' is unsupported by direct CNS measurement
verdicts.reason: Every number verified against the paper (PMID 41395469, PMC12698519). Cohort exact: 70 treatment-naive MS patients at first clinical onset with matched plasma and CSF, plus plasma from 26 sex- and age-matched healthy controls. Plasma dsRNA 51 ± 13 ng/ml in MS versus 44 ± 10 ng/ml in controls, p = 0.0231, Mann-Whitney U — all four values exact. CSF: 22 MS patients tested, exactly 1 detectable (the full text notes this single patient, Patient E, was positive across four independent experiments; the other 21 negative) — matches, and the abstract independently refers to 'the single patient with detectable CSF dsRNA'. IFN-gamma correlation r = 0.45, p = 0.002 exact, and the abstract's correlate list (GM-CSF, IFN-lambda1, IFN-lambda2/3, IFN-gamma, IFN-alpha2, IL-12p70) matches the claim's. Confirmed that IFIH1, MDA5, DDX58 and RIG-I expression are NOT measured anywhere in the paper — they appear only as background receptors that recognise dsRNA. The claim's inference is correctly scoped: it reports an absence as an absence rather than converting it into a finding. Note the effect size is modest (51 vs 44 ng/ml, heavily overlapping distributions) and the study is a first-onset cohort, so it does not speak to established or progressive MS.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Gouzouasis V et al., Front Microbiol 2025;16:1706133 (PMID 41395469) measured dsRNA by sandwich ELISA in matched plasma and CSF from 70 treatment-naive MS patients at first clinical onset plus plasma from 26 matched controls. Plasma dsRNA was modestly but significantly higher in MS (51 ± 13 vs 44 ± 10 ng/ml, Mann-Whitney p=0.0231; heavily overlapping distributions) and correlated with antiviral cytokines including IFN-gamma (r=0.45, p=0.002), GM-CSF, IFN-lambda1, IFN-lambda2/3, IFN-alpha2 and IL-12p70. In CSF, only 1 of 22 MS patients tested had detectable dsRNA. IFIH1/MDA5 and DDX58/RIG-I were not measured. There is therefore no direct measurement supporting elevated dsRNA ligand or MDA5 engagement within the MS CNS; the peripheral signal is real but modest and confined to first-onset patients.

verdicts.claim: There is NO published Ifih1-/- EAE study and NO study of MDA5 in the cuprizone model
verdicts.reason: I re-ran all four queries against the PubMed E-utilities API and reproduced the counts exactly: 'cuprizone[tiab] AND (Ifih1[tiab] OR MDA5[tiab] OR "RIG-I"[tiab])' = 0; '("EAE" OR "experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis") AND ("Mda5-deficient" OR "Ifih1-/-" OR "MDA5 knockout" OR "Ifih1 knockout")' = 0; '("experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis"[tiab] OR EAE[tiab]) AND (Ifih1[tiab] OR MDA5[tiab])' = 1, and that single hit is PMID 22566948, a Front Immunol review by Prinz and Knobeloch, not a primary study; '(Ifih1 OR MDA5) AND (EAE OR encephalomyelitis)' = 15. I additionally ran 'cuprizone AND (Ifih1 OR MDA5)' without field tags = 0, and retrieved titles for all 15 hits of query 4 plus a broader demyelination query: none is an Ifih1-/- EAE experiment (they are TBK1 deficiency, ME/CFS, AGS clinical series, coronavirus/norovirus virology, the Theiler's papers already in this claim set, and reviews). Two scope caveats. Absence from title/abstract-restricted queries is weaker than 'no published study' — a cell-type-conditional Ifih1 knockout could be reported without those terms in the title or abstract, and PubMed indexing lags. And 'systematic PubMed queries' overstates four keyword searches. The substantive conclusion nevertheless holds and is the single most useful negative in this claim set.
verdicts.corrected_claim: As of these searches (reproduced independently), PubMed title/abstract queries return zero primary studies of Ifih1-/- (MDA5-knockout) mice in EAE and zero studies of MDA5/RIG-I in the cuprizone model; the only EAE+MDA5 title/abstract hit is a review (Prinz M, Knobeloch KP, Front Immunol 2012;3:67, PMID 22566948). No oligodendrocyte-, astrocyte- or microglia-conditional Ifih1 knockout in any demyelination model was found. All EAE evidence for the RLR pathway is therefore indirect — global Mavs-/- (Dann 2012) or ligand/constitutive-signalling pharmacology (Dann 2012; Hansen 2022). This is an absence in keyword-indexed title/abstract search, not a proof of non-existence; note also that MDA5 knockout HAS been tested in a viral demyelination model (TMEV, Jin 2012).

verdicts.claim: Ifih1 is absent from the interferon-responsive oligodendrocyte signatures of every major recent demyelination single-cell/epigenomic study except Falcao 2018
verdicts.reason: This is a compound universal negative across six studies, and verifying it requires reading full supplementary gene tables for each — a gene's absence from a summary signature list in a fetched abstract or results section does not establish its absence from the underlying differential-expression output. I could not confirm the absences. What I could check: the citations themselves. PMIDs and DOIs for (a) Aboelnour, Nat Commun 2026, 10.1038/s41467-026-72383-y, PMID 42151131 ('A comparative transcriptomic analysis of mouse demyelination models and multiple sclerosis lesions'), (b) Hou, Cell Rep 2023, PMID 36952346, and (c) Zheng, Nat Neurosci 2025, PMID 41249698 all resolve correctly and match their descriptions. One citation is WRONG: (f) is cited as 'Oji S et al. PLoS One 2016;11(3):e0151244, PMID 26989859', but PMID 26989859 is 'Evaluation of the Biological Activity of Opuntia ficus indica as a Tissue- and Estrogen Receptor Subtype-Selective Modulator' in Phytotherapy Research — an unrelated paper. The correct PMID for the Oji NMO/EAE type I IFN signature paper is 26990978. Substantively, the framing is also in tension with evidence the claim does not consider: Kapil et al., Glia 2012 (PMID 22736486) reports that Mda5 transcripts ARE present in FACS-purified mouse oligodendroglia and ARE upregulated by infection in vivo, so Ifih1 is not outside interferon-responsive oligodendroglial biology — it is simply a low-abundance ISG unlikely to surface in top-marker signature lists from sparse single-cell data, which is a detection-sensitivity issue rather than evidence of absence.
verdicts.corrected_claim: Ifih1 does not appear among the reported interferon-responsive oligodendrocyte signature genes in the summary gene lists of several recent demyelination single-cell/epigenomic studies (Aboelnour et al., Nat Commun 2026, PMID 42151131; Hou et al., Cell Rep 2023, PMID 36952346; Zheng et al., Nat Neurosci 2025, PMID 41249698; Meijer et al., Neuron 2022; Kenigsbuch et al., Nat Neurosci 2022; Oji et al., PLoS One 2016 — correct PMID 26990978, NOT 26989859 as cited). Those signatures are dominated by Ifit1/Ifit3/Mx1/Irf7-type ISGs and MHC-I/II genes. However, absence from a published summary signature list is NOT verified absence from the underlying data — I could not check the supplementary tables — and Ifih1 is a low-abundance transcript that sparse single-cell assays are poorly powered to call.
